(4) of:--Hé his bróðer ádráf of éðele, Chr. 380; P. 11, 10: Sat. 201: Bo. 18. Gif man folan of ádrífe, Ll. Th. i. 72, 1. Ðæt hé ðæt deófol of men ádrífe, Bl. H. 43, 23. Hí woldon heora kynehláford of his cyneríce ádrífan, Chr. 1075; P. 211, 20: Sat. 174. Se frumstól ðe hié of ádrifen wurdon, Gen. 964. (5) út:--Út ádriofan arcebant, Wrt. Voc. ii. 9, 28. Ðá heretohan ðe hí &aelig-acute;r út ádrifon, hí woldon eft út ádrifan for hiora oferméttum, Bt. 16, 2; F. 50, 11. Ýð út feor ádráf on Wendels&aelig-acute; wígendra scola, Met. 26, 30. Ðæt Egypti ádrifen Moyses út, Ors. 1, 5; S. 34, 16. Út ádrífende explodens, An. Ox. 17, 22. Út ádrifenum explosis, út ádrifenre explosa, Wrt. Voc. ii. 32, 14, 15. [Goth. us-dreiban: O. H. Ger. ar-tríban expellere, repudiare.]
á-drifenness, -drígan. v. onweg-ádrifenness, á-drýgan.
á-drincan. Add: I. to drink up, quench thirst:--Ic of ádrince ebibo, Ælfc. Gr. 275, 9. Hw&aelig-acute;r hié wæteres hæfden þæt hié mehten him þurst of ádrincan, Ors. 2, 5; S. 80, 10. II. to be drowned; of ships, to be sunk:--Manega menn ádrincað on ánum dæge tógædere, ðe on mislicum tídum tó middanearde cómon, Hml. S. 5, 275. Eall ðæt mancynnes elles wæs, eall hit ádranc, Wlfst. 10, 13. On ð&aelig-acute;re s&aelig-acute; ádranc Pharao, Hml. Th. ii. 200, 17: Chr. 933; P. 107, 4. Heora feala ádruncon, 794; P. 57, 14: Ors. 1, 7; S. 38, 34. Ðeáh ðe hié &aelig-acute;r eorþe bewrigen hæfde, oððe on wætere ádruncan, Bl. H. 95, 15. Ð&aelig-acute;r wearþ monig mon ofslægen and ádruncen, Chr. 853; P. 66, 2: Ors. 2, 5; S. 82, 27. Heora folces wæs V M ofslagen, and heora scipa xxx gefangen, and iiii and án hund ádruncen . . . and Rómána scipa ix ádruncen, 4, 6; S. 176, 12-14. [Þene put &thorn-bar; hit adronc inne, A. R. 58. In ane watere heo adronken, Lay. 2490. Þat water þer Abren was adrunken, 2497. In þe se adronke he was, R. Glouc. 430. O. H. Ger. ar-trinkan to be drowned; ar-trunken crapulatus (a vino): Ger. er-trinken.]
á-drúgian, -drúwian. Add: I. intrans. To dry up, (1) of material containing moisture (lit. and fig.):--Ádrúgað (aruit) heorte mín, Ps. Srt. 101, 5. Wæstmas ádrúgiaþ, Bl. H. 59, 3. Ádrúgade exaruit, Mk. R. 4, 6. Ðá w&aelig-acute;tan hrægel ádrugedon, Bd. 5, 12; S. 631, 25. Míne bán ádrúchedon, Ps. L. 101, 4. Hig ádrúwodon aestuaverunt, Mt. 13, 6. Ádrúwodon ðá hláfas swá swá stán, Hml. S. 23 b, 520. Oþ ðæt ðæt dolh ádrúgie, Lch. ii. 208, 24. Ðeáh wé treówu for hrædlíce tó ð&aelig-acute;m weorce dón ne mægen for grénnesse &aelig-acute;r ð&aelig-acute;m ðe hí ádrúgien tamen non repente in fabrica ponitur lignum, ut prius vitiosa ejus viriditas exsiccetur, Past. 445, 2. Ðonne lungena wel ádrugode synd, Lch. ii. 216, 8. (2) of fluids:--S&aelig-acute; ádrúgaþ, Bl. H. 91, 27. Ádrúwode seó s&aelig-acute; xxx. míla, Shrn. 150, 21. Seó eá ádrúwode him ætforan, Hml. S. 19, 96. &AElig-acute;rþan þe ðæt flód mihte beón ádrúwod, Angl. vii. 36, 336. II. trans. :--Ádrúgie desiccet, Wrt. Voc. ii. 139, 27. v. un-ádrúgod.
á-drýgan. Add: to dry up (lit. and fig.). (1) to extract the moisture from material:--Hé ðá miltan ádrígeð, Lch. i. 334, 24. Gást unrót ádrígð (exsiccat) bánu, Scint. 167, 11. Hé ealle ðá costunga of his ágnum líchoman ádrígde omni illa tentatione carnis caruit, Gr. D. 190, 24. Hit ádríg, Lch. i. 332, 26. Ádríg tó duste, ii. 144, 1. Genim ácmistel and ádríge, 88, 5. Ádríged on réce, 216, 8. Swá swá treówu swíður ádrýgde bióð on eorðan quo plus in infimis humor excoquitur, Past. 445, 3. (2) to dry up a fluid:--Ðú ádrýgdes (exsiccasti) flódas, Ps. Srt. 73, 15. Hé ðone Reádan S&aelig-acute; ádrígde, Ors. 1, 7; S. 38, 29. Heortes horn hafað mægen &aelig-acute;lcne w&aelig-acute;tan tó ádrígenne, Lch. i. 334, 3. (3) to dry up moisture on material, wipe off:--Ádréið abstergit, Kent. Gl. 764. Seó hand ðínre spr&aelig-acute;ce ádrígde (tersit) fram mé ðone tweón, Gr. D. 150, 25. Hé ð&aelig-acute;re hýde giocðan of ádrýgde, Past. 71, 11. Ádrýg horu absterge sordes, Hy. S. 23, 3. &AElig-acute;lc mon ádrýge of óðerra monna móde ðone wénan be him &aelig-acute;lces yfeles, Past. 451, 22. Ðæt hé mæge ádrýggean (-drýgean, Hatt. MS.) (tergat) of monna heortan ðæt fúles sié, 74, 21. Hát gefeormian mín blód and ðonon ádrýgan, Bl. H. 183, 27. (4) to dry material on which there is moisture, wipe dry:--Se wísdóm ádrígde mínes módes eágan, Bt. 3, 1; F. 4, 27.
Á-DRYSENDLIC--&AElig-acute;CELMEHTE 9
á-drysendlic. v. un-ádrysendlic.
á-drysnan; p. ede To extinguish, repress:--Unsmyltnise ádrysnede tempestatem compescens, Mk. p. 3, 6. Ðæt fýr ne bið ádrysned (non extinguitur), Mk. L. 9, 46: Rtl. 38, 23. v. un-ádrysnende.
á-drysnendlic, adsa. v. un-ádrysnendlic, adesa.
á-dumbian. Add:--On ðám dóme ádumbiað ðá ýdelan lyffeteras, Hml. Th. ii. 570, 35. 'Beó ðú dumb' . . . And hé ðá ádumbode, i. 202, 7. Wið ðon ðe wíf f&aelig-acute;runga ádumbige, Lch. iii. 58, 16. Hét hé ðone hund ádumbian, Hml. S. 31, 1133. Se fæder wæs ádumbod, Hml. Th. i. 352, 32. Hí ealle wurdon ádumbode, ii. 486, 11.
á-dún, -dúne (-a). Add: (1) á-dún:--Feall nú ádún, Hml. Th. i. 166, 19: Hml. S. 11, 108. Hé ofdr&aelig-acute;d slóh ádún, 23, 718. (2) á-dúne (-a):--Feól hé ádúne, Hml. Th. 1, 316, 29. Hí lédon heora w&aelig-acute;pna ádúne, Hml. S. 29, 171. Clif áscoren rihte ádúne, 31, 316. Heáfod ádúne gewended, Bl. H. 173, 4. Ásend ðeh ádúna (deorsum), Lk. L. 4, 9. Cumað ádúne of heofonum tácn, Wlfst. 137, 12. Hé his gesyhða ádúna on eorðan besette, R. Ben. 31, 8. Úre blód fleóð tó úrum fótum ádúne, Hml. S. 11, 191. Doppettan ádúne tó grunde, Hml. Th. ii. 516, 7. v. of-dúne.
á-dustrian to imprecate(?):--Ðá ongann hé ádustriga (&ustriga, R.) tunc coepit detestari, Mt. L. 26, 74. Cf. &ustrungæ abominationem, Mt. R. 24, 15.
á-dw&aelig-acute;scan. Add: I. to extinguish fire, light (lit. or fig.):--Ðæt wæter and seó eorþe eallunga ne ádw&aelig-acute;sceþ ðæt fýr, Bt. 33, 4; F. 130, 14. Ð&aelig-acute;m gelícost ðe mon drýpe &aelig-acute;nne eles dropan on án micel fýr, and þence hit mid ð&aelig-acute;m ádw&aelig-acute;scan; ðonne is wén, swá micle swíðor swá hé þencð ðæt hé hit ádw&aelig-acute;sce, ðæt hé hit swá micle swíðor ontýdre, Ors. 4, 7; S. 182, 25. Sunne wearð ádw&aelig-acute;sced, Cri. 1133. Móna biþ ádw&aelig-acute;sced, Bl. H. 93, 18: Angl. viii. 315, 38. Ádw&aelig-acute;scedum extirpatis (fomitibus), An. Ox. 1134. II. to put an end to, put dawn, suppress a practice, doctrine, &c.:--Seó sunne ðá þeóstre ádw&aelig-acute;scþ, Bt. 4; F. 6, 33. Swá swá wæter ádw&aelig-acute;scð fýr, swá ádw&aelig-acute;scð seó ælmysse synna, Hml. Th. ii. 106, 7. Hié ádw&aelig-acute;scað ðá sibbe, Past. 359, 22. Ðæt hé ð&aelig-acute;ra gedwolmanna gedyrstignesse ádw&aelig-acute;scte, Hml. Th. i. 70, 7: Hml. S. 26, 13. Hé heora goda offrunga ádw&aelig-acute;scte, 15, 34. Drýcræft ádw&aelig-acute;scan, 14, 54: 23, 362: 37, 13. Bodunge ádw&aelig-acute;scan, Hml. i. 586, 33. III. to put down, suppress, destroy a person:--God ðá h&aelig-acute;ðenan ðeóda ætforan heora gesihðum eallunga ádw&aelig-acute;scte, Hml. Th. i. 46, 20. Ic beóde ðæt hé ðæne unrihtwísan tó rihte gebíge gyf hé mæge; gyf hé ne mæge, ðonne wille ic ðæt hé hine on earde ádw&aelig-acute;sce, oððe út of earde ádr&aelig-acute;fe, Cht. E. 230, 25. Se preóst is ádw&aelig-acute;sced (he was killed by a fall), Hml. Th. ii. 164, 8. Ádw&aelig-acute;sced explodatur i. deleatur (draco), An. Ox. 814. v. un-ádw&aelig-acute;sced.
á-dw&aelig-acute;scedlic, -dw&aelig-acute;scendlic. v. un-ádwæscedlic, -ádw&aelig-acute;scendlic.
á-dwelian. Dele -dwealde, -dweald, and add: I. intrans. To wander, stray:--Nýtenu hé hét faran áweg tó ð&aelig-acute;re eówode ðe hí of ádwelodon, Hml. Th. ii. 514, 23. Ðá hrægel from h&aelig-acute;lo gife ne ádweledon indumenta a gratia curandi non vacarunt, Bd. 4, 31; S. 611, 6. II. trans. (in Dict.) v. next word.
á-dwellan; p. -dwealde; pp. -dweald. I. to lead astray, seduce:--Ðá ðe galdorcræftas begangaþ and mid ð&aelig-acute;m unwære men beswícaþ and ádwellaþ, Bl. H. 61, 24. Hý deófol ádwealde, Wlfst, 11, 8. Ðá beóð ádwealde and þurh deófol beswicene, 5, 7. II. to retard, impede, obstruct, hinder:--Ðæt hé his láre ðurh drýcræft ádwellan sceolde, Hml. Th. ii. 412, 26. [Cf. O. H. Ger. ar-twelan torpere; ar-twellen to delay (intrans..]
á-dwínan. Add:--Ðá nigontýne geár gedóð ðæt án dæg mid ð&aelig-acute;re nihte ádwínð, and swylce ic swá cweðe tó náhte gewyrð, Angl. viii. 308, 32. Áduínendan tabida, Txts. 104, 1044.
a-dýdan, -dylegian, -dylf. v. á-dídan, -díligian, -delfan.
á-dysigian; p. ode To become foolish:--Manna mód syndon earmlíce áþýstrode and ádysgode, Wlfst. 185, 12.
æ. Omit the remarks on this letter.
&aelig-acute;. Add: &aelig-acute;(w); g. d. ac. &aelig-acute;, &aelig-acute;e, &aelig-acute;we (g. &aelig-acute;s in N. Gospels); g. pl. &aelig-acute;a; f. and n. (? in Bd. 4, 5; S. 573, 17). I. law, &c.:--Ðis is seó &aelig-acute; (lex) ðe Moises foresette, Deut. 4, 44: Past. 5, 25. Ðætte &aelig-acute;nigum folce his &aelig-acute;genu &aelig-acute; gelícade tó healdenne, Ors. 5, 15; S. 250, 19. Æew Dryhtnes, Ps. Srt. 18, 8. Ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute; (&aelig-acute;s, L.) láréow, Mt. 22, 35. &AElig-acute;we juris, Wrt. Voc. ii. 45, 18. Ð&aelig-acute;re ealdan &aelig-acute;we veteris legis, An. Ox. 40, 20. Ðæt hé of ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;we ne cerre, Past. 175, 5: 181, 1: 439, 30. Aee legem, Ps. Srt. 26, 11. &AElig-acute;a legum, Germ. 388, 16. &AElig-acute;wum cerimoniis, Hpt. xxxiii. 239, 26. II. matrimony:--Se hálga wer ð&aelig-acute;re wíflufan wordum stýrde unryhtre &aelig-acute;, Jul. 297. Lufiað eówere wíf on &aelig-acute;we . . . and healdað eówere &aelig-acute;we, Hml. Th. ii. 322, 26. Wíf ðæt him mid rihtre &aelig-acute; (rihtum &aelig-acute;we, v. l.) forgifen sí, Bd. 4, 5; S. 573, 17. Be ðám ðe &aelig-acute;we brecað de eo qui adulterat, Ll. Th. ii. 180, 12. Ic l&aelig-acute;rde weras ðæt hí heora &aelig-acute;we heóldon, Hml. Th. i. 378, 25: ii. 222, 18. See also &aelig-acute;w in Dict., and take &aelig-acute; life under this word. v. æfter-, sundor-, tungol-&aelig-acute;; cyric-, maegden-, riht-&aelig-acute;w.
&aelig-acute;-bær. Substitute: &aelig-acute;-b&aelig-acute;re (-bére); adj. Brought to light (of the criminal or the crime where guilt is manifest), notorious, proved:--&AElig-acute;b&aelig-acute;re (-bére) morð (apertum murdrum, Lat. Vers.), Ll. Th. i. 410, 5. Áb&aelig-acute;re, Wlfst. 274, 24. Se &aelig-acute;b&aelig-acute;ra þeóf (fur probatus, Lat. Vers.), Ll. Th. i. 390, 27. &AElig-acute;béra (-b&aelig-acute;ra), 268, 22. &AElig-acute;b&aelig-acute;re hórcwénan, 172, 21. &AElig-acute;b&aelig-acute;re manslagan, 324, 11. &AElig-acute;b&aelig-acute;re (-bére) manswican, Wlfst. 46, 27. &AElig-acute;bére apostatan, 165, 28. ¶ &AElig-acute;b&aelig-acute;re þeóf occurs in a list of privileges granted to a monastery:--On eallan þingan . . . ðe ð&aelig-acute;r mid rihte tó gebyrað, mid fyrdwíte and fyhtwíte and &aelig-acute;b&aelig-acute;re þeóf and griðbryce and foresteall and hámsócne, C. D. iv. 222, 23. [All þe&yogh;&yogh;re æbære unnþannkess, Orm. 7189. Þu ebure (ebare, 2nd MS.) sot, Lay. 2271. Þat eber file, C. M. 813. O. Frs. ábere, áubere.] v. á-b&aelig-acute;ran. See also ébere morþ in Dict.
&aelig-acute;-béc, -ber, -bilignes. v. &aelig-acute;-bóc, -b&aelig-acute;re, -byligness. In &aelig-acute;-bl&aelig-acute;cnys read Lchdm. i.
&aelig-acute;-bl&aelig-acute;cung. v. á-bl&aelig-acute;cung.
&aelig-acute;-bl&aelig-acute;te(?); adj. Livid, pale:--On &aelig-acute;bl&aelig-acute;tan (-bl&aelig-acute;can? v. &aelig-acute;-bl&aelig-acute;ce) and w[litan] albo vultu, An. Ox. 46, 19. v. blát.
æ-bléc. Substitute: &aelig-acute;-bl&aelig-acute;ce; adj. Pallid, pale, livid:--&AElig-acute;bl&aelig-acute;ce decolor, pallidus, Germ. 392, 69: pallidus, An. Ox. 1868. On plúmfeðerum hé líð ac þéhweðere oft &aelig-acute;bl&aelig-acute;ce, E. Stud. viii. 473, 19. Hé wearð geangsumod, and &aelig-acute;bl&aelig-acute;ce on nebbe cwæþ, Hml. S. 37, 213. Ðá áxode hé mid &aelig-acute;bl&aelig-acute;cum andwlitan his réðan cwelleras, 129. Be hiora híwe . . . hí beóð &aelig-acute;bl&aelig-acute;ce, Lch. ii. 232, 2.
&aelig-acute;-bóc book of law:--&AElig-acute;béc libri juris, Wrt. Voc. ii. 53, 78.
&aelig-acute;-bod. Add: A statute: &AElig-acute;bod pragma, Wrt. Voc. i. 20, 34. &AElig-acute;bodas, 35.
&aelig-acute;-br&aelig-acute;ce (&aelig-acute;w-, eáw-); adj. Law-breaking. (1) sacrilegious, impious:--Gehýrde gé ð&aelig-acute;ra deófla frófor on ðisum eáwbr&aelig-acute;cum ðe úre godas geyrsode ne ondr&aelig-acute;t? Hml. Th. i. 426, 20. (2) adulterous:--Ðæt se wer gewítnað on &aelig-acute;wbr&aelig-acute;cum wífe, ðæt wrecð God on &aelig-acute;wbr&aelig-acute;cum were, 378, 26. Eáwbr&aelig-acute;cum, ii. 322, 18. Be ðám ðe &aelig-acute;we brecað oððe &aelig-acute;wbr&aelig-acute;ce (adulteram) habbað, Ll. Th. ii. 180, 12.
&aelig-acute;-brec. Dele.
&aelig-acute;-breca (&aelig-acute;w-breca, q. v. in Dict.), an; m. An adulterer; of a man in orders, one who does not observe celibacy:--Se man ðe his riht&aelig-acute;we forl&aelig-acute;t and óðer wíf nimð, hé bið &aelig-acute;wbreca (adulter), Ll. Th. ii. 184, 22. Ðá &aelig-acute;wbrecan ðe þurh heálicne hád ciric&aelig-acute;we underféngan, and syððan ðæt ábr&aelig-acute;can, 334, 14. &AElig-acute;wbrecan and ðá fúlan forlegenan, Wlfst. 26, 15. v. &aelig-acute;-bryce.
&aelig-acute;-brecþ, e; f. Sacrilege:--Þurh &aelig-acute;brecþe per sacrilegium, Ps. L. fol. 182 b.
æbreda. v. æfreda.
&aelig-acute;-brucol; adj. Sacrilegious:--&AElig-acute;brucolon sacrilegis, Germ. 402, 86.
&aelig-acute;-bryce (&aelig-acute;w-bryce, q. v. in Dict.):--Adultery; of a churchman, neglect of celibacy:--Ðá ðe on sinscipe wuniað and heora &aelig-acute;we healdað búton &aelig-acute;wbryce, Hml. A. 21, 178. Ðá ðe &aelig-acute;wbryce ne wyrceað, 19, 140. Sé ðe ofer his &aelig-acute;we h&aelig-acute;mð, hé is forlír ðurh his &aelig-acute;wbryce, Hml. Th. ii. 208, 17. Nis nánum weófodþéne álýfed ðæt hé wífian móte . . . nú is þeáh ð&aelig-acute;ra ealles tó fela ðe ðone &aelig-acute;wbryce wyrcað, Ll. Th. ii. 334, 17, 22. Scyldað eów wið &aelig-acute;wbrycas (-brecas, v. l.), Wlfst. 40, 12. &AElig-acute;wbricas, 130, 4.
æbs. Substitute: Æbs, æps, æspe (from confusion with æspe aspen), a fir-tree:--Æps (æbs v. l.) abies, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 14, 11: 52, 14. Æps abies, Wrt. Voc. i. 80, 24. Etspe ii. 98, 14. Æspe, 4, 10. [From Latin.]
&aelig-acute;-bylg; m.:--Geæfnan &aelig-acute;bylg Godes to excite God's anger, Gú. 1211.
&aelig-acute;-bylga, an; m. Anger:--&AElig-acute;bylgan indignationem, Ps. L. 77, 49.
&aelig-acute;-bylgan, -byligan, -bylian. Add:--&AElig-acute;bylgað exasperant, Ps. Spl. 65, 6. &AElig-acute;biliaþ, 67, 7. v. ge-&aelig-acute;byl(i)gan.
&aelig-acute;-byl(i)gness. Add:--&AElig-acute;bylgnis indignatio, Bl. Gl. Of ðám leahtre (weámét) cymð hreám, and &aelig-acute;bilignys, Hml. Th. ii. 220, 14. Hé hí mid gedréfedre &aelig-acute;bilignysse him fram ádráf, 24, 30: Ap. Th. 4, 10. Racha getácnað &aelig-acute;bylignysse oððe yrre, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 279, 18. &AElig-acute;bilignysse, 280, 3. Ðæt heó ðá &aelig-acute;bylignysse gebéte ðe heó Gode ábylgð iram Dei quam excitaverit placare, Ll. Th. ii. 188, 4. v. a-bylgnes in Dict.
&aelig-acute;-byl(i)gþ(u); f. (but n. in El. 401). Add: (1) anger:--Ébylgðu indignatio, Ps. Srt. 68, 25. In ébylgðu in indignatione, 29, 6. Gif hwylce beóð ðára ðe hwæt &aelig-acute;bylhða wið óðre habbað, ðonne sceolan hig ðá forgyfan if there are any of those that have any angry feelings against others, they shall give up those feelings, Ll. Th. ii. 434, 7. (2) what causes anger, offence, injury:--Ðá sendon Rómáne &aelig-acute;rendracan and b&aelig-acute;don ðæt him man gebétte ðæt him ð&aelig-acute;r tó ábylgðe (&aelig-acute;-, v. l.) gedón wæs missi a Romanis legati, ut de illatis quererentur injuriis, Ors. 4, 1; S. 154, 11. Nánum syllende &aelig-acute;nige &aelig-acute;byligþe (offensionem), Scint. 116, 14. Wé ðæt &aelig-acute;bylgð nyton ðe wé gefremedon wið ðec, El. 401. Þeáh wé &aelig-acute;bylgð wið hine oft gewyrcen, synna wunde, 513. [Cf. O. H. Ger. gi-buluht ira.] v. a-bylgþ in Dict.
&aelig-acute;c an oak. Dele; the passage belongs to ác, q. v.
&aelig-acute;-cambe, -cembe, an; f. Oakum:--Écambe s[t]uppa, Txts. 99, 1925. &AElig-acute;cemban s[t]upparum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 82, 15. [O. H. Ger. á-chambi stuppa.]
&aelig-acute;-celma. Add:--Écilma palagra, Txts. 85, 1500. &AElig-acute;cilma, Wrt. Voc. i. 288, 70. &AElig-acute;celma, ii. 67, 61. &AElig-acute;celman mulas, An. Ox. 1386.
&aelig-acute;celmehte; adj. Having chilblains:--Écilmehti palagdrigus, Txts. 85, 1523.
10 &AElig-acute;CEN--&AElig-acute;FEN-GEREORDIAN
&aelig-acute;cen; adj. Of oak. [In Lch. iii. 52, 2 for &aelig-acute;cenan read(?) &aelig-acute;renan.] [O. H. Ger. eichín: Icel. eikinn.] v. next word.
&aelig-acute;cen a wood of oaks:--&AElig-acute;cen roboretum, Wrt. Voc. i. 285, 82.
æcer. Add: I. in a general sense, field, land:--Æcer ager, Wrt. Voc. i. 53, 53. Si jaceat, jaceat in ungildan ækere, Ll. Th. i. 301, 23. (v. un-gilde.) I a. of arable land:--Gesáwen æcer vel land seges, Wrt. Voc. i. 53, 55. Se æker, Past. 411, 18. Hé on his æcere eóde, and his sulh on handa hæfde, Ors. 2, 6; S. 88, 8. Se H&aelig-acute;lend fór ofer æceras (acras, R.) abiit Jesus per sata, Mt. 12, 1. Hiora gem&aelig-acute;nan æceras oþþe gærs, Ll. Th. i. 128, 7. I b. the crop raised on the land (cf. Icel. akr crop):--Ðá ðá ðæt án corn feóll, ð&aelig-acute;r árás þicce æcer (seges), Gr. D. 240, 3. Ne þolie hé ðára æcra (æcera, v. l.), Ll. Th. i. 146, 5. II. a definite quantity of land, an acre. The acer seems to have been four rods broad, and forty rods long. v. Seebohm, Vill. Comm. s. v. acre, and Sax. Engl. i. 96:--Æceras jugeri, Wrt. Voc. ii. 46, 5. Twelf æceras m&aelig-acute;de, C. D. vi. 244, 12. xl æcera (cf. quadraginta jugeribus, l. 7), 1, 18. iii. æcera br&aelig-acute;de (v. passage under weall-stellung in Dict.), Ll. Th. i. 224, 9. v. bydel-, lín-, sulh-æcer, bóc-æceras.
æcer-ceorl. Add:--Æcerceorl rusticus, Wrt. Voc. i. 73, 33. [Cf. Icel. akr-karl a ploughman or reaper.]
æceren. v. æcern.
æcer-geard, es; m. An enclosure of arable land (? = Icel. akra-, akr&dash-uncertain;gerði) or the fence of a field (? v. geard):--On ðone æcergeard; á be ð&aelig-acute;m gearde, C. D. iii. 458, 24. v. next word.
æcer-hege, es; m. A field-hedge:--On ðone æcerhege; ondlong ðæs æcerheges, C. D. iii. 33, 2.
æcer-m&aelig-acute;lum; adv. By acres:--Ðæt land líð hídm&aelig-acute;lum and æcerm&aelig-acute;lum, C. D. vi. 98, 5.
æcer-mann. Add:--Æcerman agricola, Wrt. Voc. i. 74, 67. [Akerman, Halliw. Dict., O. H. Ger. achar-man arator: Icel. akr-maðr.]
æcern. Add:--Ðis æceren (æcern, v. l.) haec glans, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 61, 8: 312, 6: glandix, Wrt. Voc. i. 289, 29: ii. 41, 27. Heó eteð hnyte oþþe æceran, Lch. iii. 144, 20.
æcern-spranca, an; m. An acorn-sprout:--Æcernspranca (æcer-, v. l.) oððe ác ilex, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 69, 15.
æcer-s&aelig-acute;d, es; n. Seed for an acre:--Man sælde ðæt æcers&aelig-acute;d hw&aelig-acute;te, ðæt is twégen sédl&aelig-acute;pas, tó six scillingas, and ðæt bærlic, ðæt is þré sédl&aelig-acute;pas, tó six scillingas, and ðæt æcers&aelig-acute;d áten, ðæt is feówer sédl&aelig-acute;pas tó feówer scillingas, Chr. 1124; P. 254, 14-16. vi. æcers&aelig-acute;d . . . tó tióþunge . . . viiii. æcerséd (cf. twá hund æccra s&aelig-acute;d, 26; feórð healf hund æcere séd, 21), C. D. B. iii. 367, 30, 31, 27, 28.
æcer-splott, es; m. An acre-plot, an acre:--Ðæs healfes weres bóc and ðæs æcersplottes ðe ð&aelig-acute;rtó líð (cf. Cum unius jugeris sibi adjacentis portione, 134, 33), C. D. vi. 136, 12.
æcer-teóþung, e; f. Tithe from the produce of arable land:--Áríse seó æcerteóðung á be ðám ðe seó sulh ðone teóðan æcer &aelig-acute;r geeóde, Wlfst. 310, 24. [Cf. Icel. akr-tíund tithe paid on arable land.] v. Seebohm, Vill. Comm. pp. 114 sqq.
æcer-týning, e; f. Fencing of fields:--Æcertýninge .xv. gyrda, C. D. iii. 451, 2.
æcer-weg, es; m. A field-road:--Andlang æcerweges . . . eft on ðone æcerweg, C. D. vi. 137, 17, 22.
æcer-weorc, es; n. Field-work, agricultural labour:--Fra[m] hys æcerweorce agresti bonus, Germ. 391, 60. [Icel. akr-verk field-work, harvest-work.]
&aelig-acute;-cilma. v. &aelig-acute;-celma.
&aelig-acute;-cnósle; adj. Degenerate:--&AElig-acute;cnósle degener, ignobilis, dissimilis parentibus, &aelig-acute;cnóslum ádle degeneri languore, Wrt. Voc. ii. 138, 30-32: 75. v. ge-&aelig-acute;cnóslian.
&aelig-acute;-cræftig. Add:--&AElig-acute;cræftiga Pharisaei, &aelig-acute;cræftgum Pharisaeis, Mt. L. 12, 24, 38.
&aelig-acute;d(d)er, e; f. &aelig-acute;d(d)re, an; f. (wæter-&aelig-acute;dre occurs once neuter). Add to &aelig-acute;dre: I. a channel for fluids:--Ðín édra thy fountain (vena), Kent. Gl. 107: 330. Ealle eorðan &aelig-acute;ddre onsprungon ongeán ðám heofonlican flóde, Wlfst. 206, 18. &AElig-acute;þro botre (cf. botrus fossa, via imbribus excavata, Migne), Wrt. Voc. i. 287, 28. &AElig-acute;ddrum cataractis, An. Ox. 515. Ðæt wæter gewende þurh ðá díglan &aelig-acute;ddran ðisse eorþan (per occultas terrae venas), Angl. vii. 36, 342. I a. in reference to living things:--&AElig-acute;ddre arteria, Wrt. Voc. i. 64, 63: vena, 71, 44. His cræft gecymþ on &aelig-acute;lcere &aelig-acute;dre, Bt. 34, 11; F. 152, 2. Blód l&aelig-acute;tan of ðám swíðran earme on ð&aelig-acute;re niþeran &aelig-acute;dre, Lch. ii. 210, 10: 82, 16. Lege on ðá &aelig-acute;dre, 148, 18. Swá swá &aelig-acute;ddran licgeað on ðæs mannes líchaman, iii. 254, 22. On óðrum mónþe ðá &aelig-acute;dron beóð geworden, on lxv and þreó hundræd hí beóð tód&aelig-acute;lede, and ðæt blód ðonne flóweð on ðá fét, Nar. 49, 27. Ic eów, &aelig-acute;ddran (venae), bidde ðæt gé wylspringas ontýnan tó teárum, Dóm. L. 26. Tócnáwan be his &aelig-acute;drena hrepunge (by feeling his pulse) hweðer hé hraðe swulte, Hml. S. 3, 569. &AElig-acute;ddrum fibris, venis, An. Ox. 376: fibrarum rivulis, 11, 135. Wiþ ðá ðe habbað ætstandene &aelig-acute;dran, swá ðæt ðæt blód ne mæg hys gecyndelican ryne habban, Lch. i. 90, 11. II. a sinew:--Tól&aelig-acute;tenum &aelig-acute;ddrum laxis fibris, Hy. S. 102, 22. Ðá forcurfon hié him ðá twá &aelig-acute;dran on twá healfa ðára eágena resectis palpebris, Ors. 4, 6; S. 178, 23. III. a rein, kidney:--Héðir renis, Txts. 93, 1731. &AElig-acute;ddran renes, Wrt. Voc. i. 65, 25. &AElig-acute;dran (éðre, Ps. V.), Ps. Spl. 15, 7. Édran, Kent. Gl. 884. Éðra renium, Txts. 410, 27. Wið &aelig-acute;ddrena sáre, Lch. i. 190, 7. &AElig-acute;drena, 232, 17. &AElig-acute;ddran (éðre, Ps. V.) reues, Ps. Spl. C. 7, 10. v. geótend-, lungen-, middel-, wind-&aelig-acute;d(d)re.
&aelig-acute;d[d]er-seax. Add:--Flebotomum blódseax oððe &aelig-acute;dderseax. Græce namque fleps vena, tomum vero incisio nominatur, Wrt. Voc. ii. 39, 22.
æd-fæst. Dele, and see æt-fæstan.
ædre. l. &aelig-acute;dre: &aelig-acute;dre ( = &aelig-acute;ðre? cpve. of eáðe) levius, Wrt. Voc. ii. 53, 58.
&aelig-acute;-fægred disfigured:--&AElig-acute;fæ(g)rede larbatos [cf. hreófe larbatos (the passage is the same in both glosses), Wrt. Voc. ii. 86, 64; se unfægera larbata (facies), 95, 68], An. Ox. 4936.
æ-fæst (&aelig-acute;w-, eáw-, -fest). Add: I. religious:--Se &aelig-acute;wfæsta (religiosus) wer Laurentius, Gr. D. 12, 17. Mynstermen and widwan eáwfæstes lífes, Ll. Th. ii. 440, 27. Tó ðám &aelig-acute;wfæstum heápe, Hml. S. 28, 67. &AElig-acute;wfæstra manna líc hominum religiosorum cadavera, Ll. Th. ii. 160, 24. Mid eáwfæstum monnurn, 176, 1. Se weorðscipe ðisse worolde is gecierred tó weorðscipe ð&aelig-acute;m &aelig-acute;wfæstum, ðæt ðá sindon nú weorðoste ðe &aelig-acute;wfæstoste sindon; for ðon lícet monig ðæt hé &aelig-acute;wfæsð láreów sié, Past. 27, 2-5. &AElig-acute;feste (eáwfæste, v. l.) men, R. Ben. 119, 7. II. married:--Yfel &aelig-acute;wbryce bið ðæt &aelig-acute;wfæst (eáw-, v. l.) man mid &aelig-acute;mtige forlicge, Ll. Th. i. 404, 21. Se apostol áwrát be eáwfæstum werum: 'Lufiað, gé weras, eówere wíf on &aelig-acute;we,' Hml. Th. ii. 322, 25. Ic manode &aelig-acute;wfæste wíf, i. 378, 27.
æ-fæstan, Wrt. Voc. ii. 44, 72. v. æt-fæstan.
&aelig-acute;-fæsten (&aelig-acute;w-). Add:--On &aelig-acute;wfæstenum ic gesyngode, Angl. xi. 102, 66. &AElig-acute;fæstenu ic oft ág&aelig-acute;lde, 99, 62: Ll. Th. ii. 144, 23.
&aelig-acute;-fæstlic; adj. I. legitimate:--&AElig-acute;wfæstlicere legitime, An. Ox. 851. II. religious:--Hé forgitt ðæt hé &aelig-acute;r &aelig-acute;fæstlices (-fest-, Cott. MSS.) geðóhte obliviscitur quidquid religiose cogitavit, Past. 57, 8.
&aelig-acute;-fæstlíce; adv. Religiously:--Lifde hé &aelig-acute;festlíce his líf religiosam gerens vitam, Bd. 5, 12; S. 627, 10.
æ-fæstnes (&aelig-acute;w-, eáw-, -fest-, -feast-). Add:--&AElig-acute;fæstnis cl&aelig-acute;ne religio munda, Rtl. 29, 11. Ege Drihtnes ingehýdes &aelig-acute;wfæstnyss (religiositas), Scint. 65, 9. Aefeastnisse religionis, Rtl. 96, 9. Gewítan fram ðám bígange úre &aelig-acute;festnysse, Bd. 1, 7; S. 477, 21. Hí áxode hine hwylcere eáwfæstnysse hé w&aelig-acute;re, Hml. S. 22, 204. Eáwfæstnysse (regularis) discipline, Hpt. Gl. 403, 16. Mid &aelig-acute;fæsnesse, R. Ben. 139, 7.
æf-dæl. Substitute: æf-dæll, -dell, es; n.:--Tó æfdæll (-delle, R.), Lk. L. 19, 37. v. of-dæle. Cf. next word.
æf-dýne, es; m. A descent, declivity:--Æfdýni (&e-hook;sdyni, UNCERTAIN MS.) defexum, decliuium (cf. deuexu[m], declibium, descensum, Corp. Gl. Hessels. 41, 140), Hpt. 33, 250, 3.
æ-felle, a-felle. l. &aelig-acute;-felle.
&aelig-acute;fen. Add: &aelig-acute;fen[n], éf(e)rn; [m. and] n. I. evening:--&AElig-acute;fen vesperum, bedtíd serum, Wrt. Voc. i. 53, 15. Seó niht hæfð seofan d&aelig-acute;las . . óþer is uesperum, ðæt is &aelig-acute;fen, ðonne se &aelig-acute;fensteorra betwux ð&aelig-acute;re repsunge æteówað, Lch. iii. 242, 28: Angl. viii. 319, 28. Ðá éfern (éfen, R.) warð vespere facto, Mt. L. 26, 20. Ðá hyt &aelig-acute;fen (éfern, L.; æt &aelig-acute;fenne, R.) wæs cum sero factum esset, Mt. 27, 57. Éfrn, Mk. L. 11, 11, 19. Hí &aelig-acute;ton &aelig-acute;ne on dæg, and ðæt wæs tó &aelig-acute;fennes, Bt. 15; F. 48, 9. Éfernes, Mt. p. 20, 5. &AElig-acute;r &aelig-acute;fenne, Bd. 1, 27; S. 496, 28. On ðám &aelig-acute;fene, Mt. 26, 20. Oð ðæt &aelig-acute;fen forð fram dæges orde, El. 139. Metod æfter sceáf &aelig-acute;fen &aelig-acute;rest, Gen. 138. II. eve, the evening preceding a day (of festival). v. eáster-, mæsse-, mónan-, sunnan-, Þunres&dash-uncertain;&aelig-acute;fen:--Ðám restedæges &aelig-acute;fene (éfenne, R.; éfern, L.) sé ðe onlíhte on ðám forman restedæge, Mt. 28, 1. Árwurðiað ðisne &aelig-acute;fen, and ðone freólsdæg ðe eów tó merigen becymð, Hml. Th. ii. 370, 1. In ðone hálgan &aelig-acute;fen Pentecosten, Chr. 626; P. 24, 8. On ðone hálgan &aelig-acute;fen Inuentione s&c-tilde;e crucis, 912; P. 96, 30. On twelftan &aelig-acute;fen, 1053; P. 182, 38. v. gestran-&aelig-acute;fen.
&aelig-acute;fen-dreám. Add:--Se &aelig-acute;fensang sý geendod mid feówer sealma dreáme . . . ealle ðá óþre sýn tó ðám &aelig-acute;fendreáme gesungene vespera quattuor psalmorum modulatione canatur . . . reliqui omnes in vespera dicendi sunt, R. Ben. 43, 7-18.
&aelig-acute;fen-gebéd. l. -gebed, and add Wrt. Voc. i. 28, 30.
&aelig-acute;fen-gereord, e; f. Substitute: es; n. and add: Used in pl. for a single meal:--Gif hit beó seó tíd &aelig-acute;fengereordes, árísen hý sóna swá hý heora mete hæbben, and sitten on ánre stówe si tempus fuerit prandii mox ut surrexerint a cena sedeant omnes in unum, R. Ben. 66, 15. Æfter his &aelig-acute;fengereorde post caenam, Bd. 3, 11; S. 536, 12: Angl. xiii. 437, 1034. Úre Dryhten offrode æt his &aelig-acute;fengereorde, Btwk. 218, 9. W&aelig-acute;ron geworden Drihtnes &aelig-acute;fengereordu facta est cena Domini, Hml. A. 153, 41. Seó gálnes æt hyre &aelig-acute;fengereordum (in caena) sitt, Prud. 40 a. Hé sæt mid him æt ð&aelig-acute;m &aelig-acute;fengereordum, Bl. H. 73, 5: 143, 6. Martha gearwode ðám H&aelig-acute;lende &aelig-acute;fengereordu, 67, 26. Heora underngereordu and &aelig-acute;fengereordu hié mengdon tógædere, 99, 23.
&aelig-acute;fen-gereordian. l. -gereordan; p. de To provide with supper:--Dagum on ðám &aelig-acute;fengereorde synt gebróþru diebus quibus cenaturi sunt fratres, Angl. xiii. 437, 1030. v. next word.
&AElig-long;FEN-GEREORDUNG -- &AElig-long;FNIAN 11
&aelig-long;fen-gereordung, e; f. Supper :-- T&o-long; &aelig-long;fengereordunga lambes ad cenam Agni, Hy. S. 82, 3.
&aelig-long;fen-geweorc, es; n. Evening-work :-- Sele bollan fulne t&o-long; gedrin-canne æfter &aelig-long;fengeweorce, Lch. ii. 190, 3.
&aelig-long;fen-gifl. Add :-- Gyf w&e-long; fæsta&d-bar; and &d-bar;æt underngereord t&o-long; &d-bar;&a-long;m &aelig-long;fengifle healda&d-bar;, &d-bar;onne ne bi&d-bar; &d-bar;æt n&a-long;n fæsten, ac . , . bi&d-bar; &d-bar;æt &aelig-long;fengyfel getwifealdad, Ll. Th. ii. 436, 30. Gif h&y-long; on tw&a-long; m&aelig-long;l eta&d-bar;, s&y-long; gehealden &d-bar;æs pundm&aelig-long;tan hl&a-long;fes se þridda d&aelig-long;l t&o-long; &d-bar;&a-long;m &aelig-long;fengifle, R. Ben. 63, 16. Uton n&u-long; br&u-long;can &d-bar;isses undernmetes sw&a-long; &d-bar;&a-long; sculon &d-bar;e hiora &aelig-long;fengifl on helle gefeccan sculon prandete tamquam apud inferos coenaturi, Ors. 2, 5; S. 86, i: Past. 27, 8 : 323, 19.
&aelig-long;fen-gl&o-long;ma, an; m. Evening-twilight :-- Seó niht hafa&d-bar; seofon t&o-long;&d-bar;d&aelig-long;lednyssa. Crepusculum ys seó forme, &d-bar;æt ys &aelig-long;fengl&d-bar;ma, Angl. viii. 319, 27: Lch. iii. 242, 27.
&aelig-acute;fen-glommung, e j f. Evening-twilight :-- Sw&a-long; &d-bar;æt oft on middre niht geflit cyme&d-bar; &d-bar;&a-long;m behealdendum hwæþer hit s&i-long; &d-bar;e &aelig-long;fenglommung &d-bar;e on morgen deágung ita ut media saepe tempore noctis in quaestionem ueniat intuentibus, iterum crepusculum adhuc permaneat uespertinum, an iam nduenerit matutinum, Bd. S. 473, 31. &AElig-acute;fenglommunge crepusculum, Hy. S. 16, 31.
&aelig-long;fen-hrepsung. v. &aelig-long;fen-repsung.
&aelig-long;fen-lic. Add: -- &E-long;fernlicum t&i-long;dum vespertinis horis, Rtl. 174, 37.
&aelig-long;fen-l&i-long;ce; adv. In the evening :-- &A-long;rl&i-long;ce mane, &e-long;fenl&i-long;ce vespere, Rtl. 166, 3.
&aelig-long;fen-lof, es; n. Even-song :-- Æfter &aelig-long;fenlofe post uespertinalem laudem, Angl. xiii. 437, 1035.
&aelig-long;fen-mete, es; m. Add :-- &AElig-acute;fenmete cena, Wrt. Voc. i. 290, 66 : ii. 17, 26. Ðende hiá æt &d-bar;&aelig-long;rn &aelig-long;fenmete w&e-long;run coenantibus eis, Mt. R. 26, 26.
&aelig-long;fen-mete; adj. (?) Provided with supper; :-- UNCERTAIN(=-æt?) &e-long;fenmeti w&e-long;ron hiá coenantibus eis, Mt. L. 26, 26. v. preceding word.
&aelig-long;fen-r&aelig-long;ding, e; f. An evening reading; collatio (apud monachos sacrorum librorum lectio quae maxime post coenam coram iis fiebat, Migne) :-- Ðænne &aelig-long;fenr&aelig-long;ding (collatio) byþ ger&aelig-long;dd, Angl. xiii. 393, 400. T&a-long;cne &aelig-long;fenr&aelig-long;dincge gestyredum signo collationis moto, 416, 723. Niht-sang aefter æfterr&aelig-long;dincge (l. &aelig-long;fen-) completorium post collationem, 423, 828.
&aelig-long;fen-repsung, e; f. Eventide,night-fall :-- H&e-long; sl&e-long;p sw&a-long; hw&aelig-long;r sw&a-long; hine seó &aelig-long;fenrepsung gem&e-long;tte he slept wherever night overlook him, Hml. S. 236, 154, Sunne heó &d-bar;&a-long; t&o-long; setle &a-long;hylde, and &d-bar;&aelig-long;re &aelig-long;fenrepsunge geneálæhte, 498.
&aelig-long;fen-rima. Dele.
&aelig-long;fen-sang. Add :-- Ne s&y-long; &aelig-long;fensang geendod b&u-long;tan &d-bar;&a-long;m drihtlican gebede. R. Ben. 38, 15. Se &aelig-long;fensancg mid antefene s&y-long; gecweden, 39, 20. Se &aelig-long;fensang s&y-long; geendod mid feówer sealma dreáme, 43, 7. Ðone lofsang (the Magnificat) &d-bar;e w&e-long; singa&d-bar; on Godes cyrcan æt &aelig-long;lcum &aelig-long;fensange, Hml. Th. i. 202, 26. S&e-long; &d-bar;e . . . dæghw&a-long;ml&i-long;ce his circan ges&e-long;can ne mæge, h&e-long; h&u-long;ru &d-bar;inga on &d-bar;&a-long;m sunnandagnm . . . þider cume t&o-long; . . . &AElig-acute;fensange, Hml. A. 144, ii. Singan &aelig-long;fen oþþe nihtsange cantare vesperum aut completorium, Coll. M. 34, 3. &AElig-acute;fensang vesperam, Angl. Xiii. 392, 385 : vespertinalem sinaxim, 425, 863: 432, 964. &AElig-acute;fensangas singan vesperas celebrare, 415, 711.
&aelig-long;fen-sceóp,-spræc. l. &aelig-long;fen-scop, -spr&aelig-long;c.
&aelig-long;fen-steorra. Add :-- &AElig-acute;fensteorra hesperos, Germ. 394, 329. Ðes &aelig-long;fensteorra hic vesper, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 43, 12. Se f&i-long;fta is gehaten Venus, s&e-long; is &aelig-long;fensteorra, Scrd. 18, 36. Vesperum, &d-bar;æt is &aelig-long;fen, &d-bar;onne se &aelig-long;fen-steorra æteówa&d-bar;, Lch. iii. 242, 28.
&aelig-long;fen-þ&e-long;nung, -þegnung. Add: I. evening service of the Church :-- &AElig-acute;fen&d-bar;&e-long;nunge singe &a-long;nra gehwilc vespertinum officium canat unusquisque, Angl. xiii. 422, 823. H&y-long; scylon embe &d-bar;&a-long; nigo&d-bar;an t&i-long;de heora mæssan gestandan and æfter &d-bar;&a-long;m heora &aelig-long;fenþ&e-long;nunga. Hml. A. 141, 74. II. serving of food in the evening, supper :-- &AElig-acute;fenþ&e-long;nunge. cene, R. Ben. I. 71,I. H&i-long; &a-long;r&i-long;sa&d-bar; fram &aelig-long;fenþ&e-long;nunge (cena), 74, 10. &AElig-acute;fenþ&e-long;nunga ge-&d-bar;&o-long;nre cena facta, Angl. xiii. 437, 1030. Gif h&i-long; sceolan on &aelig-long;fen gereordian of &d-bar;&a-long;m sylfan punde se þridda d&aelig-long;l s&i-long; gehealden t&o-long; &a-long;gifenne on &aelig-long;fen-þinungum, R. Ben. I. 71, 3.
&aelig-long;fen-þeówdóm. Add :-- -Wrt. Voc. i. 28, 30.
&aelig-long;fen-t&i-long;d. Add :-- Hoc vesperum o&d-bar;&d-bar;e vespere bi&d-bar; &aelig-long;fent&i-long;d, Ælfc. Gr. 2. 43, 12 note. &A-long;feóll (&a-long;s&a-long;h, v.l.) seó &aelig-long;fent&i-long;&d-bar; ilæs dæges diei tardior hora incubuerat, Gr. D. 83, 15. H&e-long;r wæs Eádweard cyng ofslagen on &aelig-long;fent&i-long;de, Chr. 979; P. 123, 6. On &aelig-long;fent&i-long;d. Shrn. 116, 8. On &d-bar;&a-long; &aelig-long;fent&i-long;d. Nar. 29, 21. In éferntíd vespere, Mt. L. 8, 16. On &e-long;fnit&i-long;d UNCERTAIN (&e-long;fern-, R.) sero, Mk. L. 13, 35. Oþ &aelig-long;fent&i-long;d ad vesperum, Bd. l, 27; S. 496, 34.
&aelig-long;fen-t&i-long;ma., Add :-- On &aelig-long;fent&i-long;man &u-long;re Dryhten offrode æt his &aelig-long;fengereorde, Btwk. 218, 9: Hml. S. 15, 58.
&aelig-long;fen-tungel. Dele &aelig-long;fenian, &aelig-long;fenung. v. &aelig-long;fnian, &aelig-long;fnung. æfer, Lch. ii. 22, 7. v. &a-long;for.
æfer&d-bar;e, an; f. A plant-name :-- Dolhsealf: &a-long;crind, æfer&d-bar;e . . . , Lch. ii. 94, 14. Æfert&d-bar;e niþeweard, 110, I. Nim æferþan nioþowearde, 142, 23: 340, 3.
æfesa (-e; f, f), an; m. Produce of woods on which swine might be fed :-- Mid mæste and mid æuesan . . . and ic ann &d-bar;æt &d-bar;ridde swun (?) of æuesan &d-bar;æs n&e-long;xtan wudes &d-bar;e l&i-long;þ t&o-long; kyngesbyrig cum porcorum esca et cum fructibus . . . quoaue dono tertiam sarcinam iumentariam fructuum qui nascuntur in sylua proxime ad kyngesbyrig sita, C. D. iv. 202, 2-12. [In the Domesday of St. Paul's of the year 1222 (Camden Society, 1858) is this entry: ' Debent dare de singulis animalibus . iij. ob' UNCERTAIN annum si ad pasturam dm venerint similiter de equis et de singulis porcis .j. &d-bar;. UNCERTAIN Garsavese, ' p. 51. See also note p. lxviii on garsavese, where another instance of its use is given as well as an instance of a verb avesare (avesabit porcos).] v. æfesn, æfes-weorc.
æfesc. v. efes.
æfesn. Add; Pannage, v. æfesa, and E. Stud. 27, 218 : æfesne obscenitas. v. æpsen.
æf-&e-long;st. l. æf-est(-æst, -ist), æfst, æfstu; m. f. Add; I. in a bad sense :-- Se dierna æfst. Past. 79, 13. Be &d-bar;&a-long;m is &a-long;writen &d-bar;ætte &d-bar;is fi&aelig-long;sclice l&i-long;f sié &aelig-long;fes&d-bar; (invidia), 235, 13. For &d-bar;æs æfstes scylde per livoris vitium, 237, i. Æfestes, Wrt. Voc. ii. 50, 12. Mid &d-bar;&aelig-long;re biteran æfeste, Bl. H. 25, 7. Mid &d-bar;&a-long;m þyccylum &d-bar;&aelig-long;re æfæste invidiae, Gr. D. 117, 28: 118, 2. Æfstu, Ps. Th. 69, 4. Hié hié nylla&d-bar; healdan wi&d-bar; &d-bar;&aelig-long;m æfste (livore) . . . for &d-bar;æs lytegan fióndes æfeste (invidia) deá&d-bar; bec&o-long;me ofer eor&d-bar;an, Past. 233, 17-19. &A-long;weorpan &d-bar;one æfst, 25. Hié him æfest t&o-long; gen&a-long;man they became envious of him, Bl. H. 7, ll. Æfeste &a-long;nforl&aelig-long;tan, G&u-long;. 158 : Fä. 36. Æfest invidiam, Mt. p. I, 10. Þurh æfeste (æfist, L.), Mt. R. 27, 18 : Mk. R. 15, 10. N&i-long;&d-bar; and æfesta odium et invidiae, Ll. Th. ii. 174, 32. Æfisto invidias, Rtl. 25, 25. II. in a good sense, zeal :-- Be g&o-long;dum æfste (zelo) &d-bar;e munecas habban sceolon, R. Ben. 131, II. Elnung &l-bar; æfista h&u-long;ses &d-bar;ines zelus domus tuae, Jn. R. 2, 17.
æfeste (?); adj. Envious :-- Se æfæsta (æfæstiga, v. l.) mæssepreóst, Gr. D. 117, 18. v. æfestian.
æf-&e-long;stian, -&e-long;stigan. Substitute: æf(e)stian. I. to envy :-- Hit þweora manna þeáw is &d-bar;æt h&i-long; æfæstia&d-bar; &o-long;þra manna g&o-long;dd&aelig-long;de mos pravorum est invidere aliis virtutis bonum. Gr. D. 117, 4. II. to grow envious :-- Æfestian libescant, Wrt. Voc. ii. 50, 41. v. æf(e)stigian, æf(e)stung, æfeste.
æf(e)stig. Add: I. in a bad sense, envious :-- Beón andetta &d-bar;æt h&e-long; æfestig s&y-long;, Bl. H. 65, 4. Ne s&y-long; h&e-long; æfestig (zelotipus), R. Ben. 121, 13. Æfstig emulus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 143, 46. Se æfæstiga mæssepreóst. Gr. D. 117, 18. Æfestiga, æfstigea, 118, 20. Hw&a-long; mæg beón unges&aelig-long;lgra &d-bar;onne se æfstiga (-ega, v. l.), Past. 231, 22. Ðæs æfestigan invidi, Hy. S. 16, 3. Ne s&y-long;n w&e-long; t&o-long; æfestige (-æst-, v. l.), Wlfst. 253, 6. Ð&a-long; æfestgan (sefstegan, v. l.) invidi, Past. 229, II. Æfestigra manna, R. Ben. 92, 12. Ðaelig-long;m æfstegum invidis, Past. 233, 16. II. in a good sense, zealous (against) :-- Æfstig wi&d-bar; &o-long;;&d-bar;ra monna yfelu contra aliena vitia aemulator, Fast. 79, 12.
æf(e)stigian; p. ode. I. with acc. to envy, be envious of :-- Hié æfestigea&d-bar; &o-long;þera, monna g&o-long;dd&aelig-long;de, Gr. D. 117, 4. Ð&a-long; æfestgodon &d-bar; æt sume men, Shrn. 74, 28. Se ealda feónd ongan æfstigian (invidens) &d-bar;æs &o-long;&d-bar;res lufan, Gr. D. 99, 7. II. with prep. to took with envy or ill will on, have envy towards :-- Ðes iunga man ne æfestiga&d-bar; on n&a-long;num &d-bar;ingum &d-bar;e h&e-long; h&o-long;r gesih&d-bar;, Ap. Th. 14, 25. Se &a-long;wyrgda g&a-long;st æfestgaþ on &d-bar;&a-long; &d-bar;e h&e-long; gesyhþ t&o-long; Gode higian, Bl. H. 29, 21. Ð&a-long; geseah h&e-long; dæs s&a-long;cerdes m&o-long;d byrnan and æfæstigian wiþ his l&i-long;fe, Gr. D. 119, 6. v. ge-aelig;(e)stigian.
æf(e)stung, e; f. Envy :-- Mid þyccylum &d-bar;&aelig-long;re æfestunge, Gr. D. 117, 28. Æfstunge, 118, 2.
æf(e)s-weorc, es; n. Pasturage :-- Æfsweorc sive l&aelig-long;nes landes bryce fructus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 39, 31, v. æfese, æfesn.
æf-gælþ, e; f. Superstition :-- Efgælþe superstitionis, An. Ox. 8, 186. Æfgælþe superstitione, 8, 176 : 3233. Æfgælþa, 4021. &I-long;delum æfgælþum superstitiosa cultura, 3933.
æf-ger&e-long;fa glosses exactor :-- Ð&y-long; l&aelig-long;s se doemere sele&d-bar; &d-bar;ec &d-bar;&aelig-long;m æf-groefe (exactori) and se æfgroefa (exactor) senda&d-bar; &d-bar;ec in carcern, Lk. L. 12, 58.
æf-grynde, es; n. An abyss:-- Þ&i-long;ne d&o-long;mas synt sw&a-long; deópe sw&a-long; sw&a-long; æfgrynde judicia tua abyssus multa, Ps. Th. 35, 6. [O. H. Ger. ab-grunti; n. abyssus. Cf. Goth. af-grundiþa an abyss.]
æf-gydel (?); adj. Idolatrous, superstitious :-- &I-long;delum &l-bar; feóndlicum æfgidelum (-gildum?; the ide is not clear; v. Angl. vi. :oi: cf. also An. Ox. 3933 (v. æf-gælþ), where the same passage is glossed, and see note there superstitiosa, Hpt. Gl. 498, 77. [Cf. O. H. Ger. ab-got idolum.]
æf-hende(-hynde); adj. Absent :-- Gif h&e-long; æfhynde byþ si absens fuerit, Angl. xiii. 387, 316. v. of-hende, ge-hende.
&aelig-long;-firmþa; f. Offscourings, sweepings, dregs, refuse :-- Æfyrm[þa] purgamenta (spurca latrinarum), An. Ox. 3918. Add the quotation in Dict. under æ-fyrrnþa. Cf. &a-long;-feorrnian.
æfne ability, v. efne.
&aelig-long;fnian. Add :-- Ð&a-long; &d-bar;&a-long; se dæg &aelig-long;fnode vesperascente die, Gr. D. 75, 2. Oþ &d-bar;æt hit &aelig-long;node, Hml. S. 13, 27. Swylce hit &aelig-long;fnige, Lch. iii. 260 7.
12 &AElig-acute;FNUNG--ÆFTER-H&AElig-acute;TU
Mid ðí ðe hit &aelig-acute;fnian wolde, Hml. S. 23, 245. &AElig-acute;fni(g)endum ðám dæge, Gr. D. 253, 8.
&aelig-acute;fnung. Add:--On &aelig-acute;fenunga, Hml. S. 11, 43. On &aelig-acute;fnunge, 153; Hml. Th. ii. 334, 34: Lch. iii. 238, 27. Seó sunne g&aelig-acute;ð on &aelig-acute;fnunge under ðyssere eorðan, 240, 14. &AElig-acute;fnunge crepusculo, An. Ox. 85.
[&aelig-acute;fr-ælc(-ic) every:--On &aelig-acute;frice styde in omnibus omnino locis, C. D. iv. 209, 20. &AElig-acute;uric ríce man, Chr. 1137; P. 264, 1. v. &aelig-acute;fre, III.]
[&aelig-acute;fr-&aelig-acute;nig any at all:--Mid &aelig-acute;fr&aelig-acute;nige þinge, C. D. iv. 209, 24. v. &aelig-acute;fre, III.]
&aelig-acute;fre. Add: I. ever; semper, (1) of eternity:--Wæs &aelig-acute;fre on his écum r&aelig-acute;de ðæt hé wolde gewyrcan ðás woruld, Hex. 22, 7. N&aelig-acute;nig ys sé ðe &aelig-acute;fre lybbe, Scint. 215, 2. (2) of continuity or continuous recurrence in time, at all times, on every occasion:--&AElig-acute;fri is deinceps, An. Ox. 56, 103. Wearð &aelig-acute;fre fleám ástiht, and &aelig-acute;fre hí æt ende sige áhton, Chr. 998; P. 131, 15. Full neáh &aelig-acute;fre þe óðer man very nearly every other man, 1086; P. 217, 29. Gif wé &aelig-acute;fre wiðsacað deófle, Hml. Th. i. 170, 16. &AElig-acute;fre swá hí neár and neár eódon, Hml. S. 23, 424. II. ever, at any time, in any case; unquam:--Ne wearð wæl máre &aelig-acute;fer (&aelig-acute;fre, v. l.) gieta, Chr. 937; P. 109, 24. Ne him líg sceðeð &aelig-acute;fre tó ealdre, Ph. 40. Gé wyllað sweltan &aelig-acute;r ðan ðe gé &aelig-acute;fre his geleáfan wiðsacon, Hml. Th. ii. 308, 9. Búton heó hit &aelig-acute;fre gebéte, Hml. S. 17, 156: An. 1014. III. giving emphasis as in whatever, (as) ever, &c.:--Swá rihtlíce geséman swá him &aelig-acute;fre rihtlícost þúhte, C. D. iii. 292, 32. Eall ðæt &aelig-acute;fre betst wæs, Chr. 1048; P. 174, 23. Hwæt ðis &aelig-acute;fre beón scyle? Hml. S. 23, 532. Hú hé &aelig-acute;fre embe hý sceolde, 311. &AElig-acute;fre ðeáh (any how) for his hálgena earnunge, hé him ðis geþanc on móde ásende, 313. &AElig-acute;fre &aelig-acute;lc d&aelig-acute;l his cynnes, 348. &AElig-acute;fre &aelig-acute;lcne Deniscne cyning útlagede hí gecw&aelig-acute;don, Chr. 1014; P. 145, 11. Ymbe &aelig-acute;fre &aelig-acute;lce neóde, Wlfst. 20, 19: Ll. Th. i. 372, 30. Gif &aelig-acute;fre &aelig-acute;nig (cf. &aelig-acute;fr-&aelig-acute;nig) man ciricgrið ábrece, 340, 6.
æf-reda, an; m. Tow, oakum:--Naptarum heordena, æbreda, ácumba (for the original here glossed cf. An. Ox. 1649), Wrt. Voc. ii. 59, 58. Putamine of æfredan, ácumban, An. Ox. 3728. Stamine æfredan, putamine of hniglan, 7, 266. [In this word perhaps -reda is for earlier -r&aelig-acute;da, connected with ge-r&aelig-acute;dan, which is used of dressing the hair; in the same way Icel. greiða is used, and ull greiða = to card or comb wool, so that æf-reda might compare with &aelig-acute;-cambe.]
&aelig-acute;fric, æfse, æfst. v. &aelig-acute;fr-&aelig-acute;lc, æspe, æfest: æfstnung, Hpt. Gl. 436, 32 (æstnung, MS. v. Angl. vi. 99). l. costnung, cf. An. Ox. 1260.
æfs-weorc. v. æfes-weorc.
æftan. Add: From behind:--&AElig-acute;lc óþerne æftan heáweð, Wlfst. 160, 4. [Goth. aftana: Icel. aptan.] v. wiþ-æftan.
æftemest. Dele superlative of æfter, and add:--Se æftemysta cwyde, Hml. Th. i. 554, 14. From heora &aelig-acute;restan cyninge oþ heora æftemæstan (-mest-, v. l.), Ors. 6, 1; S. 252, 14. [Goth. aftumists.] v. æftera.
æften(?) evening:--Eftern lócað aduesperascit (the glosser seems to have read vesper aspicit: in the Rushworth gloss also the word has been misunderstood, as it is rendered by éfern longeð ðú wást, the last two words apparently suggested by -scit), Lk. L. 24, 29. Cf. Icel. aptan.
æften-stemn, Wrt. Voc. i. 63, 37 l. æftera stemn.
æfter. Add: A. prep. I. with dat. (1) marking position:--Ðá eóde ðæt wíf æfter him, Bt. 35, 6; F. 170, 13. (2) marking direction:--Beheald æfter ðé look behind thee, Bl. H. 245, 6. (3) marking order, sequence:--Ðæt hé æfter him tó eallum his gestreónum fénge, Ors. 5, 13; S. 244, 23. Stephanus ðone martyrdóm æfter Gode ástealde, Hml. Th. i. 50, 1. (4) marking order in time:--Æfter ðissum gefeohte, Chr. 871; P. 72, 5. (5) marking extension, with an object which determines position or direction, among, through, along:--Ðá giemmas licggeað tóworpne æfter str&aelig-acute;ta endum (in platearum capite) . . . æfter str&aelig-acute;tum, Past. 135, 3-4. Wé móston búian æfter ðám folce, Ps. Th. 28, 8. Faran gind lond swá swá l&aelig-acute;ce æfter untrumra monna húsum, Past. 59, 23. Hé æfter wudum fór and on mórfæstenum, Chr. 878; P. 74, 29. Fóron hié æfter ð&aelig-acute;m wealda, 894; P. 84, 27. Ðá gesáwon wé men æfter ð&aelig-acute;re eá féran vidimus hostes per medium amnem praetervehi, Nar. 11, 18. Hí hine drógan æfter d&aelig-acute;m stánum on ð&aelig-acute;re eorðan, Shrn. 74, 31. Andlang ð&aelig-acute;re rinde oþ ðone helm, and siððan æfter ðám bogum, Bt. 34, 10; F. 150, 3. Æftær þiódwege in ðone díc; æfter díce, C. D. v. 187, 30. (6) with an object to which an action (pursuit, search, inquiry, &c.) is directed:--Hé stód æfter ús gewend, and cliopode æfter ús, Past. 405, 35. Rád séo fird æfter ð&aelig-acute;m herige, Chr. 896; P. 89, 19. Hé him æfter rád, 878; P. 76, 12. Ðæt ðá gódan men niman æfter þeora gódnesse, and for(f)león yfelnesse, 1086; P. 221, 24. Ðá sende se cyng æfter Anláfe, 994; P. 129, 15. Heora wíf him sendon &aelig-acute;rendracan æfter, Ors. 1, 10; S. 44, 20. Hé lét hine faran æfter ðám feó, Hml. Th. ii. 358, 23: Chr. 997; P. 131, 28: 1048; P. 171, 19. Wé æfter ferscum wætre hié frúnon, Nar. 11, 22. Winnan æfter ríce, Chr. 685; P. 39, 23: Ors. 6, 28; S. 278, 9. His geréfan niéddon hí æfter gafole (pressed them for tribute), 6, 34; S. 290, 24: Bt. 16, 2; F. 52, 3. &AElig-acute;ghwylc hine þreátode æfter ðám bócum, Shrn. 123, 29, 32. (7) with an object which serves as example or measure:--Æfter steor&dash-uncertain;wíglunge juxta constellationem, An. Ox. 7, 179. Æfter ð&aelig-acute;re tíde (secundum tempus) ðe hé geáxode, Mt. 2, 16. Him eákiað æfter ð&aelig-acute;m mægenum ðá costunga, Past. 163, 8: Hml. S. 13, 130. Æfter ðínum willan, Bt. 26, 1; F. 90, 23. Lufian wé úrne Sceppend æfter úrum gemete, Bl. H. 5, 35. Forgolden æfter his gewyrhtum, 45, 2. Ðes mónaþ is se ýtemesta æfter Lýdenwarum, Angl. viii. 306, 8. Se H&aelig-acute;lend cwæþ æfter bíspellum heora, Mt. R. 22, 1. Niman geðyld æfter Iobe, Hml. Th. ii. 328, 28. Æfter æþelborennysse oferhýdige haughty after the manner of noble birth, 174, 7. Æfter ðon accordingly, Bl. H. 81, 27. Hit biþ geornlic ðæt mon heardlíce gníde ðone hnescestan mealmstán æfter ð&aelig-acute;m ðæt (according as) hé þence ðone soelestan hwetstán on tó ger&aelig-acute;ceanne, Ors. 4, 13; S. 212, 28. II. with acc. (rare except in Northumbrian Glosses):--Æfter hrædlice tíde, Ors. 1, 10; S. 44, 28. Æfter óðer healf hund daga, Gen. 8, 3. Æfter ðás post haec, Lk. L. R. 10, 1. Ende . . . swylcne hé æfter worhte, Jud. 65. Hé ðá gesihð lúteð æfter, Sal. 402. Æfter tíd secundum tempus, Mt. L. 2, 16. III. with instrumental:--Æfter ðýs lífe, Bt. 11, 2; F. 36, 1. B. adv. (1) of time:--Monncwealm ðe him raðe ðæs æfter com, Ors. 2, 6; S. 86, 25. Ðisse ádle fruman mon mæg ýþelíce gelácnian . . ., and æfter unéð, Lch. ii. 232, 17. Ðá æfter féng tó ðám ercebiscopdóme Iustus, Chr. 616; P. 24, 23. (2) of position:--His wíf beláf æfter in ðám castele, Chr. 1076; P. 211, 29. (3) of direction, cf. A. 6:--Ðá fór Eádweard æfter, Chr. 905; P. 94, 1: 999; P. 133, 9. Hig aefter ridon, Jos. 2, 7. v. sprecan, VI. ¶.
æftera. v. æfterra.
æfter-&aelig-acute;; f. Second-law, Deuteronomy:--Seó bóc ðe is genemned . . . on Grécisc Deuteronomium . . . and on Englisc seó æfter&aelig-acute;, Deut. proem.
æfter-boren. Dele [ = æfter-genga, q. v.], and add:--Æfterbora (l. -en) postumus, An. Ox. 17, 34.
æfter-cyning, es; m. A succeeding king:--Þá æftercyningas reges posteriores, Bd. 2, 14; Sch. 173, 20.
æfter-eala, an; m. l. æfter-ealo (-a, -u); n.: æfter-fæce, dele.
æfterest. v. æfterra.
æfter-fyl(i)gan; p. de To follow:--Ðæt folc nú gyt ðæt tácn æfter&dash-uncertain;fylgeað, Ors. 1, 5; S. 34, 22. Ðá ðe æfterfylydon quae sequebantur, Mt. L. 21, 9. Mildheortnys ðín æfterfylge (subsequetur) mé, Ps. L. 22, 6. Án scort ræps æfterfylige (subsequatur), R. Ben. 34, 13: 60, 4. Æfter ð&aelig-acute;m ræpsum æfterfyligan (-fylian, v. l.) óþre syx sealmas, 33, 21. Ðes æfterfiligenda cwyde is egefull, Hml. Th. i. 130, 28. Seó hálgung ðæs æfterfilgendan bisceopes, Chr. 984; P. 124, 3. Æfterfylgendre prepostero, Wrt. Voc. ii. 66, 77. Ðás æfterfylgendan (-fylig-, v. l.) láre, Gr. D. 1, 16. Ðá æfterfiligendan yrmða, Hml. Th. i. 408, 18.
æfter-fylgedness, e; f. A sequel:--Ne forl&aelig-acute;t ðú ðá æfterfylgednysse swá hálwendre gerecednysse, Hml. S. 23 b, 365.
æfter-fylgend. Add:--Alexandras æfterfylgendas, Ors. 3, 11; S. 142, 11. Heora æfterfyligendas successores eorum, Bd. 2, 5; S. 506, 2. Him sylfum and his æfterfiligendum eallan, Chr. 995; P. 128, 39.
æfter-fylgendlíce; adv. In continuation or succession:--Hié ðus æfterfylgendlíce mid blisse clypiað subsequuntur gaudentes et dicentes, R. Ben. 27, 11.
æfter-fylgendness, e; f. Success:--Æfterfyligendnyssum successibus, Hy. S. 11, 8.
æfter-fylgung, e; f. Pursuit:--Efterfylginc sectatio, Kent. Gl. 371. v. gedwild-æfterfylgung.
æfter-fylian. v. æfter-fyl(i)gan: æfter-gán, dele: æfter-gegengedness. v. æfter-gengness, II.
æfter-genga. Substitute for first quotation:--Æftergenga posterus, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 275, 3, and add: I. one living at a later time; where those of the same stock are referred to, a descendant:--Æftergencgena posteriorum (natorum), Hpt. Gl. 445, 60. Æftergen(gena) liberorum, i. filiorum, An. Ox. 584. Æftergengcum nepotibus, 3370: posteris, Germ. 399, 344: futuris, Hpt. Gl. 485, 41. Sume men w&aelig-acute;ron gió . . . ðá bisnodon hiora æftergengum, Bt. 39, 11; F. 230, 3. II. one coming after in an office, a successor:--Æftergenga successor, i. subsequenter obtinens locum, An. Ox. 1996. Eádwine and twégen his æfter&dash-uncertain;gengan, Hml. S. 26, 10. Ðá apostolas . . . eác heora æftergengan, Hml. A. 56, 146. III. a follower of a creed, &c.:--Æftergengum sequipedes, sequaces (catolicae fidei), An. Ox. 1957.
æfter-gengel, es; m. A successor[:--Nán mín æftergengles (successores) . . . mín curs and ealle mín æftergengle, C. D. v. 30, 11. 23. Cf. Mine aððele uoregenglen, Lay. 25082. O. H. Ger. náh-gengil a familiar.]
æfter-gengness, e; f. I. posterity:--Æftergencnesse posteritatis, An. Ox. 849. Æftergencgnesse posteritate, 2695. Æftergennysse, 3610. Ð&aelig-acute;ra gesceafta æftergengnyssa, Hml. Th. ii. 206, 10. II. succession in an office:--For ð&aelig-acute;re gewissan æftergencgnysse (-gegencgednysse, v. l.), ðæt is ðæt se sunu sceolde symle fón tó ðám háde æfter his fæder geendunge, Hml. S. 10, 219. Mid fæderlicre æftergengnysse in lineal succession, 18, 385. III. inferiority of position, occupation of the lowest place:--Mid æftergencnysse hylde extremitate contentus, R. Ben. I. 33, 14.
æfter-h&aelig-acute;tu. Substitute: æfter-h&aelig-acute;þa (-e?), an; m. (f.?) Parching by heat after wet:--Mid ungem&aelig-acute;tre hærfestw&aelig-acute;tan and æfterh&aelig-acute;þan humor aestatis vel autumni divitis indigesta illecebra, Ors. 3, 3; S. 102. 7. v. h&aelig-acute;þung.
ÆFTER-HÝRIGEAN--&AElig-acute;G-HWANAN 13
æfter-hýrigean. l. æfter-hyr(i)gan, and add:--Mé gelamp ðæt ic ðæt gehýrde, ðæt ic æfterhyrgan ne mæg me audire contingit quod imitari non valeo, Gr. D. 182, 16.
æfter-ild(o). v. æfter-yldo in Dict.
æfter-lic; adj. Second:--Ðý æfterlicum háde secundi sexus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 83, 72.
æfterra, æft(e)ra; cpve.: æft(e)resta; spve. I. where relation of two objects is marked, (1) in time, latter:--Se æfterra anweald--se &aelig-acute;rra, Bt. 16, 1; F. 50, 12. Wæs heora æftra sýð wyrse ðonne se &aelig-acute;rra, Chr. 1001; P. 133, 25. (2) in place, hinder, lower:--Ðæt &aelig-acute;rre folc and ðæt æfterre those before and those behind, Bl. H. 81, 25. Se æftera stemn puppis, Wrt. Voc. i. 63, 37. Se æftra streám aquae inferiores, Jos. 3, 16. On ð&aelig-acute;m æftran teáme bimus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 12, 70. I a. giving order of a group in a series, latter:--Sý alleluia gecweden mid ðám syx æftrum (posterioribus) sealmum, R. Ben. 39, 17. I b. where there are more than two objects the superlative æftresta = last:--Ðreó frigedagas, se &aelig-acute;resta . . . se nýhsta . . . se æftresta, Angl. xi. 3, 69. II. where there is juxtaposition, immediate sequence, next, following:--On ð&aelig-acute;m æfterran geáre ðæs anno post hunc subsequente, Ors. 3, 6; S. 108, 15. On ðám æftran geáre þe se ar&c-tilde;&b-bar; wæs gemartyrod, Chr. 1013; P. 143, 9. On ð&aelig-acute;m æfteran dæge, Bl. H. 71, 34. Ðýs æftran geáre sequente anno, Nar. 30, 11. III. as an ordinal, second:--&AElig-acute;rest . . . se æftera . . . ue þridda, Chr. 827; P. 60, 27. Sió æfterre tá . . . sió feórðe tá, Ll. Th. i. 90, 20. Hér endað sió forme bóc and onginð sió æfterre, Ors. 1, 14; S. 58, 12: 1, 7; S. 36, 26. Ðá æðelu ð&aelig-acute;re æfterran ácennesse (regenerationis), Past. 85, 15. Ðæs æfteran sealmes capitul, Ps. Th. 2, arg. On ð&aelig-acute;re æfteran míle fram Róme, Bl. H. 193, 19.
æfter-r&aelig-acute;ding. v. &aelig-acute;fen-r&aelig-acute;ding.
æfter-r&aelig-acute;pe a crupper:--Æfterr&aelig-acute;pe postela, Wrt. Voc. i. 23, 15. Mid æfterr&aelig-acute;pum postelis, Hpt. 31, 14, 336. [O. H. Ger. after-reifi postelina.] Cf. æfter-ráp in Dict., where add: [O. H. Ger. after-reif postella].
æfter-rídan. l. æfter rídan.
æfter-sang. Substitute: Matins:--Se forma tídsang is úhtsang mid ðám æftersange ðe ðártó gebirað, Ll. Th. ii. 376, 6. Tó æftersange ad matutinas, Angl. xiii. 396, 449: 402, 528. Æftersanga symbolnys matutinorum sollempnitas, R. Ben. I. 43, 2. Æftersangum matutino, 46, 13. Æftersangas matutinas, Angl. xiii. 428, 904. [In R. Ben. I. 45, 17 æftersanc vespera is probably a mistake for &aelig-acute;fensanc.]
æfter-sanglic; adj. Of matins:--Lofe hí singon æftersingallice (l. sanglice) laudes psallant matutinales, Angl. xiii. 398, 476.
æfter-spræc, -sprecan. l. æfter-spr&aelig-acute;c, æfter sprecan. v. sprecan, VI. ¶.
æfter-weard. Substitute: I. adj. (1) later, latter:--Ver novum fore&dash-uncertain;weard lencten vel middewærd lencten, ver adultum æfterweard lencten. Eodem modo et aestas et autumnus vocantur, Wrt. Voc. i. 53, 27. (2) being behind (?), absent:--Ðeáh ðe hé lícumlíce ð&aelig-acute;r æfterweard (æfweard, v. l.) w&aelig-acute;re quamvis corporaliter absens, Bd. 3, 15; Sch. 264, 6. II. adv. prep. After:--Hí urnon ealle him æfterweard, Hml. S. 31, 995. Weorþan æfterweard to be after, to pursue, follow:--Iohannes heów ðæt hors mid ðám spuran and wearð him æfterweard . . . and cwæð tó ðám fleóndum, Ælfc. T. 18, 22: Rä. 16, 14. Petrus wearð æfterweard Peter followed, Hml. Th. i. 374, 6. v. æfte-weard.
æfter-weardness, e; f. Posterity:--Æfterweardnesse posteritatem, Wrt. Voc. ii. 65, 66.
æfter-wearþ v. æfter-weard.
æfter-writen; adj. (ptcpl.) Written later on:--Ðá &aelig-acute;rgenemnedan l&aelig-acute;cedómas and ðá æfterwritenan, Lch. ii. 186, 12.
æfte-weard. Dele first quotation, and add:--On æfteweardum ð&aelig-acute;m sealme in the latter part of the psalm, Ps. Th. 38, arg. On æftewyrdne December, and on foreweardan Ianuarie ðám mónþe, Lch. iii. 154, 12. ¶ substantive use:--On æfteweardan ðæs regoles, Hml. S. 3, 150. On æfteweardan ylde heó bið on bedde lange licgende, Lch. iii. 184, 6. Hand sceal habban h on forewerdan and d on æfteweardan, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 292, 3.
æf-þanc, &c. Add:--Æfþancan invidia, An. Ox. 8, 161: Angl. xiii. 33, 157. Gif hwylc yfeld&aelig-acute;de man þurh &aelig-acute;nigne æfþancan óþerne begaleþ, Lch. i. 190, 9. Sé ðe l&aelig-acute;rð sunu his on æfþuncan (in zelum) hé ásent feónd he that teacheth his son grieveth the enemy (Ecclus. 30, 3), Scint. 176, 12. Ðá wræc hé his æfþancas on his feóndum, Guth. 14, 4.
æftresta, æf-þunca. v. æfterra, æf-þanc.
æftum; adv. After:--Swilce ne wæs oþ þis nú ne æftum ne weorþaþ, Mt. R. 24, 21.
æf-weard. Add:--Æfweardum (absente) ðám abbode, Gr. D. 35, 32: 64, 11. Sé cwið yfel ð&aelig-acute;m deáfan, sé ðone æfweardan t&aelig-acute;lð surdo maledicere est absenti derogare, Past. 453, 2. Hé ðá word ðára æfweardra swá geara wiste swá ðára andweardra, Guth. 70, 4: Gr. D. 311, 1. Hé sægde ðá æfweardan þing andweardum mannum praesentibus absentia nuntiare coepit, 126, 11: Guth. 86, 9. [O. H. Ger. aba-wart absens.]
æf-weardness. Add:--Hí ofer ðæt swá dón noldon in ðæs fæder æfweardnysse, be ðám hí ong&aelig-acute;ton ðæt hé him symble wæs ondweard on his gáste, Gr. D. 127, 25. On heora hláfordes æfweardnysse, 29, 2.
æf-wela, an; m. Decrease of wealth:--Gyf man méte &thorn-bar; hé his hús timbrie &thorn-bar; byð his weaxnes (&thorn-bar; hys gód byþ weaxende, v. l.). Gyf him þince &thorn-bar; his hús sí tóworpen sum æfwela (ætlætnes, v. l.) him bið tóweard, Lch. iii. 170, 13.
æf-wirdla, -werdla. Add:--Dispendium, i. damnum, impedimentum, defectio, periculum, detrimentum æfwerdla, wonung, wom, wana, vel hénþa, Wrt. Voc. ii. 140, 68. Æfwyrdlan dispendio, An. Ox. 353: detrimentum, i. contemtum, 452: jacturam, Wrt. Voc. ii. 43, 67. Ðæt hé him ðæs befæstan eówdes nánne æfwirdlan (&aelig-acute;wyrdlan, v. l.) hæbbe ut detrimenta gregis sibi commissi non patiatur, R. Ben. 14, 9. Ðæt hí hwylcne æfwyrdlan (&aelig-acute;wyrdlan, v. l.) geþrowedon heora ágenra sáwla animarum damna patirentur, Gr. D. 50, 24. Scipes æfwyrdlan navis jacturam, 141, 13. Æfwerdlan áræfnede damna pertulit, 205, 1. Ðá æfwerdlan (&aelig-acute;wyrdlan, v. l.) selfe hire leoma ipsa detrimenta membrorum, 284, 5. Æfwyrdlan, An. Ox. 965: 1864. v. &aelig-acute;-wirdla.
æf-wirth(u) (?); f. Degradation, disgrace:--Nyðerunga, æfwyrðe detrimenta, R. Ben. I. 16, 6.
æ-fyrmþa. Dele: washing, ablutions; and see &aelig-acute;-firmþa.
æg. l. &aelig-acute;g, and add:--Dó &aelig-acute;ges ðæt hwíte tó, Lch. ii. 20, 12. Genim &aelig-acute;ges ðæt geoluwe, 22, 19. &AElig-acute;ges geola, 130, 12. Nó ðonne bútan med&dash-uncertain;mycelne d&aelig-acute;l hláfes and án henne &aelig-acute;g mid lytle meolc wætere gemengedre hé onféng, Bd. 3, 23; S. 554, 33. Þreó &aelig-acute;gero, Shrn. 135, 18. Gif hit festendæg sié selle mon fisces and butran and aegera ðaet mon begeotan maege, C. D. i. 293, 11. Genim nigon &aelig-acute;gra . . . and nim eall swá fela dropena wínes swá ð&aelig-acute;ra &aelig-acute;gra beó, Lch. i. 380, 1-5. Sellan &aelig-acute;gra tó súpanne, ii. 220, 7. Genim gebr&aelig-acute;dde &aelig-acute;gru, 100, 11. Gif hé gesihð henne &aelig-acute;gru lecgan, iii. 204, 30. Hwæt máre ytst ðú? Wyrta and &aelig-acute;gra, Coll. M. 34, 27.
&aelig-acute;-gafol(-e?); adj. Free from tax, rent, &c.:--Án híwissce &aelig-acute;gefæles landæs hidam liberam, C. D. v. 137, 23.
&aelig-acute;gen. See other instances under ágen: &aelig-acute;ger-felma; m. (not f.).
&aelig-acute;ger-geolu, wes; n. The yolk of an egg:--Aegergelu fitilium, Txts. 62, 429.
&aelig-acute;-gewrítere. In Kent. Gl. 245 'legum conditores' is rendered by a word which Zupitza reads as scepttenras. This in Junius' copy of the MS. is given by ægewriteras. The scept is uncertain, and Zupitza gives egewritteras as a more possible reading than that of Junius.
&aelig-acute;g-gemang, es; n. A mixture of eggs:--Aeggimong ogastrum (olgastrum, 46), Wrt. Voc. ii. 115, 44. &AElig-acute;ggemang, 63, 38. [Beþe mid aagemogc, Lch. iii. 38, 2.] v. &aelig-acute;g-mang.
&aelig-acute;g-hwá. Add:--Hió geh&aelig-acute;t him &aelig-acute;ghwæs genóg abundantiam promittit, Past. 71, 23: Sch. 94. Sélre byð &aelig-acute;ghwám, An. 320: El. 1270: Met. 8, 5. &AElig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;m, B. 1384: Sat. 363: Met. 8, 38. Fira &aelig-acute;ghwám, Ps. Th. 134, 3. Ic eom gehéned on &aelig-acute;ghwám humiliatus sum usquequaque, Past. 465, 29. Hét ic &aelig-acute;ghwæt swá dón swá hé ús bebeád, Nar. 27, 14. &AElig-acute;ghwæt gefremman ðæs ðe hié woldan, Bl. H. 137, 1. Hé him &aelig-acute;ghwæt sealtes beorge, Lch. ii. 130, 8. ¶ &aelig-acute;ghwæs in every respect, quite, altogether:--&AElig-acute;ghwæs hé wæs ansund incolumis inventus est, Gr. D. 213, 7. Se earm stód ungebígendlic &aelig-acute;ghwæs þám ágendfreán ungewylde, 254, 38: Th. 44: Jul. 593: Cri. 1421. &AElig-acute;ghwæs unt&aelig-acute;le, B. 1865. Æghwæs unrím quite countless, 3135. &AElig-acute;ghwæs ealne dæg tota die, Ps. Th. 55, 4.
&aelig-acute;g-hw&aelig-acute;r. Dele á-hw&aelig-acute;r, and add: -hwár, -wern. I. local, (1) in every place, (a) referring to the whole of space:--God bið á wesende and &aelig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r ondweard, Bl. H. 19, 26. &AElig-acute;ghwár, 23, 21. (b) of limited space:--Oeghuer, -huuér, óghuuaer vulgo, passim, Txts. 107, 2173. &AElig-acute;giwern passim, An. Ox. 11, 160. Wé forhealdað &aelig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r (-hwár, v. l.) Godes gerihta, Wlfst. 157, 14. Hié hergodon &aelig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r be ðám s&aelig-acute;, Chr. 918; P. 98, 12: 998; P. 131, 13. Him wæs &aelig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r wá, Sat. 342. &AElig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r onbútan circumquaque, An. Ox. 2, 251. &AElig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r on eorþan, Gen. 2705. Geneósian ealra þeóda &aelig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r landes ad visitandas omnes gentes, Ps. Th. 58, 5. &AElig-acute;ghwár eorðan usquequaque, Ps. L. 118, 107. [In Met. 10. 58 substitute:--the likes of them are everywhere.] (2) to every place, in every direction:--Se wind mæg féran &aelig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r, Rä. 41, 69. Hié sendon &aelig-acute;gwern æfter fultume, Ors. 4, 1; S. 154, 22. II. in every case:--Bið andgit &aelig-acute;ghw&aelig-acute;r sélest, B. 1059: Gú. 573. III. in every respect:--&AElig-acute;ghwáre usquequaque, R. Ben. I. 36, 10.
&aelig-acute;g-hwæþer. Add: I. of two, (1) substantival:--Wæs &aelig-acute;ghwæþer sáwla full, Bd. 5, 12; S. 627, 39: Cri. 1577: Sal. 108. &AElig-acute;ghwæþer óþerne oftrædlíce út dr&aelig-acute;fde, Chr. 887; P. 80, 28. Fæder ðára æðelinga &aelig-acute;ghwæðres, Rä. 47, 5. &AElig-acute;ghwæðres . . . worda and weorca, B. 287. &AElig-acute;ghwæðrum wæs bróga fram óðrum, 2564. Hæfde &aelig-acute;ghwæþre (-hwæþer?, but for pl. cf. II. below) ende geféred an end had come to both, 2844. (b) adjective:--&AElig-acute;ghwæþer ende líþ on s&aelig-acute;, Bd. 1, 25; S. 486, 21. II. of more than two:--Ðrittig manna . . . &aelig-acute;ghwæþere ðára w&aelig-acute;ron on droht&dash-uncertain;nunge munuclífes well gel&aelig-acute;red, Bd. 4, 4; S. 570, 36. ¶ &AElig-acute;ghwæþer ge . . . ge (and) both . . . and:--Hí &aelig-acute;ghwæðer ge an farað ge eft cumað, Met. 20, 12. &AElig-acute;ghweþer, Bl. H. 125, 8: 215, 13. Forwyrnednesse &aelig-acute;ghweðer ge on mete, ge on hrægle, ge on &aelig-acute;ghwylcum þinge, 219, 29. Wæs &aelig-acute;gweðer ð&aelig-acute;m eádigan were ge seó Godes lufu hát . . . and him wæs eác manna lufu mycel, 225, 35. v. &aelig-acute;gþer.
&aelig-acute;g-hwanan. Add: I. local, (1) of motion, from all sides:--Gegadorode micel folc hit &aelig-acute;gþer ge of Cent, ge of Eást-Seaxum, ge &aelig-acute;ghwonan of ðám níhstum burgum, Chr. 921; P. 102, 12. Wé beóð
14 &AElig-acute;G-HWIDER--&AElig-acute;-LAGOL
&aelig-acute;ghwanum cumene, Dóm. L. 120. (2) where action proceeds from all sides and its operation is felt on all sides, on all sides:--Mid costungum wé sint &aelig-acute;ghwonon útan behrincgde, Past. 163, 16. Éghwanon gecnissed, Hml. S. 30, 192. Hé hine &aelig-acute;ghwanon mid ð&aelig-acute;re róde tácne gew&aelig-acute;pnode, 23 b, 776. Hí mon &aelig-acute;ghwanone sécan sceolde, 23, 236. Nú is &aelig-acute;ghwonon hreám and wóp, nú is heáf &aelig-acute;ghwonon, nú is &aelig-acute;ghwonon yfel and slege, and &aelig-acute;ghwonon ðes middangeard flýhþ from ús, Bl. H. 115, 15-17. II. fig. on all sides, in every respect, utterly:--Ic eom gehéned &aelig-acute;ghwonane humiliatus sum usquequaque, Past. 465, 29. Ne forl&aelig-acute;t ðú mé &aelig-acute;ghwanan (usquequaque), Ps. L. 118, 8. Ic mé ongite &aelig-acute;ghwonan scyldigne, Bt. 8; F. 24, 12. Ic &aelig-acute;ghwanane eom unges&aelig-acute;lig, Hml. S. 30, 205.
&aelig-acute;g-hwider. Add: In every direction:--Hí férdon &aelig-acute;ghwider, Chr. 1011; P. 141, 21. Hé &aelig-acute;ghwider beseah on &aelig-acute;ghwilce healfe, Hml. S. 23, 503. Dún mid blóstmum gegyred &aelig-acute;ghwyder ymbútan mons floribus usquequaque vestitus, Bd. 1, 7; S. 478, 23.
&aelig-acute;g-hwilc. Add: I. as substantive, (1) absolute:--Egsan sceal &aelig-acute;ghwylc habban, Ps. Th. 75, 9. &AElig-acute;ghwylc gecwæð, B. 987. His brúcan mót &aelig-acute;ghwylc on eorðan, Sch. 66. Hé tó &aelig-acute;ghwylcum sóð sprecende wæs, Bl. H. 223, 29. Fýr biþ ymbútan on &aelig-acute;ghwylcum, þeáh hé uppe seó, Sat. 265: An. 350. (2) with a genitive:--&AElig-acute;ghwylc ðára manna, Bl. H. 37, 3. Hæleða &aelig-acute;ghwylc, Sat. 194. Gumena &aelig-acute;ghwilc, Gen. 465. &AElig-acute;ghwylc ánra heora, Bl. H. 121, 8. Þeóda &aelig-acute;ghwilc hæfdon . . ., Met. 26, 43. &AElig-acute;ghwilc heora tóstencte weorðan sceolden, 29, 88. Æt &aelig-acute;ghwylcum ánra, Gú. 4. &AElig-acute;ghwylcne ánra ðára ðe him bið egesa tó me, Kr. 86. &AElig-acute;ghwylc ealra, Ps. Th. 134, 8. Oeghwelce ðinga omni modo, Wrt. Voc. ii. 115, 50. &AElig-acute;ghwylce þinga, 63, 42. II. as adjective:--&AElig-acute;ghwelc man, Bt. 24, 3; F. 84, 11. &AElig-acute;ghwylc heáhgeréfa wæs gewita, Bl. H. 177, 14. &AElig-acute;ghwylc mennisc leahter, 163, 15. &AElig-acute;ghwylces mannes d&aelig-acute;da, 83, 13. &AElig-acute;ghwylces mennisces monnes gemet, 163, 35. Bútan &aelig-acute;gwylcum leahtre, 4. Tó &aelig-acute;ghwilcre unríhtnesse, 241, 4. &AElig-acute;lce wígw&aelig-acute;pna and &aelig-acute;ghwylce woruldsaca l&aelig-acute;te man stille, Wlfst. 170, 9. ¶ with án, (1) substantival, cf. I. 2:--Ðæt úre &aelig-acute;ghwylc án mæg éce líf geearnian, Wlfst. 283, 21. Æt &aelig-acute;ghwylcum ánum ðára, Bl. H. 127, 33. (2) adjectival:--&AElig-acute;ghwylcum ánum men gyldan, Bl. H. 123, 33: 125, 7. &AElig-acute;ghwylce áne dæge, 91, 29.
&aelig-acute;-gift, e; f. Substitute: &aelig-acute;-gift, es; m. or n.; e; f. (cf. &aelig-acute;-rist for gender) A giving up, return, repayment, restoration:--Sigelm ágef Godan .xxx. punda . . . Ðá ætsóc Goda ðæs feós &aelig-acute;giftes (Goda negavit sibi xxx libras persolutas fuisse), Cht. Th. 201, 29: 202, 6. Bæd Ælfsige &aelig-acute;giftes his mannes (a woman who had been stolen from him), and hé hine ágef, 206, 30. &AElig-acute;gifta redditus, An. Ox. 5, 38: 8, 300. v. á-gifan.
æ-gilde; adv. l. &aelig-acute;-gilde; adj., and add:--Unpaid for, applied to a slain man for whom wergild was not paid:--Gyf þr&aelig-acute;l ðæne þegen áfylle, licge &aelig-acute;gylde (-gilde, v. l.) ealre his m&aelig-acute;gðe; and gyf se þegen ðæne þr&aelig-acute;l ðe hé &aelig-acute;r áhte áfylle, gylde þegengylde, Wlfst. 162, 8.
æg-l&aelig-acute;c, -l&aelig-acute;ca. l. &aelig-acute;g-l&aelig-acute;c, -l&aelig-acute;ca.
&aelig-acute;g-mang a mixture of eggs:--Aegmang agastrum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 99, 55. v. &aelig-acute;g-gemang.
ægnan; pl. Awns (awn, with husbandmen, the spire or beard of barley or other bearded grain, Bailey), chaff, refuse, husks:--Aegnan paleae, Txts. 85, 1526: quisquiliae, 91, 1696. [En graunge vus gardet des arestes (fro agunes), Wrt. Voc. i. 155, 1. Hec arista a nawn, 233, col. 2. Awene, awne arista, Promp. P. 18. Goth. ahana paleae: Icel. ögn; pl. agnar (-ir) chaff: O. H. Ger. agana arista, migma, festuca.]
ægnetrem. v. trem in Dict.: ægnian. l. &aelig-acute;gnian, and substitute:--v. ágnian.
&aelig-acute;g-scill, e; f. An egg-shell:--Cl&aelig-acute;nes huniges áne &aelig-acute;gscylle fulle, Lch. iii. 6, 29. iii &aelig-acute;gscylla, 14, 22. Twá &aelig-acute;gscille fulle, i. 376, 8.
&aelig-acute;g-þer. Add: I. substantival:--&AElig-acute;gþer ðára ðe com from mé, Bt. 7, 3; F. 20, 5. Hyra &aelig-acute;gðer ríxade .xxx. wintra, Chr. 560; P. 19, 2. Wit h&aelig-acute;man sceoldon, and uncer láþette &aelig-acute;gþer óþer, þeáh þe hé hit óþrum ne s&aelig-acute;de, Shrn. 39, 22. Heora &aelig-acute;gðer óðerne ofslóg, Ors. 2, 3; S. 68, 18. Ðára folca &aelig-acute;gðer on óðerum micel wæl geslógan, 3, 1; S. 98, 6. &AElig-acute;gðer heora on óðer háwede, Chr. 1003; P. 135, 12. Hé hié &aelig-acute;gðres benam ge heora cyninges ge heora anwaldes, Ors. 2, 1; S. 64, 9, 12: Ll. Th. i. 346, 5. Hit willnaþ ðára &aelig-acute;gþres, Bt. 34, 11; F. 152, 9. &AElig-acute;gðrum emnneáh, 39, 7; F. 222, 8. Of &aelig-acute;gðrum his ríca, Ps. Th. 9, 36. Ðá dyde hé him &aelig-acute;gþer tó gewealdon, Ors. 3, 7; S. 112, 25. Hú ne hæfdon wé &aelig-acute;r gereht ðæt ðá ges&aelig-acute;lþa and sió godcundnes án w&aelig-acute;re? Sé ðe ðonne ðá ges&aelig-acute;lþa hæfþ, ðonne hæfþ hé &aelig-acute;gþer; sé ðe ðon(n)e &aelig-acute;gþer hæfþ, hú ne bið sé ðonne full eádig?, Bt. 34, 5; F. 138, 33. On &aelig-acute;gðer þ&aelig-acute;ra bóca sind feówertig cwyda, Hml. Th. ii. 2, 13. Hwí sceal ic beón bed&aelig-acute;led &aelig-acute;gðer mínra sunena (utroque filio), Gen. 27, 45. Ne hafað hió eágena &aelig-acute;gðer twéga, Rä. 40, 11. Ðæt hé mehte &aelig-acute;gþerne ger&aelig-acute;can, Chr. 894; P. 84, 26. II. adjectival:--Æt &aelig-acute;gþrum cirre, Chr. 918; P. 98, 29. Hét hé &aelig-acute;gðer eáge út ádón, 1095; P. 231, 27. III. conjunction, (1) with two clauses:--&AElig-acute;gðer wið Eást-Engle ge wið Norðhymbre, Chr. 906; P. 94, 22. (2) with more than two:--&AElig-acute;gþer ge eargast, ge wr&aelig-acute;nast, ge ofer&dash-uncertain;módgast, Ors. 2, 2; S. 66, 28. &AElig-acute;gðer ge ðone cyning, ge his sunu, ge ealle ðá ðe cynecynnes w&aelig-acute;ron, 36: Chr. 897; P. 90, 16. &AElig-acute;gðer be ðám s&aelig-acute;riman on Eást-Seaxum, and on Centlande, and on Súð-Seaxum, and on Hamtúnscíre, 994; P. 129, 7. v. &aelig-acute;g-hwæþer.
&aelig-acute;g-wern. v. &aelig-acute;g-hw&aelig-acute;r.
&aelig-acute;-gylt. Dele a breach of the law, and add:--Égylt excesus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 107, 79. &AElig-acute;gylt, 30, 7: excessus, i. culpa, delicta, 145, 67. v. á-gyltan.
æ-gype. l. &aelig-acute;-gípe (?) without skill or cunning. Cf. geáp callidus.
æhher. v. eár.
&aelig-acute;-híw, es; n. Pallor:--&AElig-acute;híwum palloribus, An. Ox. 4897.
&aelig-acute;-híwe; adj. I. without colour, pallid:--&AElig-acute;híwe decolor, pallidus, Germ. 392, 69. Óðre hwíle hé bið bl&aelig-acute;c and &aelig-acute;híwe, An. Ox. 4897, note. II. without form, ugly, deformed:--&AElig-acute;híwe deformes (opifices turpi natura corporis), An. Ox. 2, 498.
&aelig-acute;-hlýp. Dele &aelig-acute; law.
æhri(g)e(?), an; f. The husk of an ear(?):-- Aehrian, ægrihan (æhrigan?) quisquiliae, Txts. 90, 840. v. æhher.
&aelig-acute;ht. Add: In Ll. Th. i. 6, 3 the weak form, ealle ða &aelig-acute;htan, occurs, and a form not feminine, mínes ágenes &aelig-acute;htes, 194, 16. I. what is owned, a possession:--&AElig-acute;ht res, heánra manna (man, Wrt.) vel ceorla (-ic, Wrt.) &aelig-acute;hta peculium, Wrt. Voc. i. 20, 57, 59. &AElig-acute;hta gadzarum, An. Ox. 3155. Gif ceorl deóflum gelde, hé sié ealra his &aelig-acute;hta (MS. &aelig-acute;htan) scyldig, Ll. Th. i. 40, 5, 6. Selle hé his w&aelig-acute;pn and his &aelig-acute;hta his freóndum tó gehealdenne, 60, 8. I a. of landed property:--Ðæt seó &aelig-acute;ht (hereditas) úre sý, Lk. 20, 14. Náht elles hire ne sealde búton .vi. yntsan ánre &aelig-acute;hte (possesiunculae), Gr. D. 222, 26. Hí genámon of ðæs biscopes &aelig-acute;hte (v. l. lande) twégen cnihtas; seó &aelig-acute;ht (ðæt land, v. l.) wæs undecþeódod ð&aelig-acute;re fores&aelig-acute;dan ceastre, 80, 7. Gyf ðú ðás wyrte on ðínre &aelig-acute;hte hafast oððe hyre s&aelig-acute;d on ðín hús áhéhst, Lch. i. 308, 12. Ðæt ðæt yrfe on his &aelig-acute;hte geboren w&aelig-acute;re, Ll. Th. i. 204, 14. Ic hit ágnian wille tó ágenre &aelig-acute;hte, 184, 5. I b. of movables as opposed to land:--Hw&aelig-acute;m ic mínes landes geunnen hæbbe and ealre mínre &aelig-acute;hte, C. D. iv. 55, 5. Fóe tó londe and tó ælre &aelig-acute;hte, i. 234, 29. Hwílum be áre, hwílum be &aelig-acute;hte, Ll. Th. i. 328, 12. Mínra yldrena ðe mé mín ár of com and míne &aelig-acute;hta, Cht. Th. 529, 1. Fón ðá néhstan frýnd tó ðam lande and tó ðám &aelig-acute;htan, Ll. Th. i. 416, 10: 420, 10. Of lande mid heora &aelig-acute;htum gewíten, i. 38, 2. I c. of cattle:--Gif heora menn sleán úre &aelig-acute;hta, Ll. Th. i. 288, 10. I d. of slaves. Cf. &aelig-acute;ht-boren:--Gif hwylc man his &aelig-acute;ht (servum) ofslyhð, Ll. Th. ii. 182, 29: 268, 9. II. possession:--Hilde gebohte týn hída landes hire on &aelig-acute;hte, Bd. 3, 24; S. 557, 2. Gif ðú wéne ðæt hit ðín bócland sý, ðæt ðú on eardast, and on ágene &aelig-acute;ht geseald, Wlfst. 260, 3. v. fær-, on- (?), weorold-&aelig-acute;ht.
á-éhtan to persecute:--Áoehtad gé biðon pirsequentur, Lk. L. 21, 12.
&aelig-acute;ht-boren; adj. Slave-born. v. &aelig-acute;ht, I d, and þeów-boren:--Ná ðá áne ðe freó synt, ac gyt má ðe &aelig-acute;htborene (ex conditione servili) synt, R. Ben. 138, 20.
æhte-mann. Add: a serf:--Be manna metsunge. Ánan esne gebyreð tó metsunge . . . Ðeówan wífmen. . . . Eallum &aelig-acute;htemannum gebyreð . . ., Ll. Th. i. 436, 25-33. Ðá wearð gefullod fæder and sunu mid heora innhýrede and heora &aelig-acute;htemannum, Hml. S. 5, 308. v. &aelig-acute;ht, I d.
æhtere. l. eahtere.
&aelig-acute;ht-spéd, e; f. Wealth, riches:--Gefylled is eorðe &aelig-acute;htsp&oelig-acute;de mid ðínre impleta est terra possessione tua, Ps. L. 103, 24.
&aelig-acute;ht-spédig. Add: having great possessions:--Sum ríce man and for worlde &aelig-acute;htspédig, Bl. H. 197, 27.
&aelig-acute;-hwænne. v. á-hwænne: &aelig-acute;-hw&aelig-acute;r = &aelig-acute;g-hw&aelig-acute;r, Ps. Th. 88, 31.
æl an awl. Add v. awel: æl oil. l. æle.
&aelig-acute;l. Add:--Él anguila, Wrt. Voc. ii. 100, 39. Æl, ii. 7, 1: i. 77, 65. Smæl &aelig-acute;l anguilla, 66, 6. &AElig-acute;l murænula, 5: 281, 66: ii. 55, 76: 56, 21. Eil, 114, 25. &AElig-acute;l mula, s&aelig-acute;&aelig-acute;l murenula, 57, 73-4. Ðonne ðú fisc habban wylle . . . &AElig-acute;les tácen is . . . swá swá mon &aelig-acute;l déð ðonne hine mon on spite stagan wyle, Tech. ii. 124, 6-11. v. leaxas and hundteóntig &aelig-acute;la, Ll. Th. i. 146, 20.
&aelig-acute;l, e; f. Burning:--Ðára eágan scínað swá leóhte swá is án micel blácern on &aelig-acute;le (on&aelig-acute;le? cf. on-ál) their eyes shine as bright as is a great lamp a-light, Nar. 37, 18.
&aelig-acute;-l&aelig-acute;rende. l. &aelig-acute;-l&aelig-acute;rend.
&aelig-acute;-l&aelig-acute;te; adj. Desert, desolate:--Oð ðæt heora burga weorðan &aelig-acute;l&aelig-acute;te and weorðan heora eardas swýðe áwéste donec desolentur civitates absque habitatore, et domus sine homine, et terra relinquetur deserta, Wlfst. 47, 21. v. next word.
&aelig-acute;-l&aelig-acute;te, an; f.: es; n. A desert:--&AElig-acute;l&aelig-acute;tan (á-, Wrt.) deserta, s. vocata quae mm seruntur, Wrt. Voc. ii. 139, 14. Wéstensetlan ðe feor fram mannum gewítað and wéste stówa and &aelig-acute;l&aelig-acute;tu lufiaþ, R. Ben. 134, 12. v. preceding word.
&aelig-acute;-l&aelig-acute;te, an; f. A divorced woman:--Ne gewífige on gehálgodre nunnan ne on &aelig-acute;l&aelig-acute;tan &aelig-acute;nig crísten man, Wlfst. 271, 13: 308, 9: Ll. Th. i. 318, 18. &AElig-acute;l&aelig-acute;ten, 364, 26. v. preceding words, and á-l&aelig-acute;tan.
&aelig-acute;-l&aelig-acute;ten. v. preceding word.
&aelig-acute;-lagol; adj. Legislative:--&AElig-acute;lagol legifer, Germ. 397, 363.
ÆLAN--ÆLMES-LÍCE 15
ælan. l. &aelig-acute;lan, and add: I. to kindle light, fire:--Hí fýr &aelig-acute;lað, Wal. 22. Ne scyle nán mon bl&aelig-acute;cern &aelig-acute;lan under mittan, Past. 43, 2. &AElig-acute;ldon adolent, incendunt, Germ. 402. 68. II. to burn up. v. Ph. 222: 526: Cri. 813 (in Dict.). III. to burn, expose to fire what is not consumed:--Se deópa seáð giémeð g&aelig-acute;sta, &aelig-acute;leð hý mid ðý ealdan líge, Cri. 1547. [Se geréfa hét bringen leaden fæt, and hét hit mid wætere áfyllan, and dyde hit &aelig-acute;len swýþe hát, Nar. 46, 4.]
&aelig-acute;-láreów, es; m. A doctor of the law, a Pharisee:--Gebed ðæs &aelig-acute;láruas oratio pharisaei, Lk. p. 9, 13. Mið &aelig-acute;lárua apud pharisaeum, p. 7, 10. &AElig-acute;láruas pharisaei, p. 5, 5. Ðá &aelig-acute;láruuas, 5, 17. Tó ð&aelig-acute;m aeláruum, Jn. 9, 13.
ælaþ, aelbitu. v. ealaþ, ilfette.
&aelig-acute;lc. Add: I. each (1) substantival:--&THORN-bar; &aelig-acute;lc preósta scrífe, Ll. Th. ii. 258, 9. &AElig-acute;lc ð&aelig-acute;ra ðe ðás míne word gehýrð, Mt. 7, 24. &AElig-acute;lces mé þincþ ðæt hé sié wyrþe . . . þone weorþscipe hé forgifþ &aelig-acute;lcum ðára ðe hine lufað, Bt. 27, 2; F. 96, 29-32. Hira geféra ælces ðára ðe wel doo, Past. 75, 12. Unscildig eówres &aelig-acute;lces blódes, 379, 14. (1 a) combined with án:--Nim ðyssa wyrta &aelig-acute;lcre ánre swá micel swá ðára óþra, Lch. iii. 72, 14. On &aelig-acute;lcum ánum hí sint ealle, Bt. 33, 3; F. 126, 15. (1 b) with óþer, where there is reciprocal action:--Bere eówer &aelig-acute;lc óðres byrðenne, Past. 219, 12. Þurh ðæt ðe hí him sylfe &aelig-acute;lc óþerne forfóre, Chr. 1052; P. 181, 22. Hí þegniað &aelig-acute;lc óðum, Met. 25, 12. (2) adjectival:--Hwílum on áne healfe, hwílum on &aelig-acute;lce healfe, Chr. 892; P. 82, 34. (2 a) combined with án:--&AElig-acute;lc án hagelstán wegeð fíf pund, Wlfst. 228, 6. On &aelig-acute;lcre ánre talentan wæs lxxx punda, Ors. 4, 6; S. 170, 28. (2 b) in plural, all:--Wæs hé &aelig-acute;lcum witum láþ, Bt. 28; F. 100, 27. On &aelig-acute;lcum þingum, R. Ben. 15, 20. Se ilca is wendende &aelig-acute;lce onwaldas, Ors. 2, 1; S. 64, 2. &AElig-acute;lce misd&aelig-acute;da ágyldan, Ll. Th. i. 328, 15. Hí forbudon &aelig-acute;lce wífunga, ii. 374, 35: 286, 30. &AElig-acute;lce wígw&aelig-acute;pna l&aelig-acute;te man stille, Wlfst. 170, 8. II. in excluding phrases, any:--Búton &aelig-acute;lcon þegne Créca lond sécan, Ors. 4, 1; S. 156, 32. Búton &aelig-acute;lcre hreówe, 2, 1; S. 64, 7: Past. 37, 2. Búton &aelig-acute;lcere méder . . . búton &aelig-acute;lcum eorðlicum fæder, Hml. Th. ii. 6, 5-7. On ánum báte bútan &aelig-acute;lcum geréþrum, Chr. 891; P. 82, 19. Wiðútan &aelig-acute;lcon w&aelig-acute;pnon, 1086; P. 220, 28. II a. combined with án:--Bútan &aelig-acute;lcre ánre tale (printed arentale), Cht. Th. 563, 16. See also &aelig-acute;fre, III.
&aelig-acute;lc-hwega, -hugu every:--Ðæt ic hwelcnehugu (&aelig-acute;lcne-, Cott. MS.) d&aelig-acute;il gesecge Alexandres d&aelig-acute;da, Ors. 3, 7; S. 110, 13.
ælcor, ælcra. v. elcor, elcra: ælecung. v. R. Ben. 14, 7 note.
æled. l. &aelig-acute;led, and dele) [pp. ofælan].
æled-fýr. l. &aelig-acute;led fýr: æle-lendisc. v. ele-lendisc.
æle-gr&aelig-acute;dig; adj. Very greedy, ravenous:--Gezabel sceolon etan ælegr&aelig-acute;dige hundas, Hml. S. 18, 213.
æle-midde, an; f. The exact middle; only in the phrase on æle&dash-uncertain;middan=just in the middle:--Seó firmamentum tyrnð symle onbútan ús. . . . Seó eorðe stent on ælemiddan, Lch. iii. 254, 16.
