Ð&aelig-acute;re sunnan h&aelig-acute;tu wyrcð fíf d&aelig-acute;las on middanearde. . . . Án ð&aelig-acute;ra d&aelig-acute;la is on ælemiddan, weallende, 260, 20. Wæs óðer treów on ælemiddan paradisum, Hex. 24, 17. Agnes stód on ælemiddan gesund, Hml. S. 7, 223. Ðá héngon ðá cempan Críst on ælemiddan, and ðá twégen sceaðan him on twá healfa, Hml. Th. ii. 254, 22.
æ-leng. l. &aelig-acute;-lenge, &aelig-acute;linge, and add:--Mé þincþ ðæt . . . tó &aelig-acute;lenge (MS. -legge) tó gehýranne, Shrn. 195, 21. On &aelig-acute;lengum ðingum geðyldige, Past. 41, 16. v. next two words, and see elenge, alange in N. E. D.
&aelig-acute;-lenge, &aelig-acute;linge tedium, weariness:--Ðý l&aelig-acute;s &aelig-acute;linge út ádrífe selflicne secg, (Met. Einl. 6.)
&aelig-acute;-lengness, &aelig-acute;lingness, e; f. Tedium, weariness:--&AElig-acute;lengnes fastidium, Wrt. Voc. ii. 146, 46. &AElig-acute;lingnysse þolaþ rihtwís tedium patitur justus, Scint. 216, 9.
ælepe origanum, Wrt. Voc. i. 68, 28. [Wülcker prints ælere; perhaps ælene should be read: cf. origanum elene, Lch. iii. 304, col. 1.]
&aelig-acute;le-puta; m. l. &aelig-acute;le-púte; f., and add:--Myne vel &aelig-acute;lepúte capito, Wrt. Voc. i. 55, 75.
&aelig-acute;-léten. Dele. v. &aelig-acute;-l&aelig-acute;te.
æle-wealdend almighty:--Ælewealdend fæder cuncti parens, Germ. 401, 128. [O. Sax. alo-waldand.] v. eall-wealdend.
Ælf, e; f. The Elbe:--Ælfe múða ð&aelig-acute;re ié, Ors. 1, 1; S. 16, 6, 27. Icel. Elfr.]
ælf. l. e; f., and add:--Gif men hwilc yfel costung weorþe oþþe ælf oþþe nihtgengan, Lch. ii. 344, 16. v. dún-, land-ælf; ilf.
-ælfen. Add: feld-, s&aelig-acute;-, wæter-ælfen: æl-fer, n. l. æl-faru; f.
&aelig-acute;l-fisc, es; m. An eel:--Ic geeácnode tó ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;rran sylene týn þúsenda &aelig-acute;lfixa &aelig-acute;lce geáre ðám munecum, C. D. iii. 61, 5.
æl-fremed (el-). Add: I. strange, foreign, not belonging to one:--Næs mid him [god] elfremed (alienus), Cant. M. ad fil. 12. Se ælfremeda Heródes ðæs ríces geweóld, Hml. Th. i. 82, 4. Hé earmlíce geendode on ælfremedum earde, Hml. S. 25, 547. On eorðan elfremedre in terra aliena, Ps. L. 136, 4. Þurh ælfremede horwan gefýled defiled by others' pollution, Hml. S. 7, 129. Ealle middaneardlice ðing swá swá ælfremede forhogigende cuncta hujus mundi velut aliena spernendo, Hml. Th. ii. 130, 1. II. with fram, stranger to anything, without a share in, free from:--Se munuc sceal beón ælfremed fram eorðlicum d&aelig-acute;dum, Hex. 36, 24. Swá freóh fram deáðes sárnysse swá swá ælfremed fram líchamlicere gewemmednysse, Hml. Th. i. 76, 15. Culfre is fram geallan biternysse ælfremed, 584, 35. Wé w&aelig-acute;ron þurh synna ælfremede fram Gode; ðá wurde wé eác ælfremede fram his englum getealde, 38, 15. Fram ðám écan wurðmynte ælfremede beón, Hml. A. 21, 169.
Ælfric. For an account of Ælfric see 'Ælfric, a new study of his life and writings,' by C. L. White (Yale Studies in English).
ælf-sciéne, -sciéno; ælf-scínu. Take together under ælf-scíne.
ælf-siden. Add:--Þeós sealf is gód wiþ &aelig-acute;lcre feóndes costunga and ælfsidenne, Lch. ii. 334, 18. [Cf. (?) Icel. síða to charm; seiðr a charm.]
ælf-þone; f.? Dele ?: æl-fylc. l. æl-fylce.
&aelig-acute;l-hýd(?), e; f. An eel-skin:--Man sceal habban &aelig-acute;lhýde, ofnrace, mexscofle, Angl. ix. 265, 2.
&aelig-acute;-lic (&aelig-acute;w-). Add: I. of law, concerned with law, belonging to law:--Hé (John) wæs &aelig-acute;gðer ge &aelig-acute;lic ge godspellic, Hml. S. 16, 101. &AElig-acute;lice legalia (volumina), An. Ox. 4949. Tó ðám fíf &aelig-acute;licum bócum, Hml. Th. i. 188, 20: 98, 33: Hml. A. 24, 14. II. in accordance with law, fixed by law, legal, legitimate:--&AElig-acute;licere legitimae, Hpt. Gl. 411, 69. Oð ðæt hí becómon tó &aelig-acute;licre yldo until they came of age, Hml. A. 129, 439. Oð &aelig-acute;lice yldo, 132, 536. &AElig-acute;wlice legitimi, Angl. xiii. 369, 57. &AElig-acute;licera (-e, MS.) beboda praeceptorum legalium, An. Ox. 1017. Tó ðám &aelig-acute;licum onsægednyssum, Num. 18, 2. &AElig-acute;lice legalia (scita), An. Ox. 5144. II a. with special reference to marriage, v. &aelig-acute;:--&AElig-acute;ulic h&aelig-acute;mæd legitimum connubium, An. Ox. 415. &AElig-acute;wlices gegæder&dash-uncertain;scipes legitime jugalitatis, 582. Ácenned of &aelig-acute;licum gesinscype, Bd. 1, 27; S. 495, 22. Tó &aelig-acute;licum gyftum, Hml. A. 129, 441.
&aelig-acute;-líce; adv. Lawfully, legitimately:--&AElig-acute;líce lybbende, Hml. A. 24, 12. Æwlíce legitime, Angl. xiii. 369, 50.
&aelig-acute;-lifne (?); adj. Without means of support (v. lifen), nourished by others (?):--Aelifnae alumnis (alumni?), Ep. Gl. 3 d, 38.
&aelig-acute;ling burning. Substitute:--Lígræsc vel &aelig-acute;ling coruscatio, i. fulgor, splendor, Wrt. Voc. ii. 136, 3. Synna ne beóð n&aelig-acute;fre áfeormode for nánes fýres &aelig-acute;lincge, Hml. Th. ii. 590, 20.
æling weariness. v. &aelig-acute;-lenge: &aelig-acute;lingness. v. &aelig-acute;-lengness.
ælmes-bæþ, es; n. Washing of the poor done as an act of charity:--Sceóte man ælmessan . . . hwílum ælmesbæð, hwílum þearfena fótþweál, Wlfst. 171, 2.
ælmes-d&aelig-acute;d, e; f. An alms-deed, a charitable action:--Ðá ðing ðe God bebeád, ðæt is . . . ælmesd&aelig-acute;da, Hml. Th. ii. 22, 10: 602, 10. Nis nán ðearfa fram ælmesd&aelig-acute;dum áscyred, 106, 8. Hé on ælmesd&aelig-acute;dum áwunode in eleemosynis permansit, Bd. 5, 19; S. 636, 28. Gif se mon áhefð his handa tó ælmesd&aelig-acute;dum, Bl. H. 37, 24: H. R. 17, 27: Wlfst. 238, 24. Mid ælmesd&aelig-acute;dum and mid óðrum gódum weorcum, 142, 24. Góde weorc begán and ælmesd&aelig-acute;da, 286, 6: Hml. Th. ii. 100, 21.
ælmes-feoh. Add:--Peter's pence (v. Alms-fee in N. E. D.), Ll. Th. i. 432, 9.
ælmes-full; adj. Liberal with alms, charitable:--Ælfgár &b-tilde; se ælmes&dash-uncertain;fulla, Chr. 1021; P. 154, 30. Wé gehýrdan secgan be ðám ælmesfullan hú góde sáwle hé hæfð, Hml. A. 166, 61. Ælmysfulle eleemosynis largi, Ll. Th. ii. 224, 27. [Sein Martin þe bigan on his guwuðe to bien almesful, O. E. Hml. ii. 85, 10. Milde and allmessfull, Orm. 9931.]
ælmes-gedál, es; n. Distribution of alms:--Bisceopes dægweorc . . . his ælmesgedál, Ll. Th. ii. 314, 22: Wlfst. 171, 3. Ælmesgedál d&aelig-acute;le man gelóme, mete dám of hingredum, 74, 2.
ælmes-georn. Add:--Heó wæs swíðe ælmesgeorn, and ðá ðearfan . . . mid cystigum móde . . . áfédde, Hml. Th. i. 60, 14. Ælmysgeorn, Shrn. 98, 4. Sýn wé rummóde þearfendum mannum and earmum ælmesgeorne, Bl. H. 109, 15. Ælmesgeorne and árd&aelig-acute;de wið earme men, 131, 2. Mildheorte and ælmesgeorne, 95, 26: Wlfst. 109, 12. [Elmes&yogh;eorn nes heo nefre, O. E. Hml. i. 43, 32.]
ælmes-gifa, an; m. An almsgiver:--Sé ðe w&aelig-acute;re gítsiende óðra manna þinga, weorðe of his ágenan rihte begytenan ælmesgyfa (-gifa, v. l.) georne, Wlfst. 72, 4.
ælmes-gifu, e; f. What is given as alms, alms:--Ðæt ðæt heom góde men tó ælmesgife for Godes lufan sealdon, Wlfst. 159, 20.
ælmes-hláf, es; m. Bread given as alms:--Willa ic gesellan of ðém ærfe ðe mé God forgef &aelig-acute;lce gére CL. hláfa, L. hwítehláfa, CXX. elmes&dash-uncertain;hláfes, Cht. Th. 474, 26.
ælmes-leóht, es; n. Light brought to church by one keeping a vigil during a fast:--Ðonne man fæste . . . forl&aelig-acute;te man &aelig-acute;lce worldbysga, and læges and nihtes swá man oftost mæge on cirican gewunige, and mid ælmesleóhte wacigan ðár georne, Ll. Th. ii. 288, 1.
ælmes-lic; adj. I. of the nature of alms, eleemosynary, charitable:--Hié hígon gefeormien and hígon ús mid heora godcundum gódum sw&aelig-acute; gemynen sw&aelig-acute; ús árlic and him ælmeslic si&aelig-acute;, Cht. Th. 476, 34. Swé hit him rehtlicast and elmestlicast wére, 465, 24. II. depending upon alms, poor:--Ælmysli[cum] paupertino, An. Ox. 56, 302.
ælmes-líce; adv. Charitably:--Fóe hé tó thaem londe and hit forgelde and thaet wiorth gedaele fore hiora gástas suae aelmeslíce and suae rehtlíce suae hé him seolfa on his wísdóme geleornie, C. D. i. 234, 34.
16 ÆLMES-MANN--ÆNBR&E-hook;CE
ælmes-mann, es; m. An alms-man (v. N. E. D.), one supported by alms, a bedesman or a beggar:--Ðeáh se man nime &aelig-acute;nne stán and lecge on fúl slóh, ðæt se ælmesman mæge mid ðám óðrum fét steppan on ðá cl&aelig-acute;nan healfe, Wlfst. 239, 10. On ælmesmannes híwe, Hml. S. 23, 562. Ðæt gé dæghwámlíce d&aelig-acute;lan ælmessan . . . ælmesmannum oððe wydewum, Wlfst. 238, 28: Lch. i. 400, 17. Ðonne wille ic ðæt man nime tó &aelig-acute;lcan ðissa háma twelf ælmesmen, and gif hwæt hera &aelig-acute;nigan getíde, sette man ð&aelig-acute;r óþerne tó, C. D. B. iii. 75, 38.
ælmes-riht, es; n. A right or obligation in reference to alms (cf. Riht is ðæt man bet&aelig-acute;ce . . . þriddan d&aelig-acute;l (folces ælmessan) ðám þearfum, Ll. Th. ii. 256, 30):--&AElig-acute;ghwilc ælmesriht ðe man on Godes ést scolde mid rihte georne gel&aelig-acute;stan, &aelig-acute;lc man gelitlað oððe forhealdeð, Wlfst. 159, 21. Ðr&aelig-acute;lriht w&aelig-acute;ron generwde and ælmesriht gewanode, 158, 16.
ælmesse. Add: I. alms, what is given in charity:--Wist vel ælmesse stips, Wrt. Voc. i. 17, 8. Ælmesse agape, 33: eleemosyna vel agape, 28, 56. Swá swá wæter ádw&aelig-acute;scð fýr, swá ádw&aelig-acute;scð seó ælmysse synne, Hml. Th. ii. 106, 7. Ne selle mon tó fela . . . ðý l&aelig-acute;s him gehreówe sió ælmesse, Past. 325, 8. Ðé þúhte &aelig-acute;fre tó lytel úre ælmesse, Wlfst. 241, 3. Ælmæssan stipis, Wrt. Voc. ii. 78, 35. Ðæt gé dæg&dash-uncertain;hwámlíce d&aelig-acute;lan ælmessan be ðám d&aelig-acute;le ðe &aelig-acute;lcum men tó onhagige, þeáh hit ne sý bútan feórðan d&aelig-acute;l ánes hláfes, Wlfst. 238, 26. Wé l&aelig-acute;rað ðæt preóstas swá d&aelig-acute;lan folces ælmessan ðæt hig . . . folc tó ælmessan gewænian. And wé l&aelig-acute;rað ðæt preóstas sealmas singan ðonne hí ðá ælmessan d&aelig-acute;lan, Ll. Th. ii. 256, 7-11. Ic ðás elmessan gesette ob mínem erfelande, Cht. Th. 475, 26. Hwæt sceoldon ðé úre ælmessan? Wlfst. 240, 15. 'Forgyfað, and eów bið forgyfen. Syllað, and eów bið geseald.' Ðás twá ælmessena cynn ús sind tó begánne, Hml. Th. ii. 100, 31. Ðæt góde weorc ðára ælmæssena, Gr. D. 320, 25. Geornfull on árfæstum wæstmum ælmesena, Bd. 4, 11; S. 579, 7. Tó ælmessum ad agapem, Wrt. Voc. ii. 86, 57. II. a charitable action:--Þeáh se man ne nime búton &aelig-acute;nne stán and ðæne gelecge on fúl slóh, ðæt se ælmesman mæge mid óðrum fét stæppan on ðá clænan healfe, ðæt him byð swýþe micel ælmesse, Wlfst. 303, 11. Ic bidde eów þæt (þ&aelig-acute;re?) ælmyssan ðæt ic móte ánes þinges áxian, Hml. S. 23, 721. III. an offering:--Éghwelc cwicu almes (almus, L.) omnis victima, Mk. R. 9, 49. [Perhaps the word shows Celtic influence; cf. Old Irish almsan.]
ælmes-selen, e; f. Alms-giving:--Ðæt hálige gebed and seó hlútre lufu Godes and seó ælmessylen, Wlfst. 146, 4: Dóm. L. 28, 9. Fæsten and wæccan and ælmessylena æfter úrum gemete, Bl. H. 73, 27. Tó ðám weorce ælmæssylena eleemosynarum operibus, Gr. D. 329, 13: 321, 24. Hé hit hæfde geearnod mid ælmæsselenun and gódum weorcum, 330, 18. Mid bénum and mid ælmessylenum, Ll. Th. ii. 324, 32.
ælmes-weorc, es; n. Alms-deed, work of charity:--Ðæt wé úre synna béton mid fæstenum and mid gebedum and mid ælmesweorcum, Bl. H. 25, 17. [To wirrkenn allmeswerrken, Orm. 10118.]
&aelig-acute;lpig. v. án-lípig.
æl-syndrig quite apart, single:--Ælsyndrio singuli, Lk. R. 2, 3.
æl-tæw. l. æl-t&aelig-acute;we, -teáwe, -teówe, -tówe, and add:--Ic ongite ðætte ælt&aelig-acute;we anweald nis on nánum woruldríce, Bt. 33, 1; F. 120, 3. Se geleáfa strengra bið ð&aelig-acute;r ð&aelig-acute;r hé ælt&aelig-acute;we bið, Hml. Th. i. 250, 20. Hyt is ælt&aelig-acute;we gyf hí mon hreáwe swylgeþ, Lch. i. 344, 16. Hyra (joy and sorrow) náðer ne mæg beón æltéwe bútan óðrum, Prov. K. 71. Se mon ðe his módgeðanc æltówe byþ, Gr. D. 2, 5. Hé hét geáxian sumne ælt&aelig-acute;wne drý, Hml. S. 14, 49. Ic ðá égðyrle macige ðe ælteówe beóð, 36, 69. Ðá ælt&aelig-acute;wan mód ðára gódra esna piae subditorum mentes, Past. 199, 3. Ðeáh hié wieten ðæt hié ælt&aelig-acute;we ne sín cum de imperfectione reprehendunt, 7. Hé ne nom náne ware húlice hié w&aelig-acute;ron, for ðon hiera wæs má forcúþra ðonne ælt&aelig-acute;wra, Ors. 5, 4; S. 224, 23. Hæfde ic ælteówe þénas n&aelig-acute;re ic ðus eáðelíce oferswíðed, Hml. S. 11, 226.
æl-t&aelig-acute;wlíce. Add:--Ðone mon ðú meaht gelácnian ælt&aelig-acute;wlíce, Lch. ii. 348, 16, 22.
æl-þeód, &c., &aelig-acute;-manne, æmbern. v. el-þeód, &c., &aelig-acute;-men, embren.
&aelig-acute;-melle: adj. Insipid:--Insipidun, quod saporem non habet, hoc est unmeagle sive &aelig-acute;melle, Wrt. Voc. ii. 49, 37. Cf. á-mællad.
&aelig-acute;-melness. Add: I. want of energy or of interest, sloth:--Se sixta heáfodleahtor (accidia) is ásolcennys oððe &aelig-acute;melnys. Se leahtor déð ðæt ðám men ne lyst nán ðing tó góde gedón, ac g&aelig-acute;ð him ásolcen fram &aelig-acute;lcere dugeðe, Hml, Th. ii. 220, 22. &AElig-acute;mylnys, Hml. S. 1, 107. II. weariness, tedium, disgust:--&AElig-acute;melnes fastidium, Wrt. Voc. ii. 146, 46. Ð&aelig-acute;r beóð ealle unrótnyssa, ádl and yrre and &aelig-acute;melnys taedia, tristitiae, indignatio, languor (Dóm. L. p. 25, 115), Wlfst. 139, 18: Dóm. L. 228. Unrótnes, &aelig-acute;melnys taedia, tristitiae, 260. Snoffan &aelig-acute;mylnysse nausiae tedio, Angl. xiii. 369, 50. &AElig-acute;mælnessa fastidia, Hpt. 33, 238, 5.
&aelig-acute;-men. Add: &aelig-acute;-menne, &aelig-acute;-mann (? v. next word; for declension cf. &aelig-acute;-mód):--Ðá wundrade Alexander hwý hit swá &aelig-acute;menne w&aelig-acute;re vacuam civitatem ratus, Ors. 3, 9; S. 134, 12. Hié hit ð&aelig-acute;r swá &aelig-acute;menne métton, 2, 4; S. 76, 16.
&aelig-acute;-menne solitude:--'Ðú beþorftest ðæt ðú hæfdest dígele stówe and &aelig-acute;manne (-menne?) &aelig-acute;lces óðres þinges (ista solitudinem meram desiderant) and fæáwa cúðe men.' Ðá cwæð ic: 'Ic nebbe nán ðára ne ðonne &aelig-acute;menne ne óðera manna fultum ne dýgela stówe,' Shrn. 165, 8-12.
&aelig-acute;merge, an; f. I. embers, ashes:--Se hláf wæs mid ðám glédum and mid ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;myrgan (-yrian, -ergean, v. ll.) (cineribus) bewrigen, Gr. D. 87, 11. Beréc hý on háte &aelig-acute;mergean, Lch. iii. 30, 18. II. fig. dust:--Ic nán gást ne eom ac &aelig-acute;merge and axe and eall fl&aelig-acute;sc, Hml. S. 23 b, 286. [O. H. Ger. eimuria busta: Icel. eimyrja; f. embers.]
&aelig-acute;met-bed(d), es; n. An ant-hill:--Genim &aelig-acute;metbed mid ealle, ðára ðe hwílum fleogað, beóþ reáde, Lch. ii. 338, 21.
æmete. l. &aelig-acute;met(t)e, and add:--&AElig-acute;mette formica, Wrt. Voc. i. 78, 65. &AElig-acute;mete chameleon, ii. 15, 59. Swá þicce hié áweóllon swá &aelig-acute;mettan, Nar. 11, 13. Émetan formicas, Kent. Gl. 1102. Geseah ic micelne &aelig-acute;mettena heáp, Hml. A. 204, 315.
&aelig-acute;met-hwíl. Add:--Ðæs restedæges &aelig-acute;methwíle (æn-, MS.) Sabbati otium, An. Ox. 40, 18.
&aelig-acute;met-hyll. Add:--Past. 191, 25.
&aelig-acute;metta, &aelig-acute;meta, &aelig-acute;mta. Add:--On &aelig-acute;mettan in tranquilitate, Past. 59, 1. Beóð hié swíður on hiera móde geswenced for ð&aelig-acute;m &aelig-acute;mettan (&aelig-acute;mtan, Hatt. MS.) ipsa deterius sua quiete fatigantur, 126, 24, Swá oft swá hí &aelig-acute;mtan (&aelig-acute;mettan, v. l.) habbaþ quotiescumque vacant, Bd. 4, 25; S. 601, 16: Ll. Th. i. 236, 3. v. un-&aelig-acute;metta.
&aelig-acute;mettig, &aelig-acute;metig, &aelig-acute;mtig. Add: I. of space, empty, void, vacant:--Seó stów ne bið nóht longe &aelig-acute;mettugu, Shrn. 82, 24. &AElig-acute;mettig, &aelig-acute;mtig, Bd. 4, 30; Sch. 537, 6. &AElig-acute;mtig innoþ, Scint. 57, 4. Gyt is rýmet &aelig-acute;mtig, Hml. Th. ii. 376, 9. &AElig-acute;lc beód &aelig-acute;mtig (vacua) byþ gesewen, Coll. M. 28, 33. Ðæt &aelig-acute;mtige fæc bufon ð&aelig-acute;re lyfte, Lch. iii. 242, 16. &AElig-acute;ne émptige cytan, Hml. S. 33, 170. &AElig-acute;mtige fatu mid wíne áfyllan, Hml. Th. ii. 58, 14. I a. with gen.:--Byden &aelig-acute;lces eles &aelig-acute;mtig, Gr. D. 160, 10. II. devoid, void of, free from:--'Wes ðú hál, geofena ful.' Heó wæs ful cweden, næs &aelig-acute;metugu, Bl. H. 5, 5. II a. with gen.:--&AElig-acute;metig gástlicra mægena, Bl. H. 37, 9. Hí wiðinnan &aelig-acute;mtige w&aelig-acute;ron ðæs gódan ingehýdes, Hml. Th. ii. 570, 7. II b. with fram:--Hé wæs &aelig-acute;mtig fram ðám incundan andgite, Hml. Th. ii. 556, 1. Spr&aelig-acute;c &aelig-acute;mtegu fram mægenes byrðene, Gr. D. 151, 1. Ídelne and &aelig-acute;mtigne fram ðám écum gódnyssum, Hml. Th. i. 204, 11. III. unoccupied, at leisure, exempt from:--Ic eom &aelig-acute;mtig (&aelig-acute;mptig, v. l.) vacat mihi, Ælfc. Gr. 206, 13. Martha swanc, and Maria sæt &aelig-acute;mtig, Hml. Th. ii. 440, 1. Se &aelig-acute;mettega (&aelig-acute;metiga, Hatt. MS.), Past. 190, 18. Ðonne hig bysega nabbon and &aelig-acute;mtige synd, R. Ben. 84, 19. Swá hié &aelig-acute;mettegran (&aelig-acute;metegran, Hatt. MS.) beóð ðonne óðre men, Past. 190, 14. III a. with gen.:--Hié &aelig-acute;mettige (&aelig-acute;mtige, Hatt. MS.) beóð ð&aelig-acute;re scíre, Past. 126, 23. Ðá menn ðe &aelig-acute;mtige beóð ðæs ðæt hié for óðre men swincen, 191, 13. III b. with fram:--Fram ðám gewinne ð&aelig-acute;re þénunge &aelig-acute;mettig (&aelig-acute;mtig, &aelig-acute;metig, v. ll.) wæs a labore et ministerio vacabat, Bd. 4, 3; Sch. 351, 11. III c. with tó, free to do:--Ð&aelig-acute;m ðe &aelig-acute;mettig (&aelig-acute;metig, Hatt. MS.) bið his ágenne willan tó wyrceanne illi sibimet vacanti, Past. 190, 24. Hié wilniað ðæt hié bión freó and &aelig-acute;mettige (&aelig-acute;mtige, Hatt. MS.) tó gástlicum weorcum, 134, 26. IV. unmarried:--Gif hwylc &aelig-acute;mtig man (vacuus homo) gewemme óðres wíf . . . And gif hwylc man ðe on his rihtan gesynscipe libbe &aelig-acute;mtigne man (vacuam) gewemme, Ll. Th. ii. 164, 32, 34. Yfel &aelig-acute;wbryce bið ðæt &aelig-acute;wfæst man mid &aelig-acute;mtige (émtige, v. l.) forlicge, i. 404, 22. Hí gemengan wið ðá &aelig-acute;mtegan wífmen (feminis vacantibus), Past. 401, 24.
&aelig-acute;met(ti)gian, &aelig-acute;mtig(i)an. Add: I. to empty:--Ic &aelig-acute;mtige (émtigie, &aelig-acute;mptig(i)e, v. ll.) vacuo, Ælfc. Gr. 137, 4. II. fig. v. &aelig-acute;mettig, II:--His spr&aelig-acute;c wæs &aelig-acute;metegod (vacua) ð&aelig-acute;re mycelnyssé his gódan mægnes, Gr. D. 151, 1. III. to be at leisure. v. &aelig-acute;mettig, III:--Ne on dæge ðú aemtiga (vaces), Scint. 31, 8. Aemetgiað vacate, Ps. Srt. 45, 11. Hí &aelig-acute;mtian vacent, R. Ben. I. 81, 15. III a. with dat. (in Latin glosses) to devote one's self to, take time for:--&AElig-acute;mta r&aelig-acute;dincge vaca lectioni, Scint. 222, 5. Sé ðe émtige (vacet) ídelnesse, R. Ben. I. 83, 8. R&aelig-acute;dinge hí &aelig-acute;mtian, 82, 9, 14. Émtian, 83, 15. III b. with reflex. pron. and tó:--Mid ymnum hé hine &aelig-acute;metegode tó Gode studebat hymnis Deo vacare, Gr. D. 282, 4. &AElig-acute;mtigað eów tó r&aelig-acute;dinge vacate lectioni, Ælfc. Gr. 206, 13. Ðá men ðe hié selfe tó ð&aelig-acute;re ciricean wlite &aelig-acute;mtegian sceoldon, Past. 135, 5. v. ge-, un-&aelig-acute;mettgian.
&aelig-acute;mettigness, e; f. Emptiness; an open space:--Ádrifen fram ð&aelig-acute;re heortan &aelig-acute;mtignesse ab ipso cordis ostio repulsa, Gr. D. 35, 17.
&aelig-acute;-mirce; adj. Excellent, distinguished; egregius, Wrt. Voc. ii. 30, 28.
&aelig-acute;-mód. Add:--Émód amens, Wrt. Voc. ii. 100, 15. &AElig-acute;mód, 6, 57. W&aelig-acute;ron ðá synna ealle ádílegode bútan ánre; seó wæs seó m&aelig-acute;ste, and heó wearð ðá &aelig-acute;mód, Hml. S. 3, 553. Man sceal l&aelig-acute;wedum mannum secgan be heora andgites m&aelig-acute;ðe, swá ðæt hí ne beón ðurh ðá deópnysse &aelig-acute;móde, Hml. Th. ii. 446, 8.
&aelig-acute;mta, &aelig-acute;mtig, &c. v. &aelig-acute;metta, &aelig-acute;mettig, &c.
&aelig-acute;-mynde, es; n. Want of care (?), neglect:--Funde ic hwæt eorðe mæg wið andan and wið &aelig-acute;minde and wið ðá micelan mannes tungan . . . beó gé gemindige mínes gódes, Lch. i. 384, 22.
&aelig-acute;myrge. v. &aelig-acute;merge.
ænbr&e-hook;ce. This in the facsimile of the MS. seems to be the form in El. 1029, the passage given in the Dict. under an-bróce (q. v.). If æþelu
ÆNCNETRYM--&AElig-acute;R 17
be taken as a noun, the first part of the word might be (?) &aelig-acute;n (cf. &aelig-acute;n-lic), and the meaning be unique (?).
æncnetrym = &aelig-acute;n(i)gne trym (?) or ængne trym (?) a narrow step; an acc. used adverbially with same force as colloquial a little bit (?). The word pedetemptim (An. Ox. 7, 221: 8, 165) is glossed by this form in the passage: Qui pedetemptim in pubertatis primordio instrumentis medicinallbus imbuti, Ald. 41, 33. v. trem in Dict.
&aelig-acute;ne. Add: I. as adverb answering question how often:--&AElig-acute;lce dæg &aelig-acute;ne semel per diem, Jos. 6, 3. Oft næs &aelig-acute;ne, Wlfst. 243, 2: El. 1253. Oftor ðonne &aelig-acute;ne, Ll. Th. ii. 334, 1. &AElig-acute;ne ðrowade Críst ðurh hine sylfne, ac dæghwomlíce bið his þrowung geedníwod þurh gerýnu ðæs húsles, Hml. Th. ii. 276, 10. Ná &aelig-acute;ne ac &aelig-acute;fre, Hml. S. 1, 141. I a. as multiplier:--&AElig-acute;ne seofon beóð seofon, Angl. viii. 304, 28. II. with ordinal force, a first time:--Ðá wæs se deófol &aelig-acute;ne oferswíðed. . . . Ðá wæs se deófol óðere síðe oferswíðed, Hml. Th. i. 168, 35-170, 31. Hí hine swungon &aelig-acute;ne and óðre síðe, ii. 302, 9. &AElig-acute;ne hé sende and eft, i. 522, 1. III. marking indefinite time, once, at any time:--Hweðer ðá ðe ð&aelig-acute;r beóð &aelig-acute;ne (semel) besæncte, sculon hí ð&aelig-acute;r beón aa byrnende, Gr. D. 334, 4: 108, 24. Sé ðe &aelig-acute;ne ð&aelig-acute;ron befylð, ne wyrð hé n&aelig-acute;fre álýsed, Hml. Th. ii. 352, 29: Hml. S. 23, 375. Gif ðú &aelig-acute;ne behátest Gode hé wyle ðonne habban ðæt ðú him behéte, Hex. 50, 4. IV. of past time, once, at some former time:--Ðá ðe &aelig-acute;ne mid sygefæstum deáde middangeard oferswíððe, Hml. Th. i. 84, 31. Þurh ðé Freá &aelig-acute;ne ón ðás eorðan út síðade, Cri. 329. Ic ðé &aelig-acute;ne ábealh, ðá wit Adam eaples þigdon, Sat. 410 (substitute this for translation in Dict.). V. at once:--&AElig-acute;ne ic fare tó ðé and ádílgige ðé semel ascendam in medio tui et delebo te, Ex. 33, 5. Ðanne samod becumað eall engla werod . . . &aelig-acute;ne bið geban micel, Dóm. L. 128. v. &aelig-acute;nes.
æned, &aelig-acute;n-ége. v. ened, án-eáge.
&aelig-acute;nes; adv. Once. I. cf. &aelig-acute;ne, I:--&AElig-acute;nes ic swór semel juravi, Ps. L. 88, 36. Gif bescoren man gange him an gestlíðnesse, gefe him man &aelig-acute;nes, Ll. Th. i. 38, 13. II. cf. &aelig-acute;ne, II:--Ðá se bróður ðás word gehýrde &aelig-acute;nes, hé forhtode . . . and óðere nihte hé wæs gemanod mid ðám ylcan wordum, Gr. Ð. 338, 4.
&aelig-acute;net-ness. v. next word.
ænett, es; n. Solitude, retirement:--&AElig-acute;nettes solitudinis, An. Ox. 2383: anachoreseos, 3638. &AElig-acute;nyttes, 2, 233. Tó ð&aelig-acute;re stówe his leófan &aelig-acute;nettes (ánetnysse, &aelig-acute;netnesse, v. ll.) ad locum dilectae solitudinis, Gr. D. 105, 27. Cf. ánett.
&aelig-acute;nga. Substitute: Solitary:--Hé lifað leódum feor, lócað geneahhe fram ðám unl&aelig-acute;dan &aelig-acute;ngan hláford he lives far from men, from the wretched solitary often are his lord's looks turned, Sal. 382. v. ánga.
&aelig-acute;ngan-cundes; adv. In a way that is unique (?):--Críst stód ofer ádle (alde, MS.) &aelig-acute;ngancundes (as none other did), Lch. iii. 36, 25.
ænge; adv., Ængle. v. ange, Engle.
&aelig-acute;nig. Add: I. substantival, (1) absolute:--Ic l&aelig-acute;re ðæt &aelig-acute;nig ne áfýle . . . hine sylfne, ne &aelig-acute;nig ne healde yrre on his heortan tó lange, ne &aelig-acute;nig ðurh worldhoge forsorgie tó swýðe, Wlfst. 69, 14-16. &AElig-acute;nigum cuivis, cuilibet, Wrt. Voc. ii. 137, 66. Næs riht on ð&aelig-acute;re stówe &aelig-acute;nigne tó ácwellanne, Nar. 30, 2. ¶ gen. pl. combined with &aelig-acute;lc to emphasize? cf. ánra gehwilc:--Gefultuma mé ánegra (-e, v. l.) &aelig-acute;lces fylstes bed&aelig-acute;led, Hml. S. 23 b, 441. [Or ? áneg = single, sole; cf. O. Sax. énag: O. H. Ger. einag unicus.] (2) with gen.:--Ic mé ne ondréd ðæt mé ð&aelig-acute;ra &aelig-acute;nig beswice, Nar. 30. 1. Aenge þinga quoquo modo, Wrt. Voc. ii. 118, 60. II. adjectival:--On &aelig-acute;nige óðre wísan aliter, Wrt. Voc. ii. 2, 56. Ic &aelig-acute;nigra mé weána ne wénde, B. 932. II a. with qualitative force:--Ne beó ðú &aelig-acute;nig manslaga, Wlfst. 66, 17. [O. Sax. énig: O. H. Ger. einíc.]
&aelig-acute;n-íge, &aelig-acute;nig-wiht. v. án-íge, wiht, II a in Dict.
&aelig-acute;niht. Add: I. as substantive:--Ne &aelig-acute;niht hiá gel&aelig-acute;dde ne quid tollerent, Mk. L. 6, 8. Ne ondueardest ðú &aelig-acute;niht (quicquam), 14, 60. &AElig-acute;niht of ð&aelig-acute;m ðá ðe geségon, Lk. L. 9, 36. Ne spildic of ð&aelig-acute;m &aelig-acute;niht &l-bar; óht non perdidi ex ipsis quemquam, Jn. L. 18, 9. Ne spræc ic &aelig-acute;niht locutus sum nihil, 20. Wyrca &aelig-acute;night facere quicquam, 5, 30: 9, 33: Lk. L. 20, 40. II. as adjective:--Næfdes ðú mæht wið mec &aelig-acute;neht (ullam), Jn. L. 19, 11. III. as adverb:--Ne forstondes &aelig-acute;niht wífigæ non expedit nubere, Mt. L. 19, 10: Mk. L. 5, 26: Jn. L. 6, 63.
&aelig-acute;n-lic. Add: I. only, single:--Aenli simplex, Txts. 115, 156. Ðú ðe &aelig-acute;nlic eart Godes bearn, Hml. S. 23, 806. &AElig-acute;nlican míne unicam meam, Ps. Spl. 34, 20. II. alone, solitary:--&AElig-acute;nlic (unicus) and ðearfa ic eom, Ps. Spl. 24, 17. III. excellent, peerless, &c.:--Hú beorht, mire, &aelig-acute;nlic O preclara, i. splendida, An. Ox. 1266. &AElig-acute;nlic aurea, 1461: Hy. S. 24, 7. Sum swíðe &aelig-acute;nlic wer and forem&aelig-acute;re quidam spectabilis vir, Gr. D. 307, 1. Adrianus wæs geong and &aelig-acute;nlic, Shrn. 59, 28. Fæger on ansýne and &aelig-acute;nlic, 88, 13. &AElig-acute;nlicu Godes drút alma Dei genetrix, Dóm. L. 290. &AElig-acute;nlicum claro, An. Ox. 3082: preclaram, 3721. Hí ealle licgað on &aelig-acute;nlicum wurðmynte, Hml. S. 29, 333. Tó Antiochia ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;nlican byrig, 3, 298. On Eferwíc ðæt &aelig-acute;nlice mynster, 26, 109. Tó &aelig-acute;nlicum aurea (in astra), An. Ox. 1438. Hé oft dyde swýðe &aelig-acute;nlice ðincg, Hml. S. 13, 270. Ðá &aelig-acute;nlecan heápas investes catervas, Wrt. Voc. ii. 44, 40. &AElig-acute;nlicre (elicre, Wrt.) wæs prestare, 81, 64. &AElig-acute;nlicoste pulcherrima, i. speciosissima, An. Ox. 2113. Hé arn tó ánum ylpe ðe ð&aelig-acute;r &aelig-acute;nlicost wæs, Hml. S. 25, 581. [Ungerím swýðe &aelig-acute;nlices folces, Chr. 1120; P. 249, 20.]
&aelig-acute;n-líce. Add:--&AElig-acute;nlíce gefretewod, Hml. S. 9, 24: 18, 341. Ðá cwæð ðæt folc ðæt hé &aelig-acute;nlíce spræc, 18, 111: 36, 79: Hml. A. 103, 44.
&aelig-acute;n-lípe, -lípig, -ness. v. án-lípe, -lípig, -ness: æ-not, l. &aelig-acute;-note: æpel-. v. æppel-: æpening. v. æppel-cynn.
æppel. Add: nom. ac. pl. æp(p)la, ap(p)la, æpplas (apples of eye); gen. pl. appla, æpplena; m.: appla (-u, v. finger-æppel), æppel (? æppel mala, Wrt. Voc. ii. 54, 40); n. I. an apple (in a special and in a general sense as in oak-apple):--Æppel pomum, Ælfc. Gr. 31, 4. &E-hook;ppel malum, Kent. Gl. 962. Scoldon hangigan reáde apla (mala punica). Hwæt is getácnod ðurh ðá reádan apla (appla, l. 13)? Se æppel bið betogen mid rinde, Past. 95, 3-6. On ðæs æples (pomi) gewilnunge, 309, 17. Eaples, Sat. 411. Æppeles seáw, Lch. i. 350, 2. Æples, ii. 132, 11. Æpples, 111, 36, 31. Sing ðæt galdor on ðone æppel, 38, 4. Gebr&aelig-acute;dedne æppel, súme æppel, ii. 132, 14, 15. Of ðám treówe ðe man háteþ mórbeám nim æppel . . . hwítne æppel ðe ðonne gyt ne reádige, i. 330, 19-22, 25. Ðá ðá Adam geæt ðone forbodenan æppel, Hml. Th. ii. 240, 21. Líðe æppla (appla, v. l.) mitia poma, Ælfc. Gr. 274, 13. Gecyrnlede (-u in margin) appla mala granata, Hpt. Gl. 496, 60: An. Ox. 2, 258. Ðá Affracaniscan æppla mala punica, Wrt. Voc. ii. 83, 52. Æpla, Lch. ii. 244, 2. Æpplena pomorum, Ps. L. 78, 1. Appla dactilorum, An. Ox. 2394. Wið gréne æpla, Lch. ii. 208, 10. v. milisc in Dict. II. an apple-shaped object:--Æpples sphaerae, Wrt. Voc. ii. 32, 44. Cnuca tósomne ðám gelíce ðe ðú ánne æppel wyrce, Lch. i. 250, 10. II a. an eye-ball:--Gif se æppel léf biþ, Bt. 38, 5; F. 204, 29. Se óðer æppel wæs geémtigod, and se óðer hangode gehál æt his hleóre, Hml. S. 21, 280. Beóð ðá æplas hále . . . sió scearpnes ðæs æples (æpples, Hatt. MS.) . . . Ðurh ðone æpl ðæs eágean, Past. 68, 2, 4, 17. v. cod-, corn-, hunig-, weax-æppel.
æppel-b&aelig-acute;re. Add:--Æpelbére malifer, Wrt. Voc. ii. 54, 44.
æppel-berende; adj. Apple-bearing:--Æppilberende pomiferam, Rtl. 98, 33.
æppel-cynn, es; n. A kind of apple:--Selle him etan . . . manigfeald æppelcynn, peran, æpeningas (medlars), Lch. ii. 180, 14.
æppel-cyrnel, es; n. Substitute: An apple-pip:--Æppelcyrnlu mala granata (the glosser seems to have read this as = pips of apples, instead of = apples with pips; cf. the more correct gloss in Hpt. Gl. 496, 60 (v. under æppel)), Wrt. Voc. ii. 54, 43.
æppel-fæt, es; n. A vessel for carrying apples:--Æppelfæt (-fæc, MS.) apoforeta, vasa pomis ferendis apta, Hpt. 31, 15, 401.
æppel-sceal. l. -scealu, and add: The sheath that encloses the pip of an apple:--Filmenum, æpelscealum ymb ðá cyrnlu cittis, Wrt. Voc. ii. 17, 69.
æppel-treów. Add:--Apoltré (or = apuldre, q. v. ?) malum, Lk. L. 6, 22. Æpeltreówu granata (v. æppel), Wrt. Voc. ii. 42, 2.
æppel-tún. Add:--Æppeltún pomerium, Wrt. Voc. i. 84, 53. Eappultún, Ps. Srt. 78, 1. '&AElig-acute;lc gód treów . . . and yfel treów . . .' Ne m&aelig-acute;nde úre Drihten ðá treówa ðe on æppeltúne weaxað, Hml. Th. ii. 406, 10. On æppeltúne gán anxsumnysse getácnað, Lch. iii. 206, 17. Binnon his æppeltún in hortum arboribus consitum, Hml. A. 100, 269. On orcgearde . . . on æppeltúnum in hortis, Past. 381, 14, 16.
æppel-wín. Add:--Æppelwín idromelum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 49, 57.
æps a fir-tree. v. æbs: æps aspen. v. æsp.
æpsen; adj. Impudent, shameless, foul:--Æpsin frontosa, An. Ox. 7, 301. v. next two words.
æpsen, æf(e)sn, e; f. Impudence, foulness:--Ungerísendre æfesne (ungerysenre æfsna in marg.) indecens obscenitas, Hpt. Gl. 492, 60: An. Ox. 3674 (where see note).
æpsenness, e; f. Shame, disgrace:--Æpsenyss dedecus, Scint. 174, 9.
ær; m. l. &aelig-acute;r.
&aelig-acute;r; adj. Add: [Without positive (for &aelig-acute;rne mergen l. &aelig-acute;rnemergen), but see &aelig-acute;r; adv.]:--From &aelig-acute;ran morgene, Chr. 538; P. 17, note 11. Ðá ðe on &aelig-acute;ran tíman lífes w&aelig-acute;ron, Lch. iii. 436, 5. Ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;ran h&aelig-acute;le incolomitati pristinae, An. Ox. 4354. On ðá &aelig-acute;ran h&aelig-acute;le, 1875. On &aelig-acute;rum tídum, Lch. iii. 432, 21: 442, 22. On ðám twám &aelig-acute;rrum bócum, Hml. S. pref. 41. Hé bebeád &aelig-acute;rest monna primus statuit, Ors. 6, 30; S. 284, 8: Shrn. 49, 20. Æt &aelig-acute;restan, Lch. ii. 118, 19. v. &aelig-acute;rra.
&aelig-acute;r; adv. I. positive, (1) early:--Swýþe &aelig-acute;r in dagunge primo diluculo, Bd. 4, 23; S. 596, 17. Swýþe &aelig-acute;r on morgen, Ps. Th. 45, 5. (2) expressing readiness, quickness, soon:--Sweord &aelig-acute;r gebr&aelig-acute;d gúðcyning, B. 2562. Hé wel &aelig-acute;r árás . . . Se apostol cwæð tó him: 'For hwon árise ðú swá hraðe?, Gr. D. 227, 4. Nýtenu etað swá &aelig-acute;r swá hí hit habbað, Hml. S. 16, 317. Ðú wilt higian ðon &aelig-acute;r ðe ðú hine ongitest, Bt. 11, 2; F. 34, 8. Ðonne &aelig-acute;r ðe hé ðæt gewealdleþer forl&aelig-acute;t . . ., ðonne forl&aelig-acute;taþ hí ðá sibbe, 21; F. 74, 31. II. cpve. (1) earlier, before:--Dæge &aelig-acute;r pridie, Wrt. Voc. ii. 68, 50. &AElig-acute;r dudum, ante, An. Ox. 1920: jam, 5483. &AElig-acute;r ðonne hé, B. 1182. Gefyrn &aelig-acute;r jam, An. Ox. 56, 93. &AElig-acute;r gefyrn, Cri. 63. &AElig-acute;r oððe æfter, 1692. &AElig-acute;r biforan, 468: El. 1132. [See also síþ in Dict.] ¶ on &aelig-acute;r previously, beforehand:--Drihten ðe on &aelig-acute;r wát eal ðæt tóweard is, Lch. iii. 436, 20:
18 &AElig-acute;R--&AElig-acute;RENDIAN
Hml. Th. i. 114, 3: Chr. 1067; P. 201, 26. Hé wolde warnian on &aelig-acute;r, Gen. 6, 6. Fela þing wiste se hálga wer on &aelig-acute;r, lange &aelig-acute;r hí gelumpon, Hml. S. 31, 788. (1 a) making present perfect and preterite pluperfect:--Redic ete &aelig-acute;r, ne mæg ðé nán man áttre áwyrdan if you have eaten radish, nobody can injure yon by poison, Lch. ii. 110, 10. Ðæt feoh ðæt hí &aelig-acute;r l&aelig-acute;fdon the money they had left (when they were spending before, v. l. 200), Hml. S. 23, 213. Wáron ð&aelig-acute;re hl&aelig-acute;ddre stapas áléfede on &aelig-acute;r the steps of the ladder had been weakened, 31, 602. (2) marking readiness, sooner:--Ic nóht ðon &aelig-acute;r blon I stopped none the sooner, Bd. 5, 6; S. 619, 15. Náhte ðý &aelig-acute;r, Gr. D. 152, 17. ¶ with correlative conjunction. v. &aelig-acute;r; conj. (1) before:--Hié &aelig-acute;r flugon, &aelig-acute;r hié tógædere geneál&aelig-acute;cten, Ors. 4, 6; S. 170, 24: Past. 433, 28. Ðæt hé hié forceorfe &aelig-acute;r, &aelig-acute;r hié on ðá eágan feallen, 141, 10. Hé wolde on &aelig-acute;r ðæt godspell áwrítan, &aelig-acute;r ðám ðe hé gewende him fram, Hml. S. 15, 139. (2) sooner:--Manegum men is leófre ðæt hé &aelig-acute;r swelte, &aelig-acute;r hé geseó his wíf and his bearn sweltende, Bt. 10; F. 28, 39. &AElig-acute;r ic mé sylfne ofsleá, &aelig-acute;r ðon ic sende míne hond on ðás f&aelig-acute;mnan, Shrn. 130, 26. III. superlative (&aelig-acute;rest), first:--Ðú meaht &aelig-acute;lcne unðeáw on ð&aelig-acute;m men &aelig-acute;resð be sumum tácnum ongietan . . . &aelig-acute;r hé hit mid wordum cýðe, Past. 157, 19. Tó hwilces tíman se steorra him &aelig-acute;rst æteówode, Hml. Th. i. 78, 18. &AElig-acute;st of ánre byrig, ðonne of óðerre, Ors. 3, 7; S. 112, 22. Hé angan tó smeágenne &aelig-acute;rest þinga hú hé his líf gerihtl&aelig-acute;can meahte, Lch. iii. 438, 29: Ll. Th. ii. 316, 11. v. &aelig-acute;ror.
&aelig-acute;r; conj. Add: (1) with indic. (or uncertain):--Hý hié hindan ofrídan ne meahte, &aelig-acute;r hié on ðám fæstenne w&aelig-acute;ron, Chr. 877; P. 74, 18. Hí cw&aelig-acute;don ðæt Críst n&aelig-acute;re, &aelig-acute;r hé ácenned wæs of Marian, Hml. Th. i. 70, 5. Hit long first wæs &aelig-acute;r hé út wolde faran tó gefeohte, &aelig-acute;r him mon s&aelig-acute;de ðæt hié wolden faran tó Italiam, Ors. 5, 8; S. 232, 4. (2) with subjunctive:--Hé hét átimbran ðá burg, &aelig-acute;r hé ðonan fóre, Chr. 919; S. 100, 14. Nánwuht ne byð yfel, &aelig-acute;r mon wéne ðæt hit yfel seó, Bt. 11, 1; F. 32, 30. (3) with the verb to be inferred:--Ðæt se Fæder w&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;r se Sunu, Hml. Th. i. 290, 7. Nán þing næs &aelig-acute;r hé, Hml. S. 1, 65. Blódl&aelig-acute;s is tó forgánne fíftýne nihtum &aelig-acute;r hláfmæsse, Lch. ii. 146, 8. Ðá geácsedon ðá consulas ðæt &aelig-acute;r, &aelig-acute;r Hannibal, Ors. 4, 10; S. 198, 23. Heó cymð &aelig-acute;r, &aelig-acute;r ðá wyrðmynðu, Past. 209, 16. See &aelig-acute;r; adv. II. ¶, III.
&aelig-acute;r; prep. Add: I. with dat. (1) before a certain time or circumstance:--&AElig-acute;r ð&aelig-acute;re teóðan tíde, Ll. Th. ii. 436, 7. &AElig-acute;r Martines mæssan, Chr. 971; P. 119, 23. &AElig-acute;r Crístes gefl&aelig-acute;scnesse, P. 4, 22. &AElig-acute;r Pendan deáþe, Bd. 3, 21; S. 551, 29. &AElig-acute;r ð&aelig-acute;re costunge, Past. 103, 25. &AElig-acute;r ðæs monnes hryre, 299, 18. &AElig-acute;r anginne, Hml. S. 1, 17. (1 a) before the proper time. v. &aelig-acute;r-&aelig-acute;t:--Ðæt men &aelig-acute;r tíman ne gereordige, Hml. S. 16, 316. &AElig-acute;r m&aelig-acute;le, Hml. Th. ii. 590, 25. (2) ago, cf. for:--&AElig-acute;r monigum geárum (ante annos plures) be his lífe wé áwriton, Bd. 4, 28; S. 605, 12. Ðæt nú &aelig-acute;r þrím geárum geworden wæs quod ante triennium factum est, 4, 32; S. 611, 11. (3) marking priority:--His bróþor &aelig-acute;r him ríce hæfde, Bd. 3, 14; S. 539, 19. Gif hire forðsíð getímige &aelig-acute;r him, Wlfst. 304, 23. Hé &aelig-acute;r worolde rícsode, Past. 33, 13: Cri. 1346, (4) marking preference (in the phrase &aelig-acute;r ðám (ðan) ðe):--Sum wíf wolde hire líf forl&aelig-acute;tan, &aelig-acute;r ðan ðe heó luge, Hml. S. 12, 179. Wolde se cwellere mid him sweltan, &aelig-acute;r ðan ðe hé hine slóge, 19, 102. Hí sweltan woldon, &aelig-acute;r ðan ðe hí wiðsócon Gode, and heora líf áléton &aelig-acute;r ðan ðe heora geleáfan, 19, 102-3. II. with acc.:--God &aelig-acute;r ealle worulda, Hml. Th. ii. 280, 13: 596, 28. Wæs hé beforan &aelig-acute;r þá þreó geár gecrístnod, Bl. H. 215, 36.
&aelig-acute;ra, an; m. A scraper (of brass):--Aera, &aelig-acute;ren screop strigillus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 121, 41.
&aelig-acute;-r&aelig-acute;fe (-reáfe); adj. Discovered:--Hí drifon stacan on Wulfstánes feder, and ðet werð &aelig-acute;reáfe, Cht. Th. 230, 16. v. á-ráfian.
&aelig-acute;r-&aelig-acute;t, es; m. Eating too soon [v. &aelig-acute;r; prep. I. (1 a); cf. Ll. Th. ii. 436, 6, 33-38]:--Míne synna . . . on &aelig-acute;r&aelig-acute;te and on oferfylle, Angl. xi. 102, 88. Swá hwæt swá wé misdóð . . . on &aelig-acute;r&aelig-acute;te and on oferdrince, xii. 514, 10. Leahtras . . . ðæt is &aelig-acute;r&aelig-acute;tas and oferdruncennessa, Wlfst. 135, 2. Wið &aelig-acute;r&aelig-acute;tas, 290, 32.
&aelig-acute;r-beþóht; adj. Premeditated:--Hwæðer ðe gewealdes ðe unge&dash-uncertain;wealdes, hwæðer ðe f&aelig-acute;rlíce ðe þurh &aelig-acute;rbeþóhte wísan, Ll. Th. ii. 428, 12.
ærc a chest. v. earc: ærce archbishop's pallium, v. arce in Dict.
ærce-biscop. Add:--Arcebiscop archiepiscopus, Wrt. Voc. i. 42, 3. Hér forðférde Sigeríc arcebisceop, Chr. 994; P. 126, 10. Ærcebiscepes (erce-, v. l.) burhbryce .xc. sci&l-bar;&l-bar;., Ll. Th. i. 88, 7. Gif mon beforan ærcebiscepe gefeohte, 70, 18. Ic geliornode æt mínum ærcebiscepe, Past. 7, 21: Chr. 601; P. 20, 21. Ercebis&c-tilde;, 625; P. 24, 5.
ærcebiscop-dóm, es; m. Archiepiscopal dignity, archbishopric:--Æfter him féng Mellitus tó arce&b-bar;dóme (ercebiscopdóme, 23, 27), Chr. 616; P. 24, 2.
ærcebiscop-ríce. v. arcebiscop-ríce in Dict.
ærcebiscop-stól, es; m. Archiepiscopal see:--Æfter him féng Mellitus tó arce&b-bar;stóle, Chr. 616; P. 22, 37: 988; P. 125, 16. Hé gesæt his arce&b-bar;stól inthronizatur cathedra archipresulatus sui, 1048; P. 172, 4.
ærce-diácon. Add:--Arcedeácon (-diácon), Gr. D. 186, 21. Ðæs arcedeácnes innoþ, 187, 3. Arcediácones geban, Ll. Th. ii. 290, 24. Archidiácones, Shrn. 115, 31. Sumne ercediácon, Hml. S. 29, 213. v. erce-diácon in Dict.
ærce-hád. v. erce-hád in Dict.
ærce-ríce, es; n. Archbishopric:--Se cyng sealde Rótbearde ðæt arceríce, Chr. 1051; P. 170, 31.
ærce-stól, es; m. Archiepiscopal see:--Ælfeáh féng tó ðám ærcestóle, Chr. 1006; P. 136, 8. Arcestóle, 988; P. 125, 24. Wæs Dúnstán æt ðám ercestóle, Hml. S. 21, 458. Hé heóld ðone arcestól mid mycclan weorðmynte, Chr. 1069; P. 204, 11.
&aelig-acute;r-d&aelig-acute;d. Add:--Hú micel is ðæt wíte ðe byð for &aelig-acute;rd&aelig-acute;dum . . . cyningc wile déman ánra gehwylcum be &aelig-acute;rd&aelig-acute;dum quanta malis maneant tormenta . . . adveniet judex mercedem reddere cunctis, Dóm. L. 93, 96: Wlfst. 137, 1, 3.
&aelig-acute;r-dæg, II. Add:--Se cyning ne gemunde ðára monigra teónena ðe hiora &aelig-acute;gðer óþrum on &aelig-acute;rdagum (dudum) gedyde, Ors. 1, 12; S. 52, 23. Ðá burg, seó wæs on &aelig-acute;rdagum heora ieldrena éðel urbem, auctorem originis suae, 4, 5; S. 168, 10.
-&aelig-acute;re -oared, in cmpds.:--&AElig-acute;nne scegð .lxiiii. &aelig-acute;re, Cht. Crw. 23, 8. [Icel. -ærr.]
&aelig-acute;-reáfe. v. &aelig-acute;-r&aelig-acute;fe.
&aelig-acute;ren. Add: I. brazen:--&AElig-acute;ren ceác, Past. 105, 2. &AElig-acute;renu elebyt lenticula, Wrt. Voc. ii. 50, 75. &AElig-acute;ren byt, i. 25, 17. Aeren screop strigillus, ii. 121, 41. Ásleah .iiii. scearpan mid &aelig-acute;cenan (&aelig-acute;renan?) brande, Lch. iii. 52, 2. &AElig-acute;renne bogan arcum aeneum, Ps. Th. 17, 33. &AElig-acute;nne &aelig-acute;renne oxan, Hml. S. 30, 421. Áne &aelig-acute;rene anlícnysse, Hml. Th. ii. 166, 2. &AElig-acute;rne, Bl. H. 239, 21. Gyldene, sylfrene, &aelig-acute;rene, cyperene, Ors. 5, 2; S. 216, 3. Ðá &aelig-acute;renan scyttelas, Bl. H. 85, 7. Ðá érnan, Ps. Srt. 106, 16. II. sounding as brass, tinkling(?):--Tinnulus, a tinniendo dicitur, id est eran (=&aelig-acute;ren?), Wrt. Voc. ii. 122, 45. [O. H. Ger. érín.]
&aelig-acute;ren-byt. l. &aelig-acute;ren byt. v. &aelig-acute;ren: &aelig-acute;rend. v. &aelig-acute;rende.
&aelig-acute;ren-dæg. l. &aelig-acute;ran dæg. v. &aelig-acute;r; adj.
&aelig-acute;rend-bóc. Add:--&AElig-acute;rendbéc pi(c)tacia (cf. &aelig-acute;rendgewritu, An. Ox. 4839), Wrt. Voc. ii. 86, 53.
&aelig-acute;rende. Add: I. a message:--Mycel wæs ðes &aelig-acute;rendwreca, and mycel &aelig-acute;rende bróhte hé, Bl. H. 9, 13. Ðíslic &aelig-acute;rende se pápa onsende and ðás word cwæð, 205, 22. Hé geswór ðæt hé ðæt &aelig-acute;rende ábeódan wolde . . . Æfter hé hit áboden h&aelig-acute;fde, hé hié heálsade ðæt hié nánuht ðára &aelig-acute;renda ne underfénge . . . Ás&aelig-acute;don his geféran hú hé heora &aelig-acute;renda ábeád, Ors. 4, 6; S. 178, 10-22. Earmra manna &aelig-acute;rende wrecan (&aelig-acute;rendo ábeódan, v. l.), Bd. 3, 6; Sch. 209, 20. &AElig-acute;rende wreccan legationem volvere, 2, 9; Sch. 146, 25. Se ealdormon geliéfedlíce ðára &aelig-acute;renda anféng, Ors. 3, 1; S. 96, 20. Hieówsiende for ðám &aelig-acute;rendum ðe se wítga him s&aelig-acute;de, Ps. Th. 50, arg. Sóna swá se hálga man ðás &aelig-acute;rendu gehýrde (quo audito), Gr. D. 29, 14. Geatweard ðe mid gesceáde cunne andswara syllan and &aelig-acute;renda underfón, R. Ben. 126, 16. Ðurh Nóðhelmes &aelig-acute;renda and gesægene (cf. hé mé ealle . . . onsende ðurh Nóðhelm, l. 2), Bd. pref.; S. 472, 8. II. an errand, a mission:--Gif hwelc ríce mon on his hláfordes &aelig-acute;rende færþ, cymþ ðonne on ælþeódig folc si quis multiplici consulatu functus in barbaras nationes devenerit, Bt. 27, 3; F. 98, 21. Ðá hwíle ðe hé fór on heora &aelig-acute;rende, Chr. 1064; P. 192, 6. Fór Aldred ofer s&aelig-acute; ðæs kynges &aelig-acute;rende, 1054; P. 185, 24: 1065; P. 193, 11. Medmycel &aelig-acute;rende wé ðyder habbað, and ús is þearf ðæt wé hit þéh gefyllon, Bl. H. 233, 11. S&aelig-acute;don ðæt hí hæfdon nyt &aelig-acute;rende (&aelig-acute;rend, v. l.) and nytne intingan sumne haberent aliquid legationis et causae utilis, Bd. 5, 10; Sch. 600, 9.
&aelig-acute;rend-fæst; adj. Bound on an errand:--Férde sum &aelig-acute;rendfæst ridda . . . and l&aelig-acute;dde hit forð mid him ð&aelig-acute;r hé fundode tó, Hml. S. 26, 221.
&aelig-acute;rend-gewrit. Add:--&AElig-acute;rendgewrit commonitorium, Wrt. Voc. ii. 22, 33. Án &aelig-acute;rendgewrit of Lædene on Englisc áreccean, Past. 3, 15. Sumes geréfan dohtor hé áhredde fram fefore þurh his &aelig-acute;rendgewrit, Hml. Th. ii. 512, 9. &AElig-acute;rendgewrite pittacia, Wrt. Voc. ii. 67, 21. Pitaciolis, i. membranulis bócfellum, &aelig-acute;rendgewritum, An. Ox. 4570.
&aelig-acute;rendian. Add: I. to go on an errand (acc.), act as emissary or advocate in a matter:--Se munuc ðe hit &aelig-acute;rendode the monk that had been sent on this business, Gr. D. 29, 28. Gif hwelc forworht monn bitt úrne hwelcne ðæt wé hine l&aelig-acute;den tó sumum rícum menn and him geðingien, . . . Gif hé mé cúð ne bið, ic wille him cueðan: 'Ne mæg ic ðæt &aelig-acute;rendigean (&aelig-acute;rendian, Cott. MSS.)' si quis veniat, ut pro se ad intercedendum nos apud potentem quempiam virum, qui nobis est incognitus, ducat, protinus respondemus: 'Ad intercedendum venire non possumus,' Past. 63, 5. I a. to go on an errand to (tó) a person:--Ðá sende hé monn tó ð&aelig-acute;m arcebisceope and tó Eádberhte, and him héht sæcgan ðæt hé wilnade ðæs londes. Ðá se ærcebisceop and Eádberht hit w&aelig-acute;run &aelig-acute;rndiende tó cyninge when they were advocating the matter to the king, Cht. Th. 47, 30. II. to go on an errand for a person (dat.) to (tó) another, intercede:--Grípan on ðá scíre ðæt hé &aelig-acute;rendige óðrum monnum tó Gode apud Deum intercessionis locum pro populo arripere, Past. 63, 7: Gen. 665. III. to go on a mission for an object (gen.), negotiate for:--Ðá &aelig-acute;renddracan ðe his cwale &aelig-acute;rendedon (-odon, &aelig-acute;rnddedon, v. ll.) those who had been sent to procure his death,
&AElig-acute;REND-RACA--ÆSCEN 19
Bd. 2, 12; Sch. 160, 23. III a. with dat. of person for whom:--Se esne ðe &aelig-acute;rendað his woroldhláforde wífes the servant who is sent to procure a wife for his lord, Past. 143, 1. [He bad heom arndien him to þan kingen, Lay. 23315. Ernde me to þi lauerd funde preces ad dominum, Kath. 2127.] v. ge-&aelig-acute;rendian.
&aelig-acute;rend-raca. Add:--Yldest &aelig-acute;rendraca a responsis, i. magister responsorum, Wrt. Voc. i. 60, 33. Hé ðæs &aelig-acute;rendes &aelig-acute;rendraca wæs from Alexandre, Ors. 3, 11; S. 144, 22. Swifte &aelig-acute;rendracan veltes, Wrt. Voc. i. 18, 23. &AElig-acute;rendracum gerulis, An. Ox. 7, 281. &AElig-acute;renddracan, Past. 39, 3: Bd. 2, 12; Sch. 160, 22.
&aelig-acute;rend-scip, es; n. A small boat, a skiff:--&AElig-acute;rendscip scapha, Wrt. Voc. i. 63, 31.
ærend-secgan. Dele: &aelig-acute;rend-spræc. l. -spr&aelig-acute;c.
&aelig-acute;rendung. Substitute: I. carrying a message, acting as an emisary:--Gif hwylc bróðor gedyrstl&aelig-acute;cð ðæt hé &aelig-acute;nige geþeódr&aelig-acute;dene nime wið ðone ámánsumedan, oðþe þurh &aelig-acute;nige spr&aelig-acute;ce oðþe þurh &aelig-acute;niges óþres mannes &aelig-acute;rendunge (by any other man's carrying a message), R. Ben. 50, 13. II. a message, an errand:--Ðæt wæs hræd &aelig-acute;rendraca; sé tylode tó secganne hys &aelig-acute;rndunge &aelig-acute;r ðon ðé hé lyfde, Shrn; 95, 21. [&THORN-bar; we þurh hire erndunge (intercession, mediation) moten iseon hire, Marh. 23, 16: O. E. Homl. i. 207, 31.]
&aelig-acute;rend-wreca. Add:--&AElig-acute;rendwreca(n) unnytnesse nugigerelus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 60, 31. Gabriel wæs ðissa brýdþinga &aelig-acute;rendwreca, Bl. H. 3, 19. Érendwrica legatus, Txts. 180, 10. Philippes tíd ðæs apostoles and ðæs Godes &aelig-acute;rendwrecan, Shrn. 78, 4. Ærendwreocan, 108, 14. Ðá sende hé his &aelig-acute;rendwreocan tó Wulfhearde, Cht. Th. 47, 9. Érendwrecan legati, Ps. Srt. 67, 32. Ðá kyningas Gode and his &aelig-acute;rendwrecum hérsumedon, Past. 3, 6. God sendeþ his engla gástas tó &aelig-acute;rendwrecum, Bl. H. 203, 14. v. wrecan, I b in Dict.
&aelig-acute;rend-wreccan (?); p. wrehte To deliver a message:--Ðá eóde hé in swá swá hé his hláfordes &aelig-acute;rende secgan sceolde; and mid ðý hé ðá geswippre múþe líccetende &aelig-acute;rend (&aelig-acute;rende, v. l.) wrehte (&aelig-acute;rendwrehte?) intravit quasi nuntium domini sui referens; et cum simulatam legationem ore astuto volveret, Bd. 2, 9; Sch. 146, 23.
&aelig-acute;r-gedón. Add:--Dryhten hine ðreáde for his &aelig-acute;rgedónum weorcum, Past. 443, 27. Ðá ðe ðá &aelig-acute;rgedónan synna wépað, 177, 23.
&aelig-acute;r-gefremed; adj. Before-committed:--Ðá &aelig-acute;rgefremedan synna, Ll. Th. ii. 434, 14.
&aelig-acute;r-gel&aelig-acute;red; adj. Previously instructed:--&AElig-acute;rgeléred praemonita, Mt. L. 14, 8.
&aelig-acute;r-genemned. Add:--Ealle ðá &aelig-acute;rgenemnedan l&aelig-acute;cedómas, Lch. ii. 186, 11.
&aelig-acute;r-gescod. l. &aelig-acute;r gescód, and see ge-sceþþan.
&aelig-acute;r-glæd. Substitute: Kind from of old?, very kind:--Eów mihtig God miltse gecýððe &aelig-acute;rglade to you mighty God hath shewn mercy exceeding kind, Exod. 293. v. next word.
&aelig-acute;r-gód. Substitute: Good from of old?, very good. v. exs. in Dict., and cf. (?) O. Sax. ér-þungan.
&aelig-acute;r-hwílum; adv. In earlier times, formerly:--Ðá micclan welan ðe hig &aelig-acute;rhwílon áhton, Guth. 14, 23. Oft ic nú miscyrre cúðe spr&aelig-acute;ce, and þeáh uncúðre &aelig-acute;rhwílum (quondam) fond, Met. 2, 9. Cf. &aelig-acute;r-dæg.
&aelig-acute;r-ildo (?); f. Former age:--&AElig-acute;ryeldo antisitus (but the Latin in Ald. 152, 31 is ante situm), Wrt. Voc. ii. 91, 19. &AElig-acute;reldo anteritus (has the glosser read anteritas?), 5, 52.
&aelig-acute;ring. Add:--On &aelig-acute;ring mane, Mk. L. 13, 35. On &aelig-acute;ringe diluculo, 1, 35.
&aelig-acute;-rist. Add: es; n.:--Se drihtenlica &aelig-acute;rist anastasis dominica, An. Ox. 2753. Seó wunderlice &aelig-acute;rest eallum mannum wæs geopenod, Shrn. p. 6. Ðæt gem&aelig-acute;nelice &aelig-acute;rist, Hml. Th. i. 394, 25. Mínes &aelig-acute;ristes dæg, 74, 18: ii. 224, 25. Ðone tóhopan deádra monna &aelig-acute;ristes (-restes, Hatt. MS.) . . . Ðá Saducie andsacedon ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;riste . . . ðá Fariséos geliéfdon ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;riste, Past. 364, 4-6. On ðám &aelig-acute;riste. Mt. 22, 28-30: Mk. 12, 23: Lk. 20, 33: Hml. Th. i. 394, 32. Æfter ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;riste, Ps. Th. 47, arg. [O. H. Ger. ur-rist resurrectio.] v. eft-&aelig-acute;rist.
&aelig-acute;r-leóf; adj. Very dear:--[Æ]rl[e]óf gratus, An. Ox. 56, 296.
&aelig-acute;r-lic, -líce. v. ár-lic, -líce.
&aelig-acute;r-lyft, e; f. The air of early morning:--Sió þicce &aelig-acute;rlyft gravis, Wrt. Voc. ii. 41, 74.
&aelig-acute;r-morgen. Add:--Diluculum, ðæt is se &aelig-acute;rmærien (-mergen, v. l.), betweox ðám dægrede and sunnan upgange, Lch. iii. 244, 6. Se &aelig-acute;r-merigen wæs fram Adam oð Nóe, Hml. Th. ii. 74, 18. Gewordenum ðám &aelig-acute;rmergene mane facto, Gr. D. 72, 11. &AElig-acute;rmergenne, 201, 25. From &aelig-acute;rmorgenne oð heáne undern, R. Ben. 74, 10. From &aelig-acute;rmergenne (-morgene, MS. E.), Chr. 538; P. 16, 12. &AElig-acute;rmergen mane, Wrt. Voc. Ii. 58, 65. On &aelig-acute;rmergen, Ps. Th. 5, 3. On &aelig-acute;rmorgenum in matutinis, Ps. L. 72, 14. v. ærne-mergen, ár-morgen in Dict.
&aelig-acute;r-morgenlic (ár-); adj. Of the early morning:--Ármorgenlic auroram, Rtl. 182, 37. Ármorgenlicum tídum matutinis horis, 124, 15. v. &aelig-acute;rne-mergenlic.
ærn. Add: [older ræn. v. ærn-þegen]:--Gif ealo áwerd sié, genim elehtran, lege on ðá feówer sceátas ðæs ærnes and ofer ðá duru and under ðone þerxwold and under ðæt ealofæt, Lch. ii. 142, 11. Healde hine mon on óðrum ærne (húse, v. l.), Ll. Th. i. 64, 15: Bl. H. 221, 16. Seó reáde netele ðe þurh ærne in wyxð, Lch. iii. 52, 12. Genim grun&dash-uncertain;deswyligean ðá ðe on ærenu wexeð, 48, 29. v. bæþ-, beód-, geréf-, hálig-, mete-, mót-, sealt-, spr&aelig-acute;c-, stál-, wæsc-, wíte-ærn; tigel-ærne: earn in Dict.
ærnan. Add: v. ymb-ærnan: ærne. v. tigel-ærne: &aelig-acute;r-nemd. v. &aelig-acute;r-nemned.
&aelig-acute;rne. l. &aelig-acute;rne-mergen, -morgen early morning:--Cl&aelig-acute;nnyss sý swá swá &aelig-acute;rnemergen (diluculum), Hy. Srt. 16, 27. Diluculum, ðæt is se &aelig-acute;rnemergen, Lch. iii. 244, 6. Se dæg hæfð þreó tód&aelig-acute;lednyssa. . . . Seó forme hátte mane, ðæt ys &aelig-acute;rnemergen, . . . seó niht hafað seofon tó&dash-uncertain;d&aelig-acute;lednyssa . . . seó seofoðe ys . . . diluculum, ðæt ys &aelig-acute;rnemergen, Angl. viii. 319, 21, 34. From &aelig-acute;rnemorgen oð undern, R. Ben. 74, 10. Fram &aelig-acute;rnemærien oð ofer midne dæg, Hml. S. 3, 341. On &aelig-acute;rnemærgen (-merien, v. l.), 344. On &aelig-acute;rnemergen primo mane, Coll. M. 20, 29. On ealne &aelig-acute;rnemergen, Chr. 1050; P. 170, 14. On &aelig-acute;rnemorgen (&aelig-acute;rmergen, -morgen, v. ll.) mane primo, Bd. 5, 6; Sch. 578, 23.
&aelig-acute;rnemergen-lic; adj. Of the early morning:--Mæssan &aelig-acute;rnemergen&dash-uncertain;lice missam matutinalem, Angl. xiii. 384, 277. v. &aelig-acute;r-morgenlic.
&aelig-acute;r-nemned; adj. Before-named:--Se &aelig-acute;rnæmda cyning, Ll. Th. i. 36, 8.
ærning. Add:--'Hwæt ðú mé mycel yfel dést mid ðínre ærninge.' And ic nóht ðon &aelig-acute;r ð&aelig-acute;re ærninge blon 'quam magnum vae facis mihi sic equitando.' Et ego nihilominus coeptis institi vetitis, Bd. 5, 6; Sch. 576, 19. Mid swíðe geswenctan horse for ærninge vehementer equo in cursu fatigato, Gr. D. 38, 30. v. f&aelig-acute;r-ærning.
ærn-þegen, es; m. The officer of a house:--Rendegn aeditus, templi vel aedis minister, Txts. 109, 1137.
&aelig-acute;ror. Add: (1) temporal, earlier, before:--Nán mann &aelig-acute;ror nán swylc ne gemunde, Chr. 1032; P. 159, 5. &AElig-acute;rer hé hit &aelig-acute;r&aelig-acute;rde, 1086; P. 219, 4. Swá swá wé áwriton &aelig-acute;ror, Ælfc. T. Grn. 4, 15. (2) rather:--Ðaacute; óðre þrý godspelleras áwriton &aelig-acute;ror be Crístes menniscnysse, Hml. Th. i. 70. 3.
&aelig-acute;rra. Add:--Ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;rran prioris, An. Ox. 1675: Hml. Th. i. 62, 16. Tó ðám &aelig-acute;rrum in pristinum, An. Ox. 1831: Hml. Th. i. 68, 19. On &aelig-acute;rron dæg nudiustertius, Ælfc. Gr. 224, 2. On his ðæt &aelig-acute;rre mynster in primum suum monasterium. Bd. 5, 19; S. 641, 17. Ðæt (what) &aelig-acute;rran woroldwitan ger&aelig-acute;ddon, Ll. Th. i. 350, 6.
&aelig-acute;rst, ærþe-land, ærþling. v. &aelig-acute;r; adv. III, irþ-land, irþling.
&aelig-acute;r-wacol. Add:--Se apostol &aelig-acute;rwacol tó ð&aelig-acute;re cyrcan com, Hml. Th. i. 74, 20.
&aelig-acute;s. Add: (1) food:--Áwyrpað his líc fugelum tó &aelig-acute;se and hundum tó mete, Hml. S. 37, 235. Næs se here swá strang ðæt on Angelcynne &aelig-acute;s him gefetede, Chr. 975; P. 121, 12. (2) a bait:--Ðá getímode ðám deófle swá swá déð ðám gr&aelig-acute;digan fisce, ðe gesihð ðæt &aelig-acute;s, and ne gesihð ðone angel ðe on ðám &aelig-acute;se sticað: bið ðonne gr&aelig-acute;dig ðæs &aelig-acute;ses, and forswylcð ðone angel mid ðám &aelig-acute;se, Hml. Th. i. 216, 9-13. Angel vel &aelig-acute;s ic (the fisherman) wyrpe, Coll. M. 23, 11. Fugel, ðonne hé gífre bið, hé gesihð ðæt &aelig-acute;s (escam) on eorðan, and ðonne for ð&aelig-acute;m luste ðæs metes hé forgiet ðæt grin, Past. 331, 17.
æsc. Add: I. ash-tree (v. C. D. vi. 252-3 for the large number of place-names in which æsc occurs):--Æsces sceal m&aelig-acute;st there must be most of ash, Lch. ii. 86, 8. IV. a ship:--Aesc cercilus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 103, 56. Æsc cercylus, 14, 16. Ðá Deniscan leóde on Norðhymbra lande gelendon mid æscum, Hml. S. 32, 31. v. ceaster-æsc.
æ-scære. l. &aelig-acute;-sc&aelig-acute;re.
&aelig-acute;scan to demand:--And ðæt ceápgild áríse á ofer .xxx. pæn&g-tilde; oð healf pund syþþan wé hit &aelig-acute;scað, Ll. Th. i. 234, 16.
&aelig-acute;-scapo. v. &aelig-acute;-sceap.
&aelig-acute;sce. Add: I. question, inquiry:--Uton áhsien úrne Drihten . . . Wé gehýraþ æfter ðisse &aelig-acute;scan (-ean, v. l.) (post hanc interrogationem) Drihten andswariendne, R. Ben. 3, 16. Hé angan tó befrínenne . . . Hé wearð æfter ðysse &aelig-acute;scan ontend, Lch. iii. 432, 29. Ðá áxunga ð&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;scan tówríðende interrogationi interrogationem jungens, Hml. S. 23 b, 495. II. as a legal term, search for stolen cattle:--Beó sý &aelig-acute;sce forð let the search go on, Ll. Th. i. 234, 17: 238, 9. Ðæt man ne forl&aelig-acute;te náne &aelig-acute;scan, 232, 18: 234, 25. Fó sé syþþan tó ðe ðæt land áge and hæbbe him ðá &aelig-acute;scan, 352, 17.
&aelig-acute;-sceáda, an; m. Bran:--Healmes láf stipulae, ceaf palea, &aelig-acute;scéda migma, Wrt. Voc. i. 38, 51-3. &AElig-acute;sceádan furfures, purgamentum farinae, ii. 152, 4. Cf. á-sceádan.
&aelig-acute;-sceap, es; n. What is cut off, a remnant, patch:--Ðæt ésceapa commissura, Lk. L. 5, 36. &AElig-acute;scapo subsiciva, Wrt. Voc. i. 287, 34. v. scip a patch.
æsceda. v. &aelig-acute;-sceáda: æsce-geswáp. v. sw&aelig-acute;pa in Dict.
æscen. Substitute: f., m. or n. A (wooden) vessel, pail, bottle [v. ashen; sb. in D. D.]:--Æscen lagena, Wrt. Voc. i. 25, 8. Arn án wencel mid treówenum æscene (treówene æscne, v. l.) (lignea situla), Gr. D. 11, 21. Of ðám æscene ðe is óðre namon hrygilebúc gecleopad . . . and of ðám óðran æscene, Cht. Th. 439, 25, 29. Man sceal habban trogas, æscena, Angl. ix. 264, 15. v. next word.
20 ÆSCEN -- ÆT
æscen; adj. Add: -- Genim grénne æscenne stæf, Lch. ii. 42, 10.
æscene vastaretur, An. Ox. 37, 4 [ = ? &aelig-acute;-scefe; cf. (?) scafan: O. H. Ger. ar-scaban eradere].
æsc-fealu; adj. Ashy-coloured: -- Æscfealu vel æscgr&aelig-acute;g cinereus, deterrimus color. Wrt. Voc. ii. 131, 14.
æsc-gr&aelig-acute;g; adj. Ashy-grey. v. preceding word: æschetung, Hpt. 510, 66. v. ceahhetung.
æsc-man. Add: -- Andlang streámes æt æscmannes yre (yfre?), C. D. vi. 100, 7. Æscmen piratici, Wrt. Voc. ii. 68, 13.
æsc-stéde, -þræc. l. æsc-stede, -þracu.
æscstede-ród, e; f. A cross marking a battlefield ? :-- Of dære greátan apeldre on æscstederóde, C. D. iii. 135, 22.
æsc-þrote. Add: -- Aescthrotae ferula, Txts. 64, 450. Æscþrote, Wrt. Voc. ii. 38, 78: furula, 35, 29: firula, i. 67, 80: ferula, i. harundo, virgula vel nomen holeris, ii. 147, 70. Æscþrotu annuosa ( = anchusa. v. Lch. ii. 368), i. 30, 52. Niþeweard æscþrotu, Lch. ii. 36, 19.
&aelig-acute;-sellend, es; m. A law-giver :-- Se m&aelig-acute;ra &aelig-acute;syllend Móyses, Hml. A. 24, 13. &AElig-acute;sellend legislatorem, Ps. L. 9, 21. v. &aelig-acute;-syllend in Dict.
&aelig-acute;-slítend, es; m. A law-breaker :-- &AElig-acute;slítendras praevaricantes, Ps. L. 118, 119, 158.
&aelig-acute;-smæl a contraction of the pupil of the eye :-- Wiþ &aelig-acute;smælum and wiþ eallum eágna wærce, Lch. ii. 338, 1 : 2, 9 : 36, 16, 19.
&aelig-acute;-smogu; pl. n. The slough of a snake; exuviae :-- Sceal mon n&aelig-acute;dran &aelig-acute;smogu seóþan on ele, Lch. ii. 236, 4. v. in-smoh.
æspe aspen. Add :-- Aespe arbutus, Txts. 41, 202. Aespe aespae, espe tremulus, 103, 2048. Æspe, Wrt. Voc. i. 285, 36. Tó ð&aelig-acute;re gemearcodan æfsan, C. D. v. 195, 11.
æspe abies, v. æbs.
æsp-hangra, an; m. An aspen wood :-- On ðonæ æsphangran, C. D. v. 173, 11. v. hangra.
&aelig-acute;-(eá-)spryng, -sprynge; m. f. (?): -spring; n. I. source, fountain, spring :-- Oft &aelig-acute;springe út áwealleð . . hé siðþan tósceáden wyrð, Met. 5, 12. Wæs se &aelig-acute;spring (sió &aelig-acute;spryng, Hatt. MS. ) sió sóðe lufu, Past. 48, 12. Gif wé ðone biteran wille æt ð&aelig-acute;m &aelig-acute;sprynge forwyrcean, 307,1. Ealle ðás gód cumaþ of ðám &aelig-acute;sprenge Godes mildheortnesse, Bl. H. 29, 11. Ðá gemétton hí eáspryng (&aelig-acute;sprincg), Gr. D. 129, 4. Cúðberihtus án &aelig-acute;spring (eá-, v. l.) of drígre eorðan wæs gel&aelig-acute;dende, Bd. 4, 28; Sch. 518, 2. Of éspryngum de fontibus. Ps. Srt. 67, 27. II. departure, defection, v. á-springan, II :-- N&aelig-acute;nig ðæs fród leofað ðæt his (the sun's) mæge &aelig-acute;springe witan, hú geond grund færeð goldtorht sunne in ðæt wonne genip under wætra geþring. Sch. 77.
&aelig-acute;stel. l. æstel; Wrt. Voc. i. 81, 23 : Ælfc. Gr. Z. 31, 9.
æ-swáp. v. sw&aelig-acute;pa in Dict., and An. Ox. 608: 4155.
&aelig-acute;-swíc ; m. l. &aelig-acute;-swic; n., dele [&aelig-acute; law . . .] and add: -- Néd is cumende &aelig-acute;swic (scandala) ; hweþre þonne wá þ&aelig-acute;m menn þe þurh hine &aelig-acute;swic (scandalum) cymeþ, Mt. R. 18, 7. &AElig-acute;swice, wróhte insimulatione, .i. acussatione, An. Ox. 4842. Hé symble ús ætstandeþ tó &aelig-acute;swice ad decipiendum semper assistat. Gr. D. 221, 15. In éswic in scandalum, Ps. Srt. 105, 36. [O. H. Ger. á-suih scandalum.]
&aelig-acute;-swíca. l. -swica, and add: -- &AElig-acute;swica desertor, seductor, Wrt. Voc. ii. 139, 12. Ðæt hé w&aelig-acute;re leás drý and scyldig &aelig-acute;swica, Bl. H. 175, 8. Hé ongan hine cígan &aelig-acute;swica (impostorem). Gr. D. 200, 13. Þára &aelig-acute;swicena gástas apostatas spiritus, 304, 28.
&aelig-acute;-swic[c] ; adj. Apostate :-- Ðá &aelig-acute;swiccan gástas apostatas spiritus, Gr. D. 304, 28.
&aelig-acute;-swice, es; m. Failure in the keeping of the law :-- Þurh lahbrycas and &aelig-acute;swicas, Wlfst. 164, 3.
&aelig-acute;-swícian. l. -swician, and add: I. to desert :-- Ic ðé n&aelig-acute;fre ne &aelig-acute;swicige. Hml. Th. ii. 246, 2. Ealle gé mé &aelig-acute;swiciað, 244, 33. II. to be apostate :-- &AElig-acute;swician apostatare, Wrt. Voc. ii. 3, 2. III. to offend :-- Gif honde ðíne &aelig-acute;swicæþ ðec . . gif eágan ðín &aelig-acute;swiceþ ðec, Mt. R. 18, 8, 9. Sé &aelig-acute;swicað óðrum ðc hine on Godes d&aelig-acute;le beswícð, Hml. Th. i. 514, 18. Gif ðín hand þé &aelig-acute;swicige, 516, 4. Ðe l&aelig-acute;s wé hí &aelig-acute;swicion, 512, 2. v. ge-&aelig-acute;swician.
&aelig-acute;-swicness, e ; f. Offence :-- On &aelig-acute;swicnesse in scandalum, Ps. L. 105, 36.
&aelig-acute;-swícung. l. -swicung, and add: I. seduction, deceit :-- Álýs ús from deóflicum costnungum and fram eallum &aelig-acute;swicungum unrihtwísra wyrhtena, Hml. S. 11, 42. II. sedition :-- Folcslite vel &aelig-acute;swicung seditio. Wrt. Voc. i. 21, 30. III. offence :-- &AElig-acute;swicung scandalum, Ps. L. 48, 14. 'Mannes bearn . . gegaderað of his ríce ealle &aelig-acute;swicunga.' On ðám upplican ríce is heálic sib, and ð&aelig-acute;r ne bið nán &aelig-acute;swicung gemét, Hml. Th. ii. 562, 24. Wá middangearde for &aelig-acute;swicungum . . Neód is ðæt &aelig-acute;swicunga cumon, i. 514, 33: 516, 1. Intinga &aelig-acute;swicunga (scandalorum), R. Ben. I. 115, 4. Æswicunga (scandala) hí fédað, 109, 17 Ne ástyra ðú &aelig-acute;swicunga ánigum men on lífe, Hex. 44, 27.
&aelig-acute;-swind inert, sluggish :-- Ésuind, ásolcen iners, Wrt. Voc. ii. 111, 27. &AElig-acute;swind, 45, 50. v. á-swindan.
æt. Add: A. prep. followed by a case. I. with dat. (1) temporal, at :-- Æt ð&aelig-acute;m ýtmestan dæge, Bl. H. 51, 8. Æt þisse ilcan tíde, 91, 14. Æt twám cierrun and æt ð&aelig-acute;m þriddan cierre, Ors. 5, 7; S. 228, 28. (l a) where the time is fixed by an occurrence or a condition :-- Æt orwénum lífe in extremitate vitae, Ll. Th. ii. 170, 18. Gif æt þirsa UNCERTAIN misd&aelig-acute;da hwelcere se hund losige, i. 78, 5. Gif his mon getilað æt ð&aelig-acute;re yfelan w&aelig-acute;tan (when the evil humour is present), Lch. ii. 240, 18. Æt &aelig-acute;nigre neóde, Wlfst. 171, 11. Lofsang æt ðám wundrum singan, Hml. S. 21, 246. (1 b) with absolute dat. (cf. similar use in Gothic and Icelandic) :-- Æt þám gewordenan &aelig-acute;fne, Nic. 10, 36. (2) local (a) where there is motion to an object :-- Hié héton Ióhannes æt his mynstre gebrengan, Ors. 6, 10; S. 264, 21: Bt. 7, 3; F. 22, 1. Æt hám gebring, Lch. ii. 292, 25. (b) motion from :-- Se sceocca sceall ásw&aelig-acute;man æt ús, . . . and Gríst hine ádr&aelig-acute;fð þæt hé ús derian ne mæge, Hml. S. 17, 203. (c) rest (α) marking point at which, object by or in contact with which something is placed :-- Hé geseah áne hl&aelig-acute;dre standan æt him . . . æt ð&aelig-acute;m uferran ende Dryhten hlinode, Past. 101, 19. Ðá gesáwon hí ð&aelig-acute;r monige men æt him beón (adfuisse), Bd. 3, 11; S. 536, 21. Hé ges&aelig-acute;ton æt mé (circa me), óþer æt mínum heáfde, óþer æt mínum fótum, 5, 13; S. 632, 35. Gegyred myd h&aelig-acute;ran æt hyre lýchaman, Shrn. 149, 20. ¶ in place-names :-- On ð&aelig-acute;r estówe ðe is cweden Æt twyfyrde, Bd. 4, 28; S. 606, 5. In loco qui uulgari dictione nuncupatur at Archet, C. D. ii. 213, 33. Kóka ealdormon tówearp ðá burg æt Hierusalem, Past. 311, 6. (β) marking person with whom or place at or in which a person resides :-- Ða beféng Ælfsige þone mann æt Wulfstáne, Cht. Th. 206, 23. Leófríc æt (who lived at) Hwítciricean . . . and Godwine æt Worðige, Chr. 1001; P. 132, 6, 8. Seó cyrice sceal fédan þá þe æt hire eardiaþ. Bl. H. 41, 28. (3) in various cases (a) marking object with which one is occupied :-- Hí æt láre w&aelig-acute;ron, Hml. S. 29, 10. Ic stande æt gebede, Ps. Th. 5, 3. Hé sæt æt þ&aelig-acute;m &aelig-acute;fengereordum, Bl. H. 73, 4. (b) marking person with whom another is brought into relation :-- Hé hæfde mycele gife æt his hláforde, Gen. 39, 4. Swá ús bið æt Gode, ðonne wé wið hine gesyngiað. Past. 425, 4. Hit stent on úrum dihte hú ús bið æt Gode gedémed, Hml. Th. i. 52, 32. (c) implying adhesion :-- Ealle ðá men þe æt þ&aelig-acute;re láre w&aelig-acute;ron þæt mon Pompeius ofslóg omnes interfectores Pompeii, Ors. 5, 12; S. 242, 23. Hé feóll mid eallum ðám englum ðe æt his r&aelig-acute;de w&aelig-acute;ron, Hex. 18, 3. (d) marking object on which action takes effect :-- Þonne áh se teónd áne swingellan æt him, Ll. Th. i. 132, 9. Wé magon beón nyttran æt him utilius apud eos proficimus, Past. 211, 21. Wé habbað gedón swá swá ús swutelung fram eów com æt ðám &b-bar;. Æðelnóðe, Cht. Th. 314, 2. Ðæt his fót æt stáne oþspurne. Bl. H. 29, 31. (e) marking object in respect to which some condition or circumstance is given, in the case of (a) of persons :-- Sé ðe scyldunga b&aelig-acute;de æt (in the case of) ofslagenum þeófe, Ll. Th. i. 204, 27. Be ordále æt þám mannum þe oft betihtlede w&aelig-acute;ron, 202, 24. (β) of things :-- Æt þám feówer tóðum fyrestum, æt gehwylcum, .vi. scillingas, Ll. Th. i. 16, 2, 14, 15 : 18, 17. Ic eom unscyldig æt þ&aelig-acute;re tihtlan, 180, 16. Ðæt hé feorh ne geséce æt openre þýfðe, 392, 3: 240, 30. Æt þýfðe gewita beón, 200, 20. Ealles folces þing byð þe betere æt þám þýfðum, 238, 20: 250, 5. Æt eallum slyht and æt ealre þ&aelig-acute;re hergunge and æt eallum þám hearmum. . . man eall onweig l&aelig-acute;te, 288, 1. Hwæt tó bóte mihte æt þ&aelig-acute;m f&aelig-acute;rcwealme, 270, 9: Cht. Th. 265, 10. Ðæt se mæssepreóst æt þám þingum (in illis rebus) þone bisceop áspelian móte, Ll. Th. ii. 176, 33. (f) marking source (α) at or from which something is got :-- Hé geceápade mid his feó æt þ&aelig-acute;m consule þæt. . . , Ors. 5, 7; S. 228, 15. Hwæt hæfst ðú æt þám gifum?, Bt. 13 ; F. 38, 4. Hé hine gebohte æt þám mannum, Gen. 39, 1: Hml. S. 29, 150. (β) at or from which something is sought, learnt, known, &c. :-- Leornige gehwá Godes beboda æt wísum láreówum, Hml, S. 12, 136. Hé undernam láre æt him, 29, 76. Hí ætgædere gel&aelig-acute;rede w&aelig-acute;ron æt Aristotolese sibi apud Aristotelem condiscipulum, Ors. 3, 9 ; S. 132, 2. Eówer blód ic ofgange æt wilddeórum and eác æt þám men, Gen. 9, 5. Ic ne mæg findan æt mé seolfum þæt ic hine geseó, Ors. 5, 12; S. 244, 1. (g) where there is contributory payment :-- Æt &aelig-acute;lcon sti&l-bar;&l-bar;, penig, Ll. Th. i. 226, 3. Æt heáfde peninc, æt sylh peninc, gesyfledne hláf &aelig-acute;t hreócendum heorðe, Wlfst. 170, 20. (h) with verbs of saving, redeeming, &c., from :-- Ðæt lond æt him álésan, Ors. 1. 10; S. 44, 9. Gyf hit man æt ðeófes hands áhret, Ll. Th. i. 226, 4. Hí áhreddon þæt cild æt þám wulfe, Hml. S. 30, 186. (i) marking object of which one is deprived :-- Gif hwylc man reáfige óðerne æt his dehter si homo quis alterum filia sua spoliaverit, Ll. Th. ii. 208, 7. Gif man beó æt his &aelig-acute;htan bereáfod, i. 286, 16: Gen. 43, 18: Ex. 32, 25. Hé hine ber&aelig-acute;dde æt þám ríce, Chr. 887; P. 80, 18. (j) marking source from which action proceeds :-- Hé wearð ácweald æt his witena handum, Hml. Th. i. 60, 4. Hí w&aelig-acute;ron gemartyrode æt þám mánfullan Nero, Hml. S. 29, 117. Heó wearð geh&aelig-acute;led æt þám apostole, 36, 264. II. with instrumental :-- Æt sume cierre, Past. 131, 12. III. with acc., marking limit. Cf. oþ. (1) temporal, until :-- Hé hit nó ne ylde æt nón, þonne hé tó middes dæges sceolde hám cuman, Gr. D. 206, 22. Seó is nú get æt þysne andweardan dæg mid wuldrum geweorþod, Bl. H. 125, 17. Ríneþ blódig regn æt &aelig-acute;fen, 91, 34: 93, 3. Eall eorþe bið mid þeóstrum oforþeaht æt þá endlyftan tíd, 93, 6. (2) local, unto, up to :-- Hí hine besencton on þá eá æt his cneówa, Bl. H. 43, 30. Geond ealle eorþan g&aelig-acute;þ heora swég, æt þá ýtmestan gem&aelig-acute;ro heora lár and heora
&AElig-acute;T -- ÆT-FORAN 21
word, 133, 35. Andlanges ð&aelig-acute;re díc æt ðæne ellenstyb, C. D. iii. 24, 3. B. adv. or without following case. (l) where there is motion to an object :-- Sé sé ðe swelc ne sié d&aelig-acute;r nó æt ne cume, Past. 59, 10. Ic eów cleopode tó mé, ac gé mé noldon æt cuman, 247, 21. (2) motion from :-- Eówerne gefeán eów nán mon æt ne genimð. Past. 187, 22. Wiþ ðæt beón æt ne fleón, Lch. i. 96, 25. (3) rest :-- Mid eallum his geféran ðe ðær æt w&aelig-acute;ron (qui aderant), Bd. l, 25; 8. 487, 7: Gr. D. 220, 6. Æt w&aelig-acute;ron úre bróþru, Bd. 4, 5; S. 572, 12. Ðé men ðe him æt w&aelig-acute;ron, 5, 5; S. 618, 6: Hml. S. 30, 144. Mé w&aelig-acute;ron æt manige men, Gr. D. 83, 13. Búton ic æt wese (adsim) eów. Coll. M. 28, 21. Ic bidde þæt þú æt sý mínum sangum, Lch. i. 308, 22. Ð&aelig-acute;m bréðer ðe him æt stód, Shrn. 64, 12: Bl. H. 149, 31. Ðá ðe mé æt s&aelig-acute;ton qui mihi adsederant, Bd. 5, 13 ; S. 633, 12. See also passages in Dictionary under æt-befón, -beón, -eom, -gebicgan, -gebrengan.
&aelig-acute;t. Add: I. food :-- Æt edulium, Wrt. Voc. ii. 29, 5. He &aelig-acute;tes ne gimde, Ælfc. T. Grn. 3, 16. Tó móse, &aelig-acute;te ad edulium, i. ad uescendum, An. Ox. 3762. Be &aelig-acute;te de cibo, Ll. Th. ii. 128, 20. Seó leó bringð his hwelpum hwæt tó etanne; hié gecýðað on ð&aelig-acute;m &aelig-acute;te . . . , Ors. 3, 11; S. 142, 25. Wurmum tó &aelig-acute;te, Wlfst. 145, 19. Hé tó micel nimð on &aelig-acute;te oððe on w&aelig-acute;te, Hml. S. 16, 270. &AElig-acute;t foresceáwian, Hml. Th. ii. 138, 35. Þú scealt þá óþre &aelig-acute;tas sellan, Lch. ii. 90, 12. See also passages under w&aelig-acute;t. II. eating :-- Be ðæs lambes &aelig-acute;te de agni esu, An. Ox. 40, 29. For æppla and hnuta &aelig-acute;te from the eating of apples and nuts, Lch. ii. 246, 91. Sé þe hine gelaðode tó &aelig-acute;te (ad manducandum), Gr. D. 128, 29. Swylce þá gebrocu þæs hláfes þurh þone &aelig-acute;t (per esum) weóxon, 252, 23. v. &aelig-acute;r-, fl&aelig-acute;sc-, un-&aelig-acute;t.
&aelig-acute;ta. Add: v. hláf-&aelig-acute;ta.
æt-beran. Add :-- To carry off :-- Swerie hé &thorn-bar; hé &aelig-acute;fre ne stele ne feoh ne ætbere, Ll. Th. i. 332, 21.
æt-berstan. Add: I. of actual motion, (l) absolute :-- Hé ætbærst and hé ys geworden né tó wealdgengan, Ælfc. T. Grn. 18, 5. Se here ætbærst, Chr. 992; P. 127, 17. Uneáþe cwic ætberstende, Coll. M. 27, 3. (2) when person from whom or place from which is given, (a) dat. :-- Hé heom ætbærst, Chr. 1052 ; P. 179, 21. (b) with adv. or prep. :-- Sé ætbærst ðanon, Chr. 605 ; P. 23, 10. N&aelig-acute;re &thorn-bar; hí on niht út ne ætburston of þ&aelig-acute;re byrig, 943; P. in, 17. (3) where direction, road, or manner of escape is given :-- His geféran mid fleáme ætburston, Hml. Th. ii. 248, II. Þá menn up ætberstan intó þ&aelig-acute;re byrig, Ll. Th. i. 286, 2. Þá hé ne ætburste on wætere, Chr. 1050 ; P. 167, 34. II. fig. (l) to escape, be free from the power of a person (dat.) :-- Ic ne mæg þám Almihtigan ætberstan on lífe oþþe on deáðe, Hml. S. 25, 100. (2) to escape, be safe from danger, evil, &c. (a) with dat. :-- Ne mæg nán ætberstan þám gem&aelig-acute;nelican deáðe, Hml. A. 54, 105. Sé þe wile synnum ætberstan, Scrd. 22, 43. (b) with acc. :-- Hí ætberstaþ frecnyssa evadunt pericula, Coll. M. 25, l. (3) of things, to be lost to a person (dat.) :-- Hit feoh him ætbyrst, Hml. S. 12, 85 : Wlfst. 142, 7. Ne ætberst þám bydele his geswinces edleán, Hml. Th. ii. 534, 16.
æt-bredan; &c. l. æt-bregdan, -brédan; p. -brægd, -br&aelig-acute;d, pl. -brugdon, -brúdon; pp. -brogden, -bróden, and add: To take away from (with dat. or with preps, of, fram) :-- Ætbr&aelig-acute;t detorsit, Germ. 397, 368. I. with idea of deprivation :-- God forgeaf ðá &aelig-acute;hta, and God hí eft ætbr&aelig-acute;d, Hml. Th. ii. 328, 30. Drihten mancynne ætbr&aelig-acute;d wuldor, þæt hé him wuldor forgeáfe, i. 578, 15. II. with idea of spoliation :-- Ic ætbréde vel ic forgrípe diripio, i. rapio, abstraho, eripio, Wrt. Voc. ii. 140, 48. Gif ic þurh unriht fácn &aelig-acute;nigum men áht ætbr&aelig-acute;d (abstuli), Ll. Th. ii. 136, 9. Hé ætbr&aelig-acute;d mé míne frumcennedan, and nú óðre síðe forstæl míne bletsunga, Gen. 27, 36. Hig ealle heora bigleofan ætbrúdon, Jud. 6, 4. Nele hé his &aelig-acute;hta him ætbrédan, Hml. Th. ii. 532, 21. Þá wyrta þe hé mid stale gewilnode tó ætbrédanne, Gr. D. 25, 16. Gif nýten byð ætbróden (caplum ab hostibus), Ex. 22, 10. Þá land þe ðá h&aelig-acute;ðenan ætbrodon hæfdon, Hml. S. 30, 307. Æt-bróden direpta, An. Ox. 3647. III. with idea of rescue :-- Ic ætbréde oððe áhredde eripio, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 168, 9. Sé ðe úre fæderas feóndum ætbr&aelig-acute;d, Hml. S. 19, 153. Þám þe hé þám deófle ætbr&aelig-acute;d, 29, 156. IV. with idea of seduction :-- &THORN-bar; hé ús fordó and ús Drihtne ætbréde, Hml. A. 5, 122. Þá Gode gebróhte þe se deófol ætbrédan wolde, Hml. S. 5, 24. V. with idea of withdrawal, abstention :-- Se wísdóm hine sylfne ætbrét fram módes híwunge. Hml. Th. ii. 326, 3. Hé hine ætbr&aelig-acute;d þám fl&aelig-acute;sclicum lustum, i. 58, 18. Hí ætbrúdon menn fram fl&aelig-acute;sclicum lustum, 576, 23. Hé ætbréde (subtrahat) his líchaman of mette, R. Ben. I. 85, 5. VI. with idea of withholding, prevention :-- Ic ðé ætbréde míne rénas, þæt heó þínre eorðan ne rínað, Wlfst. . 159, 25. Hé ætbr&aelig-acute;d &thorn-bar; gefeoht he would not let the battle take place, Hml. S. 31, 126. Ætbródenum his d&aelig-acute;le of wíne, R. Ben. I. 77, 14. VII. with idea of destroying, putting an end to :-- &THORN-bar; þú ádýlegie synna, þú þe synna ætbrýtst. Hml. S. 3, 544. Sé de ætbrýt and ádýlegað middaneardes synna, Hml. Th. ii. 38, 29. Þá blisse ús ne ætbrét nán man, Hml. A. 78, 144. Sé þe ætbr&aelig-acute;t (aufert) gást ealdra, Ps. L. 75, 13. Sé ðe ætbrúde synna, Hml. Th. ii. 40, 9. God mihte heora geswinc him ætbrédan, 162, 5. v. æt-brédendlic in Dict.
æt-bryidan. v. brigdan
æt-clifian. Add :-- Ætfélun (vel ætclofodon in a later hand) adheserunt, Ps. V. 101, 6.
æt-clíðende glosses aderentem, Txts. 181, 64. Cf. cliða.
æt-déman to give judgement adverse to a claimant (dat.) in respect to what he claims (acc.) :-- Ðá ætdémdon him Myrcna witan land búton hé his wer águlde, Cht. Th. 207, 32. Cf. æt-reccan.
&aelig-acute;te. Add :-- Eft, sealf; &aelig-acute;tan gecnúa, lege on, Lch. ii. 118, 28. v. self-&aelig-acute;te.
-&aelig-acute;te. v. micel-, ofer-&aelig-acute;te.
æt-eáca, an; m. An addition, appendix :-- Etheácan appendices, An. Ox. 53, 18.
æt-ealdod; adj. Too aged :-- Þonne heó forwerod byð and teámes ætealdod (too old to bear children), Hml. A. 20, 159.
æt-eáwan, æt-eom, æt-eów-, &aelig-acute;tere, &aelig-acute;tern, æt-éw-. v. æt-íwan, æt, æt-íw-, sceáp-&aelig-acute;tere, &aelig-acute;tren, æt-íw-.
æt-fæstan. Add: I. to inflict :-- Æ(t)fæstan inpingere, Wrt. Voc. ii. 44, 72. II. to commit, entrust, deposit :-- Ædfæst depositum. Wrt. Voc. i. 21, 4. II a. to give in marriage :-- Þá ætfæste hé mé míne efen-þeówene, seó þe wæs &aelig-acute;r óðres gemecca. Shrn. 39, 8. Cf. oþ-fæstan.
æt-fæstnian; p. ode To commit, deposit :-- Hweðer geleornodest þú þe myd þám eágum þe mid þám ingeþance ? Þá cwæð ic: Mid &aelig-acute;gðrum ic hyt geleornode. . . . Þá eágan hyt ætfæstnodon mínum ingeþance, Shrn. 175, 10.
æt-faran; p. -fór To go away, make off :-- Án fox þone scóh geiæhte and ætfaran (-en, MS.) þóhte. Shrn. 14, 23. Cf. oþ-faran.
æt-feallan. Add: I. lit. to fall, drop from :-- Þám cwellere ætfeóll his gold, Hml. S. 12, 216. II. fig (l) to fall away, (a) diminution :-- Ætfealle sió bót þ&aelig-acute;m godfæder swá ilce swá &thorn-bar; wíte þám hláforde déð. Ll. Th. i. 150, 18. (b) deterioration :-- &THORN-bar; geleáfa swá earmlíce ætfeallan sceolde, Hml. S. 23, 373. (c) desertion :-- Se l&aelig-acute;weda mót óðre síðe wífigan, gyf his wíf him ætfylð, Ll. Th. ii. 346, 22. His frýnd him ætfeallað. Hml. S. 12, 85 : Wlfst. 142, 6. (2) to befall, come upon :-- Hé bið ácólod and for þon ælfilð him wæterbolla, Lch. ii. 206, ll. Cf. oþ-fellan.
æt-fecgan, -felgan. v. æt-feólan : æt-feohtan, dele I.
æt-feólan. l. æt-feólan, and add: (from -feolhan); p. -fealh, pl. -fulgon, and -f&aelig-acute;lon (as if from -felan). I. to adhere, cleave (lit. and fig.) :-- Ætfileð adhereat, Ps. Srt. 136, 6. Ætfalh adhesit, 43, 25: 62, 9. Ætfélun (-fulgon), Ps. Spl. C.) adheserunt, 24, 21. Ætfealan (not -feolan as in Dict.), 72, 28. II. fig. of continued action, to stick to, (a) with idea of diligence, be instant in :-- Ðæt hé geornlíce ætfealh ð&aelig-acute;re ðénunge ministerio sedulus insistere, Bd. 3, 19; S. 547, 14. Ðá hé geornlíce his leornunge ætfealh cum lectioni operam dedisset, 4, 23; S. 596, 16. Hié geornlíce heora gebedum ætfulgon. Bl. H. 201, 18. Ætfeolh ðú ðínum fæstenum jejuniis insiste, Bd. 4, 25; S. 599, 41. Ðearf is &thorn-bar; ic weacenum ætfeóle, S. 601, 3. Ðæt gé ætfeólen ð&aelig-acute;re láre ut praedicalioni servias, Past. 375, 5. (b) with idea of persistence :-- Ðá ætfealh se gesíþ geornlíce his bénum comes obnixius precibus instans, Bd. 5, 4; S. 617, 12. III. to press, impress, (a) lit. :-- Wrít þám horse on þám heáfde foran Crístes m&aelig-acute;l and on leoþa gehwilcum þe þú ætfeólan mæge, Lch. ii. 290, 24. (b) fig. :-- Þá þá him eádmódlíce ætfeólan his þegnas and l&aelig-acute;rdon hine, &thorn-bar; hé onfénge &thorn-bar; yrfe cum ei discipuli humiliter imminerent, ut possessiones acciperet, Gr. D. 201, 9. Cf. oþ-feólan.
æt-feorrian to take away :-- Ná ætfeorra þú non auferas, Scint. 160, 7.
æt-ferian. Add :-- Man mid unrihte N. orf ætferede, Ll. Th. i. 180, i. Cf. oþ-ferian.
æt-fleón. Add: (l) absolute, to escape, flee away :-- Ðá óðre ætflugon, Hml. S. 25, 294: Chr. 1056; P. 186, 31. Hé ofslóh þá þe ætfleón ne mihton, 1068 ; P. 203, 26. Fleón hé mæg, ac hé ætfleón ne mæg. Ap. Th. 7, 5. (2) to escape from (dat.) :-- Him nán þing ætfleón ne mæg, Hml. S. I. 44. Wé r&aelig-acute;daþ be þ&aelig-acute;re león, &thorn-bar; ðá óðre deór þe mihton hire ætfleón þurh heora fóta swiftnysse, &thorn-bar; hí beóð swá áfyrhte &thorn-bar; hí fleón ne durron, Hml. A. 63, 280. (3) to escape to (tó) :-- Hé tó scypum ætfleáh, Chr. 1076; P. 211, 28. Ðá óðre ætflugon tó Philistéa lande, Hml. S. 25, 321. Þén scip ætfleó tó hwilcre friðbyrig, Ll. Th. i. 286, I. Cf. oþ-fleón.
æt-fón. Substitute: To arrest, apprehend, attach stolen or lost property :-- Gif man óðrum mæn feoh forstele, and se ágend hit eft ætfó. Ll. Th. i. 30, 8. Gif feoh man eft æt þám mæn in Cent ætfó, 34, 6. Cf. 160, 8.
æt-foran. Add: I. prep, (l) local, (a) confronting, (α) of persons, before, in the presence of, in the sight of :-- Ætforan (ante) þ&aelig-acute;re en-gelican gæderunge, An. Ox. 1749. Wé synd hér ætforan (coram) þé, Coll. M. 34, Hé waes Gode gecwéme and gife ætforan him gemétte, Gen. 6, 8: II. (/3) of objects, before, in front of :-- His sceatt ætstód ætforan him, Hml. S. . 12, 54. Þone fótscamul ætforan his bedde (æt his reste foran, v.l.), Gr. D. 20, 28. (b) preceding, in front of, at the head of :-- Gáð ætforan þám folce praecedite populum. Jos. 3, 6. (2) temporal, (a) marking date :-- Ætforan scs UNCERTAIN Andreas mæssan, Chr. 1010; P. 141, 3. l, (b) marking priority :-- Swá wel haldan swá &aelig-acute;nig kyngc ætforan him betst dyde, Chr. 1066; P. 200, 22. (3) marking precedence, preference :--
22 ÆT-FYLIGAN -- ÆÞELO
Hé geendebyrde þone unspédigan fiscere ætforan ðám rícan cásere, Hml. Th. i. 578, 10. &THORN-bar; heregyld wæs &aelig-acute;fre ætforan óðrum gyldum þe man geald, Chr. 1052; P. 173, 22. II. adv. Before, beforehand :-- W&aelig-acute;ron þá wælisce men ætforan mid þám cynge, Chr. 1048; P. 174, 9.
