h&aelig-acute;med-wíf. For 'Cot. 136 Lye' substitute :-- H&aelig-acute;medwíf matrona, Wrt. Voc. ii. 59, 19.
h&aelig-acute;mend, es; m. An adulterer, a fornicator :-- H&aelig-acute;mend inceslalur (-or ?), Wrt. Voc. ii. 44, 47. v. unriht-, wóh-h&aelig-acute;mend.
h&aelig-acute;mere. Add :-- God fordémð þá dyrnan forligeras and þá unrihtan h&aelig-acute;meras, Hml. A. 19, 145. v. unriht-, wóh-h&aelig-acute;mere.
h&aelig-acute;mestre. v. níd-h&aelig-acute;mestre : -h&aelig-acute;mingas. v. -h&aelig-acute;me; pl. m. : hæn. v. hen : h&aelig-acute;nan. Add: v. ge-h&aelig-acute;nan.
hænep. Add :-- Hænep canafel sylvatica, Wrt. Voc. i. 69, 16: cannabum, ii. 128, 4: cannabin, 6. Hænep (henep, v. l.). Ðeós wyrt þe man cannaue silfatica and óþrum naman hænep (henep, v. l.) nenmeþ, Lch. i. 228, 15-17.
-hæp, -hæplic, -hæplicness. v. ge-hæp, ge-hæplic, ge-hæplicness.
hæppan (?); p. te To move accidentally(?), to slip :-- Þá slóh sum h&aelig-acute;þen man to þám hálgan were, ac mid þám swenge hæpte &thorn-bar; swurd him of handum (the sword slipped mil of his hand), and ne mihte man hit n&aelig-acute;fre syððan findan (cf. þæt w&aelig-acute;pen wand áweg mid þám siege of þæs réðan handum, Hml. Th. ii. 510, 22 : nyste hé f&aelig-acute;ringa hw&aelig-acute;r ; &thorn-bar; seax cóm þe hé &aelig-acute;r on handa hæfde, Bl. H. 223, 17 : all three passages refer to the same event in the life of St. Martin), Hml. S. 31, 477. [Cf. N. E. D. nap to go by chance.]
hæpse. Add :-- Ne sceolde hé nán ðing forgýman ðe &aelig-acute;fre tó note mehte ; ne forda músfellan, ne, &thorn-bar; git l&aelig-acute;sse is, to hæpsan pinn, Angl. ix. 265, 9, Hæpsan, loca eluslilla (arcarum reserantur), An. Ox. 4003.
hæpsian. Add :-- Sero, seras, ic hæpsige, is ð&aelig-acute;re forman geðeódnysse, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 166, 1. v. be-hæpsian.
h&aelig-acute;r. Add: I. a hair :-- Hér pilus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 117, 40. (1) a human hair, hair of a person's head :-- Hér (capillus) of heófde iówrum ne bid forloren, Lk. R. L. 21, 18. &THORN-bar; fýr heora ne æthrán, ne furþum án h&aelig-acute;r heora heáfdes, Hml. S. 30, 454. Ne mæhtú énne hér (unum capillum) húit geuirce, Mt. L. 5, 36. Him Þá h&aelig-acute;r (his h&aelig-acute;r, v. l.) áfeóllon fills cadentibus, Gr. D. 157, 8. Héras (capilli) heáfdes, Mt. L. 10, 30. Héro (hér, R. ), Lk. L. 12, 7. Heora wæs má þonne h&aelig-acute;ra on mínum heáfde, Ps. Th. 39, 14. Ne efesiad eów ne eówre h&aelig-acute;r ne sciron (non facietis calvitium), Deut. 14, (2) a hair of an animal :-- Of n&aelig-acute;rum (of hérum ð&aelig-acute;ra camella, Mt. L. 3, 4) de pilis, Wrt. Voc. ii. 71. 61. Wullan fliásum, hérum. Txts. 151, 4. H&aelig-acute;rum, Rä. 36, 4. II. a number of hairs together (1) a lock. v. h&aelig-acute;r-locc :-- H&aelig-acute;ra cincinnarum. Au. Ox. 1199. (2) a fringe :-- Ðá hér fimbrias, Mt. L. 23, 5. III. with collective force, hair (1) of persons :-- H&aelig-acute;r cesaries, pilos, Wülck Gl. 290, 11. Unbeganum locca fexe and fúliendum h&aelig-acute;re inculta criniculorum cesarie et squalente capillatura, An. Ox. 1214. (2) of animals :-- Sume bróhton gáte h&aelig-acute;r . . . þæt gate h&aelig-acute;r getácnode þá stíþan d&aelig-acute;dbóte, Ælfc. Gen. Thw. 3, 31-6, v. heáfod-h&aelig-acute;r.
h&aelig-acute;re. Add: I. sackcloth used as a garment, a hair-shirt :-- Hé scrýdde hine mid h&aelig-acute;ran and mid axan bestreowode, Hml. S. 31, 445. Mid héran eilicio, Ps. Srt. 34, 13. Heó (St. Cecilia) wæs gegyred myd h&aelig-acute;ran æt hyre líchaman, and onufan þ&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;ran heó wæs gegyred myd golde áwefenum hrægelum, Shrn. 149, 20. Hí mid h&aelig-acute;ran hí gescrýddon tó líce they wore sackcloth next their skin, Hml. S. 12, 36 : Hml. A. 108, 207. Heó áwearp hire h&aelig-acute;ran and hire wudewan reáf, 109, 228. II. sackcloth used to lie on :-- Hé oftost læg uppon ánre h&aelig-acute;ran on þ&aelig-acute;re baran flóra, Hml. S. 31, 853. On stíþre h&aelig-acute;ran licgende, 1351 : Hml. Th. ii. 516, 31. [v. N. E. D. hiere.]
hærean-fagol. Have the glossers misunderstood the word herinaciis, and supposed it to be the name of a bird ? Can the hærean represent herin and fagol be a mistake for fugol? and in the other gloss, hâtte-fagol, is hatte = hatte, andfago/ for fugol, so that the gloss would mean herinacius is the name of a bird ?
h&aelig-acute;ren. Add :-- Heó gegyrede hý mid h&aelig-acute;renre tunecan and mid byrnan, &thorn-bar; is mid lytelre hacelan, Shrn. 140, 30.
hærfest. Add: I. autumn, the third ofthe four seasons. [It began on August 7 and November 6 was its last day :-- Þæs (after Lammas day) hærfest cymð ymb seofon niht bútan ánre wonan . . . Syþþan (after All Saints' day) wintres dæg on syx nihtum genimð hærfest mid herige six days after Lammas autumn comes . . . six days after All . Saints' day winter time captures autumn, Men. 140-204] :-- Tó hærfestes emnihte, Chr. 1048; P. 174, 21. On hærfeste gefór se here on Miercna lond, 877 ; P. 74, 21, Ætforan hærfeste forbarn &thorn-bar; hálige mynster s&c-tilde;e Paule, 1086 ; P. 218, 22. Wé weorðiaí heáhengles tiid on hærfeste, Michaheles, Men. 177. Ðis wæs on hærfest, Chr. 918 ; P. 100, 2. Hé saet on þám biscopríce ealne þone sumor and þone hærfest, 1048 ; P. 172, 14. Herfest, 1006; P. 136, 16. I a. as the season for the ripening and gathering of fruits :-- Hærfest byð hréðeádegost, hæleðum bringeð géres westmas, Gn. C. 8. Swá nú lencten and hærfest, on lencten hit gréwð, and on hærfest hit fealwað, Bt. 21 ; F. 74, 22. Se wæstmb&aelig-acute;ra hærfest bryngþ rípa bléda, 39, 13 ; F. 234, 15. Hærfest cymð, wlitig wæstmum hladen, Men. 140. Me mæcg on hærfeste rípan, in Agusto and Septembri and Octobri. . . fela tilða hám gæderian . . . &aelig-acute;r tó túne tó slid winter cume, Angl. ix. 261, 14-20. II. the part of Autumn in which the fruits of the earth are gathered in, harvest, v. hærfestlic; II. , hærfest-mónaþ, hærfest-tíd ; II :-- Agusius síhð tó mannum mid genihtsumum hærfeste and autumnus cymð tó mancynne binnan seofon nihta fyrste, Angl. viii. 311, 18. On hærfeste wícode se cyng on neáweste þáre byrig, þá hwíle þe hié hira corn gerypon, Chr. 896; P. 89, 8. Mon eorðan wæstmas on hærfeste hám gel&aelig-acute;deð . . . on rypes tíman, Ph. 244. II a. rendered in late Latin versions by Augustus (cf. Augustus messis, messis tempus, Migne) :-- On hærfeste (in Augusta), ðá fullan wican &aelig-acute;r S&c-tilde;a Marian mæssan (Sept. 8), Ll. Th. i. 92, 6. Berebryttan gebyreð corngebrot on hærfæste (in Augusta), 440, 2. iii dagas &aelig-acute;lcre wucan on hærfest (in Augusta), 432, 32 : 434, 7. ¶ in a late MS. it is used as the name of the month, August :-- On Iuli mónðe. . . On hærfest. . . On Setembre, Angl. . . . 185, 10.
hærfest-lic. Add: I. autumnal, v. hærfest; I. :-- Hærfestlicere autumnali (tempore), An. Ox. 3838. On hærfæstlice (árfæstlice, MS. ) tíde (in autumnali tempore, i. e. August 20), fíf dagum &aelig-acute;r S&c-tilde;e Bartholomeus mæssan (August 25), Guth. Gr. 157, 59. II. of harvest, v. hærfest; II :-- Hé wearð ofslagen þurh þ&aelig-acute;re sunnan h&aelig-acute;tan on hærfestlicre tíde mortuus est in diebus messis hordeaceae, Hml. A. 108, 198.
hærfest-mónaþ. Add: cf. hærfest; II a.
hærfest-tíd, e; f. I. autumn, v. hærfest; I :-- Þú þá treówa on hærfesttíd heora leáfa bereáfast, and eft on lencten óþru leáf sellest, Bt. 4; F. 8, 6. II. harvest-time, v. hærfest; II :-- On sumera and on hærfesttíde, þonne mon wæstmas in somnode tempore aestatis, quo fruges erant colligendae, Bd. 4, 4 ; Sch. 369, 7.
hærfest-tíma, an; m. Autumn :-- Autumnus. &thorn-bar; ys hærfesttíma, cymð tó mancynne binnan seofen nihta fyrste autumn comes on the seventh of August, Angl. viii. 311, 18.
h&aelig-acute;riht. l. h&aelig-acute;riht(e), and for ' crinitus, . . . Lye' substitute :-- Þá h&aelig-acute;rihtan setosa (vervecum vellera), Wrt. Voc. ii. 87, 27,
hæring. Add :-- Hæring sordino, Wrt. Voc. i. 281, 64. Heringas sardinas, Txts. 94, 910.
h&aelig-acute;r-loccas, Hpt. Gl. 526, 45. Perhaps this should be read h&aelig-acute;r, loccas. Cf. fexa &l-bar; h&aelig-acute;ra cincinnoriim, 435, 5.
hærn. Substitute for passages :-- Hraen, raen fiustra, undae, Txts. 60, 400. Flód oððe hærn flustra, Wrt. Voc. ii. 33, 32. Hærn eft onwand árýða geblond, An. 531.
h&aelig-acute;r-n&aelig-acute;dl. For ' Lye ' substitute :-- Mid þráwincspinle, h&aelig-acute;rn&aelig-acute;dla calamistro, An. Ox. 1200.
h&aelig-acute;r-sife, es; n. A hair-sieve :-- Man sceal habban . . . hérsyfe, Angl. ix. 264. 14. [O. L. Ger. hár-sif setatium : O. H. Ger. há[r]-sib(-sip) cribellnm, sedatium. ]
h&aelig-acute;s. Add: I. a bidding, an order :-- Streclicere h&aelig-acute;se (quod) violenti pr&e-hook;cepti (imperio complendum jubelur), An. Ox. 1294. Petrus and Andreas be Crístes h&aelig-acute;se forléton heora nett . . . hí æfter stemne ánre h&aelig-acute;se þæt þæt hí hæfilon forgeáton, Hml. Th. i. 578, 24. Deóflu be eówere h&aelig-acute;se þá deófolseócan forléton, 64, 26. Seó menigo háligra sáula mid Drilitnes h&aelig-acute;se w&aelig-acute;ron of þ&aelig-acute;m cwicsúslum áhafena, Bl. H. 87, 18. Be hyre ágenum cyre, ná geneádod mid nánre h&aelig-acute;se, Hml. A. 32, 204. Þurh his hálige h&aelig-acute;s, An. 1522: 1588: El. 86: Wlfst. 255, Féran sceal þurh freán h&aelig-acute;se sundor ánra gehwæs sáwl of líce, Az. 92. Hé hét him tó clypian ealne þone here &thorn-bar; hí his h&aelig-acute;se gefyldon, Hml. S. 28, 27: Angl vii. 52, 406. Hé gehýrde þá word þæs hátendan, ac hé yldode &thorn-bar; hé þá h&aelig-acute;sa gefyllan nolde audivit jubentis verba, sed implere distulit, Gr. D. 159, 16. Hé bead þæs apostoles h&aelig-acute;sa (-e, v. l.) Dyonisie, Hml. S. 29, 63. II. an invitation from a superior :-- S&c-tilde;s Paulinus þ&aelig-acute;re cyricean scíre onféng mid þæs arcebisceopes h&aelig-acute;se and Eádboldes þæs cyninges (innitatione Honorii amistitis et Eadbaldi regis). Bd. 2, 20 ; Sch. 188, 12. III. an office, service one is bidden to perform (?) :-- Þénunge. h&aelig-acute;se munia, Wrt. Voc. ii. 57, 8. v. níd-h&aelig-acute;s; hátan.
hæsel galerus. Dele.
hæsel hazel. Add :-- [H]aesil, haesl auellanus, Txts. 38, 50. Hæsl abellanus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 7, 42 : abellanus vel colurnus, i. 285, 24. Haesil, haesl corylus, Txts. 50, 236. Of ð&aelig-acute;re apoldre on ðæne hwítan hæsl, ðonnæ of ðám hwítan hæsle on hnuttwíc eástewearde, C. D. v. 221, 18. [The word occurs in a great many local names, [v. C. D. vi. 293, col. 2.]
hæsel-hnutu. Add :-- Haeselhnutu abelena, Wrt. Voc. ii. 98, 14. Haslhnutu abellana, 4, 52. Hæslhnute cyrnel nuculeus sive nucleus, 62, 37.
HÆSEL-R&AElig-acute;W -- H&AElig-acute;ÞEN 499
hæsel-r&aelig-acute;w, e; f. A row of hazels:-- On ðá hæselr&aelig-acute;we, C. D. iii. 77. 4-
hæsel-wrid, es; n. m (?). l. hæsel-wríd, -wriþ, es; m. , and add :-- On ðone miclan hæslwríð wiðneoðon ðæt gráfet; of ðám hæsl-wríðe, C. D. v. 194, 14. v. wríd.
hæsel-wyrt. Dele: hæssec. v. hassuc.
hae-swealwe, an ; f. A kind of hawk :-- Haesualwe (Sweet suggests s&aelig-acute;-) astur, Txts. 43, 234. Cf. beoru-swealwe.
hæt. Arfd; -- Haet mitra. Wrt. Voc. ii. 114, 13. Hæt tiara, 85, 42 : capititim, An. Ox. 5320. Hættes mitr&e-hook;, 5242 : Wrt. Voc. ii. 87, 45. Camb on hætte oððe on helme erista, 19, 10. Eówre hættas mitr&e-hook;, 55, 21: 70. Haetas mitras, Txts. 113, 75.
h&aelig-acute;t heat. For forms that might be taken as oblique cases of such a nominative see h&aelig-acute;tu : h&aelig-acute;ta. v. scyld-h&aelig-acute;ta.
h&aelig-acute;tan. Add: I. trans. (1) to communicate heat to :-- -Gedó on calic, menge æfter þon wið wader, and h&aelig-acute;te, Lch. ii. 24, 25. (2) to cause the sensation of warmth in :-- L&aelig-acute;cedóm . . . tó h&aelig-acute;tenne untrumne magan. Lch. ii. 158, 21. II. intrans. To be warm :-- Haetendae calentes, Txts. 48, 206. v. for-, ge-, in-, on-h&aelig-acute;tan.
h&aelig-acute;te. Dele last passage, and add :-- H&aelig-acute;te calor, . . . h&aelig-acute;te micel fervor, Wrt. Voc. i. 53, 40, 42 : 76, 73, 75. I. the quality of being hot :-- Belimpð seó h&aelig-acute;ðung tó ð&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;tan, Hml. Th. i. 286, 3. &THORN-bar; seó sunne mid hyre h&aelig-acute;tan middaneardes wæstmas ne forbærne, Lch. iii. 250, 16. Þurh ð&aelig-acute;re sunnan h&aelig-acute;tan, 276, 16. Þæt hellice fýr hæfð unásecgendlice h&aelig-acute;tan and nán leóht, Hml. Th. i. 532, 2. I a. the sensation caused by contact with fire :-- Ne undergyte gé þæt eówre gléda náne h&aelig-acute;tan mínum líchaman ne gedóð, ac swíðor célinge?, Hml. Th. i. 430, 12. II. heat as an element present in all bodies, fire as one of the four elements :-- Ðunor cymð of h&aelig-acute;tan and of w&aelig-acute;tan. Seó lyft týhð ðone w&aelig-acute;tan tó hyre neoðan and ðá h&aelig-acute;tan ufon, and þonne hí gegaderode beóð, seó h&aelig-acute;te and se w&aelig-acute;ta binnon ð&aelig-acute;re lyfte, þonne winnað hí him betweóman mid egeslicum swége, and &thorn-bar; fýr ábyrst út ðurh lígett gyf hé máre biþ þonne se w&aelig-acute;ta; gyf se w&aelig-acute;ta byð máre ðonne &thorn-bar; fýr þonne fremað hit, Lch. iii. 280, 2-9. Nis nán licliamlic þing de næbbe ðá feówer gesceafta him mid, &thorn-bar; is lyft and fýr and eorðe and wæter . , . Úre líchaman habbað &aelig-acute;gðer ge h&aelig-acute;tan ge w&aelig-acute;tan, eorðan and lyft, 272, 27-274, 8. III. a hot condition of the atmosphere, hot weather :-- Sió h&aelig-acute;te hæfð genumen þæs súðd&aelig-acute;les máre þonne se cyle þæs norðd&aelig-acute;les hæbbe. Ors. i; S. 24, 28. Cóm swá micel h&aelig-acute;te (ila jugis et torrida siccitas) giend Rómáne þæt ealle heora eorðwæstmas forwurdon, 2, 6; S. 88, 15. Cýtan ár&aelig-acute;ran &thorn-bar; hí wið cyle and wið h&aelig-acute;ton hí sylfe geburgon, Hml. S. 23, 419. For þæs sumores h&aelig-acute;tan, Bl. H. 59, 4. Se hara þonne hé on sumura for swíðlicre h&aelig-acute;tan geteórud byþ, Lch. i. 226, 23. III a. a region of hot atmosphere, a torrid zone :-- Án þ&aelig-acute;ra d&aelig-acute;la is on ælemiddon weallendo . . . þonne beóð on twá healfa þ&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;tan twégen d&aelig-acute;las gemetegodc, Lch. iii. 260, 24. IV. of bodily condition, a state of feeling hot :-- Tó eácan þ&aelig-acute;m hié derede &aelig-acute;gþer ge þurst ge h&aelig-acute;te besides this their being so thirsty and hot injured them. Ors. 5, 7; S. 230, 17. Him cóm on swá micel h&aelig-acute;te and swá micel þurst &thorn-bar; hié him heora feores ne wéndun they got into such a state of heat and thirst that they gave up hope of life, 6, 13; S. 268, 12. IV a. a feverish or inflamed condition of body :-- Wið ðæs magan h&aelig-acute;tan, Lch. i. 268, 1. Ðeós wyrt geh&aelig-acute;leð mænigfealde untrumnyssa . . . eágena sárnysse and h&aelig-acute;tan, 272, 2. V. of intense feeling or passion :-- Hætan incentiua (Melantiae carnis incentiua illecebrosis stimulis agitabant, Aid. 59, 18), An. Ox. 4226. v. lencten-, sumer-h&aelig-acute;te; hát.
hætera. In bracket dele 'O. H. Ger. hadarun . . . clout', and odd: v. N. E. D. hater.
h&aelig-acute;þ a heath, h&aelig-acute;þ a plant. Take these together, for ' e ; f. ' substitute es; n. m, , and add: I. a heath, a tract of uncultivated, waste land, (1) masc. :-- Andlang ð&aelig-acute;re díc tó ð&aelig-acute;m h&aelig-acute;ðe foreweardan . . . ; ðonne westweard ofer ðone h&aelig-acute;ð, C. D. iii. 264, 2-4. Úp on ðene h&aelig-acute;ð; ofer ðene h&aelig-acute;ð, 384, 26. (2) neut. :-- Ofer ðæt h&aelig-acute;ð, C. D. iii. 392, 3, 5. On ðæt h&aelig-acute;ð westeweard, 427, 33. On ðæt héð westeweard, v. 212, 18. v. mór-h&aelig-acute;þ. II. a plant-name :-- Haeth, haet (cf. haet-colas, 53, 570), hét calomacus (-chuns), calomancus, Txts. 52, 269. H&aelig-acute;þ colomacus, genesta, Wrt. Voc. ii. 134, 35. H&aelig-acute;ð calomacus, 13, 33. Haeth, haedth, haet thymus, Txts. 102, 1007. H&aelig-acute;þ timus, Wrt. Voc. i. 285, 68. H&aelig-acute;ð alucurus vel thimus, ii. 10, 38. H&aelig-acute;þ brogus, 127, 25 : mirica, i. 33, 54. Smeóce mid h&aelig-acute;þe and &thorn-bar; ylce on wíne drince, Lch. i. 354, 24. ¶ the word is found in many compounds, (1) as the first part of words denoting localities, h&aelig-acute;þ-beorh, -burh, dún, -feld, -gára, -hricg, -leáh, -slæd, v. C. D. vi. 293, 294. (2) as part of proper names, v. Txts.
h&aelig-acute;þ, e; f Drynessfrom /teat, parched condition :-- Mycel h&aelig-acute;te ferfor, swaloð cauma, drúgað oððe h&aelig-acute;ð siccitas, Wrt. Voc. i. 76, 77. [Cf. O. H. Ger. hei uredo, ge-hei cauma; ar-, far-heién.] See next word, and h&aelig-acute;þung, for-h&aelig-acute;þan.
h&aelig-acute;þa, an ; m. Parching by heal :-- Hé gebæd &thorn-bar; God forgeáfe þ&aelig-acute;e eorðan rénas, for þan ðe se h&aelig-acute;ða þá hýnde ðá eorðan . . . þá ásende Drihten rénscúras aad þá eorðan gewæterode þe &aelig-acute;r wæs forburnen, Hml. S. 14, 168. v. æfter-h&aelig-acute;þa (where dele queries as to form and gender), and preceding word.
h&aelig-acute;þan. v. for-h&aelig-acute;þan; h&aelig-acute;þung, and two preceding words.
h&aelig-acute;þ-cole. Substitute: haeþ-cole a plain-name :-- Haelcolae colomata, Wrt. Voc. ii. 105, 16. H&aelig-acute;ícole colomate, 15, 20. H&aelig-acute;þcole stena, i. 68, 68 (in a list of plant-names).
h&aelig-acute;þen. Add; -- H&aelig-acute;þene geneliatici. Wrt. Voc. ii. 40, 53. A. as adj. (but sometimes where used predicatively might belong to B. ) I. referring to times covered by Old and New Testaments. (1) of persons, (a) not believing in Jehovah, not of the Jewish religion :-- Giethro, ðeáh hé h&aelig-acute;ðen and elðiódig w&aelig-acute;re, Past. 130, 12. H&aelig-acute;ðen heriges wísa (Nebuchadnezzar), Dan. 203. &THORN-bar; wíf wæs h&aelig-acute;ðen Sirofénisces cynnes erat mulier gentilis Syrophoenissa genere, Mk. (W. S. , L. , R. ) 7, 26. H&aelig-acute;ðenes heaðorinces (Holofernes') heáfod, Jud. 179. H&aelig-acute;ðnum folce (the people of Sodom), Gen. 2416. Þone h&aelig-acute;ðenan hund (Holofernes), Jud. no. Óðre þeóda, h&aelig-acute;ðene herigeas, Ps. Th. 78, 10. (a α) gentile (as used in the A. V. ) v. B. I. aα :-- Gerihtnes h&aelig-acute;þenra þeóda, Bl. H. 163, 23. Hé bid geseald h&aelig-acute;þnum mannum he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles (Lk. 18, 32), 15, 9. Betwuxn h&aelig-acute;ðnum monnum among the Gentiles (i. Cor. 5, l), Past. 211, 8. ¶ the part put for the whole :-- Áhangen h&aelig-acute;ðenum folmum, El. 1076. (b) used of a Samaritan as opposed to a Jew :-- Samaritanus, &thorn-bar; is h&aelig-acute;ðin monn, Lk. L. 10, 33. Des wæs h&aelig-acute;ðin hic erat Samaritanus, 17, 16. (2) of things. Cf. II 3 :-- H&aelig-acute;þenu godu dii gentium, Ps. Th. 95, 5. Ge s&aelig-acute;don &thorn-bar; þá h&aelig-acute;ðnan tída w&aelig-acute;ron beteran þonne þá crístnan, Ors. 6, 37 ; S. 296, 18. Ne swerigen gé n&aelig-acute;fre under h&aelig-acute;ðene godas (per nomen exlernorum deorum non jurabitis. Ex. 23, 13), Ll. Th. i. 54, 23. II. referring to Christian times, (1) of persons, (a) not of the Christian religion :-- Swá hwylc h&aelig-acute;þen (gentilis) man swá forl&aelig-acute;t h&aelig-acute;þen wíf. . . Gyf hyra óðer biþ h&aelig-acute;þan, óþer gefullod, Ll. Th. ii. 144, 12-14. Heó wæs &aelig-acute;ryst h&aelig-acute;ðen and wælgrim . . . þá gélýfde heó on God and onféng fulwihte, Shrn. 139, 4-7 : Hml. S. 7, 264. Astrias, h&aelig-acute;ðen and hygeblind, Ap. 46. H&aelig-acute;ðen hildfruma, Jul. 7. Se h&aelig-acute;þena man, Bl. H. 223, 10. Þ&aelig-acute;m h&aelig-acute;þnan cásere (Nero), 171, 29. Þæt h&aelig-acute;þene weorod, 221, 30. Eác wearð on Ispanie &thorn-bar; þá h&aelig-acute;ðenan men (the Moors) fóran and hergodan uppon þám Xpenan mannan . . . hí áweg ádrifan eall þet h&aelig-acute;ðena folc, Chr. 1086; P. 221, 33-222, 3. Þén hié (the Goths) h&aelig-acute;þene w&aelig-acute;re, Ors. 2, 8; S. 94, 9. Heora fæder and módor [w&aelig-acute;ron] h&aelig-acute;þena þá gýt, Hml. S: 5, 36. H&aelig-acute;dne, Bl. H. 211, 20. Þ&aelig-acute;r h&aelig-acute;þene men deóflum onguldon, 221, 3. Manige h&aelig-acute;þne men ungeleáfsume, 129, 24. Be þára h&aelig-acute;þenra manna fleáme, 203, 4. Of h&aelig-acute;þenum mágum ethnicis (i. gentilibus) parentibus, An. Ox. 2416: Hml. S. 31, 13. &THORN-bar; man crístene menn of earde ne sylle húru on h&aelig-acute;ðene leóde, Ll. Th. i. 304, 16. ¶ the part put for the whole :-- Þurl. h&aelig-acute;ðene hand, Ap. 60. (a a) used specially of the Scandinavian invaders of England , v. (c), B. II. I a :-- Wit begétan ðás béc æt haeðnum herge mid uncre claene feó, Txts. 175, 4. Hié w&aelig-acute;l geslógon on h&aelig-acute;þnum herige (h&aelig-acute;þene here, v. l.), Chr. 851; P. 64, 22: 853; P. 64, 32. Hér h&aelig-acute;þne (h&aelig-acute;ðene, v. l.) men oferhergeadon Sceápíge, 832 ; P. 62, 9. Ofslægen from h&aelig-acute;þnum monnum, 838; P. 62, 35. Ceprl gefeaht wiþ h&aelig-acute;þene men, 851; P. 64, 11. (b) not baptized :-- &AElig-acute;ghwilc cild sí gefullod binnon nigon nihton . . . and gif h&aelig-acute;ðen cild binnon .ix. nihton þurh gímelíste forfaren sí. Ll. Th. ii. 292, 6. Cild gyf hit h&aelig-acute;ðen swelte. . . . Sé þe ofsleá his beam h&aelig-acute;ðen . . . H&aelig-acute;ðen cild gif hit bið preóst beboden . . . and hit h&aelig-acute;ðen swelte, 144, 32-35. Gif ungefullod cild f&aelig-acute;rlíce bið gebróhte tó þám mæssepreóst, &thorn-bar; hé mót fullian sóna, &thorn-bar; hit ne swelte h&aelig-acute;den, 352, 17. Cf. Gif hit bútan fulluhte gewit, 412, 24. (c) barbarous. Cf. (a α) :-- H&aelig-acute;ðen hreáfere [oþþe] flotman &l-bar; wícing barbarus praedo [vel crudelis] archipirata, Hpt. Gl. 501, 32. (2) of monstrous beings. Cf. B. II. 2 :-- H&aelig-acute;ðenes hilderinces (Grendel's), B. 986. Hé (Grendel) feorh álegde h&aelig-acute;ðene sáwle, 852. (3) of things, pertaining to non-Christian people, or to their religion and customs :-- Hearhlicre, þæs h&aelig-acute;þenan vel templicre fanatice, i. profani. Wrt. Voc. ii. 147, 38. Of h&aelig-acute;þenum gewunan apostatico ritu, An. Ox. 4920. Ic hine áwende fram h&aelig-acute;eth;enum gylde tó ðám sóðan Gode, Hml. Th. i. 468, 14. Tó þám h&aelig-acute;ðenan temple getogen, Hml. S. 2, 384. In þ&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;þenan byrig, An. 1493. H&aelig-acute;ðnum horde, B. 2216. Heora h&aelig-acute;þenan gild w&aelig-acute;ron ealle ídelu, Bl. H. 223, i. We l&aelig-acute;rað &thorn-bar; man geswíce freólsdagutn h&aelig-acute;ðen ra leóða and deófles gamena, Ll. Th. ii. 248, 11. [H]&aelig-acute;ðenra [bóca] indegitamentorum, An. Ox. 4442. On h&aelig-acute;ðnum þeáwum dweligende, Bl. H. 201, 20. Hé offrode his lác þám h&aelig-acute;ðenum godum, Hml. Th. ii. 482, 7. H&aelig-acute;ðenscipe bið I a man ídola weorðige, &thorn-bar; is &thorn-bar; man weorttige h&aelig-acute;ðene godas, Ll. Th. i. 378, 19. (3 a) profane as opposed to sacred or Christian literature :-- Hé leornoðe grammatical, craeft and þá h&aelig-acute;ðenan béc (cf. Shrn. 152, 11-18) oþ &thorn-bar; þá hálgan godspel him becómon tó hande. Hml. S. 35, 15. B. as subst. I. of pre-Christian times. v. A. I. (1) of persons, (a) one who is not a believer in Jehovah :-- Hwurfon hæleð geonge tó þám h&aelig-acute;ðenan (Nebuchadnezzar) foran, Dan. 434. Ðone ufemyston héton þá h&aelig-acute;þenan Saturnus, Angl. vii. 14, 122. Wé nú h&aelig-acute;ðenra þeównéd þoliað, Dan. 307. H&aelig-acute;þenra allophilorum (the Philistines), An. Ox. 881 : 5018. Hé hí on handgeweald h&aelig-acute;ðenum

sealde, Ps. Th. 105, 30. H&aelig-acute;þnum, Bl. H. 171, 22. (a a) a gentile, in pl, the Gentiles. v. A. I. aα :-- Alle h&aelig-acute;dno (hæðno, R. ) &l-bar; cynno middangeardes, Lk. L. 12, 30. H&aelig-acute;dna &l-bar; cynna, Mt. L. 12, 21. Þec gelegdon on láðne bend h&aelig-acute;ðene mid hondum, Sat. 540 (cf. Lk. L. R. 18, 32). Cyningas h&aelig-acute;ðna, Lk. L. R. 22, 25 : Mt. L. 20, 25. Gesald bið h&aelig-acute;ðnum, Lk. L. R. 18, 32. H&aelig-acute;dnum, Mk. L. 10, 33, 42 : Lk. L. 21, 24. Haedno gentiles, Mk. p.4, 15. (b) a believer who is not of Jewish nationality :-- Sume w&aelig-acute;ron h&aelig-acute;ðene (h&aelig-acute;dno summo, L., h&aelig-acute;ðno sume, R. gentiles quidam) þe fóron &thorn-bar; hig woldon hí gebiddan on ðám freólsdæge, Jn. 12, 20. Sæccendum h&aelig-acute;dnum (gentilibus) hine geseá uilnandum, Jn. p. 6, 14. (b β) any one not of Jewish nationality, in pl, nations other than the Jewish :-- Ofersuíðnesse h&aelig-acute;dno &l-bar; h&aelig-acute;ðinra (h&aelig-acute;ðnana, R. , þeóda, W. S.) pressura gentium, Lk. L. 21, 25, On allum h&aelig-acute;dnum, Mk. L. 13, 10. Geláeded biðon in alle h&aelig-acute;dno (þeóda, W. S., cynn, R. gentes), Lk. L. 21, 24. II. referring to Christian times. (1) of persons :-- Nú se h&aelig-acute;þena ne con úre gyfe onfón si paganus (Penda) neseit accipere nostra donaria, Bd. 3, 24; Sch. 307, 16. &THORN-bar; hí geh&aelig-acute;lan þises h&aelig-acute;ðenan eáge, Hml. S. 4, 151. Húsl sceal hálgum men, h&aelig-acute;ðnum synne, Gn. Ex. 132. H&aelig-acute;ðene sw&aelig-acute;fon dreóre druncne, An. 1004. Þá h&aelig-acute;ðnan heora þá leásan godas him laþodan on fultum, Bl. H. 201, 30. Sé þe Godes bebod ofer&dash-uncertain;hogaþ, hé biþ on h&aelig-acute;þenra onlícnesse, 49, 13. Hé wæs crísten l&aelig-acute;ce and hé eardode in h&aelig-acute;þenra midlene, Shrn. 125, 7. On h&aelig-acute;ðenra gildum libban paganis erroribus implicari, Bd. 2, l; Sch. 109, 21. (1 a) of the Scandinavian invaders of England. v. A. II. 1 a α :-- Feallan sceolon h&aelig-acute;ðene at hilde, By. 55. Þá h&aelig-acute;þenan for his geleáfan wurdon wódlíce yrre, Hml. S. 32, 113. Þá wunda þe þá wælhreówan h&aelig-acute;þenan on his líce macedon, 181. Under Norðmannum gebégde on h&aelig-acute;þenra hæfteclommum, Chr. 942 ; P. 110, 21. (2) of the devil. Cf. A. II. 2 :-- Heó þæt deófol teáh bendum fæstne, hálig h&aelig-acute;ðenne, Jul. 536.
h&aelig-acute;þen-dóm. Add: I. the belief and practice of a heathen people :-- H&aelig-acute;þendómes gentilitatis (Gregorius nostris parentibus errorem tetrae gentilitatis abstulit, Ald. 74, 13), An. Ox. 5156. Hú hé of h&aelig-acute;þendóme mæge tó crístendóme ðurh rihtne geleáfan and ðurh fulluht cuman, Wlfst. 32, 10. &AElig-acute;nne crístendóm ánr&aelig-acute;dlíce healdan and &aelig-acute;lcne h&aelig-acute;ðendóm georne forbúgan, Ll. Th. i. 314, 9. &AElig-acute;lcne h&aelig-acute;ðendóm oferhogian, 350, 12. &AElig-acute;nne God lufian and &aelig-acute;lcne h&aelig-acute;ðendóm georne áscunian, 316, 19. II. people among whom (or district in which) paganism prevails. v. Crísten-dóm ; II :-- &THORN-bar; man crístene men . . . on h&aelig-acute;ðendóme (cf. on h&aelig-acute;ðene leóde, 304, 16) húru ne gebringe, Ll. Th. i. 378, 1. v. h&aelig-acute;þen-nes.
h&aelig-acute;þen-gild. Dele passages from Num. 25, 2: 31, 16, in l. 10 for 454 read 456, and add: I. idolatry :-- Swutele synd þæs fl&aelig-acute;sces weorc . . . h&aelig-acute;ðengild manifesta swnt opera carnis . . . idolorum servitus (Gal. 5, 20), Hml. S. 17, 25. Hý fulwihte onféngon and w&aelig-acute;ron blíðran tó ðám deáðe þonne hý hér on h&aelig-acute;ðengilde lifden, Shrn. 142, 13. Nis nánum crístenum menn álýfed þæt hé his h&aelig-acute;le gefecce æt nánum stáne . . . sé ðe elles déð, hé beg&aelig-acute;ð untwýlíce h&aelig-acute;ðengild, Hml. Th. i. 474, 33. On þ&aelig-acute;re óþerre ylde man ár&aelig-acute;rde h&aelig-acute;ðengild wíde geond þás woruld, Ælfc. T. Grn. 4, 15: Jul. 15. I a. a particular form of idolatry :-- Tó manega of þám folce . . . tó þám h&aelig-acute;ðengilde bugon fliae Moab vocaverunt eos ad sacrificia sua. At illi comederunt et adoraverunt deos earum, Num. 25, 2: 31, 16. I b. idolatrous worship, an idolatrous rite or practice :-- Se mánfulla wolde his h&aelig-acute;þengild habban (celebrate his idolatrous worship,) Hml. S. 28, 26. Hí léton him betweónum tán wísian . . . hluton hellcræftum h&aelig-acute;ðengildum (with idolatrous rites) teledon betwínum, An. 1104. II. an idol. Cf. deófol-gild; II :-- Þá þe h&aelig-acute;ðengildum þeówiað idolis servientes, Hml. S. 17, 39. Bartholaméus þá h&aelig-acute;ðengild hýran ne wolde, wíg weorðian (cf. Hwí tówurpe ðú (St. Bartholomew) úre godas?, Hml. Th. i. 468, 16), Ap. 47. Oft hé h&aelig-acute;ðengield ofer word Godes weóh gesóhte, Jul. 22.
h&aelig-acute;þen-gilda. Add: gen. pl. -gilda :-- Se fæder ána h&aelig-acute;ðengilda wunode the father alone remained a heathen, Hml. Th. ii. 504, 7. Férde sum æðelboren man fram Alexandrian byrig tó Róme byrig Polemius geháten; sé wæs h&aelig-acute;þengilda, Hml. S. 35, 4. Eóden þá h&aelig-acute;ðengyldan intó heora temple clypigende tó ðám leásan gode, 4, 153. Se ealdorman wolde ðá h&aelig-acute;ðengildan forbærnan . . . 'Geðafiað húru þæt man heora &aelig-acute;hta eów sylle' . . . Þá wurdon getealde án hund þ&aelig-acute;ra h&aelig-acute;ðengylda þe ðæs temples gýmdon, and nán man ne mihte heora &aelig-acute;hta geríman, Hml. Th. ii. 484, 22. Hé ofslóh ðá h&aelig-acute;ðengildan (cf. deofolgildan, 112) he slew the priests of Baal, Hml. S. 18, 155.
h&aelig-acute;þenisc. Add: -- Þá wæs Hannibale æfter hiera h&aelig-acute;ðeniscum gewunan &thorn-bar; andwyrde swíþe láð abominatus dictum Annibal, Ors. 4, 10; S. 202, 6. Gé s&aelig-acute;don &thorn-bar; eów selfum w&aelig-acute;re betere &thorn-bar; gé eówerne crístendóm forléten and tó þ&aelig-acute;m h&aelig-acute;ðeniscan þeáwum fénge þe eówre ieldran &aelig-acute;r beeódon, 6, 37; S. 296, 21. [Icel. heiðneskr.]
h&aelig-acute;þen-mann. l. h&aelig-acute;þen mann. v. h&aelig-acute;þen; A. I. 1 b.
h&aelig-acute;þen-nes. Add: I. paganism: -- H&aelig-acute;ðennesse gentilitatis, Wrt. Voc. ii. 40, 30. Hé frægn hwæþer þá ylcan landleóde crístene w&aelig-acute;ron þe hí þá gýt on h&aelig-acute;þennesse gedwolum lifdan (an paganis adhuc erroribus essent implicati), Bd. 2, 1; Sch. 109, 19. Hé monige wæs gecígende fram h&aelig-acute;þenesse (h&aelig-acute;ðennesse, v. l.) and fram gedwolan heora lífes multos ab errore reuocans, 5, 11; Sch. 611, 5. II. people among whom (or district in which) heathenism prevails: -- Wit begétan ðás béc æt haeðnum herge mid uncre claene feó. And ðæt wit deodan . . . for ðon ðe wit nolðan ðæt ðás hálgan beoc lencg in ð&aelig-acute;re haeðenesse wunoden, Txts. 175, 4-7. [v. N. E. D. heathenesse.] v. h&aelig-acute;þen-dóm.
h&aelig-acute;þen-scipe. Add: I. the belief and practice of the heathen : --Mánfulles h&aelig-acute;þenscipes bígengcas fanatic&e-hook; gentilitatis ceremonias, An. Ox. 2623. Albanus gelýfde on ðone sóðan God, and wiðsóc þám h&aelig-acute;ðenscype, and wearð sóþlíce crísten, Hml. S. 19, 28. His fæder wæs . . . on h&aelig-acute;ðenscipe wunigende and his gemæcca samod, Hml. Th. ii. 498, 26. Hé áwende his móder of mánfullum h&aelig-acute;ðenscipe . . . and his fæder forwearð on fúlum h&aelig-acute;ðenscipe, 504, 5-11. Se geréfa þreátode hine tó h&aelig-acute;þenscipe, Shrn. 33, 10. Idele leóð þe ymbe h&aelig-acute;ðenscipe geworhte syndon, Hml. A. 142, 120. II. a particular form of heathen belief :-- Þá þrý cnihtas wiðcw&aelig-acute;don his (Nebuchadnezzar's) h&aelig-acute;þenscipe, Hml. A. 70, 131. III. the condition of being heathen :-- Heó nolde his sanda brúcan for his h&aelig-acute;ðenscipe (on account of his being a heathen), Hml. A. 110, 271. Heó nolde þurh his h&aelig-acute;þenscype habban &aelig-acute;nige synne, 115, 428. IV. a heathen practice :-- Þonne heó nele ábúgan tó nánum h&aelig-acute;ðenscipe, Hml. A. 28, 97. &AElig-acute;ghwylcne h&aelig-acute;ðenscype wordes and weorces forhogie man &aelig-acute;fre, id est idolatria et ueneficia, . . . , Wlfst. 73, 17. V. a time when (or place where) heathendom prevails :-- Þá þe secgaþ þæt þeós world sý nú wyrse on ðysan crístendóme þonne hió &aelig-acute;r on þ&aelig-acute;m h&aelig-acute;þenscype w&aelig-acute;re, Ors. 1, 8; S. 40, 25.
h&aelig-acute;þ-feld, es; m. Open uncultivated land, a heath :-- Tó m&aelig-acute;de, and se h&aelig-acute;ðfeld eal gem&aelig-acute;ne, C. D. v. 78, 32. On ðone h&aelig-acute;ðfeld, 177, 27. Úp on þone lytlan (printed hone lytland) h&aelig-acute;þfeld, C. D. B. i. 296, 25. Forheregian swá swá fýres lég déð drígne h&aelig-acute;þfeld, Bt. 16, 1; F. 50, 4. ¶ For the word as local name see C. D. vi. 294.
h&aelig-acute;þfeld-land, es; n. Moorland :-- Lindesfarona landes is syfan þú ILLEGIBLE end hýda mid h&aelig-acute;þfeldlande, C. D. B. i. 414, 18.
h&aelig-acute;ðiht. l. h&aelig-acute;þiht(e).
h&aelig-acute;ðung. Substitute: h&aelig-acute;þung, e; f. Parching or drying by heat :-- On ð&aelig-acute;re sunnan is h&aelig-acute;tu and beorhtnys; ac seó h&aelig-acute;tu drýgð, and seó beorhtnys onlýht. Óðer ðing déð seó h&aelig-acute;tu, and óðer seó beorhtnys, belimpð seó h&aelig-acute;ðung tó ð&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;tan, and seó onlíhting belimpð tó ð&aelig-acute;re beorhtnysse, Hml. Th. i. 284, 34-286, 4. v. h&aelig-acute;þan.
h&aelig-acute;ting. Add: Heating, warming: h&aelig-acute;ts, h&aelig-acute;tse. v. hægtesse.
hætsan. Add: , h&aelig-acute;tsan (?). Perhaps the word may be connected with h&aelig-acute;ts(e) ( v. hægtesse), cf. (?) later English hag to incite, urge. v. N. E. D.
hætt. v. hæt: hættende. v. hatian: hættian. Add: v. be-hættian.
h&aelig-acute;tu. Add: gen. e :-- H&aelig-acute;to calor. Wrt. Voc. i. 291, 11. I. the quality or property of being hot :-- On ð&aelig-acute;re sunnan is h&aelig-acute;tu and beorhtnys; seó h&aelig-acute;tu drýgð, Hml. Th. i. 284, 35. Þ&aelig-acute;re sunnan h&aelig-acute;tu wyrcð fíf d&aelig-acute;las on middanearde, Lch. iii. 260, 18 : Ph. 17. H&aelig-acute;to, Bl. H. 51, 21. Fýres h&aelig-acute;to, Dan. 262. Swíðe sweartes líchaman heó wæs for þ&aelig-acute;re sunnan h&aelig-acute;to, Hml. S. 23 b, 176. From haeto (calore) his, Ps. Srt. 18, 7. Þæs folces wæs fela forworden &aelig-acute;gðer ge for þurste ge for h&aelig-acute;te ( ardore solis), Ors. 6, 31; S. 286, 21. II. heat as an element in all bodies :-- Geðweorod sint . . . cele wið h&aelig-acute;to, w&aelig-acute;t wið drýgum, Met. 20, 73. Se cyle wið ðá h&aelig-acute;to and &thorn-bar; w&aelig-acute;t wið ðám drýgum, Bt. 33, 4; F. 128, 33: Met. 20, 113: 29, 50. III. a hot condition of the atmosphere, hot weather :-- Ðeostru and léht, cele and haetu (caumas), Ps. Srt. ii. p. 197, 32. Hý hit ne magon eall gebúgian, sum for h&aelig-acute;to, sum for cyle, Bt. 18, 1; F. 62, 10. &AElig-acute;lc wiht mæg bet wyð cyle þonne wið h&aelig-acute;te (omnia animantia patientius ad summum frigoris quam ad summum caloris accedant), Ors. 1,1; S. 24, 30. Feáwe men mehten beón eardfæste . . . for þ&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;te and for þ&aelig-acute;m stence . . . ge ealle þá fiscas ácw&e-acute-hook;lan for þ&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;te, 5, 4; S. 226, 2-7. Ic drífe sceáp míne tó heora l&aelig-acute;se, and stande ofer hig on h&aelig-acute;te (aestu) and on cyle, Coll. M. 20, 13. IV. of sexual passion :-- Seó gecyndelice h&aelig-acute;tu þurh &thorn-bar; mægen þæs Hálgan Gástes gestilleþ on þé (the Virgin Mary), Bl. H. 7, 27. V. great warmth of feeling, fervour :-- Se rehtgeleáfa mid haetu (calore) walle, Ps. Srt. ii. p. 201, 17. v. lencten-, sumer-h&aelig-acute;tu h&aelig-acute;te.
h&aelig-acute;tung. Dele.
h&aelig-acute;we; adj. Blue, grey :-- Haeuui, háui, heáwi cerula, Txts. 50, 221. Héuui vel gréi, háuui vel gréi, heáuui, gréi glaucum, 66, 473. h&aelig-acute;wen. Add: green :-- H&aelig-acute;wen oððe gr&aelig-acute;g gla[u]cum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 40, 72. Basu, h&aelig-acute;wen indicum, 49, 55. Gréne, h&aelig-acute;wen, fáh, deorc ceruleus, i. glaucus. Color est inter album et nigrum, subniger, 130, 34. H&aelig-acute;wen stán cyanea lapis, 137, 74. Þá h&aelig-acute;wnan s&aelig-acute;s marmora glauca, Wrt. Voc. ii. 90, 43. v. bl&aelig-acute;-, grén-, lín-, ILLEGIBLE sweart-, wel-h&aelig-acute;wen, and preceding word.
H&AElig-acute;WEN-GRÉNE -- HÁL 501
h&aelig-acute;wen-gréne; adj. Bluish green :-- Ðá h&aelig-acute;wengrénan ceruleus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 22, 38.
hafa. v. wan-hafa : hafe, Hpt. Gl. 504, 72. v. hafetian: hafecere. v. hafocere.
hafe-geat, es; n. A gate that has to be raised (?) :-- In tó hafegeæte; of hafegeæte, C. D. iv. 157, 11. Cf. tyrn-geat.
hafela. Add :-- Ne hédde hé þæs heafolan, B. 2697. Hé him of dyde helm of hafelan, 672 : 1521. Heáfde, heafolan (heofulan, lxx. 3) eágum capiti, fronti, oculis, Lch. i. lxxiv. 4. Men hafelan b&aelig-acute;ron . . . Grendles heáfod, B. 1635 : 1614. Hí Æscheres heafelan métton, 1421. Hé hafelan onhylde, Gú. 1244. Hí woldon on þám hysebeorðre heafolan gescénan, An. 1144. Hét Hildeburh hire suna sweoloðe befæstan . . . hafelan multon, B. 1120. Se beorhta beág . . . eádigra gehwám hlifað ofer heáfde. Heafelan líxað þrymme biþeahte, Ph. 604. v. wíg-heafola.
hafenian. Add: The meaning 'grasp, hold' seems supported by 0. H. Ger. hebinóa tractare, inthepinót pin sustentor, but in later English heven means to raise, a sense which would suit the passages. v. N. E. D. heven (where is quoted Noe hiuened up an auter, Allit. Pms. 53, 506).
-hafen-ness. v. á-, úp-hafenness.
hafetian. Add: , hafettan, haftian :-- Ic hafetige (afetige, hafecige, v. ll.) oððe fægnige plaudo, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 171, 7. Hafet plaudet, Kent. Gl. 611. Flódas feágað &l-bar; hafetiað flumina plaudent, Ps. L. 97, 8. Gilpað &l-bar; gulpan, hafe[tiað, -ttað ?] applaudunt, Hpt. Gl. 504, 72. Hafetiað mid handum plaudite manibus, Ps. L. 46, 2. Haftud plauditur, Germ. 394, 220. v. beaftan.
-hafness. v. wan-hafness.
hafocere. Take here hafecere in Dict., and add :-- Hafocere falconus. Wrt. Voc. ii. 147, 3.
hafocung, e; f. Hawking :-- On hafocunga leáhge, C. D. B. i. 280, 26.
-hafol. v. fæst-, wan-hafol: -hafolness. v. wan-hafolness: hafud-æcer, -land. v. heáfod-æcer, -land.
haga. Add: I. a fence or a fenced enclosure :-- Haga sepis (spinarum), Kent. Gl. 527. Fram earnes beáme Cregsétna haga an eást&dash-uncertain;halfe scéd hit tó Liówsandene . . . fram swelgende Cregsétna haga tó sioxslihtre, C. D. ii. 73, 25-28 : iii. 227, 20-23. Þ&aelig-acute;r se haga út ligeþ, Cht. E. 294, 23. Swá se haga scýt secundum quod sepes declinat, C. D. B. ii. 386, 20. Andlang hagan oð cyninges healh . . . oð þone hagan, C. D. i. 257, 33-258, 1 (and often). On ðone hagan tó pitan wyrðe . . . ofer þone feld on hagan . . . anlang herepaðes tó ðas hagan ænde, v. 13, 23-28. Úp on Afene oð ðæt ðe se alda suínhæga út scióteð tó Afene; ðonne be ð&aelig-acute;m hagan, ii. 29, 11. Inn on bróc; of ðám bróke inn on ðone hagan: æfter ðám hagan, iii. 382, 14. On ðone healdan hagan, v. 273, 6. II. an enclosed dwelling in a town :-- In ciuitate Dorouernia duas possessiunculas et tertiam dimediam, id est in nostra loquella ðridda half haga, C. D. i. 243, 13. Duas mansiones et dimidiam quod Angli dicunt þridda hialf haga, v. 68, 24. Unam uillam quod nos Saxonico án haga dicimus, ii. 57, 19. Se haga an Hámtúne, iii. 443, 16. Ðis is ðes hagan embegang circuitus eiusdem hospicii, vi. 135, 14. Ðis is ðæs hagan bóc on Winceastre, 136, 10. Cum nouem praefatae ciuitatis habitaculis, quae patria lingua Hagan appellari solent, iii. 297, 11. Twégen hagan binnan þorte, Cht. E. 239, 16. v. bóc-, deór-, gem&aelig-acute;r- (v. gem&aelig-acute;re; II. ¶), heáfod-, imb-, m&aelig-acute;r-, wulf-haga; hæg.
haga a berry. Add: I. a haw :-- Hagan cinum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 131, 11. [Cinus an haythorne and an hawe, Wlck. Gl. 572, 45.] II. used as a type of a thing of no value :-- Hagan gignalia, Wrt. Voc. ii. 42, 16.
-haga. v. án-haga.
hagal (-ol, -ul). Add: [m. and] n. (v. Ps. L. 147, 17). I. hawl (v. N. E. D. hail) :-- 'Ic sende micelne hagol . . . sweltað ealle þá þing þe úte beóð and se hagol him onufan fealð.' . . . Drihten sende hagul, Ex. 9, 18-23. Eall þæt se hagol l&aelig-acute;fde, 10, 15. Ic ásende &aelig-acute;lcne untíman, þæt bið egeslíce greát hagol, sé fordéð eówre wæstmas . . . , Wlfst. 297, 7. On hagule in pruina, Bl. Gl. I a. n. A hailstone: -- Hé ásendeþ gycelstán his swá swá hagalu (buccellas), Ps. L. 147, 17. II. a hail-storm: -- Smelt hagol imber serotinus, Kent. Gl. 560. Hagelum &l-bar; scúrum imbribus, An. Ox. 360.
hagalian. Add: -- Hit hagolade seofon niht ofer ealle Rómáne per septem dies grando lapidum terram verberavit, Ors. 5, 10; Swt. 234, 6
hagal-scúr Add :-- Ne bið þ&aelig-acute;r hagulscúras hearde mid snáwe non veniet . . . nix, grando, procella, Dóm. L. 264.
hagal-stán. v. hagol-stán: haga-þorn. v. hagu-þorn : hagian to please. Add: v. ge-, of-hagian: hagian to fence. v. ymb-hagian.
hagol-stán. Add :-- Ic sende ofer eów hagelstánas, and &aelig-acute;lc án hagel&dash-uncertain;stán wegeð fíf pund, Wlfst. 228, 6. Cymð rén and hagolstánas ofer eów, 212, 24.
hago-spind; m. a. ?1.UNCERTAIN n., and add :-- Feger is leúr &l-bar; higospind ðín pulchra est gena tua, Rtl. 4, 1. Heagospind genae, Wrt. Voc. ii. 41, 21. Heagospinnum genis, Lch. i. lxx, 5, : lxxiv, 6. Heagaspen genas, Wrt. Voc. ii. 109, 62. Haguspind oððe þunwange malas, 57, 30. Hé his eagospind mid teárum leohte lacrymarum rivulis genas rigavit, Guth. Gr. 162, 34. v. spind.
hago-steald; adj. Young and brave, warrior :-- Æðelum kinge hýrdon holdlíce hagestealde men, Chr. 1065; P. 192, 39. v. hæg-steald; adj.
hago-stealdmonn. Add: v. hægsteald-mann.
Hagustaldes-eá, -hám Hexham. Substitute :-- Hagustaldes-eá, Chr. 681: 766: 685. Hagstaldes-ee, Hagustaldee, 780. Hagustaldes-ee, Hagustaldee, 789. Eanberht Hagestaldes biscop, Hagusteald b&s-tilde; &l-bar; of Hagestaldes-ee, 806. Mon gehálgode on Agustald tó biscope, 685. Sum Godes þeów of þám bróþrum þ&aelig-acute;re cyricean æt Heagostealdes-eá (Hæge&dash-uncertain;stealdes-, Agostaldes-, v. ll. ) quidam de fratribus Hagustaldensis ecclesiae, Bd. 3, 2; Sch. 196, 19. Tó cyricean [tó] Heagostealdes- (Hægestealdes-, v. l.) eá, 4, 12 ; Sch. 414, 18 : 5, 23; Sch. 691, 18. Hé Cúðberht gehálgode tó biscope tó Hagustaldes-hám, Chr. 685. v. hæg-steald.
hagu-þorn (hago-), es; m. A hawthorn. Take here haga-þorn in Dict., and add :-- Hagudorn, heagoðorn alba spina, Txts. 36, 19.
hal a corner. v. healh.
hál. Add: I. whole, (1) not divided :-- Gif hit tód&aelig-acute;led biþ, þonne ne biþ hit nó hál, Bt. 34, 12 ; F. 152, 28. (2) with no part wanting: -- Befeste þé hálne Gode Deo te totum committe, Solil. H. 53, 12. II. of physical well-being. (1) whole, hale, sound, in good health. (a) of a living thing :-- Hé is gít hál and gesund viget incolumis, Bt. 10: F. 28, 14. UNCERTAIN Þú eart swíþe gesélig nú þú gít liofost and eart hál, 35. &AElig-acute;lc wuht wolde bión hál and libban ðára þe mé cwica ðincþ, 34, 10; F. 148, 15. Cild full hál and full ælt&aelig-acute;we geboren, 38, 3; F. 200, 22. For hwí se góda l&aelig-acute;ce selle ðám hálum men séftne drenc and óþrum hálum strangne, 39, 9; F. 226, 11. Ne mæg se unhála þám hálan gelíce byrðene áhebban. Ll. Th. i. 412, 8. Hig gemétton hálne (sanum) þone þe &aelig-acute;r untrum wæs, Lk. 7, 10. Ne beþurfon ná ðá hálan (sani) l&aelig-acute;ces, Mk. 2, 17. Ðá hálan (ðá truman, 5) incolumes, Past. 247, 3. Nys hálum valentibus) ERROR l&aelig-acute;ces nán þearf, ac seócum, Mt. 9, 12. Sume mid þ&aelig-acute;re ráde earniaþ &thorn-bar; hié sién ðý hálran, Bt. 34, 7; F. 144, 8. (b) of a part of a living thing :-- Næfð nán man tó þæs hál eágan þæt . . . , Solil. H. 34, 21. Swá swá þæs líchoman æágan hálren beóð, 44, 27. Þám æallra hálestum æágum, 47, 9. (b α) figurative :-- &THORN-bar; hé beleác on hálre tungon (in plain, unequivocal language. The later Latin version renders the passage: Qui statim conclusit et omnino confirmavit totum quod pater suus in vita sua fecerat), Cht. E. 212, 9. Forgif ús hále eágan úres modes, Bt. 33, 4; F. 132, 31. (c) of a person's condition :-- Be his hálan lýfe while in a sound state of health, Chr. 614; P. 22, 22 : 616 ; P. 22, 34: 1052; P. 183, 17. (2) uninjured :-- Nó þý &aelig-acute;r inn gescód hálan líce, B. 1503. Hál and unscendede hond gil&aelig-acute;de salvam et inlesam, manum educat, Rtl. 102, 37. Hyssas hále hwurfon in þám hátan ofne, Dan. 271. (3) where health is gained, freed from sickness, cured, whole after injury :-- Ic beó hál (salva) gyf ic hys reáfes æthríne, Mt. 9, 21. &thorn-bar; heó hál (salva) sý and lybbe, Mk. 5, 23. Hál bið (byð geh&aelig-acute;led, W. S. sanabitur) cnæht mín. Lk. L. 7, 7. Gif hé sl&aelig-acute;pð, hé byþ hál (saluus), Jn. 11, 12. Dryhten wine sínne grétte, . . . héht his líchoman háles brúcan . . . Árás þá mægene róf . . . hál, næs him gewemmed wlite, . . . bán gebrocen, An. 1472. Hálne valentem sospitem (Ald, 40, 1), Wrt. Voc. ii. 81, 4. Hié hine on róde áhéngan . . . hé hine hálne and gesundne ðý ðriddan dæge æteówde, Bl. H. 177, 27. Þín (the blind man's) geleáfa þé hálne (saluum) gedyde, Mk. 10, 52. Hí wurdon hále salui fiebant, Mk. 6, 56. Hálum monnum sanatis hominibus, Mt. p. 15, 19. (3 a) of a part of a living body :-- Þæt m&aelig-acute;den (a girl born dumb) hæfde hire spr&aelig-acute;ce mid hálre tungan, Hml. S. 31, 1118. Hálne incolumem (pupillam evulsam), An. Ox. 3471. (3 b) where the sickness from which a person is freed is given, (α) with gen. :-- Hé byþ þæs sáres hál, Lch. i. 352, 2. (β) with inst. :-- Hé biþ ece hál, Lch. ii. 308, 2. (γ) with prep. :-- Hál from februm (ridesohte, R.), Mk. 1, 31. Hál uére (wearþ geh&aelig-acute;led, W. S.) from ádle sanus fiebat a languore, Jn. L. R. 5, 4. Hé wæs hál geworden of ðám eórede sanus factus est a legione, Lk. 8, 36. III. of mental health, sane, sound (mind): -- Wód rabidus vel insanus, hál sanus, Wrt. Voc. i. 75, 57. Hál angyt, Solil. H. 28, 3. Háles módes sane mentis, Mk. 5, 15. Hálum móde sana mente, Lk. 8, 35. Þú &aelig-acute;r witan scalt hweðer wit hále sién videamus utrum sani smus, Solil. H. 32, 13. Andgit swá swá þæt hálre byð swá hyt máre geseón mæg þ&aelig-acute;re &aelig-acute;cean sunnan, 45, 2. IV. of moral or spiritual health :-- Dóð eówre heortan hige hále and cl&aelig-acute;ne, Ps. Th. 61, 8. V. safe. (1) from temporal danger. (α) secure against impending danger :-- Gefultuma mé, ðonne beó ic hál (salvus ero), Ps. Th. 118, 117. Dryhten, dó mé hálne Domine, salvum me fac, 117, 23. (β) uninjured by danger incurred, saved from peril :-- Búton þá dagas gescyrte w&aelig-acute;run, n&aelig-acute;re nán mann hál geworden (non fíeret salva omnis caro), Mt. 24, 22. &THORN-bar; hit mæge hál and orsorg fleógan tó his earde ut perturbatione depulsa sospes in patriam revertaris, Bt. 36, 1 ; F. 172, 33. Hé þone hilder&aelig-acute;s hál gedígeð, B. 300: Gn. Ex 106. Gedó mé hálne, álýs mé fram láðum, UNCERTAIN Ps. Th. 53, 1. Þá hé wearð
502 -HALA -- HÁLIG
gedofen hé cwæð, 'Drihten, gedó mé hálne,' Mt. 14, 30. Óðero hálo dyde, hine seolfne ne mæge hálne dóa, Mt. L. 27, 42. Hé hyne hálne geféng, Lk. 15, 27. (ββ) with gen. of peril from which one is saved. Cf. II. 3 b :-- Hé lifigende cwóm heaðoláces hál tó hofe gongan, B. 1974. (2) saved from spiritual danger :-- Sé ðe þurhwunað oð ende, sé byð hál (salvus), Mt. 24, 13 : 10, 22. Hwá mæg hál beon ?, Mt. R. L. 19, 25. Sé þe gelýfð and gefullod biþ, sé biþ hál, Mk. 16, 16. Hé hys folc hál gedéð fram hyra synnum, Mt. 1, 21. God wile &thorn-bar; ealle menn hále beón, Hml. S. 30, 92: Lk. 8, 12. VI. in forms of greeting. (1) with verb :-- Hál westú, Maria ave, Maria, Bl. H. 143, 17: Lch. iii. 54, 18. Wes þú, Hróðgár, hál, B. 407. (2) alone :-- Hál (hál beó þú, W. S.), láruwa have, Rabbi, Mt. L. R. 26, 49. Hál (hál wæs þú, W. S. ), cynig Júdéana, 27, 29 : Mk. L. R. 15, 18 : Lk. L. R. 1, 28. v. hæg-, sám-, wan-hál.
-hala. v. ge-hala.
halan. Substitute for 'halan . . . afterbirth': hala, an ; m. The after-birth; secundae, secundina (cf. cild-hama secundae, Wlck. Gl. 159, 31 : secundina pellis in qua concipitur infans, 677, 42), and add: [cf. O. H. Ger. halu tegmine.]
hál-b&aelig-acute;re. For ' Scint. . . . Lye' substitute: (1) of things :-- Gesceád hálbiére ratio salutaris, Scint. 206, 14. Síþfætes h&aelig-acute;lb&aelig-acute;res itineris salutaris, 206, 17. Him hí syllan andetnesse hálb&aelig-acute;rne l&aelig-acute;cedóm sibi dent confessionis salubre remedium, Angl. xiii. 394, 408. Hálb&aelig-acute;re salutiferam, Germ. 389, 6. (2) of persons, that promotes the well-being of others : -- Freónd hálb&aelig-acute;rne ic ná gescynde amicum salutarem non confundor, Scint. 195, 11.
hálettan. Add: , h&aelig-acute;lettan :-- Gif gé hálettaþ (salutaveritis) eówre bróþer, Mt. R. 5, 47. H&aelig-acute;leteþ þæt hús salutate domum, 10, 12. Þá se biscop tó mé cwóm, ðá grétte hé mé sóna and [h]álette his leódþeáwe cum me more rituque salutaret, Nar. 27, 17. Ic, Béda, Crístes ðeów and mæssepreóst, sende grétan þone leófastan cyning and hálettan Ceólwulf gloriosissimo regi Ceoluulfo Baeda famulus Christi et Presbyter, Bd. praef.; Sch. 1. 3. [O. H. Ger. heilazen salutare.] v. ge-hálettan.
hálettend. Add: cf. scyte-finger.
hál-fæst. For 'Lye' substitute :-- His sáule gyltas . . . onwreoða . . . suman swá gástlicum bréðer þe hálfæst sý and his sáule wundela geh&aelig-acute;lan cunne (spiritali seniori qui sciat curare sua vulnera), R. Ben. 72, 6.
hálga. Add: -- Þú eart Godes hálga, Mk. 1, 24. Wé sungon be eallum hálgum cantavimus de omnibus sanctis, Coll. M. 33, 27. v. sundor-hálga.
hálgian. Add: I. to make holy, sanctify :-- Hálgig &l-bar; hálga ðú (gehálga, W. S., R.) hiá . . . Fore him ic hálgiga (hálgige, W. S., gihálgo, R.) mec seolfne sanctifica eos . . . pro eis ego sanctifico me ipsum, Jn. L. 17, 17-19. II .to consecrate, set apart as sacred to God, dedicate to a religious office or use :-- On þissum geáre man hálgode þet mynster æt Westmynster . . . hine man bebyrgede innan þ&aelig-acute;re níwan hálgodre circean on Westmynstre, Chr. 1066; P. 195, 3-197, 2. Ciricean hálgian, Bl. H. 205, 24. II a. to consecrate a person to an office :-- Þeodorus biscop hine hálgode, Chr. 670; P. 35, 17. Þís ilcan geáre man gehálgode Tatwine tó arcebiscop . . . hine hálgodan Daniel and Ingwold . . . and Aldwine . . . and Aldulf, 731; P. 45, 8. Hine man hálgode tó cinge, Ll. Lbmn. 214, 25. II b. to bless a thing so that it possesses special virtue :-- Þú sunnandæg sylf hálgodest and gem&aelig-acute;rsodest hine manegum tó helpe, Hy. 9, 25. Gif hwá ordáles weddige þonne cume hé . . . tó þ&aelig-acute;m mæssepreóste þe hit hálgian scyle, Ll. Th. i. 210, 27. Háligende exorcizans (vir Deo deditus liquidas fontium limphas exorcizans et sacrae benedictionis ubertate foecundans, Ald. 37, 30), Wrt. Voc. ii. 80, 42. Hálgiende, 31, 11. II b β. to consecrate the Eucharistic elements :-- Swá oft swá man húsel hálgað, Ll. Th. i. 360, 33. III. to honour as holy :-- Hy. 5, 2 (in Dict.). IV. to keep a day holy, Bl. H. 37, 32 (in Dict.). v. ge-hálgian, un-hálgod.
hálgung. Add: I. consecration. v. hálgian; II :-- Ne sind ealle cyricean ná gelícre m&aelig-acute;ðe weoruldlíce wurðscipes wyrðe, þeáh hig godcundlíce hálgunge habban gelíce, Ll. Th. i. 360, 17. I a. consecration of a person to an office. v. hálgian ; II a :-- Hér forðférde bisceop Aðelwold, and seó hálgung þæs æfterfilgendon bisceopes . . . wæs xiii. Kt. UNCERTAIN Noú, UNCERTAIN Chr. 984; P. 124, 3. Þ&aelig-acute;r w&aelig-acute;ron æt his hálgunge twégen ercebisceopas, 979; P. 122, 23. I b. blessing that imparts special virtue. v. hálgian; II b :-- Hálgunge gecrístnad exorcismi catacizatus (ecclesiastico exorcismo catechizatus, Ald. 57, 24), Wrt. Voc. ii. 84, 55 : 31, 12. Ná béte nán man &thorn-bar; fýr (the fire at the ordeal) ná længe þonne man þá hálgunge onginne, Ll. Th. i. 226, 26. I b β. consecration of the Eucharistic elements, v. hálgian ; II b β :-- Micel is seó hálsung and m&aelig-acute;re is seó hálgung þe deófla áfyrsað . . . swá oft swá man fullað oþþe húsel hálgað, Ll. Th. i. 360, 32. II. hallowing, holding in honour as holy. v. hálgian; III :-- Seó hálgung þæs m&aelig-acute;ran naman Godes ongann ús mannum þá þá Críst wearð gefl&aelig-acute;schamed ; ac seó ylce hálgung wunað on écnysse, for ðan ðe wé on ðám écan lífe bletsiað and herigað &aelig-acute;fre Godes naman, Hml. Th. i. 270, 20 -- 23. v. ciric-, crism-, fant-, ge-, getimber-, healh-(?), húsel-, sealt-, templ-, wæter-hálgung.
hálgung-bóc a benedictional :-- Ic eom hálguingbóc, healde hine Dryhten þe mé fægere þus frætewum belegde, Nap. 35.
hálian. Add: , hálig(e)an. I. of physical health, to heal (intrans.). (1) the subject a person, to recover from wounds or illness :--Hé ongan trumian and háligean sanescere coepit, Bd. 4, 22 ; Sch. 456, 11. (2) the subject a body or part of it :-- Ðonne cólað se líchoma and hálað, Lch. i. 82, 10. Smyre &thorn-bar; neb mid; þonne sméþað hyt and hálað, 86, 9. Smyre Þá sáran góman mid oþ &thorn-bar; hý háligen, 348, 17. (3) the subject a wound, sore, &c. :-- Lege on þá wunde; þonne hálað heó sóna, Lch. i. 88, 23. Sió wunde wolde háligean (hálian, v. l.), æfter ð&aelig-acute;m ðe hió wyrmsde, Past. 258, 1. (4) the subject an indefinite hit :-- Gif men his leoðu acen . . . ðonne hálað hyt sóna (cf. gif hund man tóslíte . . . ðonne bið hit sóna hál, 15), Lch. i. 86, 23, 4. Wyrc him sealfe ðæt hit hálige, iii. 40, 16. II. to be saved. v. hál; V. 2 :-- Geþencean wé eác, gif óþer nýten w&aelig-acute;re tó háligienne and geteód tó þon écan lífe, þonne onfénge hé (Christ) heora híwe, Bl. H. 29, 5. [O. H. Ger. heilén sanescere.] v. ge-, wan-hálian.
hálig. Add; A. adjectival. I. set apart for religious use, consecrated, sacred :-- Hálig leger cimiterium, Wrt. Voc. i. 34, 9. Seó stów þe þú on stynst ys hálig eorðe (sancta terra), Ex. 3, 5. Æfter gewuna dæges hálges (diei festi), Lk. L. R. 2, 42. On dæge háligum (hálgum, R.), Mk. L. 14, 2. On hálgum beorge in monte sancto, Ps. Th. 98, 10. On háligre stówe, Mt. 24, 15. On þá hálgan ceastre, 4, 5. On &thorn-bar; hálige templ, Bl. H. 71, 17. Hálig tiber, Exod. 415. Hálige dagas kalendae, Wrt. Voc. i. 53, 35. Húslfatu hálegu, Dan. 705. Is þeós tíd ealra tíd héhst and hálgost, Bl. H. 83, 19. Alh heáhst and h&aelig-acute;ligost, Exod. 394. Betwux ðám hálegestan (hálgestan, v. l.) hálignessum, Past. 135, 9. I a. where the person to whom a thing is dedicated, in respect to whom a thing is holy, is given :-- &AElig-acute;lc w&aelig-acute;pned byð Drihtne hálig (sanctum) genemned, Lk. 2, 23: El. 1195. Hé wæs sácerd in þ&aelig-acute;re hálgan cirican, seó wæs hálig þ&aelig-acute;re eádigan f&aelig-acute;mnan, Gr. D. 88, 4. On þone Drihten þe þes háligdóm is fore hálig, Ll. Th. i. 178, 3, 12. Intó Níwan mynstre &aelig-acute;nne sylfrene hwer on þ&aelig-acute;re hálgan þrynnesse naman þe seó stów is fore hálig (cf. wið Godd geborgen and Scs UNCERTAIN Ióhannes and ealra ð&aelig-acute;ra hálgena þe seó hálige stóww is fore gehálgod, 391, 26), Cht. Th. 559, 1. II. used of Deity ; -- Hálig, hálig, hálig, Drihten God allmæhtig. Mt. p. 10, 7 : Gen. 97: 642 : Ps. Th. 98, 9. Hálig is heofonríces Weard, 10. Háliga Fæder Pater Sancte, Jn. 17, 11. Hálig Godes Sunu, Bl. H. 7, 24. Þú eart þæt hálige lamb, Hy. 8, 22. Se Hálega (Hálga, v. l.) G&aelig-acute;sð, Past. 93, 1. On þ&aelig-acute;re hálgan þrynnesse naman, Cht. Th. 558, 36. Úres þæs hálgan Godes Dei nostri, Ps. Th. 133, 2. II a. of a heathen deity :-- God, héhst and hálgost (Jupiter), Met. 26, 38. III. of persons considered to be specially devoted to, or directed by, God, e.g. angels, prophets, apostles, saints; the epithet tends to become a mere title, cf. saint, reverend :-- Sió hálge gecynd angels, Cri. 1018. Se háliga (hálga, v. l.) wer (Moses), Past. 51, 17: (Nathan), 185, 22 : (St. Paul), 99, 17 : (St. Andrew), An. 168 : (St. Guthlac), Gú. 79. Se hálga Béda, Hml. S. 26, 272. Heáhfæderas hálige, An. 877. Hálige wítigan, Sat. 460. Þá gesetton hálige fæderas and Godes folces láreówas þá tíd þæs fæstenes, Bl. H. 27, 25. Þá háligan martyras, Bt. 11. 2; F. 36, 5. Mid hálgum englum, Mk. 8, 38. III a. used of any part of such persons :-- Se hálga innoð þ&aelig-acute;re á cl&aelig-acute;nan, Bl. H. 11. 20. Hálgan stefne, Exod. 257 ; An. 56. Martiras herigað Héhfæder hálgum stefnum, Sat. 656: An. 723. Hé (St. Guthlac) his eágan ontýnde hálge heáfdes gimmas, Gú. 1276. IV. of things. (1) that pertain to God :-- Is þín nama hálig, An. 542. Seó ród . . . hálig, El. 625. Ð&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;lga ródes sancte crucis, Rtl. 94, 9 : 120, 9. Of his þám heán hálgan setle de excelso sancto suo, Ps. Th. 101, 17 : Gen. 260. Hé þé gebohte blóde þý hálgan, Seel. 30. Flód wæs ád&aelig-acute;led hálgum mihtum, Gen. 151. (2) that have their origin or sanction from God :-- Hálig gewrit sancta scriptura, Wrt. Voc. ii. 6, 2. Háliges gewrites scripturae, An. Ox. 40, 7. Hé (Peter) onféng ðone ealdordóm ð&aelig-acute;re hálgan ciericean, Past. 115, 8. On cyrclicere &l-bar; háligere hálsunge ecclesiastico i. sancto exorcismo, An. Ox. 4082. Hé hí heofonhláfe hálige (pane caeli) gefylde, Ps. Th. 104, 35. Þis hálige godspel, Bl. H. 15, 30. Þurh &thorn-bar; hálige fulwiht, 77, 3. Gif gé gehealdað hálige láre, Exod. 560. Þurh þín hálig word, An. 1420. Gástgifu vel háligu carismata, dona, Wrt. Voc. ii. 129, 5. Hálige gewreotu, Bl. H. 17, 21. (3) of divine operations (ordinary or extraordinary) in the physical world :-- Wæs hálig leóht ofer wéstenne, swá se wyrhta bebeád, Gen. 124. Cóm morgen . . . hálig of heolstre, An. 243. Cóm wuldres tácen hálig of heofenum swylce hádre sægl, 89: 1020. Hálig God oferbr&aelig-acute;dde hálgan nette (the pillar of cloud) hát&dash-uncertain;wendne lyft, Exod. 74. Hálge gimmas, sunne and mona, Cri. 692. Hihte ic tó þínra handa hálgum d&aelig-acute;dum in operibus manuum tuarum exultabo, Ps. Th. 91, 3. V. conformed to the will of God, free from sinful affection. (1) of persons, of godly character and life :-- &AElig-acute;lc gefullod man sý æfter his fulluhte hálig, Wlfst. 154, 19. &THORN-bar; n&aelig-acute;re n&aelig-acute;fre n&aelig-acute;nig tó þæs hálig mon, Bl. H. 117, 26. Hé wiste &thorn-bar; hé wæs
HÁLIG-DÆG -- HÁLSIAN 503
rihtwís and hálig, Mk. 6, 20. Hié (Abraham and Sarah) s&aelig-acute;ton bútú hálig on hige, Gen. 2780. Hié wilniað ðæt hié mon hæbbe for ðá betstan and ðá hálgestan, Past. 135, 20. (1 a) used of any part of such persons :-- Herian God hálgum reorde, Hy. 3, 58. Eorþe wældreóre swealh hálge, Gen. 1017. Manige hálige líchaman multa corpora sanctorum, Mt. 27, 52. (2) of actions, feelings, &c.:-- Biþ &thorn-bar; cl&aelig-acute;ne fæsten and hálig, Bl. H. 37, 31. Hálegu treów, Gen. 2118. H&aelig-acute;lges hygtes sanctae spei, Rtl. 3, 26. Hálgan hyhtes, Cri. 58. Hálgum sanctae (uirginitati), An. Ox. 960. Hálgum sige sancta uictoria, 2936. Be hálgum lífe de conuersatione, 4533. Fæsten and hálige wæccan, Bl. H. 73, 27. Þæt wé tó þám hýhstan hrófe gestígan hálgum weorcum, Cri. 750. Þ&aelig-acute;r þ&aelig-acute;r mon mete and drync for sóðre Godes lufan seleð, hyt bið swíðe gód weorc, and hit bið gemong óðrum hálgum weorcum geteald, Ll. Th. ii. 432, 15. VI. of animals, not destructive or dangerous, tame cattle us opposed to wild beasts :-- Inc is hálig feoh and wilde deór on geweald geseald, Gen. 201. B. substantival. I. that which is holy, a holy thing. Cf. A. I :-- Húse þínum hálig gedafenað domum tuam decent sancta, Ps. Th. 92, 7. Þæt weófod bið hálegra hálig altare erit sanctum sanctorum, Ex. 29, 37. &THORN-bar; hálige ðe of þé ácenned býð that holy thing that shall be born of thee, Lk. 1, 35. Ne sellað gé hálig (&thorn-bar; hálige, W. S. sanctum) hundum, Mt. R. L. 7, 6. II. a holy place :-- Ic ðé on hálgum ætýwe in sancto apparui tibi, Ps. Th. 62, 2. III. a holy person. (1) of a divine person. Cf. A. II :-- Háliges (Christ's) hyhtplega, Cri. 737. Gréne stondað gehroden háliges meahtum beorhtast bearwa, Ph. 79: Met. 29, 55: Ps. Th. 113, 2. Hálges, Th. 399: Gú. 814. Gif wé ús tó þám hálgan(Christ) helpe geléfað, Sat. 291. Hálgostes bl&aelig-acute;d on blá[wende] Sacrosancti flatus (i. spiritus) inspirans, An. Ox. 1526. (2) a saint, prophet, &c. Cf. A. III :-- Hé(St. Matthew) gesch sw&aelig-acute;sne geféran (St. Andrew), hálig háligne, An. 1012, Heó (St. Juliana) þæt deófol teáh, . . . hálig h&aelig-acute;ðenne, Jul. 536. Seó hálge ongon frignan, 345: 589. Háliges (Moses') láre, Exod. 307 : (St. Andrew's), An. 895 : 1391. Hálges (St. Guthlac's) lára, Gú. 979. Háligre (St. Juliana's) fæder, Jul. 61. Wearð þ&aelig-acute;re hálgan hyht geníwad, 607. Þæt þám hálgan (Noah) wæs sár on móde, Gen. 1592 : An. 48. Þ&aelig-acute;re hálgan, Jul. 246. Englas and heáhfæderas and wítgan and ealle hálige, Bl. H. 103, 33. Hálge and gecorene, Past. 467, 32. Hí hálge cwelmdon, bærndon gecorene, Jul. 15. (3) a godly person. Cf. A. V. I :-- Þurh Crístes sige ealle hálige w&aelig-acute;ron gefreólsode, þá þe him þeówiaþ on hálignesse, Bl. H. 31, 33. Eardungstów Godes his hálgan (sancti eius) synt, An. Ox. 40, 38. On gesyhðe þára háligra ante conspectum sanctorum, Ps. Th. 51, 8. Háligra helm, Cri. 529. Scyldigra scolu áscyred weorðeð from hálgum, 1609. Þinum þám hálgum, Ps. Th. 73, 4. Ne forl&aelig-acute;t God n&aelig-acute;fre his hálge, 36, 27. Mánfulle . . . hálige under heora fótum þryccaþ. Bt. 4; F. 8, 14. Hí þíne hálgan yfeladan, Ps. Th. 82, 3. IV. a sacred rite (?), consecration :-- Níuæs timbredes húses hálgum (hálgung?) encenia, Jn. p. 6, 6. v. eall-, efen-, fant-, gást-, heofon-, þurh-, un ERROR hálig.
hálig-dæg. Add: -- Giwarð háligdæg (-doeg, L. ) facto sabbato, Mk. R. 6, 2.
hálig-dóm. Add: I. holiness, sanctity. (1) of human beings. Cf. hálig; A. III, V :-- Háligdóm is fullneáh ásprungen and sóðfæstnes swýðe gelytlod defecit sanctum, diminutae sunt veritates, Ps. Th. II, l. Háligdómes sanctimonie (Christus, zelotypus sanctimoniae informator, Ald. 6, 35), Wrt. Voc. ii. 75, 58. Hé for his háligdómes (sanctitatis) mycelnesse wearð manigra mynstra fæder, Gr. D. 26, 13: 246, 22. (2) of the Deity. Cf. A. II :-- Bespreng mé mid þínum háligdóme, swá swá mid ýsopon, þæt ic beó gecl&aelig-acute;nsod, Ps. Th. 50, 8. II. a holy thing, something held sacred. (1) from its connexion with the Deity :-- Beforan ð&aelig-acute;re earce ðe se háligdóm (the two tables of stone) on wæs ðæs temples coram testamenti arca, Past. 103, 5. (2) from its connexion with Christ or a saint, a relic or collection of relics. (a) a single relic: -- Hér swutelað be þám hálgum reliquium þe Æþelstán geaf in tó sancta Marian mynstre on Exancestre . . . Nú wille wé eów segcan . . . hwæt ánra gehwilc þéra háligdóma beó. &AElig-acute;rost of þám sylfan deórwyrðan treówe þ&aelig-acute;re hálgan róde . . . , C. D. B. ii. 389, 3-38. (b) a collection of relics :-- Se ilca kyning &AElig-acute;þelstán sende ofer s&aelig-acute; getríwe men and gesceádwíse and hig férdon swá wíðe landes swá hig faran mihton and begeáton þá deórwurðestan mádmas þe &aelig-acute;fre ofer eorðan begitene mihton beón, &thorn-bar; wæs háligdóm se m&aelig-acute;sta of gehwilcum stówum wýdan and sýdan gegaderod . . . Hé . . . þone þryddan d&aelig-acute;l þæs fores&aelig-acute;dan háligdómes þyder inn (into St. Peter's Minster at Exeter) lét dón . . . eallum þám tó hylpe þe þá hálgan stówwe þe se haligdóm on is mid geleáfan gesécað. Nú wille wé eów segcan . . . hwæt se háligdóm is . . . &AElig-acute;rost . . . , C. D. B. ii. 389, 19-39. Hæbbe hé Godes unmiltse and æalles ðæs háligdómes (cf. ic eów hálsige fer ealle ðá hálgan reliquias ðe gind ealne middangeard sindon, Rtl. 114, 18) ðe ic (Æthelstan) on Angelcyn begeat, 315, 22. Hire scrín mid hiræ háligdóme, C. D. iii. 360, 8. Sende Benedictus tw&aelig-acute;gen his muneca tó Maure mid lácum, &thorn-bar; is mid háligdóme of þæs H&aelig-acute;lendes róde and of Marian reáfe and of Stephanes líchaman and of Martines reliquium, Hml. S. 6, 72. Sum wudewe wolde efsian &aelig-acute;lce geáre þone sanct (St. Edmund) and his næglas ceorfan and on scrýne healdan tó háligdóme on weófode, 32, 194. Gá man mid háligdóme út and mid háligwætere, Wlfst. 173, 13. Út ealle mid hálidóme, 181, 3. Gif hwá m&aelig-acute;ne áð on háligdóme (super sancta) swerige, Ll. Th. i. 398, 4. III. a holy place, place specially appointed for worship :-- Þá burh Hierusalem, þ&aelig-acute;r bið heora háligdóm, Hml. A. 106, 136. IV. holy doctrines :-- Ðonne hé wilnað ðæt hé háligdóm l&aelig-acute;re cum sancta studet dicere, Past. 383, 7.
háligdóm-hús, es; n. A place where holy things are kept, a sacrarium :-- Beón út ágáne diácon and pistelr&aelig-acute;dere of (on, MS. ) hálig&dash-uncertain;dómhúse mid líchaman Drihtnes egrediantur diaconus ac subdiaconus de sacrario cum corpore Domini, Angl. xiii, 422, 818.
hálig-ern. Add: -- Háligern archanum, Germ. 395, 42. Ðæt háliern wearð geopenod and þá lác w&aelig-acute;ron in gebróhte, Ap. Th. 24, 6. On hálierne sacello, An. Ox. 3237. Oð ic ingá on háligern donec UNCERTAIN intrem in sanctuarium UNCERTAIN Dei, Ps. Rdr. 72, 17. Of háligetnum de sacrariis, Germ. 392, 43.
háliglíce; adv. Holily :-- Sé byð Gode geþeódd, sé ðe hyt háliglíce déð, Nap. 35.
hálig-mónaþ. Add :-- Se mónaþ (September) þe wé nemnað hálig&dash-uncertain;mónoð, Mart. H. 182, 26.
hálig-nes. Add: I. holiness. v. hálig; A. V. :-- Hér wæs Ósuuald ofslagen . . . þæs hálines and wundor w&aelig-acute;ron manigfealde UNCERTAIN gecýdde geond ðis égland (cf. cujus quanta fides in Deum, quae deuotio mentis fuerit, etiam post mortem uirtutum miraculis claruit, Bd. 3, 9), Chr. 641; P. 27, 24. Þ&aelig-acute;re hálignesse hús domus sanctitatis, Bl. H. 163, 11. II. holiness of God. v. hálig; A. II :-- Heriað Drihten, and andetað þæt gemynd his hálignesse (sanctitatis ejus), Ps. Th. 29, 3. On munt hálignesse hís (sanctificationis suae), Ps. Vos. 77, 54. III. sanctity, saintliness. v. hálig ; A. III :-- Ðonne bið ðæt gold ásueartod, ðonne sió hálignes monnes lífes (cf. hwelc æfter hálgum háde, 25) bið mid eorðlicum weorcum gewemmed aurum obscuratur, cum terrenis actibus sanctitatis vita polluitur, Past. 133, 21. IV. holiness, sanctity UNCERTAIN of a rite. v. hálig; A. IV. 2 :-- Ðurh þæs hálgan fulluhtes hálignesse, Wlfst. 154, 19. V. an object held sacred :-- Ic hálsige þe þurh ealle hálignyssa (sanctitates) þe synt on heofonan and on eorðan, and þurh þæne fulluht and Crístendóm þe þú underfangen hæfst, Ll. Lbmn. 413, 20. VI. a holy place. Cf. hálig; B. II :--Ðu on ðínre hálignesse hér áspr&aelig-acute;ce Deus locutus est in sancto suo, Ps. Th. 59, 5. VII. religious worship, rites or practices :-- Fram þám bisceope hiora hálignesse þe hí &aelig-acute;r beeódan a pontifice sacrorum suorum, Bd. 2, 13 ; Sch. 167, 16. [Cf. Ich wulle halinesse to mine goden halden and swiðe heom wurðen, Lanm. 8049.]
hálig-portic, es; n. A sanctuary :-- Ic ingá on Godes háligportic (sanctuarium), Ps. Vos. 72, 17: 73, 7 : 82, 13. (Perhaps hálig portic should be taken; portic seems neuter, Hml. Th. i. 508, 10).
hálig-rift, e ; f. Substitute: es ; n., and add: -- Mynecena tácen is þæt þú sette þíne twégen scytefingras on þín heófod foran and stríce siþþan ádúne andlang þínra hleóra on þæs háligryftes tácnunge, Tech. ii. 129, 6. Háligrefte theristro (viduitatis), An. Ox. 2, 441. Hálirefte, 5243.
hálig-wæter. Add :-- Gá man mid háligdóme út and mid háligwætere, Wlfst. 173, 13. Sprænge se mæssepreóst háligwæter ofer hig ealle, Ll. Th. i. 226, 23.
hál-ness. v. wan-hálness.
háls. In l.UNCERTAIN I after 'forgeaf' add: , gefreóde and gefreoðade folc under wolcnum, and at end: v. mund-heáls: háls-bóc. v. heáls-bóc: halscod. v. healsed.
hálsere. Add: a soothsayer (?), diviner, an augur :-- Hálsere commentarius (cf. cotmmenta, i. ficta, fraudes, 39), Wrt. Voc. ii. 132, 42. Hálseras extipices, i. auruspices, 145, 18. v. h&aelig-acute;lsere.
hálsian, héalsian. Substitute: hálsian, halsian (?), heal&dash-uncertain;sian. I. to beseech, entreat, make solemn appeal to :-- Ic hálsie obtestor, deprecor, Germ. 402, 88. (1) where entreaty is made in the interests of the speaker. (a) with acc. of person addressed :-- Beó þú Gode underþýd, and hálsa hine (obsecra eum), Ps. Th. Srt. Vos. 36, 7. (b) with acc. of person and clause of entreaty :-- Ic ðé halsige (healsige, v. l.) &thorn-bar; ðú mé secge quaeso te, Bt. 38, 4 ; F. 202, 21. Ic þé halsige &thorn-bar; þú mé nó leng ne lette, 36, 3; F. 174, 32. Ic þé hálsie þæt þú ús miltsie, Hö. 107. Ic hálsige and gebidde mé tó þé þæt . . . , Hy. 3, 47. Hé halsaþ (healsaþ, v. l.) &aelig-acute;lcne . . . &thorn-bar; hé for hine gebidde, Bt. prooem.; F. viii. 11. Ðec wé hálsiað ðæt úre haele wunde, Ps. Srt. ii. p. 204, 9. (b α) where the entreaty is emphasized by connecting it with something sacred or highly esteemed :-- Ic hálsige (hálsigo, L. R. adiuro) þé ðurh God &thorn-bar; ðú mé ne þreáge, Mk. 5, 7: Gú. 1176. Ic þé hálsige fore þínum cildháde, Hö. 118. Wé biddað and hálsiað on Godes noman, Txts. 175, 15. Heó hyne hálsode þurh God &thorn-bar; hé ðám onfénge . . . Dryhten cwæð : 'Hé wæs þurh mé gehálsod', Shrn. 135, 18-25, Hé mec þíne lífe healsode &thorn-bar; . . . , B. 2132. (2) where the entreaty is made in the interests of the person addressed. (a) with acc. of person :--
504 HÁLSIGEND -- HÁM
L&aelig-acute;re hié and healsa (obsecra), Past. 291, 16. (b) with acc. and clause :-- Ic þé healsige &thorn-bar; ðú gesceádwíslíce &thorn-bar; ongite quaeso te, vide quam id sancte probes, Bt. 34, 3; F. 136, 18. Ic eów hálsige &thorn-bar; gé gongan tó byrgenne weligra manna, Bl. H. 99, 12. Hé hý hálsode (the accent is in the MS.) þæt hý nánuht þ&aelig-acute;ra &aelig-acute;renda ne underféngon, Ors. 4, 6; Bos 86, 25. (b α) emphasized. v. (1 b α) :-- Ic eów healsige for ð&aelig-acute;m tócyme Dryhtnes ðæt gé nó tó hrædlíce ne sién ástyrede rogamus vos per adventvm UNCERTAIN Domini, ut non cito moveamini, Past. 213, 14. Ic eów hálsige on ðone Drihten . . . þæt gé forl&aelig-acute;tan . . . , Wlfst. 232, 12. (3) of solemn appeal made in legal proceedings, to adjure :-- Ic eów hálsige on Fæder noman . . . and fer ðaere hálgen faemnan naman, &thorn-bar; gé tó ð&aelig-acute;m ordále ne gangen, gif gé scyld on eów witen, Rtl. 114, 14-22. Ic hálsige þé þurh þæne ælmihtigan God adiuro te per omnipotentem Deum, Ll. Lbmn. 413, 1. Ic hálsige obsecro, 12: obtestor, 19. Hálsie man ðone man hér. Ic eów hálsie, 415, 1. (4) to exorcize :-- Exorcismus aquae. Ic hálsigo ðec exorcizo te, creatura aque, Rtl. 100, 27. Salthálgcincg. Ic l UNCERTAIN álsigo ðec, giscæft saltes, 117, 34. (5) to imprecate :-- Háls[ode] inprecabatur, An. Ox. 4, 45. II. to augur, divine. v. hálsung; II. On wígbedde tó hálsienne ariolandi, Wrt. Voc. ii. 9, 15. v. á-hálsian ; eofulsian.
hálsigend. Add :-- Hé beád him &thorn-bar; hé w&aelig-acute;re gehádod tó exorcista, &thorn-bar; wé hátað hálsigend þe ðe bebýt deóflum &thorn-bar; hí of gedrehtum mannum faran, Hml. S. 31, 141.
hálsigendlic. Add: that earnestly entreats (of a prayer) :-- Sum wíf bær hire deádan sunu ongeán Libertinum . . . Heó mid áðsware him tó cwæð: 'Ne færst þú heonon búton þú mínne sunu mé cukenne ágife'. Hé áforhtode for hire hálsiendlican (geornfullan, v. l.) béne (expavit petitionis illius juramentum UNCERTAIN ), Gr. D. 17, 23.
hálsigendlíce. Dele: hal-stán. v. heall-stán.
hálsung. Add: , hálsung (?), healsung. I. entreaty, solemn appeal. (1) on one's own behalf. Cf. hálsian; I. 1 :-- Geneál&aelig-acute;cige gebed &l-bar; hálsung mín (deprecatio mea) on gesihþe þínre, Ps. L. 118, 169 ERROR Béne &l-bar; hálsunge míne deprecationem meam, 16, 1. God gehírde míne healsunge (deprecationem), and Drihten onféng mín gebed (orationem), Ps. Th. 6, 7. Healsunga, 38, 14. Healsunge (obsecrationem), Ps. Vos. 142, 1. Mid hálsungum cum obsecrationibus, Kent. Gl. 659. ¶ of a form of prayer used in the church service :-- Hálsung, þæt is Kyrieleison letania, R. Ben. 37, 1 : 38, 12. Hálsunge bén, þæt is Kyrieleison supplicatio letanie, id est Kyrieleism, 34, 2. (1 a) where the appeal is emphasized by an oath. Cf. hálsian; I 1 b α :-- Heó þus cwæð and mid áðe geswór . . . Hé áforhtode for ð&aelig-acute;re béne hálsunge (expavit petitionis illius juramentum), Gr. D. 17, 30. (2) adjuration. Cf. hálsian ; I 3 :-- Hálsung. Ic hálsige þé . . . , Ll. Lbmn. 413, 1 : 415, 10. Hálsuncge, Rtl. 114, 13. (3) exorcism. Cf. hálsian; I. 4 :-- Hálsunge exorcismo, i. adjuratione, An. Ox. 4083. Mid þæs sácerdes hálsunge se deófol wyrð áflýmed fram þáre menniscan gesceafte, Wlfst. 33, 21. (4) imprecation. Cf. hálsian ; I. 5, Bl. H. 99, 21 in Dict. II. divination. Cf. hálsian; II :-- Hálsung divinatio, Wrt. Voc. ii. 141, 56. v. h&aelig-acute;lsung.
hálsung-gebed. Substitute: A prayer in the service of the church :-- Hálsunggebedu supplicatio letanie, R. Ben. I. 39, 6. Cf. Gebedu letania, 42, 18.
hálsung-tíma, an; m. A time of supplication :-- Swylce fram þæs dæges úpspringe tó hálsungtíman þreó tída sýn forð áðenede, Nap. 35.
hálwenda. v. hálwende; B.
hálwende. Add: , hálwynde. A. adjective. I. conducive to physical health :-- Hálwende cleoþan medicinale, i. salutiferum cataplasma, An. Ox. 1972. Þone hálwendan cleoþan malagma, 3051. I a. figurative :-- Ðætte hié ðone hálwendan (-wyndan, v. l.) drenc ðæs æðelan wínes ne gehwyrfen him selfum tó áttre, Past. 365, 8. Hálwe[n]dne l&aelig-acute;cedóm saluberrimum malagma, An. Ox. 374. II. conducive to well-being :-- Scildend þára hálwendra (þ&aelig-acute;re h&aelig-acute;lo, Ps. Th.) Crístes his pretector UNCERTAIN salutarium x&p-tilde;i UNCERTAIN sui, Ps. Vos. Srt. 27, 8. Hálwende prosperos (successus), An. Ox. 4550. III. conducive to moral or spiritual health or well-being :-- Hálwende cynnincg saluatrix natiuitas, An. Ox. 1538. Hé wolde ð&aelig-acute;m fortrúwodum monnum andrysno hálwendes eges (saluberrimi timoris) on gebrengean, Past. 385, 16. Mid ðý hálwyndan wætre aqua salutis, 261, 8. On hálwyndre hreówsunga (salubris tristitia), 425, 17. On hálwende láre in doctrina sana, 91, 15. Ðá hálwendan forhæfdnesse difficultatem salutis, 401, 31. Þ&aelig-acute;ne hálwendne saluberrimum, i. salutare &l-bar; congruum ( Christi adventum), An. Ox. 1773. Hé ús sealde hálwendne geþóht, Bl. H. 11. 35. Manig þing þe him sylfum swíðe hálweude ERROR (salubria) w&aelig-acute;ron tó witanne, Bd. 3, 19; Sch. 280, 10. B. in weak declension used as substantive. (1) personal. Take here hálwenda in Dict., and add: -- God, se hálwynda mín Deus, salutaris meus, Ps. Srt. 26, 9: 61, 3. Úre hálwenda, Ps. L. 84, 5. Hálwynde úr, Ps. Srt. 78, 9. Se hálwynde úr, 67, 20. In Gode ð&aelig-acute;m hálwyndan mínum, 61, 8 : 94, 1 : ii. p. 193, 13. (2) of a thing :-- Þíne sóðfæstnesse and hálwendan þínre (þínne?, þine?) veritatem tuam et salutare tuum, R. Ben. I. 12, 13. v. hálwend-lic.
hálwend-lic. Add: used in weak declension as substantive. v. hálwende; B. (1) personal :-- Hé is hálwendlica mín salutaris meus, Ps. L. 61, 3. Úre hálwendlica, 64, 6: 78, 9. (2) of a thing :-- On hálwendlican þínum &l-bar; h&aelig-acute;lðe in salutare tuum, Ps. L. 118, 81. v. un&dash-uncertain;hálwendlic.
hálwendlíce. Add: so as to promote or produce bodily or spiritual health; salubriter :-- Ðis fæstin &thorn-bar; ðóhtum líchomum &aelig-acute;c gémendum hálwoendlíce gesetted is hoc jejunium quod animis corporibusque curandis salubriter institutum est, Rtl. 9, 29. I. of bodily health :-- Heó is geh&aelig-acute;led hálwendlíce ðurh Críst she is restored to perfect health by Christ, Hml. S. 9, 29. I a. figurative :-- Synne áttor hálwendfice ERROR byð geopenud on andetnysse, &thorn-bar; cwyldb&aelig-acute;rlíce lutude on geþance peccati uirus salubriter aperitur in confessione quod pestifere latebat in mente, Scint. 39, 6. II. of spiritual health :-- Oft weorðað men swíðe hálwendlíce (salubriter) áf&aelig-acute;rde mid ð&aelig-acute;m ilcan ðingum ðe hí &aelig-acute;r unnytlíce lufedon, Past. 441, 24. Is ús micel ðearf UNCERTAIN ðæt wé hálwendlíce (to cur spiritual profit; salubriter) geðencen ðá gód ðe wé forgiémeleásodon, 467, 7. Hálwendlíce (salubriter) geþreád, Gr. D. 160, 20. Críst wolde ðá ealdan &aelig-acute; &aelig-acute;r gefyllan, and siððan ðá níwan gecýðnysse hálwendlíce (with salutary effect) onginnan, Hml. Th. ii. 244, 29
hálwendnes. Add: safety, salvation; salutare :-- Ic sette on h&aelig-acute;lo (hálwendnesse, MS. T. ) ponam in salutari, Ps. Spl. 11, 6. Sóðfæstnesse þíne and hálwendnesse (salutare) ic ges&aelig-acute;de (Ps. 40, 10), R. Ben. 11, 8. God hálwendnyssa úra Deus salutarium nostrum, Ps. L. 67. 20.
ham a garment. Add :-- Colobium, dictum quia longum est et sine manicis loþa, hom vel smoc, mentel, Wrt. Voc. ii. 134, 37. Hom colobium, i. 288, 34. Ham, hom, Txts. 46, 167. Haam camisa, 50, 244. Ham, cemes, Wrt. Voc. ii. 13, 23. Ham, hacele subucula, An. Ox. 5316.
ham a ham. Add: -- Hom copla, poples, Wrt. Voc. ii. 132, 80. Hamme publite, Txts. 111, 25. [H]omme poplite, 182, 81. Hamme suffragine, An. Ox. 38, 3. Gebígedum hamme curvo poplite, Hpt. Gl. 493, 75. Homm&e-hook; puplites, Txts. 114, 102. Homme cambas (=gambas), Lch. i. lxxi. 10.
ham a piece of enclosed land, a ham (v. N. E. D.). Add: -- Hæfde hió hire gebógod on ánan wyrtigan hamme, Hml. S. 30, 312. On brádan leá on énne ham; þurh út ðone leá súð út on óðerne ham ; of ðan hamme . . . on brádan ham westeweardne; of brádan hamme . . . of m&aelig-acute;de on flexhammas; of flexhamman on minthammas . . . of ðan wæterwege on waterhammes; of ðan hamman, C. D. v. 374, 14-32. v. fleax-, flód-, mint-, mylen-, sceáp-, stigel-, wæter-hamm. See Midd. Flur, s. v.
hám. Add: I. a farm, estate :-- Tó hyre ágenum háme ad pr&e-hook;diolum suum, An. Ox. 4741. Háme pr&e-hook;dia (ut ab urbe ad propria praedia ducerentur, Ald. 69, 4), 4840. Hé forgeaf summe hám tó þ&aelig-acute;re hálgan stówe, Hml. S. 6, 232. Hé cwæð &thorn-bar; hé ne mihte embe munuclíf þá smeágan . . . ac wolde beón embe his þincg . . . and gedreóhl&aelig-acute;can his hámas, 121. I a. as a technical English term, a vill, manor (v. Se bohm UNCERTAIN Vill. Comm. s. v.):-- Fela sceal tó holdan hámes geréfan and tó gemetfæstan manna hyrde, Angl. ix. 265, 10. Þone hám æt Beccanleá . . . and æt Felhhamme and þá land þe þ&aelig-acute;rtó hýran, Cht. Th. 489, 12-18 : 2: 9: 19. Wearð ádr&aelig-acute;fed Óslác of earde . . . háma bereáfod, Chr. 975 ; P. 120, 24. Ic geeácnode intó Élégmynstre ðæs þrý hámas ðe ðus sind gehátene, Meldeburna, Earmingaford, UNCERTAIN Norðwold, C. D. iii. 60, 33. II. a dwelling, an abode. (1) on earth. (a) a habitable building, a house :-- þurhwuniendum eallum þám getimbre þæs hámes perdurante tota domus fabrica, Gr. D. 119, 27. Sum bið bylda til hám tó habbanne, Crá.UNCERTAIN 76. (b) the fixed residence of a person or family, an inhabited house, a residence: -- Gelaðode se gesíð hine tó his hám, and hé hine gesóhte and on his hús eóde and his sw&aelig-acute;senda breác rogatus a comite intrauit epulaturus domum eius, Bd. 3, 22 ; Sch. 297, 1. Æt Finnes hám, B. 1156. Hé bewiste swá hwæt swá man dyde on his háme (hám, v. l.) quaeque in ejusdem domo agebantur noverat, Gr. D. 299, 30. Ic wunode in mínum háme (hám, v. l.) þe mé gelamp in þissere byrig of mínes fæder yrfe, 313, 27. Decius áwédde . . . and ásprang sárlic wóp on ðám háme, Hml. Th. i. 434, 15. Sé ðe forlétes hús &l-bar; hám, Lk. L. 18, 29. Geþenca hweðer áwiht mani mann cynges hám séce þér ð&aelig-acute;r hé on túne byð, Solil. H. 44, 2. Hé Hróðgáres hám gesóhte, B. 717. Hé þ&aelig-acute;r háligne hám ár&aelig-acute;rde, Gú. 120: 242. Hý hleóleáse háma þoliað, 193. [On] &aelig-acute;lces cynges háma [hýrede] beóð sume on búre, sume on healle, sume on ódene, sume on carcerne, Solil. H. 44, 18. Sume wuniað on wéstennum, gesittað hámas on heolstrum, 54. Gewiton him þá wígend wíca neósian . . . Frysland geseón, hámas and heá burg, B. 1127: Chr. 937; P. 106, 18: Exod. 453. Ic hire beád gymmas . . . and m&aelig-acute;re gebytlu, hámas and hýred, Hml. S. 8, 37. (α) a place that used to be a person's home :-- Gif man mægð gebigeð . . . gif hit fácne is, eft æt hám gebrenge, Ll. Th. i. 22, 2: 10, 8. (β) in connexion with marriage, v. VII. I a :-- Abraham idese bróhte tó háme, þ&aelig-acute;r hé wíc áhte, Gen. 1721. Þ&aelig-acute;m tó hám forgeaf Hréðel ángan dohtor, B. 374. (2) not on earth :-- Hé on norðd&aelig-acute;le hám and heáhsetl heofena ríces ágan wolde, Gen. 33 : Sat. 276. Þára écena háma, Solil. H. 2, 15. Sécan þá hámas and þá árleásan
HAMA -- HÁMTÚNISC 505
eardungstówe, Seel. 70. (3) figurative, (long) home :-- Hé fores&aelig-acute;de þone dæg þe hé sceolde cuman tó Cofantreó tó his langan háme, Vis. Lfc. 90.
