íwan. Add: v. on-(an-)íwan: íw-berige. Take here eów-berige in Dict.
íwed-, eáwed-ness, e; f. Showing :-- Eáudnise ostensionem, Rtl. 113, 40. v. æt-íwedness.
-íwness. v. æt-íwness.
K
In one instance k seems used for g :-- Ðæt mód ðé &aelig-acute;r wæs keléd (áléd, v. l.) of his gewunan cum cogitatio extra usum ducitur, Past. 57, 9.
L
lá. I. Add :-- Lá aue, An. Ox. 56, 133. Wá lá wá eheu, Wrt. Voc. ii. 32, 44. II. Add: giving emphasis (1) to interrogation or exclamation :-- Lá wh&aelig-acute;r nú þá ... lá wh&aelig-acute;r sind ubi nunc ... ubi sunt, Wülck. Gl. 253, 34, 37. Lá hú, ne mót ic dón þæt ic wille?, aut non licet mihi quod volo facere?, Hml. Th. ii. 80, 25. Hwæt dó ic lá?, 104, 16. Suwiað: hwæt lá, ne gehýre gé hú myrige lofsangas swégað on heofonum?, 98, 4: Hml. S. 8, 48. Ne eart þú lá Sebastianus?, 5, 449. (2) to entreaty or command :-- Swuga, lá, swuga tace, obsecro, tace, Solil. H. 48, 7. Gecier lá, ne folga mé, ðæt ic ðé ne dyrre ofstingan, Past. 295, 15. (3) to statement or affirmation :-- Geá, lá, geá; gyf hyt nú f&aelig-acute;renga gewurde ... vere aliquantum; imo si haec repente provenerint ..., Solil. H. 34, 11. Lá ah ðeáhhwæðre se foreðancula wer bæd his fultumes sed videlicet vir providus solatium petivit, Past. 305, 1. Hit is lá ful góód þæt &aelig-acute;fre úre eágan móston geseón þæt wé wilnodon, Ps. Th. 34, 21. (4) to negation :-- Uton ændian þás bóc nú h&aelig-acute;rrihte ... Næse, lá, næse; uton ne forl&aelig-acute;tan gyét ðás bóc concludamus hoc volumen ... Non sinam omnino concludi hunc libellum, Solil. H. 49, 12.
laber. v. lawer.
lác. [If ðínne in Hml. S. 7, 119 is correct, lác is there masculine, but perhaps ðíne should be read.] II. Add; v. lác-lic :-- Se m&aelig-acute;gðhád sceal God beón geoffrod be his ágenum eyre, &thorn-bar; seó lác beo leófre þám H&aelig-acute;lende, Hml. A. 33, 234. Nolde Drihten ásendan þone ðe hé sylf geh&aelig-acute;lde tó þám sácerde mid &aelig-acute;nigre láce, Hml. Th. i. 124, 19. Gán mid láce tó Godes húse, and beran þæt cild forð mid þ&aelig-acute;re láce, 134, 22. &thorn-bar; synd þá m&aelig-acute;stan lác, Hml. A. 35, 289. Ðá lác beóð God ealra andfengeost, Past. 222, 21. Freó láca oblationes, Ps. L. 50, 21. Ic hatige þá lác þe bióð on wóh gereáfodu. ... Sé þe mé brengð lác of earmes monnes áhtum on wóh gereáfodum, ðonne bið dæt swelce hwá wille blótan ð&aelig-acute;m fæder tó ðance and tó lácum his ágen bearn ego odio habens rapinam in holocausto. ... Qui offert sacrificium de substantia pauperis, quasi qui victimat filium in conspectu patris, Past. 342, 2-10. Ðá offrunga and ðá lác (holocausta) ðe mon bróhte tó ð&aelig-acute;m weóbude, 217, 20. III. Add :-- Laac elogia, Wrt. Voc. ii. 107, 13: exenium, 69. Lác, 83, 48: munuscula, 55, 16. Ne sí munece álýféd þæt hé &aelig-acute;nig gewrit oððe sende oððe lác fram hyra mágum underfón nullatenus liceat monacho a parentibus suis litteras, eulogias vel quelibet munuscula accipere, R. Ben. 87, 11. IV. Dele; in tie instances given here lác = lácnung. Add to compounds ælmes- (Nap. 5), bríw-, drý-, sib-, word-, wróht-, wund-lác.
lácan. Add: IV. to delude, trick :-- Óðer gást l&aelig-acute;deð hine and l&aelig-acute;ceð (læceð? v. læccan) and geond land spaneð, Sal. 496. Swilce þá worulds&aelig-acute;lþa w&aelig-acute;ron rihte þá hí ðé m&aelig-acute;st geóleccan swilce hí nú sindon, þeáh þe hý þé liólcen (óleccan, v. l.) on þá leásan s&aelig-acute;lþa fortuna talis erat, cum blandiebatur, cum tibi falsae illecebris felicitatis alluderet, Bt. 7, 2; F. 18. 2. Cf. for-, ge-lácan, and Icel. leika to delude.
lác-d&aelig-acute;d. Add :-- Lácd&aelig-acute;de, cystinesse munificently, An. Ox. 3833.
lác-fæsten a fast considered as an offering :-- Ne gelýfe þæs n&aelig-acute;nig mon &thorn-bar; him ne genihtsumige &thorn-bar; fasten tó écere h&aelig-acute;lo, búton hé mid óþrum gódum hit geéce, and sé þe wille Drihtne bringan gecwéme lácfæsten, þonne sceal hé &thorn-bar; mid ælmessan and mid mildheortum weorcum fullian, Bl. H. 37, 18.
-lácian. v. ge-lácian.
lacing. The word seems to occur only as a local name :-- In loco qui dicitur Lacinge, C. D. ii. 93, 22. On Dýðmere; ðonon on Lacing; andlang Lacing on cealcford, v. 397, 15: vi. 28, 12. Cf. Lacingbróc, vi. 8, 13: 72, 31. In uilla quae cognominatur Lakingheðe, iv. 16, 28. Quandam telluris particulam qui appellatur æt Lacingahið, v. 301, 11.
LÁCNIAN -- L&AElig-acute;DAN 599
lácnian. Add :-- Lácnie medor, Wrt. Voc. ii. 58, 45. 'We lácnodon Babylón, and hió ðeáh ne wearð geh&aelig-acute;led'. Ðonne bið Babylón gelácnad, nales ðeáh fullíce geh&aelig-acute;led. ... 'curavimus Babylonem, et nan est sonata.' Babylon quippe curatur, nec tamen ad sanitatem reducitur, Past. 267, 9. Hálwende cleoþan lácniende medicinale cataplasma procurans, An. Ox. 1974. Mid lácniendum tólum medicinalibus instrumentis, 3047. v. un-lácnod, and next word.
lácnigend-lic. Add :-- Mid lácniendlicum tólum instrumentis medicinalibus, Hpt. Gl. 478, 2. v. un-lácnigendlic.
lácnung. Add: I. healing, medical care :-- Studium vel medecina, curatio vel lácnung vel gýmen vel hogu, Wrt. Voc. ii. 137, 59. Ne cann ic náht on lácnunge, Hml. S. 22, 41. Wite hé þæt hé þá gýmenne þára umtrumra sáula tó rihtre lácnunge underféng noverit se infirmarum curam suscepisse animarum, R. Ben. 51, 12. Gif hé his seócum d&aelig-acute;dum ealle lácnunge gegearewade si morbidis earum actibus universa fuerit cura exhibita, 11, 5. II. a medicine, medicament, means of healing :-- Þá hálan l&aelig-acute;ces ne lácnunge ne behófiað, R. Ben. 50, 19. Lác[nunge] medecinae, An. Ox. 382: medicamine, 4352. Lácnunge, cliþan cataplasma, 3050. Godcundra myngunga sealfunga, háligra gewrita lácnunga unguenta adhortationum, medicamina scripturarum divinarum, R. Ben. 52, 12.
lác-sang. Add: cf. offrung-sang.
lactuca. Add :-- Gif se ríca ágylte, þreá hine; þonne ytst þú þíne eástru mid grénum lactucum, mid biternesse. &thorn-bar; wát eall ceorlisc folc &thorn-bar; gréne lactucas beóð bitere; swá synt þá rícan men tó þreágenne, Angl. viii. 323, 22.
lacu. For 'A pool ... lake' substitute: A stream, water-course, and add :-- In australi atque in occidente habens torrentem cuius uocabulum Fiscesburne ... in oriente aquam quae Anglorum lingua Lake nominatur habens, quae est duarum, quae ibi sunt, ulterior ... Insuper memoratam aquam, id est Fiscesburnam ..., C.D. i. 122, 31. On scegbróc oð seó lacu scýt west þanon út on h&aelig-acute;ðfeld, C.D.B. iii. 624, 19. Oþ woggawilllacu út scýt; on þá lace oð wocggawilles heáfod, Cht. E. 266, 24. Be healfan stréme intó Sandfordes læce; swá andlang ð&aelig-acute;re lace intó Sandforda; of Sandforda eást andlang ð&aelig-acute;re lace, C.D. iv. 134, 21-24. Oð ðá lace; andlang lace út on Temese, v. 302, 34: 330, 28: vi. 2, 12: vi. 8, 26. On þá fúlan lace, v. 13, 22. On streám oþ þá laca tólicgaþ, Cht. Crw. 3, 12. ¶ as second part of a compound :-- Út on æsclace ð&aelig-acute;r æsclace fylð út on Wuorf ... of ð&aelig-acute;re ealdan díc on Grindewylles lace ... on Ættanpennes lace, C.D. vi. 48, 8-14. On brómlace; ðonne andlang streámes, iii. 452, 13. On ðá gem&aelig-acute;rlace; andlang lace, vi. 8, 26. On þá m&aelig-acute;rlace, 9, 2. On sandlace; andlang sandlice tó ceóles íge, v. 303, 3. [v. N.E.D. lake, and see Cht. E. 465: Cht. Crw. 54.] v. fisc-, m&aelig-acute;d-lacu.
lád. II. Add :-- In monasterio quod iuxta ostium aquilonale fluminis Génládae positum Raculfe nuncupatur, Bd. 5, 8. Haec sunt termina huius agri ... ab aquilone génlád, C.D. i. 238, 6. [v. D.D. yenlade; Halliwell Dict. yenlet.] IV. Add: ¶ In the phrase cyrcan lád, which seems sometimes (?) to have the same meaning as ciric-sceat. All the following passages occur in charters of Oswald, bishop of Worcester :-- Sí hit &aelig-acute;lces þinges freoh bútan ferdfare and walgeworc and brycggeworc and circanláde, C.D. iii. 5, 14: 159, 31. The corresponding forms in Latin are seen in the following passages :-- Sit praedictum rus liberum ab omni mundiali seruitio ... excepta sanctae Dei basilicae suppeditatione ac ministratione, 173, 30: 241, 35. Exeptis snct Dei aecclesiae necessitatibusus atque utilitatibus, 177, 32, Libera omnis rei nisi aecclesiastici census, 212, 29: 259, 23: 261, 15. Aeclesiastici census, id est duos modios de mundo grano, ii. 386, 30. Aecclesiae manus et sepultura praesulis in Wigurna ceastre ditioni deueniat; alias plena glorietur libertate, excepta expeditione rata, pontis arcisue constructione, 385, 15. V. leading, guiding :-- Blind gif blinde lát forel&aelig-acute;das caecus si caeco ducatum praestet, Mt. L. 15, 14. v. corn-, from, ofer-, wudu-lád.
lád. I. Add :-- Lád excussatio, Wrt. Voc. ii. 146, 25. Heora &aelig-acute;lc óþerne myngige þæt þá slápulan náne láde næbben (propter somnolentorum excusationes), R. Ben. 47, 17. II. Add :-- Gif hwá þeóf fridige, sý hé emscyldig wið mé þá þe þeóf scolde, búton hé hine mid fulre láde wið mé gecl&aelig-acute;nsian mæge, Cht. E. 251, 1. III. (mistaken for) accusation :-- Fram þrím ondréd heorte mín. ... láde (delaturam) ceastre, Scint. 224, 17.
ládian. I. In l. 3 read 241 for 244, and add: (1) to clear, excuse, defend a person :-- Manigra manna gewuna is ðæt hié hié mid ðissum wordum ládiað and cueðað: 'Wé brucað úres &aelig-acute;gnes, ne gítsige wé nánes óðres monnes,' Past. 337, 19: 439, 21. Sume þá biscopas wiðstódan stranglíce and scyldon and ládedon þá sóðfæstnesse quidam in defensione veritatis episcopi persistentes, Gr. D. 240, 10. (1 a) to clear of a charge, Past. 308, 7 (in Dict.). (2) to excuse a fault, Ors. 5, 2; S. 216, 31 (in Dict.).
ládigend-lic. Add: v. be-ládigendlic.
lád-mann. Add :-- Þá cwæð Esau: 'Ic bidde þé þæt þú nyme þe ládmenn of mínum geférum, þæt þé wegas wissigeon, Gen. 33, 15. [v. N.E.D. lodeman.]
lád-rinc. For 'The word, ... vehicularius' substitute: In attempting to determine the meaning of this word it should be noticed that lád in all its other compounds, lád-mann, -scipe, -teáh, -teów, has the force of leading, guidance. The lád-rinc seems to be a guide, and his special character in the passage given above may be inferred from the following passage :-- Si aduenae de aliis regionibus aduenirent, debebant ducatum habere ad aliam regalem uillam quae proxima fuisset in illorum uia, C.D. v. 159, 8-11. Cf. too: ductor, qui ad conducendum aliquem in via per alterius regionem datus est a quovis principe, Migne.
lád-scipe. Add :-- Ládscipe ducatum. (See passage under lád; V.)
lád-teów. Add: [from lád-þeów]. I. a leader, guide :-- Ne forl&aelig-acute;t ús, ac beó úre láðeów (ductor), ðú cans eal ðis wésten, and wásð hw&aelig-acute;r wé wícian magon, Past. 304, 15. II. a military leader, general :-- Marcellinus, Iuliuses ládteów. Ors. 5, 12; S. 240, 24. Alexandres æfterfolgeras w&aelig-acute;ron gehátene ládteówas, 3, ll; S. 150, 8. Pompeiuses legian mid his þrím ládteówum Pompeiani duces cum legionibus, 5, 12; S. 240, 21. v. &aelig-acute;- (Ps. Vos. 9, 21), fore-ládteów; l&aelig-acute;ttéwestre.
ládteów-dóm. Add :-- Under látteówdóm sub (discipline)pedagogio, An. Ox. 3014.
ládung. I. Add :-- &thorn-bar; se man gecyrre fram his synnum, gif hé wile, oððe hé bútan ládunge losie mid ealle, Hml. A. 62, 265.
-l&aelig-acute;ca For ag- l. ág-, and add: v. ge-l&aelig-acute;ca: læcan. Add: v. cneord-, cúþ-, cýþ-, fá- (t&aelig-acute;-), fremed-, ge-, gecneord-, gecúþ-, gecýþ-, geed-, gelóm-, geong-, gesamod-, ge-sw&aelig-acute;s-, geþw&aelig-acute;r-, gewundor-, sw&aelig-acute;s-, þw&aelig-acute;r-, wiþer-l&aelig-acute;can: læccan. Add: v. á-læccan; lácan; IV.
læccan (?) to blame, find fault with [v. N.E.D. lack; 5]. v. on-leccan.
læccung (?), e; f. Blaming :-- Ðá forðgáð of welerum mínum ne onsién (faciem seems to have been read) on leccungæ (tó bysmre, Ps. Spl. C.) quae procedunt de labiis meis non faciam irrita, Ps. Cant. 88, 35. [v. N.E.D. lacking, and see bracket at end of læcing in Dict.]
l&aelig-acute;ce. I. Add :-- Leáces sex camilema, Wrt. Voc. i. 22, 28. v. riht-, un-, weorold-l&aelig-acute;ce. II. Add :-- On l&aelig-acute;ces mere, C.D. v. 325, 19. On l&aelig-acute;cemere, vi. 72, 25. Tó l&aelig-acute;ces forda, 9, 11. On l&aelig-acute;ces ford, 120, 9.
-l&aelig-acute;ce, an; f. v. scín-l&aelig-acute;ce: -l&aelig-acute;ce; adj. v. eáþ-l&aelig-acute;ce and efen-l&aelig-acute;ce.
læce-cist, e; f. A medicine chest :-- Fundon hí þá áhýdde mancas in his l&aelig-acute;cecyste aureos invenerunt absconsos in medicamine, Gr. D. 344. 17.
l&aelig-acute;ce-cræft. Add: I. the art of medicine :-- L&aelig-acute;cecræft medicina, An. Ox. 3124. Wæs sum munuc, þám wæs nama lustus, sé waes gel&aelig-acute;red on l&aelig-acute;ceræfte (medicinali arte imbutus), Gr. D. 344, 6: 11. Hé áxode gif hé cúðe áht on l&aelig-acute;cecræfte, Hml. S. 22, 40. II. medical treatment :-- &thorn-bar; word winð on ús swá swá wís l&aelig-acute;ce déð þe mid stíðum l&aelig-acute;cecræfte gelácnað þone untruman, Hml. A. 6, 129. III. a recipe, remedy, medicine :-- L&aelig-acute;cecræftas (cf. l&aelig-acute;cedómas, 44, 7) wiþ healsgunde, Lch. ii. 2, 16. [v. N.E.D. leechcraft.]
l&aelig-acute;ce-dóm. Add: I. healing :-- Medecina, &thorn-bar; ys l&aelig-acute;cedómes cræft, Shrn. 152, 17. Se getýda l&aelig-acute;ce ðæs heofonlican l&aelig-acute;cedómes &aelig-acute;gðer ge ðá hálan l&aelig-acute;rde ge ðám unhálum l&aelig-acute;cedóm eówde peritus medicinae coelestis apostolus non tam sanos instituit, quam infirmis medicamenta monstravit, Past. 397, 15-17. Hé forgeaf wanhálum mannum mid his worde l&aelig-acute;cedóm, Hml. S. 22, 24. II. a medicine, remedy :-- L&aelig-acute;cedóm malagma, i. medecinam, An. Ox. 375. Cleoþan, l&aelig-acute;cedóm cataplasma, i. medicamentum, 1973.
l&aelig-acute;cedóm-ness. Add :-- L&aelig-acute;cedómnessa cataplasma, Wrt. Voc. ii. 81. 55.
l&aelig-acute;ce-finger. Add :-- Middelfinger medius, l&aelig-acute;cefinger medicus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 58, 6. [v. N.E.D. leech-finger.]
l&aelig-acute;ce-getawu; pl. n. Medical apparatus :-- Hí w&aelig-acute;ron geondsmeágende eall his l&aelig-acute;cegeteá. Þá fundon hí þá mancas in his l&aelig-acute;cecyste illius omnia medicamenta perscrutantes aureos invenerunt in medicamine, Gr. D. 344, 16.
l&aelig-acute;ce-íren, es; n. A lancet :-- Hé ásette his l&aelig-acute;ceíren (medicinale ferramentum, id est phlebotomum) on míne tungan, Gr. D. 32, 25.
-l&aelig-acute;cend, -l&aelig-acute;cere, -l&aelig-acute;cestre. v. efen-l&aelig-acute;cend, -l&aelig-acute;cere, -l&aelig-acute;cestre.
l&aelig-acute;ce-wyrht, e; f. Leech-work, medical treatment :-- Mín ádlige cneów is yfele gehæfd, þæt ne mihte nán l&aelig-acute;cewyrht áwiht gelíðian, þeah ðe heó gelóme tó geléd w&aelig-acute;re (diu est quod molestia genu tumentis oppressus nulla cujuslibet medicorum industria possum sanari, Vit. Cuth, c. 2), Hml. Th. ii. 134, 33.
l&aelig-acute;ce-wyrt. I. Add :-- Abgarus wundrode &thorn-bar; hé wearð geh&aelig-acute;led bútan l&aelig-acute;cewyrtum þurh ðæs H&aelig-acute;lendes word, Hml. S. 24, 160.
læcing. Dele, and see læccung: -læcne. v. eáþ-l&aelig-acute;cne: -l&aelig-acute;cness. v. gelóm-, þríst-l&aelig-acute;cness: l&aelig-acute;cung. Add: [v. N.E.D. leeching.]: -l&aelig-acute;cung. v. ed-, efen-, gedyrst-, gelóm-, geþríst-, neá[h]-, riht-l&aelig-acute;cung.
l&aelig-acute;dan. Add: I. to cause to move (líþan) with oneself, (1) to bring or take a person to a place or person, (a) with the person's consent :-- Ezechias l&aelig-acute;dde ðá ællðeódgan &aelig-acute;renddracan on his máðmhús, Past. 39, 3. Orfeus l&aelig-acute;dde his wíf mid him oþ þe hé eóm on &thorn-bar; gem&aelig-acute;re
600 -LAelig-acute;DE -- LAelig-acute;L
leóhtes and þeóstro; þá eóde &thorn-bar; wíf æfter him, Bt. 35, 6 ; F. 170, 12. Gif heó léng libbe þonne sé þe hié út l&aelig-acute;dde, Ll. Th. i. 66, 18. L&aelig-acute;d under earce bord eaforan þíne, Gen. 1332. Se sióca áh þearfe &thorn-bar; hine mon l&aelig-acute;de tó þám l&aelig-acute;ce, Bt. 38, 7; F. 210, 1. Þá men þe hié úp mid him l&aelig-acute;den, Ll. Th. i. 82, 11. Gif hý man út of lande l&aelig-acute;dan wille on óðres þegnes land, 256, 1 : Gen. 1774. Hát síðian Agar and Ismael l&aelig-acute;dan mid hié, 2785. (b) of enforced movement :-- Héton hiene Rómáne gebindan and gebringean beforan fæstennes geate. Þá náwþer ne hine þá hám l&aelig-acute;dan ne dorston þe hiene þider l&aelig-acute;ddon, ne his þá onfón þe hiene mon tó brohte, Ors. 5, 2 ; S. 218, 34: Chr. 796; P. 56, 9: Gen. 2016. L&aelig-acute;ddon þá leóde láðne gewinnan tó carcerne, An. 1251. L&aelig-acute;de hine tó Róme, Ll. Th. i. 264, 8. Hét hé niman þone eorl and tó Bæbbaburh l&aelig-acute;dan, Chr. 1095; P. 231, 27. In þone láðan lég l&aelig-acute;dan, Gú. 567. On gemót l&aelig-acute;ded, Cri. 795: Ph. 491. ¶ figurative :-- Óðer willa feohtende wið ð&aelig-acute;m willan his módes hine gehæftne l&aelig-acute;dde on synne gewunan, Past. 423, 19. (b α) to bring or take (to the place of) an action, lead to execution, bring to justice, &c. :-- &THORN-bar; hine man tó rihte l&aelig-acute;de, Ll. Th. i. 396, 15. Gif hé hine forstalede, &thorn-bar; hine man l&aelig-acute;dde tó þ&aelig-acute;re torfunge, 234, 8. (2) to take, carry, convey. (a) the object material :-- Ne l&aelig-acute;t hé his nánwuht of þýs middanearde mid him máre þonne hé bróhte hider, Bt. 26, 3 ; F. 94, 15. Þone gewundedan ðe mon l&aelig-acute;dde helfcuicne tó ð&aelig-acute;m giesðhúse, Past. 125, 8. Hé hét smiðian of sm&aelig-acute;tum golde áne lytle róde, ðá hé l&aelig-acute;dde on his swýðran, Hml. Th. ii. 304, 16. Æþelhelm l&aelig-acute;dde Wesseaxna ælmessan tó Rome, Chr. 887 ; P. 80, 30. Rómáne gesomnodon al þá goldhord þe on Bretene w&aelig-acute;ron . . . and sume mid him on Gallia l&aelig-acute;ddon, 418; P. 10, 20: Past. 333, 19. Hý l&aelig-acute;ddun hyne of lyfte tó earde, Gú. 398. Hwæþer gé eówer hundas and eówer net út on s&aelig-acute; l&aelig-acute;don ðonne gé huntian willaþ?, Bt. 32, 3; F. 118, 14. Tíd is &thorn-bar; þú fére and þá æ-acute;rendu l&aelig-acute;de, Gú. 1271. Ne miht ðú náht l&aelig-acute;dan of þysum lífe mid þé, Hml. S. 9, 47. Héton þá l&aelig-acute;dan ofer landsceare, teón torngeníðlan, An. 1231. Wæs líc l&aelig-acute;ded tó moldgrafe, Jul. 689. ¶ láde l&aelig-acute;dan, v. lád; III. (b) the object non-material :-- Se þeóden bebeád þrýðweorc . . . Godes &aelig-acute;rendu l&aelig-acute;dan tó Channanéum, An. 778. Frið l&aelig-acute;dan, 174. (3) to bring evidence, a case, an action, &c. , into court :-- Þá læ-acute;dde ic Aðulfes cinges yrfegewrit on úre gemót æt Langandene, Cht. Th. 486, 13. Sceal ic his word and his weorc in gewitnesse Dryhtne l&aelig-acute;dan, Gú. 693. Godwine hæfð gel&aelig-acute;d fulle láde æt ðan unrihtwífe ðe Leófgár hyne tihte, and &thorn-bar; wæs l&aelig-acute;d æt Licitfelda, Cht. Th. 373, 34. (4) to produce, bring forth :-- Wæstme l&aelig-acute;dað (-eð, MS.) cederbeámas, Ps. Th. 103, 16. Cynna gehwylc cucra wuhta þára þe lyft and flód l&aelig-acute;dað and fédað, Gen. 1298. L&aelig-acute;de seó eorðe forð cuce nítenu and creópende cinn and deór, Gen. 1, 24. (4 a) to be productive of :-- Wudu mót him weaxan, tánum l&aelig-acute;dan (cf. týdran), Hy. 4, 105. II. to accompany and show the way to, conduct, convoy, guide (lit. or fig.) :-- Þú l&aelig-acute;tst mé hider and ðider on swá þicne wudu, Bt. 35, 5 ; F. 164, 13. ' Ic ondr&aelig-acute;de &thorn-bar; ic ðé l&aelig-acute;de hidres þidres of þínum wege. ' . . . ' Ic beó swíþe fægn gif ðú mé l&aelig-acute;dest þider ic þé bidde, 40, 5 ; F. 240, 21-25. Hí l&aelig-acute;dað mid wynnum æðelne tó earde, Ph. 345. God self hine l&aelig-acute;dde ðurh ðæt wésten, Past. 304, 7. Him urnon ealle hellwaran ongeán, and l&aelig-acute;ddon hine tó hiora cyninge, Bt. 35, 6; F. 168, 29. Gif hwelc forworht monn cymð, and bitt úrne hwelcne ðæt wé hine l&aelig-acute;den tó sumum rícum menn, Past. 63, 2. &THORN-bar; &aelig-acute;lc man hæbbe þá men gearowe on his lande þe l&aelig-acute;den þá men þe heora ágen sécan willen, Ll. Th. i. 162, 24. Nú þú móst féran . . . ic þec l&aelig-acute;dan sceal, Cri. 1672. L&aelig-acute;dan weorode láreów tó lides stefnan, An. 1708. Ðá ðe óðerra monna sáula underfooð tó l&aelig-acute;danne, Past. 77, 4. III. of a commander, to march at the head of :-- Mægenwísa is trum, sé þás fare l&aelig-acute;deð, Exod. 554. Fyrd wæs gefýsed, fram sé þe l&aelig-acute;dde, 54. Mægen l&aelig-acute;dan, El. 241. Godcunde láreówas sceolan ús l&aelig-acute;dan forð æt þám dóme . . . Ges&aelig-acute;lig bið se hyrde þe þá heorde intó Godes ríce mót l&aelig-acute;dan, Ll. Th. i. 424, 8-11. Se cyng bet&aelig-acute;hte þá fyrde tó l&aelig-acute;dene Ealfríce, Chr. 992 ; P. 127, 11. IV. to guide by holding :-- Blind gif blindne l&aelig-acute;deþ, Mt. R. 15, 14. Óþerne ealdne man l&aelig-acute;dden feówer áwyrgde englas mid mycelre réðnesse, and hine besencton on þá fýrenan eá, Bl. H. 43, 28. Hí genámon þone &b-bar;., leáddon hine tó heora hústinga, and hine þ&aelig-acute;r oftor&dash-uncertain;fodon, Chr. 1012 ; P. 142, 21. ¶ wíf l&aelig-acute;dan to marry, Lch. iii. 190, 7 : 212, 8. V. to guide with reference to action or opinion, to lead to a conclusion, induce to do :-- Óðer gást l&aelig-acute;deð hine and l&aelig-acute;ceð, oð þæt his eáge bið æfþancum ful, Sal. 496. Tó hwon l&aelig-acute;ddest þú hider þeosne? why did you cause this man to come hither? Bl. H. 85, 25. Hé l&aelig-acute;dde hié mid. UNCERTAIN ligenum and mid listum speón, Gen. 588. ' Ð&aelig-acute;r ðú ongeáte hwidre ic þé nú teohhie tó l&aelig-acute;denne.' . . . ' Hwider wilt þú mé l&aelig-acute;dan?' ' Tó þ&aelig-acute;m sóþum ges&aelig-acute;lþum ic tiohhie &thorn-bar; ic þé l&aelig-acute;de, ' Bt. 22, 2 ; F. 78, 1-7. Hé teohchode hine tó l&aelig-acute;danne on lífes weg, Past. 305, 5. VI. of a road, to serve as a passage to :-- Weg þe l&aelig-acute;deþ (l&aelig-acute;das, L.) tó forwyrde . . . se weg þe l&aelig-acute;deþ (l&aelig-acute;des, L.) tó lífe, Mt. R. 7, 13-14. Gán on ðone weg þe ús létt tó heofonan ríce, Chr. 1086; P. 221, 25. VII. the object inanimate, to guide, give direction to something flexible :-- Sé þe foran l&aelig-acute;deð brídels on blancan, El. 1184. VII a. to trace a line, boundary, track, &c. :-- Gif ðá landgem&aelig-acute;re ealswá w&aelig-acute;ron swá man heó on fruman l&aelig-acute;dde, C. D. iv. 234, 34 : 235, 4. Þá þe lífes weg l&aelig-acute;dan cunnon, Wlfst. 75, 2. Gif mon secge &thorn-bar; man &thorn-bar; trod áwóh drífe, þonne mót sé þe &thorn-bar; yrfe áh trod oð tó stæðe l&aelig-acute;dan, Ll. Th. i. 352, 11. VIII. to guide a ship, steer :-- Gé þe þus brontne UNCERTAIN ceól ofer lagustr&aelig-acute;te l&aelig-acute;dan cwómon, B. 239. IX. to deal with, treat :-- Ic naman Drihtnes herige, and hine mid lofsange l&aelig-acute;de swylce laudabo nomen Dei mei cum cantico, et magnificabo eum in laude, Ps. Th. 68, 31. X. to engage or take part in, perform :-- Þá wurðiað þín weorc wordum and d&aelig-acute;dum . . . and Críst heriað and him lof l&aelig-acute;dað, Hy. 7, 25. Hé wæs eft swá &aelig-acute;r lof l&aelig-acute;dende, An. 1479. XI. to pass, go through life :-- Líf l&aelig-acute;dan on gefeán, Bt. 12; F. 36, 24. Ancorlíf, munuclíf l&aelig-acute;dan, Bd. 4, 27; Sch. 511, 2: 3, 27; Sch. 316, 4 (see all three in Dict.). XII. intrans. to take a certain direction :-- Hé ána is ealra beáma on eorðwege úp l&aelig-acute;dendra beorhtast geblówen, Ph. 178. v. be-, mis-, ofer-, ymb-l&aelig-acute;dan; under-l&aelig-acute;ded.
-l&aelig-acute;de. v. un-l&aelig-acute;d, -l&aelig-acute;de: L&aelig-acute;den. Add: [v. N. E. D. leden.] v. bóc&dash-uncertain;léden.
L&aelig-acute;den; adj. Add :-- On Lýdenre spr&aelig-acute;ce, Angl. viii. 313, 19.
L&aelig-acute;den-bóc. Add :-- Ðá ungel&aelig-acute;redan preóstas gif hí hwæt litles understandaþ of þám Lýdenbócum, Ælfc. Gen. Thw. 2, 11.
l&aelig-acute;dend a bringer :-- &AElig-acute;s l&aelig-acute;dend legislatorem, Ps. Rdr. 9, 21.
-l&aelig-acute;dendlic. v. ge-l&aelig-acute;dendlic.
L&aelig-acute;den-gereord. Add: -- Leornian sprecan on Lédengereorde discere sermocinari Latina lingua, Coll. M. 18, 34.
L&aelig-acute;den-lár, e; f. Latin lore, knowledge of Latin :-- Sé þe þurh L&aelig-acute;denláre rihtne geleáfan understandan ne cunne geleornige húru on Englisc, Wlfst. 124, 29: 126, 23.
L&aelig-acute;den-lic; adj. Latin :-- Nú hæfst þú mé ofte gebedon &thorn-bar; ic þé út árehte mid L&aelig-acute;denlicre spr&aelig-acute;ce þæs eadigestan Nicholaes gebyrdtída, Nap. 40.
L&aelig-acute;den-spr&aelig-acute;c. Add :-- Sé þe þurh Lédenspr&aelig-acute;ce rihtne geleáfan understandan ne cunne geleornige húru on Englisc, Wlfst. 126, 1.
l&aelig-acute;d-lic, -líce. v. un-l&aelig-acute;dlic, -líce: l&aelig-acute;dness. Add: v. onwegá-, wiþ-l&aelig-acute;dness.
l&aelig-acute;fan. Add: to cause to remain (lífan). I. of a deceased person, to have as remainder after one :-- Se gesibsuma l&aelig-acute;fð symle yrfeweard æfter him sunt reliquiae homini pacifico, Ps. Th. 36, 36. Hé l&aelig-acute;fde æfter him þreó sunan, Chr. 1086; P. 221, 11. Nam se óðer hí and wearð deád, ne sé s&aelig-acute;d ne l&aelig-acute;fde . . . And ealle seofon hí hæfdon and s&aelig-acute;d ne l&aelig-acute;fdon, Mk. 12, 21, 22. Gif hwá gefare and nán bearn ne gestriéne, gif hé bróðor l&aelig-acute;fe, fó sé tó his wífe, Past. 43, 13. II. to transmit at death to heirs or successors, bequeath :-- Manige for bearnléste eallne þone welan ðe hí gegaderigaþ hí l&aelig-acute;fað fræmdum tó brúcanne orbus liberis alienum censum nutrit heredi, Bt. 11, 1; F. 32, 7. Hí l&aelig-acute;fað fremdum heora &aelig-acute;hte relinquent alienis divitias suas, Ps. Th. 48, 9. Hé þám yldestan eaforan l&aelig-acute;fde folc, Gen. 1214: 1179. Hé eaferum l&aelig-acute;fde, swá déð eádig mon, lond and leÁdbyrig, þá hé of lífe gewát, B. 2470. Hí of lífe gewyton and l&aelig-acute;fdon heora &aelig-acute;hta þám æðelum mannum. Iulianus ðá d&aelig-acute;lde . . . heora landáre, þe him l&aelig-acute;fed was, Hml. S. 4, 79-82. Þonne þú heonan cyrre . . . l&aelig-acute;f ús écne gefeán, Cri. 159. Ic wilnode . . . æfter mínum lífe þám monnum tó l&aelig-acute;fanne þe æfter mé w&aelig-acute;ren mín gemynd on gódum weorcum, Bt. 17; F. 60, 16. III. to allow to remain, not to take, consume, remove, &c. :-- Hí nymað &aelig-acute;lc wiht, and uneáðe hí ám þearfiendum lytles hwæt l&aelig-acute;fað, Ll. Lbmn. 476, 11. Hí náman æt heora mágon sceattas genóge . . . and á spendon and d&aelig-acute;ldon hafenleásum mannum . . . Þæt feoh &thorn-bar; hí &aelig-acute;r l&aelig-acute;fdon (had not spent before) hí mid heom tó þám scræfe hæfdon, Hml. S. 23, 198-213. Eal monncynnes þæt þ&aelig-acute;r l&aelig-acute;fed wæs, Ors. 2, 6; S. 88, 6; Bt. 11, 1; F. 30, 19. ¶ where the object is food, not to eat :-- Wulfas on &aelig-acute;fne ne l&aelig-acute;fað náwiht oð morgen, Ll. Lbmn. 476, 3. Þæt þæt hí l&aelig-acute;fon healdan heora bearnum reliquerunt quae superfuerunt parvulis suis, Ps. Th. 16, 14. Eal &thorn-bar; fl&aelig-acute;sc &thorn-bar; wildeór l&aelig-acute;fen carnem quae a bestiis fuerit praegustata, Ll. Th. i. 54, 1. III a. to leave after subtraction :-- Dó of ðám feórþan deále eall þæt seó s&aelig-acute; his ofseten hæfþ . . . ðonne miht ðú ongitan ætte þæs ealles nis monnum máre l&aelig-acute;fed tó búgianne búton swelce án lytel cafertún, Bt. 18, 1; F. 62, 16. IV. to leave, not to take with one :-- Þá men þe hé beæftan him l&aelig-acute;fde, Chr. 755 ; P. 48, 14.
læfel. Add :-- Læfel manile, Wrt. Voc. ii. 56, 46. Hé hét geótan wæter on læfel misit aquam in pelvem, Hml. A. 155, 102. Man sceal habban . . . læflas, Angl. ix. 264, 21.
l&aelig-acute;fend. Substitute: v. l&aelig-acute;rend.
læfer. I. Add: In local names :-- Ad uadum qui uocatum Leuerford, C. D. i. 64, 12. Leuuremer Livermere (in Suffolk), iv. 245, 30. Cf. Liversedge, Liverpool; cf. eá-lifer. II. Add :-- Læfer lamina (auri), An. Ox. 2, 26. Læfrum petalis (deauratis), 5497. Leafrum, 2, 497. In Hml. Th. ii. 498, 3 læfrum translates laminis. v. reád&dash-uncertain;gold-læfer.
-læg. Add: ge-(at ge-lagu), ofer-læg.
l&aelig-acute;ge (?); adj. Fallow, unploughed; in cpds. l&aelig-acute;g-æcer, C. D. iii. 442, 9: l&aelig-acute;g-hrycg, 437, 18. v. N. E. D. lea.
l&aelig-acute;l. I. Add: -- L&aelig-acute;la uibices, An. Ox. 7, 246. L&aelig-acute;lo, 8, 184. II.
L&AElig-acute;LIAN -- L&AElig-acute;S 601
Add :-- L&aelig-acute;l liuor, An. Ox. 32, 24. ¶ The word glosses linor = envy :-- L&e-acute-hook;la liuoris (rancida liuoris inuidia, Ald. 40, 14), An. Ox. 4, 52. Cf. l&aelig-acute;lian.
l&aelig-acute;lian. Substitute: I. to hurl a dart (?) :-- &THORN-bar;te nales ðá sweartan deóblu in mínre sídan léligen, swá swá gewuniað, scytas ut non tetri daemones in latera mea librent, ut solent, iacula, Lch. i. lxxiii, 33. II. to get black and blue :-- Æfestian, l&aelig-acute;lian libescant (cf. l&aelig-acute;l; II. ¶), Wrt. Voc. ii. 50, 41.
l&aelig-acute;men. In l. 8 read l&aelig-acute;mena for l&aelig-acute;mina (v. Wülck. Gl. 404, 39), and add :-- Se líchoma l&aelig-acute;men is, for ðám þe hé of ðám geworht wæs, Verc, Först. 148, 21. Ðá ðæs æfter sexténe geárum forlét hé þone l&aelig-acute;mnan ofn ðæs menniscan líchoman, Shrn. 50, 33.
l&aelig-acute;n. Add :-- Gif ðæt God geteód hæbbe, and mé ðæet on l&aelig-acute;ne gelíð (it is to be granted me) ðæt gesibbra ærfeweard forðcymeð wépnedhádes, C. D. ii. 121, 26. Þæt þæt þe heó tó l&aelig-acute;ne onféng, Gr. D. 97, 12.
l&aelig-acute;nan. Add: I. to lend, grant temporary possession of a thing on the condition of the return of the same or its equivalent :-- Be ðám monnum ðe heora w&aelig-acute;pna tó monslyhte l&aelig-acute;nað. Gif hwá his w&aelig-acute;pnes óðrum onl&aelig-acute;ne (l&aelig-acute;ne, v. l.), Ll. Th. i. 74, 1-3. I a. to lend for a consideration, lend (money) at interest :-- Gif bisceop . . . oððe hwylc Godes þeów l&aelig-acute;nð his feoh tó unrihtun gafole (pecuniam suam injusto foenore mutuam dederit), Ll. Th. ii. 198, 14. Be þám gehádodum mannum þe hyra feoh l&aelig-acute;nað tó hýre, 194, 31. Ys forboden &thorn-bar; hé his feoh, ne his &aelig-acute;hta (pecuniam suam vel possessiones) tó nánum unrihtum gafole ne l&aelig-acute;ne; &thorn-bar; is &thorn-bar; hé hine máran ne bidde tó ágyfanne þonne hé him &aelig-acute;r l&aelig-acute;nde; ac for lufe l&aelig-acute;ne gehwá óðrum his feoh and his &aelig-acute;hta, 194, 15-19. II. to grant :-- Se góda líchama þancode Gode ealre þ&aelig-acute;re áre . . . þe hé him l&aelig-acute;nde, Wlfst. 237, 6. Wísdóm l&aelig-acute;nende &l-bar; týðiende sapientiam praestans, Ps. L. 18, 8.
l&aelig-acute;ne. Add :-- Ðæt wæs tó suíðe scortre hwíle, for ð&aelig-acute;m ðiós woruld is suíðe l&aelig-acute;nu in tempore paucorum dierum, Past. 255, 11. Sé ðe égðer wilt ge þissa l&aelig-acute;nena stóclífa ge þára écena háma, Solil. H. 2, 14.
l&aelig-acute;n-lic. Add :-- Wé sculon geþencean &thorn-bar; þis líf is l&aelig-acute;nlic þe wé nú on libbað, Ll. Th. ii. 400, 15.
l&aelig-acute;nend-lic. Add: -- Ealle þás l&aelig-acute;nendlican earfeðnessa ende habbað ac þá tóweardan ende nabbaþ, Verc. Först. 141, 7 : 142, 11.
l&aelig-acute;n-land. Add :-- Þonne is þæs londes þridde half híd þe Óswold selð Cynelme his þegne tó bóclonde, swá hé hit him &aelig-acute;r hæfde tó forl&aelig-acute;ten tó l&aelig-acute;nlonde, Cht. E. 208, 11.
læpe-wince, an : f. A lapwing :-- Laepaeuincae, lepeuuince, laepiuince cucuzata, Txts. 52, 264. v. hleápe-wince (of which læpewince seems the earliest form).
-læpped. Add: v. twi-læpped; and take after læppa.
læppa. Add :-- Lappa lanna, angulus auris, Hpt. 33, 244, 8.
-l&aelig-acute;r, empty. v. ge-l&aelig-acute;r; l&aelig-acute;re, l&aelig-acute;r-ness. [v. N. E. D. leer.].
l&aelig-acute;ran. Add: I. to show the way (lit. or fig.) to a person :-- Gáþ ealle on þone weg þe eów l&aelig-acute;raþ ðá forem&aelig-acute;ran bisna þára gódena gumena, Bt. 40, 4; F. 238, 29. Simle ic þíne weogas wanhogan l&aelig-acute;rde doceam iniquos vias tuas, Ps. C. 105. II. to show a person the way to or from, guide, direct :-- Hé mec l&aelig-acute;reð from þé on stearcne weg, Jul. 282. Hé l&aelig-acute;rde þá leóde on geleáfan weg, An. 1682. III. to guide the action of a person :-- Sió godcunde foretiohhung l&aelig-acute;rde ðone þe hé wolde &thorn-bar; þe gold hýdde, and eft þone þe hé wolde &thorn-bar; hit funde, Bt. 40, 6; S. 140, 16. IV. to show what should be observed or done. (1) where there is advising, exhorting, admonishing, persuading, instigating, &c. (a) absolute :-- L&aelig-acute;rdan hortantur, l&aelig-acute;rað hortamini, Wrt. Voc. ii. 42, 47, 48. Dióule l&aelig-acute;rende diabolo instigante, Rtl. 114, 5. (b) with personal object. (α) alone :-- Salomon cuæð: ' Dó, mín sunu, suá ic ðé l&aelig-acute;re' exhortatio subditur: Fac quod dico, Past. 193, 17. Wígend l&aelig-acute;rde helle deóful . . . and þæt word gecwæð: ' Sleáð synnigne ofer seolfes múð, ' An. 1299. On óðre wísan sint tó l&aelig-acute;ranne (cf. manianne, 19) ðá scamleásan, on óðre ðá scamfæstan. Ð&aelig-acute;m scamleásan ne wyrð nó gestiéred bútan micelre t&aelig-acute;linge, Past. 205, 21 : 179, 21. (β) to exhort, &c. to something :-- Þú þrístlíce þeóde l&aelig-acute;rest tó beadowe, An. 1187. Óðer hine tyhteð and on t&aelig-acute;so l&aelig-acute;reð, Sal. 493. (γ) with clause :-- Ic þé l&aelig-acute;re . . . þæt þú hospcwide . . . &aelig-acute;fre ne fremme, El. 522. Óðer hine l&aelig-acute;reð þæt hé lufan healde, Sal. 491. Ðás leásan spell l&aelig-acute;raþ gehwilcne man . . . &thorn-bar; hé hine ne besió tó his ealdum yfelum, Bt. 35, 6; F. 170, 15. Þú synfulle simle l&aelig-acute;rdes &thorn-bar; hió cerrende Críste hérdon, Ps. C. 55. Se deófol þone Iúdas l&aelig-acute;rde &thorn-bar; hé Drihten bel&aelig-acute;wde, Hml. A. 154, 66. Ic leófra gehwone l&aelig-acute;ran wille &thorn-bar; hé ne ág&aelig-acute;le g&aelig-acute;stes þearfe, Cri. 816: Dóm. 47: El. 1206. Sint tó l&aelig-acute;ranne ðá oferspr&aelig-acute;can ðæt hié wacorlíce ongieten admonendi sunt multiloquio vacantes, ut vigilanter aspiciant, Past. 277, 3. (2) of authoritative utterance, to prescribe, order, enjoin, direct. (a) absolute :-- Dó swá ic l&aelig-acute;re, Ll. Th. i. 184, 14. (b) with clause :-- Ic l&aelig-acute;re &thorn-bar; hé dó swá ic &aelig-acute;r cwæð, Angl. ix. 260, 8. Æt &aelig-acute;restan wé l&aelig-acute;rað &thorn-bar; &aelig-acute;ghwelc mon his áð and his wed wærlíce healde, Ll. Th. i. 60, 2. Wé l&aelig-acute;rað and biddað and on Godes naman beÁdað &thorn-bar;. . . , 364, 21. &AElig-acute;ghwilc cild sí, wé l&aelig-acute;rað, gefullod binnon nigon nihton, ii. 292, 5. (c) with personal object. (α) alone :-- Hé self dó swá swá hé óðre l&aelig-acute;rð, Past. 453, 15. (β) with a noun object, of that which is enjoined or commended :-- Óðerne hé l&aelig-acute;rde geðyld alteri patientiam proponit, Past. 291, 21. Ðæt hé l&aelig-acute;re ðá óðre eáðmétta, . . . ond l&aelig-acute;re ðá sláwan geornfulnesse gódes weorces. . . and ðá uncystgan cysta l&aelig-acute;re . . . l&aelig-acute;ren hí ðá wífgálan gesinicipe . . . and ðá forhæbbendan l&aelig-acute;ren forhæfdnesse superbis praedicetur humilitas . . . torpentibus praedicetur sollicitudo boni operis . . . tenacibus infundatur tribuendi largitas . . . incontinentibus laudetur conjugium . . . continentibus laudetur virginitas corporis, 453, 19-32. (γ) with dat. infin. :-- Þé nán neódðearf ne l&aelig-acute;rde tó wyrcanne quem non externae pepulerunt fingere caussae, Bt. 33, 4; F. 128, 11. (δ) with clause :-- Hwæt wile ðæt beón weorca ðæt ús on óðerre stówe forbiét ðæt wé hit beforan mannum dón, on óðerre l&aelig-acute;rð (cf. hét, l. 8) ðæt wé hit beforan mannum dón quid est quod opus nostrum et ita faciendum est, ne UNCERTAIN videatur, et tamen ut debeat videri praecipitur, Past. 451, 3. Hé ðone óðerne l&aelig-acute;rde ðæt hé him anwald on tuge alteri imperium proponit, 291, 20. Wé willað biddan freónda gehwylcne and eal folc l&aelig-acute;ran georne &thorn-bar; hí inwerdre heortan God lufian, Ll. Th. i. 316, 18 : 326, 1. V. to impart knowledge. (1) to declare, proclaim :-- Hí l&aelig-acute;rden hira synna, and hí hí nánwuht ne h&aelig-acute;lon peccatum suum praedicaverunt, nec absconderunt, Past. 427, 28. (2) to teach, give instruction in a subject, preach :-- Hé gewritu l&aelig-acute;reð, Sal. 50. Monige wíse láreówas winnað mid hira ðeáwum wið ðá bebodu ðe hí mid wordum l&aelig-acute;rað quod verbis praedicant, moribus impugnant, Past. 29, 22. Nán cræft nis tó l&aelig-acute;ranne ð&aelig-acute;m ðe hine &aelig-acute;r geornlíce ne leornode nulla ars doceri praesumitur, nisi intenta prius meditatione discatur, 25, 15. (3) to teach a person something. (a) with acc. :-- Þú hine þeódscipe þínne l&aelig-acute;rest de lege tua docueris eum, Ps. Th. 93, 12. Hé ús l&aelig-acute;rð nytwyrðlicu ðing, Past. 255, 12. (b) with clause :-- Sint hié tó l&aelig-acute;ranne hú hié scilen d&aelig-acute;lan, Past. 341, 16. (c) to instruct a person in a subject :-- L&aelig-acute;re mon furður on L&aelig-acute;den&dash-uncertain;geðióde ðá ðe mon furður l&aelig-acute;ran wille, Past. 7, 13. (4) to teach something to a person :-- Hé þám folce Godes gerihta l&aelig-acute;rde, Hml. Th. i. 74, 22. (5) to teach a person, give instruction to, educate, train :-- Se Wísdóm þe hit lange &aelig-acute;r týde and l&aelig-acute;rde, Bt. 3, 1; F. 4, 30. Hé in Effessia ealle þráge leóde l&aelig-acute;rde, Ap. 31. Úre fl&aelig-acute;sclican fædras l&aelig-acute;rdon ús patres carnis nostrae habuimus eruditores, Past. 255, 7, 10. Hié l&aelig-acute;rdon hira tungan, and wenedon tó leásunge docuerunt linguam suam loqui mendacium, 239, 18. Hú mislíce mon sceal menn l&aelig-acute;ran, 173, 13. Hit bið swíðe geswincful ðæt mon &aelig-acute;lcne mon scyle on sundrum l&aelig-acute;ran, hit is ðeáh earfoðre ealle ætsomne tó l&aelig-acute;ranne, 453, 10-12. Ongan his brýd wíshýdig wer wordum l&aelig-acute;ran, Gen. 1823. Hí sægdon swá fram Siluestre l&aelig-acute;rde w&aelig-acute;ron, El. 191. (6) absolute, to teach, act as teacher :-- &AElig-acute;lc wyrd is nyt þára ðe áuþer déþ, oððe l&aelig-acute;rþ oþþe wricþ quae aut exercet, aut corrigit, prodest, Bt. 40, 2; F. 236, 16. Sió sóðfæstnes self l&aelig-acute;rde docenti veritate, Past. 125, 7. Wé rehton hwelc se hierde bión sceal; nú wé him willað cýðan hú hé l&aelig-acute;ran sceal qualis esse debeat Pastor ostendimus, nunc qualiter doceat demonstremus, 173, 15. Wæs hé gemét tómiddes ðára láreówa frignende, nalles l&aelig-acute;rende (docens); for ð&aelig-acute;m hé ús wolde ðæt tó bísene dón ðætte ðá unl&aelig-acute;redan ne dorsten l&aelig-acute;ran (docere), 385, 27. &AElig-acute;r þám þe his Apostolas tófarene w&aelig-acute;ron geond ealle eorðan tó l&aelig-acute;ranne, Ll. Th. i. 56, 4. (7) intransitive, to give instruction about something :-- Se hálga heáp . . . hí ásendon tó l&aelig-acute;renne eallnm leódscipum be Crístes tócyme for middangeardes álýsednysse, Hml. Th. i. 388, 16. v. mis-, þurh-l&aelig-acute;ran; fore-, yfel-l&aelig-acute;rende.
l&aelig-acute;re should be taken here: -l&aelig-acute;re. v. earfoþ-, eáþ-l&aelig-acute;re: -l&aelig-acute;red. Add: v. gestæf-l&aelig-acute;red.
l&aelig-acute;rend, es; m. One who teaches, instigates, &c. v. l&aelig-acute;ran :-- Bep&aelig-acute;cend deceptor, l&aelig-acute;rend (printed læfend) seductor, l&aelig-acute;wend proditor, Wrt. Voc. i. 49, 16-18. Drihten &thorn-bar; ongeat, &thorn-bar; se deófol þone Iúdas l&aelig-acute;rde &thorn-bar; hé hine bel&aelig-acute;wde . . . Wiste hé &thorn-bar; hé on his godcundre mihte hæfde &aelig-acute;ghwæðer ge ðone l&aelig-acute;wend ge ðone l&aelig-acute;rend, Hml. A. 154, 71.
lærest. l. l&aelig-acute;rest. The r for s may be explained by Verner's Law.
l&aelig-acute;restre. In l. 3 for 543 read 548, and add :-- Lár hyrde hopan . . . l&aelig-acute;restre mægenes disciplina custos spei . . . magistra uirtutis, Scint. 206, 18.
l&aelig-acute;rig the border of a shield. v. ymb-l&aelig-acute;r(i)gian.
l&aelig-acute;ring-mann. Add :-- Þæs láreówes h&aelig-acute;s and þæs l&aelig-acute;rincmannes (leornincgmannes, v. l.) weorc magistri jussio et discipuli opera, R. Ben. 20, 6.
l&aelig-acute;s. Add :-- Seó l&aelig-acute;s is tóforan eallum mannum gem&aelig-acute;ne on ðám h&aelig-acute;ðfelda the pasture on the heathfield lies open to admit all men, C. D. iii. 419, 21. Án l&aelig-acute;s on waruðe, 429, 16. Sceáp l&aelig-acute;suwe (léswe, Ps. Srt.) his oues pascuae eius, Ps. L. 99, 3. On stówe l&aelig-acute;swen (l&aelig-acute;swe?, l&aelig-acute;swena?; léswe, Ps. Srt.) in loco pascuae, 22, 2. Hý létan him tó . . . þá m&aelig-acute;de . . . and twégra getýmena l&aelig-acute;se, and týn cúna forð mid þas hláfordes and his sceápa l&aelig-acute;se æfter þæs hláfordes, C. D. B. i. 544, 3. Þone þe ðis land gelytlede on l&aelig-acute;su[m ?] oððe on gem&aelig-acute;ru[m ?] qui istam terram diminuerit in pascuis siue metis, C. D. v. 253, 36. ¶ beól&aelig-acute;s pasture where there were many flowers for bees ? Cf. Beó-leáh, C. D. iii. 75, 37 :-- On beólése . . . út þurh beóleáse, C. D. B. iii. 249,
602 L&AElig-acute;S -- L&AElig-acute;TAN
31. [v. N. E. D. lease, leasow.] v. fearn-, feld- (C. D. iv. 96, 2 : vi. 39, 9), mór-, út-, wudu-l&aelig-acute;s.
l&aelig-acute;s allowance. v. beód-l&aelig-acute;s.
læs. l. l&aelig-acute;s, and in last citation þinga for þing, and add: I. adv. or conj. :-- Næfð nán man tó þæs hál eágan þæt hé &aelig-acute;ni hwíle mage lócigan ongeán þas UNCERTAIN sunnan þe wé h&aelig-acute;r geseóð, and húru þæs þe l&aelig-acute;s (all the less) gyf heó hefð unhále, Solil. H. 35, 1. Hys mé lyst swá læng swá l&aelig-acute;s, 36, 17. Ðú h&aelig-acute;tst mé forl&aelig-acute;tan þá unrótnesse, ðý l&aelig-acute;st ic . . . þý mettrumra sí, 49, 1. Þe l&aelig-acute;ste ( = l&aelig-acute;s þe) gehremde ne offenderet, An. Ox. 3675. Þe l&aelig-acute;ste (ne forte) beó gemétt bróþor ásolcen, Angl. xiii. 434, 982. II. as subst. :-- Ic oft wíscte &thorn-bar; hyra l&aelig-acute;s w&aelig-acute;re swá gewinfulra, Nar. 2, 29.
l&aelig-acute;s-hosum. Perhaps for fótleáste l&aelig-acute;shosum should be read fótleáse l&aelig-acute;-acute;sthosan footless hose, hose that did not cover the sole of the foot. v. l&aelig-acute;st; f.
læssa. l. l&aelig-acute;ssa, and add: A. as adj. agreeing with a substantive expressed or understood. I. of size, extent in space :-- Ic eom máre þonne þes middangeard, l&aelig-acute;sse þonne hondwyrm, Rä. 67, 2. L&aelig-acute;ssan ymbgang hæfð se mann þe g&aelig-acute;ð ábútan án hús þonne sé ðe ealle ðá burh beg&aelig-acute;ð. Swá eác ðe móna h&aelig-acute;fð his ryne hraðor áurnen on þám l&aelig-acute;ssan ymbhwyrfte þonne seó sunne hæbbe on þám máran, Lch. iii. 248, 10-15: Met. 28, 12. Lýssan minima, Kent. Gl. 1100. Hé þára l&aelig-acute;ssena ríca reccend is, Ors. 2, 1; S. 58, 25. Senepes s&aelig-acute;d . . . is ealra s&aelig-acute;da l&aelig-acute;st (l&aelig-acute;sest, L.), Mk. 4, 31. Se móna ealra tungla h&aelig-acute;fð l&aelig-acute;stne embegang, Angl. vii. 14, 134. II. of number, in the case of collective unities :-- Þ&aelig-acute;r máre folc sig . . . þ&aelig-acute;r l&aelig-acute;sse folc síg UNCERTAIN, Ll. Th. i. 232, 14. Hié werod l&aelig-acute;sse hæfdon þonne Húna cyning, El. 48. III. of time :-- Scyld wel gebearg líf l&aelig-acute;ssan hwíle, B. 2571. IV. of qualities, emotions, conditions, actions, or occurrences, expressing extent or degree :-- Wæs se gryre l&aelig-acute;ssa efne swá micle swá bið wíggryre wífes be w&aelig-acute;pnedmen, B. 1282. Ne þincð mé þæt wundur wuhte þe l&aelig-acute;sse, Met. 20, 117. On &aelig-acute;nigum þingum cræftig, on máran wísdóme oþþe on l&aelig-acute;ssan, Bl. H. 49, 28. &AElig-acute;nigne creft geliorman, oððe leásan oððe máran, Solil. H. 30, 22. L&aelig-acute;ssan sige hæfð sé sé ðá burhware ofercymð, Past. 218, 18. Hé forl&aelig-acute;t ðá máran gód and went hine tó ð&aelig-acute;m l&aelig-acute;ssum relictis amplioribus bonis ad minima retorquetur, 403, 5. Nó þæt l&aelig-acute;sest wæs hondgemóta, B. 2354. IV a. having a quality mentioned to a slighter extent,less in respect to (on) :-- Ic eom on mægne mínum l&aelig-acute;sse þonne se hondwyrm, Rä. 41, 95. V. of things. (1) with respect to value :-- &THORN-bar; man n&aelig-acute;nne ne slóge for l&aelig-acute;ssan yrfe þonne .XII. pæniga weorð, búton hé fleón wille . . . &thorn-bar; man ne wandode þonne þeáh hit l&aelig-acute;sse w&aelig-acute;re, Ll. Th. i. 242, 8-11. Nalæs hí hine l&aelig-acute;ssan lácum teódan, þeódgestreónum, þonne þá dydon þe hine æt frumsceafte forð onsendon, B. 43. (2) with respect to importance or interest :-- Ne sceolde hé nán ðing forgýman ðe &aelig-acute;fre tó note mehte; ne forða ( = furþum) músfellan; ne &thorn-bar; gít l&aelig-acute;sse is, tó hæpsan pinn, Angl. ix. 265, 9. Ðæt hié be ð&aelig-acute;m l&aelig-acute;ssan ðingum ongieten hú suíðe hié gesyngiað on ð&aelig-acute;m máran ut ex minori consideratione colligant, quantum in majoribus rebus delinquant, Past. 375, 23. L&aelig-acute;stra þinga [ne] geðrýstl&aelig-acute;cende áht secgan þæs ðe hé geseah, Hml. S. 23 b, 644. VI. of persons or places, in reference to rank, dignity, &c. :-- Ic eom l&aelig-acute;ssa þonne ealle þíne miltsunga, Gen. 32, 10. Man þe bið l&aelig-acute;ssa maga þon[n]e se cyninges þegn, Ll. Th. i. 154, 7. Heáfodmynstres griðbryce . . . medemran mynstres . . . gít l&aelig-acute;ssan, 342, 3. Hé m&aelig-acute;ðe cann on óðrum mannum, on his gelícum ge on l&aelig-acute;ssan mannum, Wlfst. 51, 31. Seó ilce burg Babylonia, seó ðe m&aelig-acute;st wæs and &aelig-acute;rest ealra burga, seó is nú l&aelig-acute;st and wéstast, Ors. 2, 4; S. 74, 23. Úre Áliésend, ðe mára is and m&aelig-acute;rra eallum gesceaftum, hé hine gemedomode tó biónne betwiux ð&aelig-acute;m l&aelig-acute;sðum (l&aelig-acute;stum, v. l.) and ð&aelig-acute;m gingestum monnum, Past. 301, 13. VI a. applied to the inferior or smaller of two persons or places of the same name :-- Ðæs Jacóbes leásse (l&aelig-acute;ssa, R.) móder Jacobi minoris mater, Mk. L. 15, 40. Se l&aelig-acute;ssa middangeard michrocosmos, Wrt. Voc. i. 282, 22 : 64, 13. VII. referring to (mean) conduct :-- Þætte ealra l&aelig-acute;st wæs, his gingran dohter hé nolde búton hæftniéde habban, seó wæs lytel cild etiam parvulas filias crudeli captivitate retinebat, Ors. 3, 9; S. 128, 18. VIII. of quantity :-- Him gebyriað .v. æceras tó habbanne, máre gyf hit on lande ðeáw sý, and tó lytel hit bið beó hit á l&aelig-acute;sse, Ll. Th. i. 432, 25. Sume beóð on máran áre, sume on l&aelig-acute;ssan, sume fulneáh búton, Solil. H. 44, 13. On l&aelig-acute;sse plihte, Ll. Th. i. 226, 6. Ánra gehwylc þe hafað l&aelig-acute;sse mægen, Sal. 356. B. as substantive, (1) the less :-- For hwan ne déþ hé &thorn-bar; l&aelig-acute;sse nú hé þæt máre dyde?, Bl. H. 181, 6. (2) less, a smaller amount :-- Ne w&aelig-acute;ron þás ealle gelíce lange, ac on þyssum wæs þreó þúsend wintra, on sumre l&aelig-acute;sse, on sumere eft máre, Bl. H. 119, 4. Ic for l&aelig-acute;ssan leán teohhade, B. 951. Sé þe l&aelig-acute;sse hæbbe, Ll. Th. i. 414, 19 note : Bl. H. 53, 16. Hweðer ðú máre wisse þonne ðú nú wást, þe l&aelig-acute;sse, Solil. H. 59, 8. (2 a) with gen. :-- Þæt hire þý læsse on þ&aelig-acute;m lytlan ne bið ánum fingre þe hire on eallum bið þ&aelig-acute;m líchoman, Met. 20, 179. Hí l&aelig-acute;sse ongietað ðæs ðe him hreówan ðyrfe, Past. 411, 4. Hé hit gehíwað swá þæt l&aelig-acute;st manna wát hú hé him wið þone ðeódfeónd gescyldan sceal, Wlfst. 54, 19. Ðá ðe L&aelig-acute;denspr&aelig-acute;ce l&aelig-acute;ste (l&aelig-acute;sðe, v. l.) cúðon, 9, 16. (3) what is of less importance :-- He mót &aelig-acute;gðer witan ge l&aelig-acute;sse ge máre, ge betere ge m&aelig-acute;tre, Angl. ix. 259, 23. C. as adverb :-- Sé þe l&aelig-acute;sse maga sý, Ll. Th. i. 414, 19. Swunce máre sé þe unriht gestreón on his handa stóde, and l&aelig-acute;sse sé þe þ&aelig-acute;r áriht onspr&aelig-acute;ce, 290, 5. Ic lufige &aelig-acute;lcne mínra freónda, sume l&aelig-acute;sse, sume máre, Solil. H. 16, 18. Ic ðóhte þæt hit w&aelig-acute;re l&aelig-acute;sse &aelig-acute;ðrýt (less wearisome; or? a less weariness) tó gehýrenne, Hml. Th. ii. 2, 11. &AElig-acute;lc fagnað þæs þe l&aelig-acute;ste (to a very slight extent) hé ongytan mæg, Solil. H. 31, 23. v. l&aelig-acute;s.
læst, e; f. A fault, sin :-- Wé sceolon biddan georne God þæt hé úre neóda gecnáwe and úre læsta gebéte, Nap. 41. [Icel. l&o-hook;str. v. N. E. D. last a fault.]
l&aelig-acute;stan. Add: v. ge-l&aelig-acute;stan: l&aelig-acute;ste. Add :-- Laesti vordalium, Wrt. Voc. ii. 124, 17 : -l&aelig-acute;stfullian. v. ge-l&aelig-acute;stfullian: l&aelig-acute;st-wyrhta. Add :-- L&aelig-acute;stwyrhta caligarius, Wülck, Gl. 112, 9, omitted at Wrt. Voc. i. 19. 17.
l&aelig-acute;swian. Add: I. trans. (1) with acc. :-- Hé l&aelig-acute;sode (fédde, v. l.) his swýn porcos pavit, Gr. D. 106, 28. (2) with dat. :-- Hé gewunode &thorn-bar; hé l&aelig-acute;swode þám eówde his sceápa ovium suarum gregem pascere solebat, Gr. D. 215, 5. II. intrans. of animals, to take food, graze, feed :-- Þá leásiendan pascentes (agnos), An. Ox. 5210. [v. N. E. D. leasow.] v. ed-, ge-l&aelig-acute;swian.
læt. Add: I. slow, sluggish :-- Be lattre meltunge sumra metta, Lch. ii. 160, 9. Late lento, Wrt. Voc. ii. 49, 62. On óðre wísan sint tó manianne ðá ðe bióð tó late (pigri: cf. ðá sláwan 19), on óðre ðá ðe bióð tó hrade, Past. 281, 18. I a. where the matter in which slowness is shown is noted. (1) with gen., B. 1529: Dóm. 89 (in Dict.). (2) with prep., An. 46: Ll. Th. ii. 404, 20 (in Dict.). (3) with dat. infin., Past. 281, 6 : Lk. 24, 25 (in Dict.). (4) with clause, Bl. H. 43, 22 (in Dict.). II. delayed or deferred in time, late :-- Gif se biscop þá gýt l&aelig-acute;ttra w&aelig-acute;re &thorn-bar; hé inne eóde si adhuc episcopus tardius intrasset, Gr. D. 59, 18. III. advanced in point of time in the course of the day or night, late :-- Ðá seó lætre (lættre, v. l.) tíd weóx cum hora tardior excrevisset, Gr. D. 128, 12. Hí w&aelig-acute;ron genýdde &thorn-bar; hí for þ&aelig-acute;re lættran tíde (tardiori hora) wunedon læng þonne hí sceoldon, 126, 26. Oð ðá lætran tíde, 24.
-læt. [Goth. -léte : O. H. Ger. -laz.] v. for-, ge-l&aelig-acute;t.
l&aelig-acute;tan. Add: I. trans. (1) to leave, allow to remain, abstain from taking away. (a) with noun object :-- Hé on fæstre stówe lét sum his folc, Ors. 4, 9 ; S. 190, 1. Hié þone óþerne d&aelig-acute;l þ&aelig-acute;r léton þæt lond tó healdonne, 1, 10 ; S. 46, 21. Hwilce hwíle hine wille Drihten hér on worlde l&aelig-acute;tan, Bl. H. 125, 9. Þú ne scealt nánnæ cláð betweón l&aelig-acute;tan þínum eágum and hym, Solil. H. 43, 16. (b) with clause :-- L&aelig-acute;t þé on gemyndum (keep in mind) hú þæt manegum wearð gefrége, An. 962. (1 α) to loose one's hold of, let go :-- Hé h&aelig-acute;t fealdan &thorn-bar; segl, and eác hwílum lecgan þone mæst and l&aelig-acute;tan þa b&aelig-acute;tinge, Bt. 41, 3; F. 250, 15. (2) to leave undone, unaffected, &c. :-- Gif preóst óðerne un&dash-uncertain;warnode l&aelig-acute;te, Ll. Th. ii. 294, 25 : 296, 15. Hit is wóh &thorn-bar; hí mon l&aelig-acute;te unwítnode . . . ðú &aelig-acute;r cw&aelig-acute;de &thorn-bar; hé unriht dyde, &thorn-bar; hé léte unwítnod þá yfelan, Bt. 38, 3; F. 202, 6-13. L&aelig-acute;tan wr&aelig-acute;ce stille, Gú. 170. (2 a) intrans. To desist from :-- On þane .VII. dæg lét Drehten fram &aelig-acute;ghwilcum weorce, Wlfst. 218, 26. His sunu féng tó his eorldóme and lét of ðan þe hé &aelig-acute;r hæfde, Chr. 1053 ; P. 182, 26. L&aelig-acute;tan desistamus, An. Ox. 56, 320. (3) to leave the control or management of something to some one else :-- Þú þonne l&aelig-acute;tst eal eówer færeld tó þæs windes dóme, Bt. 7, 2; F. 18, 32. Ne l&aelig-acute;t ðú tó aldiódgium ðínne weorðscipe ne des alienis honorem tuum, Past. 249, 10. Þonne sceal ic beó þæs geðafa and létan hyt tó þínum dóme, Solil. H. 32, 19. Ic hæbbe ealle þá sp&aelig-acute;ce tó Ælfhége l&aelig-acute;ten, Cht. Th. 208, 32. (4) to leave to an heir, bequeath :-- Míne sibbe ic l&aelig-acute;te eów, Past. 351, 12. Eallne þone welan hí l&aelig-acute;tað (l&aelig-acute;fað, v. l.) fræmdum tó brúcanne alienum censum nutrit heredi, Bt. 11, 1 ; F. 32, 7. (5) to quit, abandon :-- Wuton cunnian hwænne hine God l&aelig-acute;te Deus dereliquit eum, Ps. Th. 70, 10. Hé sceal l&aelig-acute;tan his wyrignesse and lufian his gebedu, Wlfst. 239, 19. Beódan Abrahame of eorðscræfe &aelig-acute;rist fremman, l&aelig-acute;tan landreste, An. 782. (6) to allow or cause the escape of a confined fluid, to discharge a missile :-- Þú þurh lyft l&aelig-acute;test mildne morgenrén, Az. 82 : 135. Hé hygegár léteð, Mód. 34. Hé l&aelig-acute;teð foreweard hleór on strangne stán, Sal. 113. 'Tód&aelig-acute;lnessa ðára wætera út léton mín eágan.' Tód&aelig-acute;ldu wæteru wé l&aelig-acute;tað út of úrum eágum 'Divisiones aquarum deduxit oculus meus.' Divisas ex oculis aquas deducimus, Past. 413, 27. Hé of stáne lét strange burnan, Ps. Th. 77, 17. Hí þára bearna blód léton swá man gute wæter effuderunt sanguinem eorum sicut aquam, 78, 3. 'L&aelig-acute;t forð ðíne willas.' . . . Ðæt is ðæt mon his wætru út l&aelig-acute;te 'Deriventur fontes tui foras.' . . . Fontes foras derivare est, Past. 373, 12-16. (7) to allow to have :-- Þá bæd Eustachius &thorn-bar; hí him fyrst léton &thorn-bar; hí him tó Gode geb&aelig-acute;don, Hml. S. 30, 424. (8) to grant temporary possession of something to (to) a person :-- Úre Drihten is swíþe gemyndig ealra þára gifena þe hé ús tó l&aelig-acute;teþ, Bl. H. 51, 24. Eádmund oferhergode Cumbraland and hit lét tó eal (eall tó, v. l.) Malculme, on &thorn-bar; gerád &thorn-bar; hé w&aelig-acute;re his midwyrhta, Chr. 945; P. 110, 34. Hé geann Leófsige þæs mannes þe hé him &aelig-acute;r tó lét, Cht. Crw. 23, 18. Dúns&aelig-acute;te beþyrfan, gif heom se cyning an, &thorn-bar; man húru friðgíslas tó heom l&aelig-acute;te Dunsetis expedit, si
-L&AElig-acute;TE -- L&AElig-acute;WEND 603
rex concedat, ut saltem pacis obsides habeant, Ll. Th. i. 356, 21. (9) to allow or cause to pass or go, l&aelig-acute;tan of to let off :-- Ic léte h&aelig-acute;þen folc ofer iów I will send heathen folk upon you, Wlfst. 223, 12. Hé hine sóna hider l&aelig-acute;t continuo illum dimittet huc, Mk. 11, 3. Hé ne lét ná of gebedum his gást he did not let his spirit off prayers, Hml. S. 31, 1357. Dém þú hí tó deáðe, swá tó lífe l&aelig-acute;t, swá þé leófre sý, Jul. 88. Gif se hláford mildheort bið, &thorn-bar; hé þá gýmeleáste tó forgyfenesse l&aelig-acute;te, Ll. Thi. 270, 19. Hét se cásere l&aelig-acute;tan león and beran tó þám cynegum, Hml. S. 24, 29. Hé hét l&aelig-acute;tan him tó twégen león, 51. Hé hét áne strange leó l&aelig-acute;tan intó him, 30, 416. Heó hire mód ongan l&aelig-acute;tan æfter þám lárum Gen. 592. Swá mycele furðor swá hé on háde is l&aelig-acute;ten, R. Ben. 112, 2. II. followed by an infinitive. (1) to permit, allow, suffer. (a) where the infinitive has a subject, and is (α) intrans. :-- Hí ne l&aelig-acute;t God on áne healfe þæs heofones bión, Bt. 39, 13; F. 234, 8. Ic wundrige for hwý God l&aelig-acute;te &aelig-acute;nig yfel beón, oððe gif hé hit geþafian wile . . . , 36, 1; F. 172, 5. Ðæt hé his feax léte weaxan, Past. 139, 25. (β) trans. :-- Ne l&aelig-acute;te gé eów &aelig-acute;lcre láre wind áweccgan, Past. 306, 8. Him w&aelig-acute;re micel ðearf ðæt hié léten Godes ege hié geeáðmédan, 321, 12. (b) where the infinitive is without subject and where now a passive construction may replace the earlier active :-- L&aelig-acute;t þé fullian let yourself be baptized, Hml. S. 5, 204. Ne léten hié nó hié on &aelig-acute;lce healfe gebígean they would not let themselves be inclined to every side, Past. 306, 4. (2) to cause, let (in to let a person know). (a) where the following infinitive has a subject :-- Ic l&aelig-acute;te hig ætwindan tó wuda dimitto eos avolar ad sylvam, Coll. M. 26, 3 : Gen. 438. Ic sígan l&aelig-acute;te wællregn, 1349. Hé leórt tácen forð úp éðigean, El. 1105. (b) where the infinitive is without subject (cf. 1 b) :-- Þú of foldan fódder neátum l&aelig-acute;test ál&aelig-acute;dan producens foenum jumentis, Ps. Th. 103, 13. Se cyng lét tóscyfton þone here geond eall þis land, Chr. 1085; P. 216, 1. L&aelig-acute;t inc geséman, Past. 349, 12. (3) in the imperative as an auxiliary :-- L&aelig-acute;t gán ðín eágean beforan ðínum fótum palpebrae tuae praecedant gressus tuos, Past. 287, 12. L&aelig-acute;t ðíne willas iernan wíde, and tód&aelig-acute;l hié deriventur fontes tui foras, et divide, 373, 4. Hláford, gif þín willa sý, l&aelig-acute;t sendan (sænde man, v. l.) &aelig-acute;rendracan mittatur, si placet, qui huc eum exhibeat, Gr. D. 35, 9. III. to behave, appear, think. (1) intrans. to behave so and so, have the appearance of being, make as though :-- Hé l&aelig-acute;t him eáðelíce ymbe þæt he takes that very easily, Wlfst. 298, 30. Þæt mancyn . . . þæs him náht ne ondr&aelig-acute;dað, ac him orsorh l&aelig-acute;tað (profess to be unconcerned), 182, 15. Se kyngc lét líhtlíce of oð &thorn-bar; hé cóm tó Englalande, and hine lét syððan tacan the king made light of it till he came to England, and afterwards had him taken, Chr. 1076; P. 211, 34. Ealle hí léton swilce hí on &aelig-acute;fen slépon, and sóna ðæs on morgen of ðám sl&aelig-acute;pe áwacedon they all comported themselves as if they had gone to sleep in the evening and soon after in the morning had waked from their sleep, Hml. S. 23, 440. (1 a) reflex., to show oneself so and so :-- Heó efenwyrðe hí lét on eallum þingum þám bisceope condignam se in omnibus episcopo praebuit, Bd. 4, 6; Sch. 384, 4. (2) trans, (a) with object and complement. (α) the object a noun, or pronoun, to regard as :-- Ic for náht l&aelig-acute;te floci fero, Germ. 393, 140. Ic hine gelícne l&aelig-acute;te wísum were similabo eum uiro sapienti, R. Ben. 4, 12. Hé bið tó eáðmód ðám yflan mannan, and l&aelig-acute;t hine him tó gelícne (regards him too much as an equal), Past. 121, 21. Wé ðisses middangeardes welan toresettað and ús leófran l&aelig-acute;tað ðonne ðá lufan þára heofonlicra eádignessa cum mundi diuitias amori caelestium praeponimus, Bd. 3, 19; Sch. 279, 2. &AElig-acute;lc wóh gé l&aelig-acute;tað tó rihte, Wlfst. 297, 27. Þ&aelig-acute;rn þe nán þing him leófre ne l&aelig-acute;tað þonne Críst his qui nihil sibi Christus carius aliquid existimant, R. Ben. 19, 15. Þára hrægla þe nú drihtguman diórost l&aelig-acute;tað, Met. 8, 11. Drihten lét hine him swá leófne &thorn-bar; hé ne geþolode &thorn-bar; hé w&aelig-acute;re medmycelne fyrst geunrótsod hunc quam dilectum Dominus attendet, quem contristari nec ad modicum pertulit, Gr. D. 90, 15. Apollinis þe hí m&aelig-acute;rne god léton, Wlfst. 197, 19. L&aelig-acute;t ðé &aelig-acute;lcne mannan . . . swá leófne swá bróðor, Hex. 44, 24: Fä. 12 : Angl. xii. 516, 24. Ðæt hé ðá ðe him underðiédde sién l&aelig-acute;te him gelíce aequalem se subditis deputet, Past. 107, 15. Ðæt hié l&aelig-acute;ten him ðæt tó genyhte ðæt hié him sellen, 320, 1. Ð&aelig-acute;r hié ne wénden ðæt hié selfe beteran w&aelig-acute;ren ðonne óðre menn, ðæt hié ne l&aelig-acute;ten hiera geðeaht and hiera wénan suá feor beforan ealra óðerra monna wénan nisi meliores se ceteris aestimarent, nequaquam cunctorum consilia suae deliberationi postponerent, 306, 1. Him þás woruld úttor l&aelig-acute;tan þonne þæt éce lif, Gú. 97. Gif þú ðé wilt dón manegra beteran, ðonne scealt þú ðé l&aelig-acute;tan ánes wyrsan, Bt. 32, 1 ; F. 114, 14. Tó hw&aelig-acute;m wé gelíc létan welle ríce Godes ? cui adsimilabimus regnum Dei ?, Mk. R. L. 4, 30. (b) with object alone. (α) the object a noun, to suppose something :-- Nán þridde be him sylfum ne lét hé búton swilce hé of his gemynde w&aelig-acute;re he had no third supposition about himself except it was as if he were out of his mind, Hml. S. 23, 634. (αα) to esteem (?) :-- Him ne bið l&aelig-acute;ten gold ne seolfor neither gold nor silver is held precious by them, Verc. Först. 106, 15. (β) the object a clause, to consider that :-- Swá ic l&aelig-acute;te on mínum geþance &thorn-bar; mé tó nánre byrig swá rihte ne gebyrige swá tó þissere byrig, Hml. S. 23, 675. Hé l&aelig-acute;t þæt hé ána sý strengra þonne hí ealle, Wlfst. 197, 21. Ic l&aelig-acute;te riht (juslum censeo) . . . &thorn-bar; sé þe þone hearm geworhte, &thorn-bar; sé þone hearm gebéte, Ll. Th. i. 418, 4. Hé lét him tó r&aelig-acute;de &thorn-bar; (what) hé þá ger&aelig-acute;dde, Hml. S. 23, 319. Þæt hé l&aelig-acute;te him tó bysne hú þá feónd forwurdon that he regard the fall of the angels as an example for himself, Sat. 196. IV. in phrases (1) with adj., án l&aelig-acute;tan, to let alone, not to meddle with :-- Gif hié þone wæstm án l&aelig-acute;tan wolden, Gen. 644. (2) with verb in infin., beón l&aelig-acute;tan to let be, cease from :-- Uton l&aelig-acute;tan bión þás spr&aelig-acute;ce, Bt. 34, 7 ; F. 144, 18. (3) with adverb. (a) behindan, (α) to leave behind (one), go away without :-- Þé behindan ne l&aelig-acute;t, þonne þú heonan cyrre, mænigo þus micle, Cri. 155. (β) to pass beyond, outstrip :-- Ðonne bist þú bufan ðám rodore, and l&aelig-acute;tst behindan þé þone héhstan heofon, Bt. 36, 2; F. 174, 16 : Met. 24, 29. (b) fram, to start from a port :-- Wé nó geseóð þá stilnesse þ&aelig-acute;re hýþe þe wé &aelig-acute;r fram léton, Gr. D. 6, 19. (c) ofdúne, to let down, to cause or allow to descend :-- Hié léton hiera hrægl ofdúne tó fótum, Ors. 3, 5; S. 106, 19, (d) úp, to put ashore :-- Hé cóm tó Sandwíc and lét þ&aelig-acute;r úp (lét dón úp, v. l.) þá gíslas, Chr. 1014; P. 145, 23. (e) út, to put to sea :-- Godwine eorl . . . lét út áne d&aelig-acute;ge &aelig-acute;r midsumeres mæsse&aelig-acute;fene, Chr. 1052 ; P. 177, 11. Sóna þæs ðe hí on scip eódon and út léton, Bd. 3, 15 ; Sch. 263, 6.
-l&aelig-acute;te. Substitute :-- -l&aelig-acute;te; sbst. v. &aelig-acute;-, blód- (Lch. ii. 16, 8), ge-l&aelig-acute;te: -l&aelig-acute;te; adj. v. &aelig-acute;-, earfoþ-l&aelig-acute;te: -l&aelig-acute;tedness. v. for-l&aelig-acute;tedness.
lætemest; adj. Add :-- On latemystum in nouissimo, Scint. 105, 8.
-l&aelig-acute;tende. v. for-l&aelig-acute;tende: -l&aelig-acute;tennesse. v. for-, tó-l&aelig-acute;tenness: l&aelig-acute;tere. Add: v. for-l&aelig-acute;tere.
læþ :-- Presumat, i. audeat læþ (= geþrístl&aelig-acute;[h]þ?), An. Ox. 955. v. ge-þrístl&aelig-acute;can.
l&aelig-acute;þ land, l&aelig-acute;þ a lathe. Take these together, and add :-- On westan Cænt ð&aelig-acute;r ðæt land and ðæt l&aelig-acute;ð tó líð, C. D. vi. 81, 19. Of Æglesforda and of ellan þám l&aelig-acute;þe þe þ&aelig-acute;r tó líþ de Æilesforda et de toto illo lesto quod ad illum manerium pertinet, C. D. B. iii. 659, 25. [v. N. E. D. lathe.]
l&aelig-acute;þan to cause to be hateful, cause a person (dat.) to shun :-- Eal þæt hé forbeóde and his gingrum l&aelig-acute;þe omnia que discipulis docuerit esse contraria, R. Ben. 11, 18. v. for-l&aelig-acute;þan (Wlfst. 165, 13).
l&aelig-acute;þettan; p. te To make hateful :-- Se oferlyfa on &aelig-acute;te and on w&aelig-acute;te déð þone man unhálne, and his sáwle Gode l&aelig-acute;ðetteð, O. E. Hml. i. 296, 6. v. láþettan.
l&aelig-acute;þ-leás. v. láþ-leás.
l&aelig-acute;þþ[u]. Add :-- Hí mé s&aelig-acute;don &thorn-bar; sum wer wunne on þ&aelig-acute;re hefigestan hatunge his gesacan, þæs l&aelig-acute;þþu (l&aelig-acute;ðð, v. l.) and feóndscipe forð weóx tó þon swíðe &thorn-bar; . . . quidam vir gravissima adversarii sui aemulatione laborabat, cujus ad hoc usque odium prorupit, ut. . . , Gr. D. 158, 27. Mid wordum laeððu (odii), Ps. Srt. 108, 3. Laeððu unrehtwísre odio iniquo, 24, 19. L&aelig-acute;ðu odium, 35, 3. Hé beseah eádmódlíce þá l&aelig-acute;þþe (l&aelig-acute;ððo, v. l.) and feóndscipe þæs æfstigan mæssepreóstes ejus odia humiliter declinavit, Gr. D. 119, 23. &THORN-bar; wé hí lufian and l&aelig-acute;ððe tó nabban, Hml. S. 16, 265.
-l&aelig-acute;ðu. v. mót-l&aelig-acute;ðu.
-l&aelig-acute;ting. v. for-l&aelig-acute;ting: lætlíce. Add: , latlíce :-- Þane latlíce (morose) wé wyllað beón ges&aelig-acute;d, R. Ben. I. 76, 4. Lætlícor tardius, 68, 3.
læt-ness, e; f. I. slowness in movement :-- Þ&aelig-acute;re sunnan lætnys binnan feówer geára fæce gewyrcð &aelig-acute;nne dæg, Angl. viii. 308, 30. Hé þá lætnysse ðæs geáres rynes geanbidode, Hml. S. 23 b, 647. II. slowness of intellect :-- Þín gerecenes weóx fram mínre lætnysse and dysegan swongernesse ex tarditate mea crevit expositio tua, Gr. D. 174. 23.
-l&aelig-acute;tness. v. á-, æt-, for-l&aelig-acute;tness.
l&aelig-acute;ttewestre, an; f. A female guide :-- Ongan ic biddan míne l&aelig-acute;ttewestran, Sancta Maria, Hml. S. 23 b, 508. v. lád-teów.
-l&aelig-acute;ttu. v. un-l&aelig-acute;ttu.
l&aelig-acute;w, léw, e; f. Injury, weakening :-- Gelíce þám dw&aelig-acute;san þe for heora prýtan léwe (through the disastrous effect of their pride ?) nellað beorgan, Wlfst. 165, 9. v. lim-, syn-l&aelig-acute;w, -léw.
l&aelig-acute;wa. Add :-- Hé is mín l&aelig-acute;wa hic me tradet, Hml. . Th. ii. 244, 5. Hwílon cweþað preóstas &thorn-bar; Crístes l&aelig-acute;wa . . . mage wið Críst hine betellan, swilce hé neádunge gefremode &thorn-bar; fácn wið hine, Hml. S. 27, 157. v. be-l&aelig-acute;wa; l&aelig-acute;we.
l&aelig-acute;wan. Add :-- Be Iúdan Scarioth þe hine l&aelig-acute;wde, Ps. Th. 3, arg.
l&aelig-acute;we (?), es; m. A betrayer :-- Him w&aelig-acute;re betere &thorn-bar; hé geboren n&aelig-acute;re þonne hé his l&aelig-acute;we (l&aelig-acute;wa, v. l.) w&aelig-acute;re. N&aelig-acute;ron þa Iúdéiscan ne se dyrna l&aelig-acute;we (l&aelig-acute;wa, v. l.) þurh God geneádode, Hml. S. 27, 163-166. Cf. (?) ge-fére, ge-síþ for declension.
l&aelig-acute;we mutilated, weakened. [v. N. E. D. lew weak.] v. hungor-, lim-l&aelig-acute;we.
l&aelig-acute;wed a layman. Dele, and see leód: -l&aelig-acute;wed, -léwed injured. v. á-, ge-léwed given under á-léfian, ge-léfed, but better separate as á-, ge-l&aelig-acute;wed. v. l&aelig-acute;w, l&aelig-acute;we, l&aelig-acute;wsa.
l&aelig-acute;wend. Add :-- Wiste Drihten hwÍ his l&aelig-acute;wend and myrðfa wæs, Hml. A. 162, 235: 154, 70. v. be-l&aelig-acute;wend.
604 L&AElig-acute;W-FINGER -- LAND
l&aelig-acute;w-finger. Take here leáw-finger in Dict. : l&aelig-acute;wing. v. be-l&aelig-acute;wing: læx. v. leax.
l&aelig-acute;wsa, léwsa. Take here léwsa in Dict.
láf. I. Add: (1) what is left, a remainder :-- Éce láf (v. éce ; I), Exod. 370. Láfa, belíuendras superstites, i. uiui, An. Ox. 3313. ¶ in the phrase tó láfe as remainder, remaining, left :-- Þrý dagas nú tó láfe syndan, Bl. H. 231, 14. Hwæt is heora nú tó láfe bútan se lytla hlísa and se nama mid feáum stafum áwriten ? signat superstes fama tenuis pauculis inane nomen litteris, Bt. 19; F. 70, 10. Þá gebróðru út fóron, and hé sylf on þám mynstre tó láfe wearð, Hml. S. 23 b, 651. Wæs se m&aelig-acute;sta mancwealm . . . swá þæt heora feáwa tó láfe wurdon pestes pene usque ad desolationem exaestuaverunt, Ors. 1, 6; S. 36, 16. Án of him tó láfe ne wunode unus ex eis non remansit, Ps. Vos. 105, 11. Ic &aelig-acute;nlípigu on þám cafertúne tó l&aelig-acute;fe oþstód, Hml. S. 23 b, 410. (1 a) what is left of something :-- Hí námon þára hláfa and fixa láfe (ðá hláfo (láfe, R.) ðára screádunga, L. reliquias fragmentorum), Mk. 6, 43, (1 b) what is left by something (gen.) :-- Þú miht hér geseón moldan d&aelig-acute;l and wyrmes láfe, Bl. H. 113, 20. Wearð se m&aelig-acute;sta d&aelig-acute;l mid hungre ádýd, and þá láfe ðæs hungres ofslóh se here, Hml. Th. i. 404, 11. II. Add :-- Him féla láf (used with collective force and taking verb in plural?) ne meahton sceððan, B. 1032. IV. Add :-- Þ&aelig-acute;r Alexandres láf wæs and his sunu, Ors. 3, 11; S. 148, 31. Of wífe &l-bar; hláfe seofa bróðra de uxore septem fratrum, Mt. p. 19, 6. &THORN-bar;te l&aelig-acute;da bróðer his láf tó wíf þæs ut ducat frater ejus uxorem illius, Mt. L. 22, 24. v. beód-, fird-, mete-láf.
laga. Add :-- Laga statutum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 137, 80. v. lagu.
-laga. v. lund-laga.
lagian. Add :-- Ic smeáde hú ic mihte eallum mínum leódscype rihtlícast lagian þá þing tó þearfe þe wé scylan healdan, Ll. Lbmn. 269, 14. v. ge-lagian.
-lagol. v. &aelig-acute;-lagol.
lagu. I. the body of rules binding on the members of a state or community :-- Hé hit béte swá swá lagu t&aelig-acute;ce (as the law directs), Ll. Th. i. 418, 14. Swá man swýðor spæc embe rihte lage swá mann dyde máre unlaga, Chr. 1086; P. 218, 19. Hí eallum folce góde lage (fulle lagu, v. l.) behéton, 1052 ; P. 180, 33. (In the passages from the Chronicle the word might be plural, v. II.) I a. where the state is named :-- On Cantwara lage, Ll. Th. i. 330, 17. On Engla lage, Wlfst. 311, 4. I b. where the name of the ruler with whom a code of laws is connected is given :-- Dene and Engle wurdon samm&aelig-acute;le tó Eádgáres lage, Chr. 1018; P. 154, 16. Ic (Cnut) wylle &thorn-bar; eal þeódscype Eádgáres lage healde, Cht. E. 231, 3. I c. the regulations that concern a particular class :-- Be leódgeðingðum and lage. Wæs hwílum on Engla lagum &thorn-bar; leód and lagu fór be geþincðum, and þá w&aelig-acute;ron þeódwitan weorðscipes wyrðe &aelig-acute;lc be his m&aelig-acute;ðe, Ll. Th. i. 190, 11. Ðegenes lagu is &thorn-bar; hé sý his bócrihtes wyrðe, and &thorn-bar; hé ðreó ðinc of his lande dó, 432, 4. Norðhymbra preósta lagu, ii. 290, 1. Ðeów swán and ðeów beócere æfter forðsíðe beón ánre lage wyrðe, i. 436, 20. I d. what is fixed by law in a particular case :-- Gif hwá þæne friðleásan man healde, béte &thorn-bar; swá hit &aelig-acute;r lagu wæs, Ll. Th. i. 384, 8. Gif hine man &aelig-acute;niges þinges teó, andswarie . . . swá hit lagu (riht lagu, v. l.) sý, 396, 1. II. one of the individual rules which constitute the law (v. I) :-- Ælfrédes laga cyninges, Ll. Th. i. 152, 13. Ðis syndon þá laga þe Æðelréd cyng and his witan ger&aelig-acute;dd habbað, 292, 1. Cyninges lage lytledon, 348, 19. Tuá lagena &l-bar; &aelig-acute;a bis legum, Germ. 388, 16. On Engla lagum, Ll. Th. i. 190, 11. Man rihte laga úp ár&aelig-acute;re, 316, 25: 328, 1. Lage, 228, 1. III. a particular branch of law :-- Mid cynelicere lage fiscali jure, An. Ox. 4844. IV. the action of the courts of law, law (in to go to law) :-- Þár þegen áge twégen costas, lufe oþþe lage, Ll. Th. i. 298, 6. Sé &thorn-bar;e rihte lage and rihte dóm forsace, 384, 16. V. of divine law. (1) (God's) law or laws :-- Gif hwá Godes lage oþþe folclage wirde, Ll. Th. ii. 296, 22. Crístene lage healdan, i. 318, 11. Crístes lage wanodan, 348, 18. Godes laga healdan, 346, 24. Godcunde laga, 306, 25. (2) the law of Moses :-- Þis is lagu and wítigan, Scint. 4, 8. God gesette þá fíf béc on þám þe is Godes lagu, and Móyses hí áwrát . . . and seó lagu forbeád mancynne sinna tó gefremmenne, Ll. Th. ii. 366, 17-23. Móyses cwæð on Godes lage, i. 196, 3. (3) the Mosaic dispensation :-- Under Móyses lage men móston lybban on máran sóftnysse þonne nú æfter Crístes ácennednysse, Hml. A. 15, 58. VI. customary rule or usage :-- Landlaga sýn mistlice . . . laga sceal on leóde luflíce leornian sé þe on lande sylf nele leósan leges et consuetudines terrarum sunt varie . . . leges debet in populis libenter addiscere, qui non vult in patria solus amittere, Ll. Th. i. 440, 23. VII. what is considered right and proper :-- Þæt wé beón wære &thorn-bar; wé náhwár ne gán of lage, Angl. viii. 308, 18. VIII. a rule of action or procedure :-- Hé l&aelig-acute;rde þæt manna gehwilc óðrum beóde þæt, þæt hé wille þæt man him beóde. Ðæt is rihtlic lagu, Wlfst. 67, 3. Þis is seó lagu þe wé healdan sculan, 274, 13. Mid stíþum lagum strictis (pudicitiae) legibus, i. ordinibus, An. Ox. 2178. VIII a. a rule laid down by one in authority for the treatment of a subject :-- Laga áwritenum gesettnessum gedémdan (orthodoxorum patrum) scita (i. decreta) scriptis decretalibus sancxerunt, An. Ox. 1964. R&aelig-acute;dborena laga iuris peritorum scita, 5226. v. burg-, folc-, griþ-, m&aelig-acute;g-, preóst-, regol-&dash-uncertain; lagu.
-lagu(?). v. út-lagu. Cf. -lah; adj.
lagu-flód. Add :-- Lagoflód diluuium, Scint. 200, 6: pelagus, Germ. 401, 8.
-lah ; adj. v. út-lah.
lah-breca. For 'Scint. 2, Lye' substitute :-- Wiðstandan þám lah&dash-uncertain;brecan resistere sacrilego, Scint. 9, 10.
lah-brecende; adj. Sacrilegious :-- Wið God múðe mid lah&dash-uncertain;brecendum woffigende erga Deum ore sacrilego blasphemantem, Scint. 9. 9.
lah-lic. For 'Scint. 9, Lye' substitute :-- Sé þe gylt his bóte lah&dash-uncertain;licre (legitima) beheófað, Scint. 46, 2. Gif hé nelle &thorn-bar; ornest oþþe ne mage, begyte him lahlicne spalan, Ll. Th. i. 489, 16.
lahlíce. Add :-- Þæt hý l&aelig-acute;ran þæt gehádode regollíce and l&aelig-acute;wede lahlíce heora líf fadian, Wlfst. 307, 15. Laglíce legitime, Angl. xiii. 394, 413.
lám. Add :-- Lám hoc argillum, An. Ox. 28, 32. Ic eom láme wiðmeten comparatus sum luto (Job 30, 19), Hml. Th. ii. 456, 13. v. mistel-lám.
lama. Add :-- Lama debilis, Wrt. Voc. i. 75, 40. Sum m&aelig-acute;den wearð lama quaedam puella paralytica, Gr. D. 228, 9. Seó wæs &aelig-acute;r fíf geár loma, Shrn. 128, 20. Þes lama w&aelig-acute;dla búton handcræfte (cf. sé læg bedryda fram cildháde oð his geendunge, 96, 21), Hml. Th. ii. 98, 16.
lamb. Add: , lemb :-- &THORN-bar; lemb agnum, Rtl. 47, 36, 14. Swá swá lamb þonne hit man scyrð, Hml. Th. ii. 16, 21. Sceáphyrdes riht is &thorn-bar; hé hæbbe . . . .i. lamb of geáres geogeðe, Ll. Th. i. 438, 23. Lombur scépa agni ovium, Ps. Srt. 113, 4. Lomberu, 6. Lo[m]bra agnorum, ii. 193, 1. .xx. lamba, C. D. ii. 64, 31. Lamba pæð, iii. 413, 29. [¶ the word does not occur frequently in local names, but Lambehíðe, C. D. iv. 156, 11, Lambahám, i. 298, 3, are instances.] v. cilfer-, púr-lamb.
lambes cerse. Add :-- Lambes cerse thiospis, Wrt. Voc. i. 68, 52.
lám-pytt. Add :-- Tó ðám lámpytte, C. D. iii. 407, 1.
lám-seáðe [?], an; f. Substitute: lám-seáþ, es; m. Cf. lám&dash-uncertain;pytt for use of the plural.
land. I. Add :-- Hé sende ofer s&aelig-acute; getríwe men, and hig férdon swá wíde landes swá hig faran mihton, C. D. B. ii. 389, 20. II. Add :-- Lond territorium, Wrt. Voc. ii. 122, 14. Landes manna scipa .xlii., Chr. 1046; P. 168, 11. Ealle þá þe þ&aelig-acute;r on lande (ealle þá landleóde, v. l.) all those in the country, Gr. D. 145, 7. Ánum ðára burgawará londes (ríces, W. S. regionis) ðæs, Lk. L. 15, 15. Wæs se fruma egeslic leódum on lande, B. 2310. Wé þé willað ferigen tó þám lande þ&aelig-acute;r þé lust myneð tó gesécanne, An. 294. Seó æftre Ethiopia land and leódgeard beligeð úton, Gen. 229. Créca land, El. 250. Þec landa gehwilc herige, Dan. 376. Wé bióð láðe on landa gehwám, folcum fracoðe, An. 408. Hit wæs eald þeáw on þissum landum, Ll. Th. ii. 408, 2. II c. fig. realm, domain :-- In lifgendra londes wynne, Cri. 437 : Gú. 790. On lande in terra (viventium), An. Ox, 4273. III. Add: (1) ground, cultivated land, soil, field :-- Brocen land vel geworht land novalis ager, Wrt. Voc. i. 37, 53. Hé hám cyrde fram pám UNCERTAIN weorce þæs landes, Gr. D. 165, 19. Hé mót neótan londes frætwa, Ph. 150. Londes ceorl the husbandman, Met. 12, 27. Swá hwá swá wille sáwan wæstmb&aelig-acute;re land, Bt. 23 ; F. 78, 21. Wé sceolon bletsian úre land, and Drihten biddan &thorn-bar; þá wæstmas þe on eorðan syndon geþeón mótan, Verc. Först. 129, 26. Blósmige land florea rura, Wülck. Gl. 256, 3. Lond beóð gefrætwad the fields are made fair, Ph. 116. Land w&aelig-acute;ron freórig, An. 1261. Seówun lond seminaverunt agros, Ps. Srt, 106, 37. Land wæterað arua rigat, Scint. 118, 14. Storm landu (arua) forhwyrfð, 51, 17. (1 a) land attached to a dwelling and in contrast with it :-- Benedictus wunode uppon lande Benedict was out in the fields of the monastery, Gr. D. 165, 14. Sé þe on londe sý he that is in the field, Mt. R. 24, 18. Wæs sunu his ældra on lond (in agro), Lk. L. 15, 25. Hé eóde út on þæt land þencende egressus fuerat ad meditandum in agro, Gen. 24, 63. (1 b) ground in a general sense :-- Hé nolde fleógan fótm&aelig-acute;l landes, By. 275. Licgað æfter lande loccas tódrifene, fex on ioldan, An. 1428. Þý l&aelig-acute;s se hw&aelig-acute;te cíða leás licge on þ&aelig-acute;m lande, Met. 12, 6. (2) ground as property, landed property :-- Landes l&aelig-acute;n precarium, Wrt. Voc. i. 21, 2. Ic gean him and his wífe þæs landes æt Stoctúne wið án hund mancosa, Cht. Th. 597, 33. Hé sealde hiora gehwæðrum hund þúsenda landes and locenra beága, B. 2995. Ic þé hneáw ne wæs landes, Gen. 2824. Næbbe ic . . . welan . . landes ne locenra beága, An. 303. Þegenes lagu is &thorn-bar; hé . . . ðreó ðinc of his lande dó, Ll. Th. i. 432, 5. Hé him brád syleð lond tó leáne, Vy. 76. (2 a) an estate in land :-- On Dyddanhamme synd .xxx. hída . . . Ofer eall ðæt land gebyrað æt gyrde .xii. pænegas . . . and náh man n&aelig-acute;nne fisc wið feó tó syllanne ðonne hláford on land byð &aelig-acute;r man hine him gecýðe. Of Dyddanhamme gebyreð micel weorcr&aelig-acute;den, Se geneát sceal wyrcan swá on lande, swá of lande, C. D. iii. 450, 11-32.
LAND-ÁR -- LANG 605
Monega land binnan þ&aelig-acute;re byrig w&aelig-acute;ron bútan &aelig-acute;lcum ierfwearde largissimae introrsum hereditates et nulli penitus heredes, Ors. 5, 2 ; S. 218, 1. Taurus bróhte þone bisceop tó sumum his landa, Hml. S. 22, 187. Ic gean Alfm&aelig-acute;re and Ælfstáne þára twégra landa æt Hættanleá, Cht. Th. 597, 24: 520, 18 : 523, 27: 524, 19. Of manegum landum máre landriht áríst tó cyniges gebanne, LI. Th. i. 432, 6. (2 b) where the extent of the land is defined :-- Ic selle Cyneswíde ðreóra hída lond. ... Nú gewríte ic hire ðæt ðreóra hída lond . .. and ic hire léte tó . . . ðæt twéga hída lond . .. and ic bidda ðæt ðis ðreóra hída lond and éc ðæt twéga . . ., C. D. ii. 100, 9-24 (and see híd; I. 2). (3) country in contrast with town :-- Be ciépemonna fóre uppe on londe, LI. Th. i. 118, 11. (3 a) on estate in the country :-- Hé genéhuade ánum ðára burgawará and sende hine on lond his (uillam suam) &thorn-bar;te gelésuade ðá bergas, Lk. L. 15, 15. IV. a land, ridge in a ploughed field. v. heáfod-land, land-gewyrpe :-- Eást on ðá furh; ðæt tó ðám sceortan lond, C. D. iii. 437, 24. Tó ðon eásteran lande, v. 194, 27. On ðæt scorte land súðeweard, 379, 32. On ðæt reáde land; fram ðám reáden lande, iii. 419, 19. [v. Philol. Trans. 1898, p. 532.] v. át- (Cht. E. 208, 34), beán-, behát-, beód-, ber[c]-, bóc-, búr-, ceáp- (C. D. iv. 294, 18), ciric-, dene-, dún-, eald-, earnung-, ering-, ete-, fen-, feoh-, fóster-, Franc-, friþ-, gafol-, gebúr-, gedál-, gehát-, geneát-, geréf-, h&aelig-acute;þfeld-, hám-, hw&aelig-acute;te-, l&aelig-acute;n-, m&aelig-acute;d-, m&aelig-acute;dwe-, mæst-, mersc-, munt-, mynster-, neáh-, norþ-, Peác-, sácerd-, scrúd-, súþ-, teóþung-, timber-, unfriþ-, uppe-, wín-, wudu-land ; útan-landes.
land-ár. Add :-- Þæt hé ná cíde be l&aelig-acute;ssan landáre ne causetur de minori substantia, R. Ben. I. 16, 13. Gehealdenum him sylfan landáre reservato sibi usufructorio, 100, 1. Hí l&aelig-acute;fdon heora &aelig-acute;hta . . . Iulianus þá d&aelig-acute;lde heora landáre þe him l&aelig-acute;fed wæs, Hml. S. 4, 82. Heó beceápode þá gymmas and eác hire landáre wið licgendum feó, 9, 54.
land-bóc. Add :-- Ðis is ð&aelig-acute;ra feówer hýda landbóc æt Wíðigleá ðe Eádgár cing hæfð gebócod Cénulfe on éce yrfe, C. D. iii. 457, 23.
land-bygen. This form in the following passage seems an error, as the law, in the title of which it occurs, deals with the sale of a fellow-countryman :-- Be landbygene (= landleóda[n] bebygene?), Ll. Th. i. 110, note I. v. land-leóda.
land-efne, es; n. Amount of landed property :-- Se cyng lét tóscyfton þone here geond eall þis land tó his mannon, and hí f&aelig-acute;ddon þone here &aelig-acute;lc be his landefne, Chr. 1085 ; P. 216, 3.
land-feoh land-tax. Cf. wudu-feoh.
