forhtlicum metum. Lch. ii. 30, 30. Þá nolde hé him geceósan welige yldran, ac þá þe hæfdon lytle worldspéda (few worldly goods), Bl. H. 23, 25 B. absolute and substantive. I. absolute. (1) that are little, (a) cf. A. I. 2 :-- Ðára lvttelra parvulorum, Mt. p. l. 6. (b) cf. A. I. 8b :-- Drihten gehealdeð þá lytlan, Ps. Th. 114, 6. (2) few. Cf. A. II. 3 :-- Woeg lytelra uia paucorum, Lk. p. 8, 7. Ofer lytla super pauca, Mt. L. 25, 21 : 23. (3) not much, only a small amount or quantity :-- Betere ys þám rihtwísan lytel (modicum) þonne þám synfullan mycel wela, Ps. Th. 36, 14. Ð&aelig-acute;m lyttel bið forgefen, Lk. L. 7, 47. On lytlum (lytelum, L. ) getrýwe . . . on lytlum unrihtwís. Lk. 16, 10: 19, 17. Hé sceal of swíðe lytlum hyt onginnan, Solil. H. 45, 16. Þonne wát ic swíðe lytel óðer nánwiht, 66, 17. Ðý l&aelig-acute;s hié fela sellen ðám ðe hié lytel sceoldon, oððe lytel ð&aelig-acute;m ðe hié micel sceoldon, Past. 321, 17. Lytel ágan. Bl. H. 49, 20. Gé sáwað micel s&aelig-acute;d and rípað litel (modicum), Deut. 28, 38. ¶• UNCERTAINwith adverb :-- Wundrum lytel mæg gedón . . . , Bt. 11, 1; F. 32, 21. Þá þurfon swíþe lytles, 14, 2 ; F. 44, 13. &THORN-bar; man crístene menn for ealles tó lytlum tó deáðe ne fordéme, Ll. Th. i. 304, 19. (3a) with gen. :-- Ic hys mæg swíðe litel ongytan oððe náwiht, Solil. H. 25, 15. Hyre þá gýt tó lytel þúhte þæs anwaldes ðe se cyningc &aelig-acute;r gewunnen hæfde non contenta terminis mulier quos a viro suo acquisitos, Ors. l, 2 ; S. 30, 17. Wé witon swíþe lytel þæs þe ár ús wæs búton be gemynde, Bt. 42 ; F. 256, 25. (3 b) in the genitive depending upon an indefinite pronoun :-- Gif þé &aelig-acute;nies willan wana biþ, ðeáh hit lytles hwæt sié si absit aliquid tuae beatitudini , Bt. 11. 1 ; F. 30, 22: 32, 20. Nánwuht ne lytles ne miceles, 30, 25 : Met. 22, 47. (3c) qualified by a demonstrative :-- Þine seofunga for þám lytlan þe þú forlure. Bt. 11, 1; F. 30, 21. (4) unimportant condition, inferior position :-- Oft hé of lytlan ár&aelig-acute;rde tó miclan þá þe him hýrdan, Ll. Th. i. 334, 6:14. II. as substantive. (l) a small quantity, piece, portion, a small thing, a trifle, Lch. ii. 336, 4 [in Dict.] (1 a) with gen. :-- Án lytel febbres, Past. 229, 3. Wudugáte geallan and lytel wínes. Lch. i. 348, 18. Lytel eles, ii. 76, 13. Diles s&aelig-acute;d lytelne, 228, 21. Glædenan rinde lytelra gedó þreó pund on glæsfæt, 252, 7. (2) of persons, (a) cf. A. I. 2 :-- Sua huá ne onfóas ríc Godes swelc lyttel (paruulus), Mk. L. 10, 15. Búta gié geworðe su&aelig-acute; lytlo (cnehtas, R., lytlingas, W. S. parvoli), Mt. L. 18, 3. Of múðe ðára lytla (cildra. R. , cilda, W. S. infantium), 21, 16. Búta wífum and lytlum &l-bar; cildum (cnehtum, R.) exceptis mulieribus et parvulis, 14, 21: 15, 38. Forlétas ðá lytlo (þá cild, R. ), 19, 14. Bróhton tó him lytle (lytlo cild, L. ), Mk. R. 10, 13. (b) cf. A. I. 8 b :-- Énne of lytlum ðisum unum de pusillis istis, Mt. L. 18, 6. Of lytlum ðassum ex minimis istis, 10, 42 : 25, 45. (3) a short time :-- Æfter lytle huíle &l-bar; ymb lytle (ymbe lytel, W. S. ) post pussillum, Mk. L. 14, 70. Embe lytel (æfter lytlum &l-bar; ymb lytle huíle, L. , æfter lytlum hwíle, R. ), Lk. 22, 58. C. adverbial use of various cases. I. to only a small extent, but slightly, not much. (1) acc. :-- Lytel fremað þeáh crísten nama bútan crístenum d&aelig-acute;dum, Wlfst. 65, 21. Lyttel lufad minus diligit, Lk. L. 7, 47. (2) with inst. :-- Sam hé hine miclum lufige, sam hé hine lytlum lufige, Solil. H. 58, 14. Þú hine gedést lytle l&aelig-acute;ssan (paulo minus) þonne englas, Ps. Th. 8, 6 : 118, 87. Ful lytle ðe gearor, Solil. H. 26, 15. II. lytlum a little at a time :-- Geót þriwa lytlum on háte þá ahsan, Lch. ii. 32, 13 : 176, 22 : 230, 21. II. lytlum and lytlum little by little, gradually :-- Hé sceal lytlum and lytlum stígan neár and near stæpm&aelig-acute;lum swilce hé on sume hl&aelig-acute;dre stíge, Solil. H. 45, 16 III. a little. (1) of distance :-- Gefoerde lytel ðona progressus pusillum, Mt. L. 26, 39. (2) of time, (a) with acc. , for a little time :-- Ðá-gét lyttel (lytel, R. modicum) mið iúh ic am, Jn. L. 13, 33. (b) with inst., a little (before) :-- Swá swá þú mé nú lytle &aelig-acute;r gehéte, Bt. 22, 1 ; F. 76, 22 : Met. 12, 13. v. for-, un-, ungemet&dash-uncertain;lytel; lytle, an ; f.: l&aelig-acute;s, l&aelig-acute;ssa.
lytel-fóta. l. (?) fitel-fóta (q. v.).
lýþer-lic. Add :-- Ðá áléde ic mínne kynegyrylan, and mé mid uncúþe hrægle and mid lýþerlice gerelan gegerede, Nar. 18, 3. [v. N. E. D. litherly, adj.]
lýþerlíce. Add: [v. N. E. D. litherly; adv.]
lyþre. l. lýþre, and add: I. of persons :-- Se lýðra man ána (the vile man alone), þonne hé forsihð Godes beboda . . . þonne bið hé deófles ðeówa, Hml. Th. i. 172, 17. Mín lýðra látteów (my rascally guide) forlét mé þus &aelig-acute;nne, Hml. S. 21, 211. Wé sceolon forseón þone lýðran deófol ( the foul fiend), Hml. Th. i. 270, 13. Hwæt synt þá wyrmas búton lýðre men?, Angl. viii. 323, 31. Hw&aelig-acute;r syndon þá wiðersacan eówre lýðran mágas (your vile kinsmen) ?, Hml. S. 23, 296. Lýþrum monnum to vile cravens, Ors. 6, 36; S. 292, 27. II. of things :-- Hú l&aelig-acute;ne and hú lýðre þis líf is on tó getrúwianne. Wlfst. 189, 3. Hit ne gedafenað &thorn-bar; man dó Godes hús ánre mylne gelíc for lýðrum tolle ( for sordid gain), Hml. S. 19, 253. Lýðre gesetnyssa vitiosa compositio, Angl. viii. 313, 26. Ne sceall nán Godes þegn for sceattum riht déman, ac healdan þone dóm búton lýðrum sceattum (without infamous bribes), Hml. S. 19, 246. Þurh lýðra s&aelig-acute;d by seed that does harm, Angl. viii. 300, 24. [v. N. E. D. lither.]
lyt-hwón. Add: I. as substantive :-- Monigo sint geceigdo, lythwón gecoren multi sunt vocati, pauci electi, Mt. L. 20, 16. Lythuó gecoreno, 22, 14. I a. with gen. :-- Lythwón becwóm Húna herges hám eft þanon, El. 142. Lythwón monna geflit paucorum homimum contentio, Mt. p. 2, 10. II. as adv. (1) of distance :-- Þ á hé wæs lythwón þanon ágán progressus pusillum, Mt 26, 39.
Onwende hé his neb áweg lythwón, Lch. ii. 284, 16, (2) of time :-- Lytle huíle (modicum) geséne wére hine cuæð and eftsóna lythuón (modicum) ne uére geséne, Jn. p. 7, 14: Gú. 363. (3) of extent, degree :-- Hé lithwón hogode embe his sáwle þearfe, Hml. S. 26, 243 : 28, 139. Se scamfæsta hæfð genóh on ð&aelig-acute;m tó his bettrunge ðæt his láreów hine suíðe lythwón gemyndgige his unðeáwa verecundis ad conversionem sufficit, quod eis doctor mala sua saltem leniter ad memoriam reducit, Past. 207, 4. (3 a) where the word is equivalent to an emphatic negative :-- Þone síðfæt him snotere ceorlas lythwón lógon . . . hwetton higerófne (far from blaming him, they urged him on), B. 203. (4) gradually, little by little :-- Lythuón onginnes from fruma, æfter ðon ðý æfterra . . . paulatim incipiens a primo, deinde secundo . . . , Mt. p. 11, 11.
lytig. Add: I. in a good sense, prudent :-- Letig astutus (Prov. 13, 16), Kent. Gl. 450: 485: callidus (Prov. 22, 3), 809. Leti, 412: versutus (Prov. 12, 23), 424. II. in a bad sense :-- Litig and p&aelig-acute;tig versuta et callida, Germ. 389, 21. Letig wer hatol vir versutus odiosus, Kent. Gl. 487. Wénst þú þæt seó mengio þínra monna þé mæge dón ges&aelig-acute;ligne ? Nese, nese. Ac gif hié yfele sint and lytige, ðonne sint hié þé pleólicran gehæfd þonne genæfd, Bt. 14, 1 ; Fox 42, note 10.
lytle, an; f. A servant-maid, female slave :-- Heó (Judith) hire lytlan ( Abram. Cf. mid ánre þínene Abra, 109, 231), Hml. A. 114, 401.
lytlian. Add: , lytlan :-- &AElig-acute;lc riht lytleð for Gode and for worulde, Wlfst. 243, 10. [v. N. E D. litele.] v. ge-lytlian.
lytling. Add: I. a child :-- L&aelig-acute;tað þá lytlingas sinite parvulos, Mt. 19, 14. Lytlungas, Ps. L. 1369. II. a person of little account, of inferior position. Cf. lytel; A. I. 7 b :-- Gif &aelig-acute;gðer ge biscopas ge preóstas æfter heora rihtan gesettednesse lifdon, þonne w&aelig-acute;re hit oferflówennis ús litlingum (nobis exiguis) áwiht níwes tó trahtnienne, Chrd. 2, 4.
lytlung, e; f. Diminution :-- Seó godcundnyss underfóhð náne lytlunge, Angl. vii. 56, 537. v. ge-lytlung.

má. Subst. or adj. Add: I. as subst. (I) with partitive genitive sing., something in addition, an additional quantity or amount :-- Ne wilnige ic heora nánes náwyt mycle má ðonne ic néde sceol habban tó mýnes líchaman héle. Solil. H. 37, 11. Ne wé wítegan habbað þæt ús andgytes má &aelig-acute;fre secgan, Ps. Th. 73, 9. (2) a greater number, more individuals of the kind specified, (a) with partitive genitive plural (or of noun of multitude) :-- Næs his folces ná má ofslagen þonne nigon, Ors. 4, 1 ; S. 156, 24. Þ &aelig-acute;r biþ wundra má þonne hit &aelig-acute;nig mæg áþencean, Cri. 989. Februarius hæfð þý geáre (leap-year) ánum dæge má daga þonne þý óðrum geáre, Angl. viii. 305, 43. (c) to express an indefinite excess over a number stated approximately :-- Sume habbað twá oþþe má. Ll. Th. i. 316, 9: 438, 13. Twá hund oððe má, El. 634: Ælfc. Gr. Z. 32, 16. (3) other individuals of the kind specified, other persons or things in addition to those mentioned :-- &THORN-bar; unriht álegde úre hlaford; &thorn-bar; hé má móte. Ll. Lbmn. 244, 36. Þæt hé menige tó þám ilcan wuda þ&aelig-acute;r ic ðás sceaftas cearf fetige hym þár má, Solil. H. 1. 11. Hwæt wille ic má cwæðan ?, 37, 6. (3a) with gen. :-- For þ&aelig-acute;m hé ne úþe þæt &aelig-acute;nig má folca for his þingum forwurde þonne hé self mid his ágenre þeóde, Ors. 2, 5; S. 80, 33. má; adv. hús and anlícnyssa þurh þ&aelig-acute;ra manna handa þe hí macodon and guton, Hml. S. 29, 181. Me mæig in Maio and Iunio . . . fiscwer and mylne macian, Angl. ix. 261, 13. Hér wearð getimbrod ð mynster on Winceastre &thorn-bar; Cynwalh lét macian, Chr. 648; P. 28, 17. Mæssereáf of ealdum cláðum macian, Hml, A. 35, 279. (2) with a substance as object :-- Cýswyrhtan gebyreð &thorn-bar; heó of wringhw&aelig-acute;ge buteran macige tó hláfordes beóde, Ll. Th. i. 438, 31. (2 a) to produce an article of food or drink by culinary or other operations :-- Bring mé twá þá betstan tyccenu þæt ic macige mete þínum fæder þ&aelig-acute;r of (ut faciam ex eis escas patri tuo), Gen. 27, 9. (3) to produce by action, bring about a condition of things, a state of feeling :-- Þá Frencisce menn macodon m&aelig-acute;st þet unseht betweónan Godwine eorle and þám cynge, Chr. 1052; P. 183, 14. (3 a) to cause something to happen to a person (dat.), cause a person to experience something :-- Þá b&aelig-acute;don hig sume þæt Samson móste him macian sum gamen, Jud. 16, 25. (3b) to make peace, (α) to bring about a condition of :-- Nis ná tó forgytane &thorn-bar; góde frið þe hé macode on þisan lande, Chr. 1086; P. 220, 13. (β) to make peace between enemies :-- Leófríc eorl cóm wið, and Harold eorl and macedan seht þ&aelig-acute;r betweónan, Chr. 1056 ; P. 186, 34. (4) to give rise to, have as a result, be the cause of :-- Gýfernyss macað þám menn mycele untrumnysse, Hml. S. 16, 272. Gítsung is wyrtruma &aelig-acute;lcere wóhnysse. Heó macað reáflác and unrihte dómas, stala and leásunga, 282 : 288. (5) in grammar, to form a case, tense, &c. , in a specified manner :-- Ðeós declinatio ne macað ná hire vocatiuum on eallum namum on áne wísan, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 31, 15. Elicio macað elicui, 175, 10. Sume ðás maciað femininum on a, 40, 8. Þá maciað praeteritum on aui, 138, 11. (6) to prepare or provide a meal, feast for guests :-- Gelíc þám cyninge þe macode hys suna gyfta simile regi qui fecit nubtias filio suo, Mt. 22, 2. (7) used with of to designate the action of causing what is denoted by the regimen of the prep. to become what is denoted by the object of the verb :-- Fornicatio macað of Crístes limum myltestrena limu, Hml. S. 16, 278. (8) said of constituent parts, to amount to :-- Þ&aelig-acute;rtóeácan syx tída ; þá máciað &aelig-acute;fre ymbe &thorn-bar; feórþe geár þone dæg and ðá niht þe wé hátað bissextum. Lch. iii. 246, 13. II. to subject to operation, manage, use :-- Iubal wæs fæder herpera and þ&aelig-acute;ra þe organan macodun Iubal fuit pater canentium cithara et organo, Gen. 4, 21. III. to cause to be or become something specified, (1) with sb. as complement :-- Superbia geworhte englas tó deóflum and ðone man macað eác, gif hé módigaþ tó swýðe, þæs deófles geféran, Hml. S. 16, 310. (2) with sb. preceded by tó, or simple dative :-- Ic macige þé mycelre m&aelig-acute;gðe faciam te in gentem magnam, Gen. 12, 2. Hé wolde hine macian tó gode, Ælfc. T. Grn. 2, 43. IV. causative uses. (1) with dependent clause, to cause something to happen, bring it about that :-- Hí macedon hit þá &thorn-bar; &aelig-acute;r wæs ful ríce, þa (&thorn-bar;?) hit wearð tó nánþing, Chr. 870; P. 71, 11. (2) to cause to move, put :-- Seó ealde cyrce wæs eall behangen mid criccum . . . and man ne mihte swá ðeáh macian hí healfe úp (not half of them could be put up on the walls), Hml. S. 21, 434. V. to do, perform. (1) with a noun of action as object :-- Hí ealle s&aelig-acute;don &thorn-bar; sé is sóð God þe swilce wundra macað, Hml. S. 22, 56. Sweriað þæt gé dón wið mé swilce mildheortnisse swá ic macode wið eów jurate ut quomodo ego misericordiam feci vobiscum, ita et vos faciatis cum domo patris mei, Jos. 2, 12. (2) to conclude a bargain, contract :-- Mid þám mannan, þe &aelig-acute;r &thorn-bar; loc makeden, Chr. 1094; P. 229, 9. (3) with sbs. expressing the action of vbs., and forming with them phrases approximately equivalent in sense to those verbs :-- Manega drýmen maciaá menigfealde dydrunga þurh deófles cræft, Hml. S. 21, 465. &AElig-acute;nig man ciricmangunge mid unriht ne macie, Ll. Th. i. 306, 28. Þæt hý him absolutionem macigan, Wlfst. 180, 12. VI. to behave, act. (1) with hit and adv. denoting manner :-- Ic nát ná forgeare hú ic hit þus macige I do not quite know how it is I behave so, Hml. S. 23, 556: 672. Þá hálgan martyras on þám scræfe s&aelig-acute;ton, and þám biscope be endebyrdnysse rehton hú hí hit macedon on Decius cáseres timan (how they had acted in the time of the emperor Decius), 786. (2) without hit :-- Riht is &thorn-bar; mynecena mynsterlíce macian, efne swá wé cw&aelig-acute;don &aelig-acute;ror be munecan (cf. riht is &thorn-bar; munecas . . . regollíce libban, 2-4), Ll. Th. ii. 322, 32.
mád. Substitute: mád-mód; adj. Senseless (v. ge-mád) :-- Sum on oferhygdo þrymme þringeð, þrintetð him oninnan ungeméde mádmód (senseless arrogance), Mód. 25.
mæc. In l. 2 for mecca read mecea.
mæcca; an; m. A consort :-- Ic hæbbe crístenne fæder. . . and his mæcca mín módor is of þyssum lífe gewiten, Hml. S. 33, 103. v. ge-mæcca.
mæcga. Add: v. óret-mæcga : -maselio. v. ge-mæclic.
m&aelig-acute;d. Dele the passage from C. D. iii. 52, 15, and add: meadow&dash-uncertain;land :-- Ðára oxena wíc and seó m&aelig-acute;d ðe ð&aelig-acute;r mid rihte tó gebyreð . . . and seó meád benorðan eá, C. D. v. 383, 14-18. Feówer æceras m&aelig-acute;de bewestan eé, i. 175, 2. [On hreódm&aelig-acute;de lace, vi. 153, 9. Móm&aelig-acute;de, iii. 449, 20.] .xii. æcras an westhealfe ð&aelig-acute;re str&aelig-acute;te, and án (æcer) médwa beneoðan ð&aelig-acute;m hliðe, iii. 52, 15. Hec sunt prata . . . stocméd healf benorðan hegforde, be stúre méda sué ðér tó limpað, ii. 65, 27. On súðm&aelig-acute;dwan; of ð&aelig-acute;re m&aelig-acute;de, iii. 77, 18. Æt ð&aelig-acute;ra hína m&aelig-acute;de, vi. 4, 26. On cuttes m&aelig-acute;d ; of þ&aelig-acute;re m&aelig-acute;de, iii. 456, 30. Onbútan ðá m&aelig-acute;dewe, iii. 386, 5. On miclan m&aelig-acute;dua (or pl. ?), iii. 81, 7. Hé eóde on þá m&aelig-acute;dwe (m&aelig-acute;de, v. l.) pratum ingressus, Gr. D. 36, 11. On bulan m&aelig-acute;dæ, C. D. v. 112, 29. On cl&aelig-acute;nan m&aelig-acute;de, 325, 17. On sméðe métue, iii. 460, 19. [On hreódméde, vi. 102, 31 : iii. 97, 30.] On ðá m&aelig-acute;d norðeweardæ, v. 340, 24: vi. 234, 7. M&aelig-acute;da prata, An. Ox. 138. On manegum landum tilð bið redre ðonne on óðrum, ge yrðe tíma hrædra, ge m&aelig-acute;da rædran, Angl. ix. 259, 10. Feldl&aelig-acute;s, m&aelig-acute;da, and yrðland, C. D. vi. 39, 9. Tó m&aelig-acute;dwuum, iii. 386, 1. Una prata on burgwara médum and an norðeweardum burgwara médum healf méd, ii. 66, 34. [Æt westm&aelig-acute;duwan; of westmédwan, iii. 82, 14.] v. dál-, sundor-, m&aelig-acute;r-, wíþig-m&aelig-acute;d.
m&aelig-acute;d-æcer, es; m. A meadow :-- Þæne hagan þe Eádwerd áhte, and þæne m&aelig-acute;dæcer þe þ&aelig-acute;r tó hýrð, Swt. A. S. Rdr. ii. 203, 13. .viii. rn&aelig-acute;dæceras. . . gebyriað tó Cenelmestúne, C. D. vi. 33, 28.
m&aelig-acute;d-díc; f. A meadow-dike :-- Of þám mere on þá ealdan m&aelig-acute;ddíc; þonne andlang díc, C. D. B. iii. 396, 32.
mæder (?). Another version of this prescription has : Ofgeót mid hlúttrum ealaþ, Lch. ii. 354, 19.
mædere. Add :-- Mædre sandix, An. Ox. 8, 345. Mædere, wád sandix, i. iacinto, 2, 436. Wealhbasu &l-bar; mædre uermiculo, 35, 4. On længtene . . . mederan settan, línséd sáwan, Angl. ix. 262, 10.
-m&aelig-acute;dla, v. ge-m&aelig-acute;dla.
m&aelig-acute;d-lacu, e; f. A meadow-stream :-- On þá m&aelig-acute;dlace ; of þ&aelig-acute;re lace, C. D. iii. 457, 6.
m&aelig-acute;d-land. Add :-- . xii. æceras gódes m&aelig-acute;dlandes (m&aelig-acute;dwe-, v. l.), C. D. B. ii. 266, 26.
M&aelig-acute;d-mónaþ July :-- M&aelig-acute;dmónaþ (Méd-, v. l.), Menol. Fox (at end); Hickes i. 215.
mæg (?) power, might, virtue :-- Mæg (mægen ?) sóðes gebedes ys hýhð sóðre lufe uirtus vere orationis est celsitudo caritatis, Scint. 4, 19. Micel ys mæg (uirtus) gif þú ná dera fram þám þe þú gederod ert, 12, 17. Hé Godes ríce . . . eallum mæge (mægene ?) fyrþrode, Lch. iii. 438, 2. Cf. maga, and (?) v. mægen-þrymnes.
m&aelig-acute;g. Add: I. a kinsman :-- Gif áðer oþþe m&aelig-acute;g oþþe fremde þá ráde forsace, Ll. Th. i. 268, 21. Léte heó hit tó sweolcum hire méga swelce hit hire tó geearnigan wille, C. D. ii. 100, 22. Ðis wæs gedón ou gewitnesse his ágenra mága Æðelstánes and Æðelhúnnes and eác Alhmundes his ágenes sunu, v. 141, 22. Ic hátu cýðan . . . mínum mégum and gefeórum, ii. 120, 5. On mínum geongum mágum, 176, 3. I a. a parent, kinsman of an earlier generation :-- On Ines dæge mínes (Alfred's) m&aelig-acute;ges, Ll. Th. i. 58, 24. Be wurþscipe mága (parentum) . . . ne scylon bearn (filii) mágum (parentibus) goldhordian ac mágas bearnum, Scint. 173, 7 -3. Bearn, beó gé underðiódde eówrum ieldrum mágum filii, obedite parentibus vestris, Past. 189, 22. Of h&aelig-acute;þenum mágum ethnicis parentibus (oriundus), An. Ox. 2417. II. kindred involved legal responsibility of its members to one another. (I) where one member was criminal, or subject to criminal prosecution :-- Áð syllan &thorn-bar; hý on heora m&aelig-acute;ge náne þýfðe nyston, Ll. Th. i. 206, 2. Gif hé cl&aelig-acute;ne beó nime hé upp his m&aelig-acute;g, 296, 10. Beó hé feówertig nihta on carcerne . . . and his m&aelig-acute;gas (mágas, v. l.) hine féden gif hé self mete næbbe, 60, 10: 120, 6: 124, 7: 148, 18: 164, 11: 202, 15: 206, 5: 228, 26 : 238, 31 : 286, 32. Gif hwylc his mága hine feormige, þonne beó hé scyldig ealles þæs þe hé áhte, 248, 8, Gif cyninges þegn ætsace . . . nime hé his mága .xii. . . . , ii. 298, 8. Gehealden hí hine .xxx. nihta, and hié hine his m&aelig-acute;gum (mágum, v. l.) gebodien, i. 64, 19. His m&aelig-acute;gum and his frióndum, 90, 8. (2) of conditions when a kinsman was injured :-- Ne gebyreð nánum m&aelig-acute;ge &thorn-bar; feoh búte þám þe sý binnan cneówe, Ll Th. i. 174, 25. Hæbbe hé his mæg forworht he shall have forfeited all claim to compensation in respect to his injured kinsman, 90, 20. Gif mon elþeódigne ofsleá, se cyning áh tw&aelig-acute;dne d&aelig-acute;l weres. þriddan d&aelig-acute;l sunu oþþe m&aelig-acute;gas (mágas, v. l.), 116, 15. Ágife mon þám m&aelig-acute;gum (mágum, v. l.) &thorn-bar; treów, 70, 10; 118, 8: 148, 15: 164, 13: 202, 16: 250, 15 : 406, 26. Se wer gebirað mágum (m&aelig-acute;gðe, v. l.), 186, 4. (3) where protection, assistance, support, is given :-- Mon mót feohtan mid his geborene m&aelig-acute;ge, Ll. Th. i. 90, 24. Gif man gehádodne oþþe ælðeódigne forr&aelig-acute;de . . . , þonne sceal him cyng beón, oþþon eorl þ&aelig-acute;r on lande and bisceop þ&aelig-acute;re leóde, for mæg and for mundboran, búton hé elles óðerne h&aelig-acute;bbe, 174, 8: 348, 6. Healden þá m&aelig-acute;gas (mágas, v. l.) þone frumstól oþ þæt hit (a minor whose father is dead) gewintred sié, 126, 6. Fón mágas tó and weddian heora mágan tó wífe, 254, 20. Ládige hé mid his mágan þe f&aelig-acute;hðe móton mid beran, 344, 26: 362, 23. Gif hwylc landleás man . . . eft his mágas geséce, 204, 6. (4) as cognisant of matters affecting the kindred :-- &THORN-bar; on cyninges and on biscopes gewitnesse gerecce beforan his m&aelig-acute;gum. Ll. Th. i. 88, 2J. III. by the law of the church marriage was forbidden within certain limits of kinship :-- Wé l&aelig-acute;rað . . . &thorn-bar; &aelig-acute;nig crísten mann binnan .vi. manna sibfæce on his ágenan cynne &aelig-acute;fre ne gewítie, ne on his m&aelig-acute;ges láfe þe swá neáhsib w&aelig-acute;re, Ll. Th. i. 364, 23. III a. of illicit intercourse :-- Gif twégen gebróðra oþþon twégen genýhe mágas wið án wíf forlicgan, Ll. Th. i. 168, 19. [v. N. E. D. may a kinsman.] v. fædering-, níd-, un-m&aelig-acute;g; ge-nídmágas.
M&AElig-acute;G -- M&AElig-acute;NAN 627
m&aelig-acute;g; f. Add: -- Seó fríðe m&aelig-acute;g ( the bird that hatches the cuckoo?s egg), Rä. 10, 9. [v. N. E. D. may a maiden.]
m&aelig-acute;g-cnafa, an ; m. A young kinsman :-- Ic gean mínum rn&aelig-acute;gcnafan (cognato) þæs landes æt Anne his dæg . . . and þæs landes æt Worþigum . . . mínum mágcnafan, C. D. B. ii. 329, 21-25.
m&aelig-acute;g-cúð. Add: -- M&aelig-acute;gcúþre cognate, An. Ox. 2700.
m&aelig-acute;g-cynren. Dele, and cf. mid cynrene, An. Ox. 1297.
mægden. Add: v. glíw-mægden.
mægden-cild. Add: -- Beó hit hysecild, beó hit m&aelig-acute;dencild sit masculus infans, sit femina, Ll. Th. ii. 190, 22.
mægden-hád. Add; girlhood :-- On hyre mægdenháde hió ( the Virgin Mary) dyde fela wundra on webgeweorce, Shrn. 127, 15.
mægden-lic. Add: -- Onféng heó þis bebod &thorn-bar; ; heó náht ofer &thorn-bar; ne dyde leóhtlices ne mægdenlicere wísan oððe merwelicre mandatum accepit, ut nihil ultra leve et puellare ageret, Gr. D. 287, 20. Gesáwon hí cuman mycel m&aelig-acute;denlic werod, Hml. S. 7, 251.
mægden-mann. Add :-- Hester, wlitig m&aelig-acute;denmann, Hml. A. 94, 82. Críst m&aelig-acute;denmann him tó méder geceás, 14, 15 : Hml. Th. i. 308, 28.
m&aelig-acute;ge. Add :-- Ic selle Cyneswíðe mínre mégan lond, C. D. ii. 100, 10.
-mége. v. un-m&aelig-acute;ge.
mægen . I. add :-- Swá hwæt swá tóforan þám neádbehéfum belifen byþ on heora mægenes tilunge quidquid necessario victui superest ex operibus manuum, R. Ben. 138, 17, Ic sylle Wulfsige mínum geréfan wið his holdum mægene ( for his loyal and able service) ánes hídes lond, Cht. E. 161, 27. Be sáre þæs magan. Gif se man &thorn-bar; mægen hæbbe l&aelig-acute;t him blód, Lch. ii. 180, 31. Hé (Aidan) munuclíce leofode . . . mid sóþum mægnum, Hml. S. 26, 82. II. add: a virtuous action :-- Þæt wé beón gódum mannum gelíce in ðám mægenum þé wé dón magon, Verc. Först. 169, 3. III. add :--Þæt eorðlice mægn þe þú hér samnast. . . eall þis mægn wát, þe hér tó gemóte cóm, þæt bín heáhsetl is þrymmes áfylled, Wlfst. 254, 13-18. v. full-, god-, heáfod-, helle-, níd-, stíþ-mægen.
mægen-fæst. Add :-- Þes eard nis eác ealles swá mægenfæst hér on úteweardan þ&aelig-acute;re eorðan brádnesse swá swá heó is tómiddes on mægen-fæstum eardum, þ&aelig-acute;r man mæg fæstan freólícor þonne hér, Hml. S. 13, 106-109.
mægenig (?), ménig; adj. Strong :-- Þurh ménige hand ( per rnantum fortem) hé hig út forl&aelig-acute;t of þís lande, Ex. 6, l.
mægen-leást. Add :-- Sum lícðrowere náhte his féðes geweald . . . hé wolde geneál&aelig-acute;can his hulce, gif hé mihte. Þá ofhreów ðám munece þæs hreóflian mægenleást, Hml. Th. i. 336, 11. Sume hí bebyrigan woldon, ac hí hrædlíce for mægenleáste swulton, 404, 2 : Hml. A. 68, 79. Gif hé ongyt þæt þæs gebodes micelnes his mihta oferstíhð, hé . . . his mægenleáste his ealdre gecýþe, R. Ben. 128, 15.
mægen-stán. Add :-- Tó mægenstánes dæne, C. D. v. 45, 23. Anlang wæges tó ð&aelig-acute;m megenstáne, iii. 411, 21.
mægen-strengo. Add : [O. Sax. megin-strengi.]
mægen-þrymm. Add : I. glory, majesty :-- Ðonne hé sit ofer setle his mægenþrymmes tunc sedebit super sedem maiestatis suae, Ælfc. Gr. Z. 237, 9 : Mt. 25, 31. On hys mægenþrymme in sede maiestatis suae, 19, 28. Swilce ic stande æt his wuldorfullan mægenþrymme foran, Hml. S. 23, 830. Seó hálige þrynnys on ánre godcundnysse &aelig-acute;fre wunigende, on ánum mægenþrymme (v. mægen-þrymnes) and on ánum gecynde, Hml. A. 2, 25. II. in a personal sense, a mighty host :-- Þurh þá twelf apostolas, and þurh ealle andetteras and hálige f&aelig-acute;mnan, and þurh ealle þá heofonlican mægenþrymmas. Ll. Lbmn. 415, 19. III. mighty power :-- Ðonne hé cymð mid his mægenðrymme tó démanne and his wuldor tó ætiéwanne cum virtutis suae gloriam venit ostendere, Past. 307, 17.
mægenþrym-nes. Add :-- Án is godcundnys, gelíce wuldor, emnéce mægenðrymnes (maiestas), Ath. Crd. 6 : Hml. Th. i. 276, 20. Mægnþrymnysse maiestatis, Ps. L. p. 247, 8. Mæg[en]ðrymnysse, Ps. L. 28, 3 : An. Ox. 3398. Mæg[en]þrymnesse maiestati, 428.
mæger. Add :-- Hig hæfdon mycele heáfda, and mægere (manigre, MS. ) ansýne erant. . . capitibus magnis, macilenta facie, Guth. Gr. 128, 114.
m&aelig-acute; g-lic. Add :-- Ðes ðegen bæd for his þeówan h&aelig-acute;lðe mid sóðre lufe, for ðan ðe heó ne tósc&aelig-acute;t n&aelig-acute;nne be m&aelig-acute;glicere sibbe ( true love does not make distinction of person in accordance with relationship), Hml. Th. i. 128, 2. Sume for m&aelig-acute;iglicre sibbe hí bebyrigan woldon some would have buried them because they were kinsmen, 404, I.
m&aelig-acute;g-myrþra. Add :-- Se treówleása fæder and m&aelig-acute;gmyrþra ( parri-cida), Gr. D. 239, 4.
mæg-ness. v. un-mægness.
m&aelig-acute;g-r&aelig-acute;denn. Add :-- Gesibbre m&aelig-acute;gr&aelig-acute;dene propinqu&e-hook; necessitudinis, An. Ox. 2810. Hé cwæð tó his hláforde þe him wæs þurh his dohtor on m&aelig-acute;grædenne accersito ejus domino sibi per f iliam propinquo, Gr. D. 181, 19. Be his freóndum þe him gesibbeste synt and þurh m&aelig-acute;gr&aelig-acute;denne nébste, Hml. A. 139, 36.
m&aelig-acute;g-sibb. Add :-- M&aelig-acute;gsibbe parentel&e-hook;, An. Ox. 5131: germanitatis, 9, 2. v. m&aelig-acute;gþ-sibb.
m&aelig-acute;gþ. I. add :-- M&aelig-acute;gþ prosapia, An. Ox. ii. 112. Cóm Críst on ðám tíman þe seó cynelice m&aelig-acute;igð áteórode, Hml. Th. i. 82, 4. Mid cynrene, miégþe prosapia, i. genus progenies, An. Ox. 1297 : stemmati, Germ. 393, 131. Hé férde embe Agathen &aelig-acute;hta, and eác wolde gehæftan ealle hire m&aelig-acute;gðe, Hml. S. 8, 210. IVa. add :-- Þ&aelig-acute;r is mid Estum án m&aelig-acute;gð þæt hí magon cyle gewyrcan, Ors. l, I ; S. 21, 14. IVc. add :-- Þæt mynster is geseted in Huicca maegðe, C. D. i. 114, 14. Ealle Breotone m&aelig-acute;gþe Crístes geleáfan onféngon omnes Brittaniarum prouinciae fidem Christi susceperant, Bd. 4, 16 ; Sch. 428, 14. v. neáh-m&aelig-acute;gþ.
mægþ-hád. Add: virginity as regards man or woman :-- Mægdthád is sé þe wunað on cl&aelig-acute;nnysse &aelig-acute;fre fram cildháde ge w&aelig-acute;pmenn ge wífmenn. Hml. A. 20, 162. Ðás hálgan n&aelig-acute;ron n&aelig-acute;fre mid wífum besmitene. Hí sindon mægðháde gehealdenre cl&aelig-acute;nnysse (virgines sunt;), 19, 125. Heó cwæð &thorn-bar; heó hine ne nánne habban wolde, gyf hire seó úplice árfæstnys geunnan wolde &thorn-bar; heó on , mægðháde Drihtne on cl&aelig-acute;nre forhafednysse cwéman mihte, Chr. 1067; P. 201, 16.
m&aelig-acute;gþ-r&aelig-acute;denn, e ; f. Relationship :-- M&aelig-acute;þr&aelig-acute;dene necessitudinis, i. amiciti&e-hook; An. Ox. 2, 109. M&aelig-acute;gðrédena necessiíudinum (Osburga niihi conlribulibus necessiíudinum nexibus conglutinata, Aid. l, 12), 7, 2. M&aelig-acute;gðr&aelig-acute;dena, Angl. xiii. 27, 2. v. m&aelig-acute;g-r&aelig-acute;denn.
mæg-þryn. m. v. mægen-þrymm. :m&aelig-acute;g-tudor. Dele, and see m&aelig-acute;g-cúþ.
m&aelig-acute;g-wine. Add: The word occurs as a proper name :-- Méguini, Txts. 159, 186, 202 : 161, 293. Iuxta terminos id est bereueg et Méguines paeð, C. D. i. 50, 14. Méguuines paeð, 54, 30.
mæg-wlite. Add :-- Hié oncneówon Crístes róde m&aelig-acute;re tácen on his m&aelig-acute;gwlite (cf. hié gesáwon Cristes róde tácen on his onsiéne. Bl. H. 243, 13), An. 1340.
m&aelig-acute;l a measure, & c. II. add: v. crístel-m&aelig-acute;l. III. add: v. undern-m &aelig-acute;l. IV. add :-- Nýtenu etað swá &aelig-acute;r swá hí hit habbað, ac se gesceádwísa man sceal cépan his m&aelig-acute;les, Hml. S. 16, 318. Þonne hí etað tó ánes m&aelig-acute;les on dæg quando in die una refectio fuerit, Chrd. 15, 7. Be hyre (St. Æthelthryð) is áwrytan &thorn-bar; heó wel drohtnode tó ánum m&aelig-acute;le fæstende, bútan hit freólsdæg w&aelig-acute;re (cf. seldon bútan máran symbelnesse má þonne &aelig-acute;ne síðe on dæge (semel per diem) &thorn-bar; heó wolde mete þicgan, Bd. 4, 19; Sch. 443, 17), 20, 42. Gif hwám geboden sý tó ðigene, and hé hit mid gebelge forsace, ne sý him tó gewilnedum m&aelig-acute;le ( hora qua desideraverit) nánre óðere þigene getíðad, R. Ben. 69, 21. Hý on án m&aelig-acute;l tó nónes gereorden ad nonam semper reficiant, 66, 5. Eten gebróþru on twá m&aelig-acute;l, þæt is &aelig-acute;rest on ð&aelig-acute;re syxtan tíde and eft on &aelig-acute;fen ad sextam reficiant fratres et ad seram cenent, 65, 14: 63, 15. (See also lencten; II.)
-m&aelig-acute;l n. v. for-m&aelig-acute;l: -m&aelig-acute;l; adj. v. ge-, gr&aelig-acute;g-, hring-, sceáden-, wunden-m&aelig-acute;l.
mælan. Add :-- Hyt ys ger&aelig-acute;dd &thorn-bar; Móyses l&aelig-acute;rde &thorn-bar; folc, and þus wordum m&aelig-acute;lde, Angl. viii. 322, 4. Hé m&aelig-acute;lde and him beforan s&aelig-acute;de praedixit, Gr. D. 103, 32. [v. N. E. D. mele.]
m&aelig-acute;l-dropa. Add: [Cf. Icel. mél-dropi foam from a horse's mouth. v. N. E. D. meldrop.]
rn&aelig-acute;le, adj. Marked, spotted :-- On m&aelig-acute;lan beorh middeweardne, C. D. v. 166, 3. v. un-m&aelig-acute;le.
-m&aelig-acute;le; n. v. ed-m&aelig-acute;le : -m&aelig-acute;le; adj. v. þúsend-m&aelig-acute;le: -m&aelig-acute;le; adj. sam-m&aelig-acute;le.
m&aelig-acute; l-sceafa. Add :-- M&aelig-acute;lscaua a caterpillar (described thus : Centenis pedibus gradior per gramina ruris, Ald. 272, 33), An. Ox. 23, 53.
m&aelig-acute; l-tíd, e; f. Meal-time :-- Hé sceal hyne gebiddan on ásettum tídum, and &aelig-acute;r m&aelig-acute;ltídum (-tíman, v. l. Nap. 84) metes ne ábítan, O. E. Hml. i. 303, 7.
m&aelig-acute; l-tíma. See preceding word.
-m&aelig-acute;lum. Add: v. byrþen-, pric-, scýr-, sn&aelig-acute;d-, stefn-, sundor-m&aelig-acute;lum.
m&aelig-acute; nan to mean. I a. add :-- Hé cýðde hwæðer hé m&aelig-acute;nde, ðe ðæs módes fóster ðe ðæs líchoman qui pastionem cordis an corporis suaderet aperuit, Past. 137, 18. I b. add :-- 'Ne sele eldiódigum. ' Hé m&aelig-acute;nde ðá áwiergedan g&aelig-acute;stas ' nec sint alieni participes tui. ' Alienos malignos spiritus vocat, Past. 373, 25. Hwæt m&aelig-acute;nde Sanctus Paulus, ðá hé his láre suá cræftelíce tósceád . . . búton ðæt hé ongeat Títum hwéne monðw&aelig-acute;rran . . . and Timotheus hé ongeat hátheortran , . . , 291, 19.
m&aelig-acute;nan to relate. Add :-- Scipia m&aelig-acute;nde (or under m&aelig-acute;nan to lament; III ?) his earfoða tó Rómána witum, þ&aelig-acute;r hié æt hiera gemóte w&aelig-acute;ron, hwý hié hiene swá unweorðne on his ylde dyden ; and ácsade hié for hwý hié nolden geþencan ealle þá brocu and þá geswinc þe hé for hira willan fela wintra dreógende wæs; and hú hé hié ádyde of Hannibales þeówdóme; and hú hé him tó þeówdóme gewylde . . . ealle Africe Scipionem pro concione de periculo salutis suae contestatum, quod sibi pro patria laborante ab ingratis denunciari cognovisset, Ors. 5, 4; S. 224, 24.
m&aelig-acute; nan to lament. I. add :-- M&aelig-acute;nes (plangent) alle cynno eorðes, Mt. L. 24, 30. M&aelig-acute;næ lugere, 9, 15. M&aelig-acute;nende tumultuantem (turbam), 23. M&aelig-acute;nende (dolentes) wé sóhton ðec, Lk. L. 2, 48. Woepende and m&aelig-acute;nende (-iende, L. ) flentes et heiulantes, Mk. R. 5, 38. M&aelig-acute;nende
628 M&AElig-acute;NE -- MÆSSE-PREÓST
and woepende lugentes et flentes, 16, 10. III. add :-- Hé wépende m&aelig-acute;nde þá unáre þe mon him búton gewyrhton dyde deplorans injurias suas, Ors. 5, 12; S. 240, 9. Giweópun alle and m&aelig-acute;ndun ðá ilca flebant omnes et plangebant illam, Lk. R. L. 8, 52. Hé wæs mænende þá d&aelig-acute;d mid micle wópe flevit, Ors. 5, 12 ; S. 242, 19. v. ge-m&aelig-acute;nan.
m&aelig-acute;ne; II. add :-- Þá synleahtras þe ús forbodene synd, þæt is . . . leásunga and m&aelig-acute;ne áþas, Wlfst. 135, 3. Ic eom anddetta m&aelig-acute;nra áða, Angl. xi. 101, 35.
-m&aelig-acute;ne-lic, -líce, -lioness, -m&aelig-acute;n-ness, -scipe. v. ge-m&aelig-acute;nelic, &c. : -m&aelig-acute;nsurnian, -ung. v. ge-m&aelig-acute;nsumian, -ung : -m&aelig-acute;nung. v. ge-m&aelig-acute;nung.
m&aelig-acute;ra ? :-- Tó werbolde .XL. m&aelig-acute;ra oððe án fóðer gyrda, C. D. iii. 451. 1.
m&aelig-acute;ran, máran. Dele máran, and in Nar. 32, 22 l. m&aelig-acute;ran (v. Angl. i. 512). Add:: v. á-, wíd-m&aelig-acute;ran.
m&aelig-acute;ran, m&aelig-acute;rian to bound, form the boundary of land :-- Ondlang ríðies ðæt hit cymð tó Cearwyllan ; ðonne m&aelig-acute;reð hit Cerwylle seoððan, C. D. iii. 404, 16. &AElig-acute;rest westan-norðan hyt m&aelig-acute;rað Wódnes díc, 456, 15. [v. N. E. D. mere, mear : D. D. mear.] v. ge-m&aelig-acute;rian.
-m&aelig-acute;ran, -m&aelig-acute;rian terminare. v. á-m&aelig-acute;ran. -m&aelig-acute;rian.
m&aelig-acute;r-bróc. Add :-- Of Afene in m&aelig-acute;rbróc . . . on ðone nearuan byge on Afene; upp andlang strémes, ðæt eft upp on m&aelig-acute;rbróc, C. D. iii. 436, 33-437, 8.
m&aelig-acute;r-cnoll a boundary cnoll :-- Of wealhgeate tó m&aelig-acute;rcnolle ; of m&aelig-acute;r-cnolle, Cht. E. 445, 11.
m&aelig-acute;r-cumb a boundary cumb :-- In m&aelig-acute;rcumb ; of ðám cumbe, C. D. iii. 399, 7.
m&aelig-acute;r-díc. Add :-- Tó m&aelig-acute;rdíc; ðonne andlang m&aelig-acute;rdíc, C. D. iii. 415, l.
m&aelig-acute;re a boundary. Add :-- Se ilca forwyrnð þ&aelig-acute;ræ s&aelig-acute; &thorn-bar; heó ne mót þone þeorscwold oferstæppan þ&aelig-acute;re eorþan (m&aelig-acute;ru follows eorðan above the line), Bt. 21 ; S. 49, n. 3. In m&aelig-acute;ru Magedan in fines Magedan, Mt. R. 15, 39. [v. N. E. D. mere, mear a boundary : D. D. mear.]
- m&aelig-acute;re illustrious. I. add :-- M&aelig-acute;ran illustris (Agnae gloriosum exemplar), An. Ox. 4276. II. add :-- M&aelig-acute;re sublimis (celsitudo), An. Ox. 1007. Hú beorht, m&aelig-acute;re, &aelig-acute;nlic o preclara (virginitatis gratia), 1266. M&aelig-acute;re celeberrimns, i. excellentissimus (Agathae rumor), 3937. On þ&aelig-acute;m m&aelig-acute;ran fæstene in celeberrimo (Alexandriae) municipio, 3418. On m&aelig-acute;rum in summo (virginitatis proposito), 5, 21. M&aelig-acute;ran potiorem (virginitatis gloriam), 4153. Swearm þá mæran m&aelig-acute;do bereáfað examen amoena prata popiilatur, 137. [v. N. E. D. mere.]
mære-mæd (?) a boundary meadow :-- Ðis syndon þá landgem&aelig-acute;ro . . . norðrihte on m&aelig-acute;rem&aelig-acute;de westewearde, C. D. iii. 416, 18.
m&aelig-acute;r-flóde a boundary channel :-- Forð on ðá díc tó m&aelig-acute;rflódan, C. D. iii. 408, 31.
m&aelig-acute;r-ford a boundary ford :-- In m&aelig-acute;rford ; of ðan forda, C. D. v. 126, 32.
mær-furh a boundary furrow :-- Andlang m&aelig-acute;rfyrh, C. D. iii. 414, 9. Æt m&aelig-acute;rfurh, 28. [v. N. E. D. mere-furrow.]
m&aelig-acute;r-geard. v. geard.
m&aelig-acute;r-haga a boundary fence :-- Andlang m&aelig-acute;rhagan . . . on þone m&aelig-acute;r-hægan, C. D. iii. 437, 1-6. v. gem&aelig-acute;r-haga under ge-m&aelig-acute;re ; II. ¶.
m&aelig-acute;r-heg. l. -hege, and add :-- Tó ðám m&aelig-acute;rhege, C. D. iii. 79, 13. Ollonc þæs gem&aelig-acute;reheges (cf. gem&aelig-acute;rheges, 1) onbútan Hreódlége; ðæt swá on þone m&aelig-acute;rhege ðe sceót tó ð&aelig-acute;re hálgan &aelig-acute;c, vi. 234, 12 : v. 126, 26.
m&aelig-acute;r-hlinc a boundary hlinc :-- Andlang weges tó m&aelig-acute;rhlinc ; andlang m&aelig-acute;rhlinces, C. D. iii. 414, 10 : 18 : 19 : 21.
-mærian. v. -m&aelig-acute;ran.
m&aelig-acute;r-lacu a boundary stream, v. lacu, where also see gem&aelig-acute;r-lacu.
m&aelig-acute;r-líc. II. add :-- Ðá frægn ic hié and áhsode hwæþer hié ówiht m&aelig-acute;rli[ces] in þ&aelig-acute;m londum wisten quos cum interrogarem si quid nossent in illa regione dignum aliquid ad spectaculum, Nar. 24, 31.
m&aelig-acute;rlíce. Add :-- M&aelig-acute;rlíce insigniter (edidit opusculum), An. Ox, 4585. Hét se cásere hine Críst wiðsacan, and hé móste beón m&aelig-acute;rlíce mid him, Hml. Th. ii. 310, 19. Wæs hyre willa m&aelig-acute;rlícor &thorn-bar; heó wolde hyre sylf hyre mægðhád behátan Gode, Hml. A. 32, 200. Se cyng þæt hús (the temple) m&aelig-acute;rlícost tó Gode bet&aelig-acute;hte þe &aelig-acute;fre &aelig-acute;r &aelig-acute;nig gewurde Wlfst. 278, 4. Hú hé be Gode mihte m&aelig-acute;rlícost wrítan, Hml. S. 15 202.
m&aelig-acute;r-pol a boundary pool :-- Andlang streámes ðæt on m&aelig-acute;rpól; ðonne of ð&aelig-acute;m póle on beánbróc, C. D. v. 198, 31.
m&aelig-acute;r-pull a boundary pull :-- On m&aelig-acute;rpul; ondlong pulles on Afene Cht. E. 445, 13.
m&aelig-acute;rsian. A. trans. III. add :-- Hí mid ege and micelan geláfan m&aelig-acute;rsodon þ&aelig-acute;re eádigan forðfóre dæg, Hml. S. 23b, 800. His gemynd sceal beón m&aelig-acute;rsad mid mæssesongum, Shrn. 84, 3. IV. add :-- Eástrun wé ná ne m&aelig-acute;rsiaþ pascha nan celebramus, An. Ox. 40, 30. Hé mérsode micele symbelnesse for þám sige, Hml. S. 30, 396. Dreám m&aelig-acute;rsodan concentum celebrabant (praefatae virgines), An. Ox 4661. V. add :-- Hé worhte fela wundra . . . se H&aelig-acute;lend hine mérsode (m&aelig-acute;rsode, v. l. ) swá, Hml. S. 27, 205. M&aelig-acute;rsi[an] extollamus, An. Ox. 56, 332. B. intrans. To become famous; clarescere :-- Manige hálige martyras . . . daga gehwylce m&aelig-acute;rsiað and scínaþ (clarescunt) for þám wundrum þe æt heora þám deádum bánum geweorðað. Gr. D. 292, 4. Manige wundra scínaþ and m&aelig-acute;rsiað (clarescunt) þe lange &aelig-acute;r w&aelig-acute;ron mannum bemiþene, 330, 21.
méér-síc a boundary sike :-- On m&aelig-acute;rsíc ; of m&aelig-acute;rsíce on m&aelig-acute;rdíc, C. D. vi. 60, 17.
m&aelig-acute;r-stán. Add: [v. N. E. D. mere-stone.] v. gam&aelig-acute;r-stán under ge-m&aelig-acute;re; II. ¶
m&aelig-acute;rsung. II. add :-- Wæs gemérsad mérsong (fama) of him, Lk. L. 4, 37. III. add :-- On þæs regoles m&aelig-acute;rsunge, Hml. S. 23 b, 151. Ealle þás d&aelig-acute;da and m&aelig-acute;rsunga [caelebrationes (Sabbati observatio, circumcisio, &c. )] wé oncnáwaþ wesan gefyllede, An. Ox. 40, 10. IV. add :-- Heora fixnoðe gelamp micel earfoðnys, þæt Crístes tácne gelumpe micel mærsung, Hml. Th. ii. 290, 6. Wé on lofsangum hyre m&aelig-acute;rða cýðað, &thorn-bar; heó ús þingige tó hyre suna, &thorn-bar; hé ús miltsige for ð&aelig-acute;re m&aelig-acute;rsunge þe wé hyre gedóó, Hml. A. 25, 34. ' UNCERTAIN v. sealmsang-, wíd-m&aelig-acute;rsung.
m&aelig-acute;r-þorn. Add :-- Of ðére þyrnan on m&aelig-acute;rþorn ; of m&aelig-acute;rþorne, D. D. vi. 221, 16.
m&aelig-acute;rþu. I. add :-- Þyses dæges þénung and ðyssere tíde m&aelig-acute;rð sprecað embe Godes tócyme, Hml. Th. i. 600, 2. Æt þ&aelig-acute;re mæssan wearð his m&aelig-acute;rð geswutelod swá &thorn-bar; se hálga gást hine ealne beféng on fýres gelýcnysse, Hml. S. 3, 475. Þú hine gewuldrast and geweorðast and him sylst heáfodgold tó m&aelig-acute;rðe gloria et honore coronasti eum, Ps. Th. 8, 6. Sceolde him man bringan ongeán crætw&aelig-acute;n . . . hiora consulum tó m&aelig-acute;rþe, þæt wæs triumpheum, Ors. 2, 4; S. 70, 35. II. add :-- M&aelig-acute;rþa insignia (ornamentorum et vestium). An. Ox. 5172. Eal swá feala m&aelig-acute;rþa ic geríme [swá] stíþnessa [þú] on bel&aelig-acute;t[st] tot ego glorias numerabo quot uINCERTAINiolentias inrogaueris, 4762. Hí ealle Godes m&aelig-acute;rða wurðodon, Hml. S. 23 b, 799. Tó þám geweorce bróhte &thorn-bar; folc gold and seolfor and deórwirþe gimstánas and menigfælde m&aelig-acute;rþa, Ælfc. Gen. Thw. 3. 31.
m&aelig-acute;r-þyrne a boundary thornbush :-- On ðá blacan þyrnan . . . of ð&aelig-acute;re þyrnan. . . andlang fúrena on m&aelig-acute;rðyrnan; ðanan on m&aelig-acute;rdíc, C. D. vi. 220, 22.
-m&aelig-acute;r-treów. v. gem&aelig-acute;r-treów under ge-m&aelig-acute;re; II. ¶ and see N. E. D. mere-tree : -m&aelig-acute;rung. v. ge-m&aelig-acute;rung.
mæslere, es; m. A sacristan, keeper of a church :-- Gá tó Abundium þám mæslere (cf. cyricweard, 4) vade ad Abundium mansionarium, Gr. D. 228, 15. [Cf. . O. H. Ger. mesinari mansionarius, ianitor, aedituus: Ger. messner.]
mæsse : I. add :-- Se H&aelig-acute;lend gehálgode hláf and wín tó húsle . . . and þá wæs seó mæsse ásteald þurh Críst, Hml. A. 71, 158. Gyf þú mæssan hacelan habban wille, þonne stríc þú mid tóspr&aelig-acute;ddum handum niþer ofer þíne breóst, Tech. ii. 119, 25. Gif þú (cf. se mæssepreóst, 18) wille mé hwylce þearfe gegearwian, geoffra þysne hláf þám ælmihtigan Gode for mé æt þínre mæssan. tó þon &thorn-bar; þú geþingie mínum synnum. Gr. D. 348, 28. I a. a particular instance of the service, a mass :-- Ðaet &e-acute-hook;ghwilc mæsseprióst gesinge fore Ósunlfes sáwle twá messan, C. D. i. 293, 31. Wæs his gewuna þæt hé wolde &aelig-acute;lce dæge habban twá mæssan, bútan hit má w&aelig-acute;re . . . Ðá cwæð hé tó his geféran &thorn-bar; hit betere w&aelig-acute;re &thorn-bar; hig þá mæssan hæfdon, Vis. Lfc. 63-67. I b. the service held on a saint's or martyr's day, a (person's) mass :-- S&c-acute;&i-short; UNCERTAIN Rufi mæsse biþ geméted on þám yldran mæssebócum, Shrn. 121, 30. S&s-acute;&a-short; UNCERTAIN Sabine mæsse bið geméted on þám níwran bócum, 123, 17 : 124, 33. v. heáh-mæsse.
mæsse-&aelig-acute;fen Add :-- Leóhtgesceotu þriwa on geáre, &aelig-acute;rest on Eáster&aelig-acute;fen, óðre síðe on Candelmæsse&aelig-acute;fen, þriddan síðe on Ealra Hálgena mæsse&aelig-acute;fen, Ll. Th. ii. 256, 28.
mæsse-bóc. Add :-- Þ reó þéningbéc, mæssebóc and bletsungbóc and pistelbóc, Cht. Crw. 23, 27. S&c-tilde;i UNCERTAIN Rufi mæsse biþ geméted on ðám yldran mæssebócum, Shrn. 121, 30: 124, 33. On þám níwran sacramentorum, &thorn-bar; ys on ðám mæssebócum, 119, 5.
mæsse-dæg. Add :-- Eádmund cyning forðférde on S&c-tilde;s UNCERTAIN Agustínus mæssedæg, Chr. 946; P. 112, 2. On S&c-acute;&e-short; UNCERTAIN Gregories mæssedæg, 951; P. 112, 7. Se cyng hét ofsleán ealle ðá Deniscan men þe on Angelcynne w&aelig-acute;ron on Bricius messedæg, 1002 ; P. 135, 2.
mæsse-hacele. Add :-- Hé stód áþenedum earmum mid mæsse[reáfe] gescrýdd, and hæfde gréne mæssehacelan on him, Vis. Lfc. 39.
mæsse-hrægel. Add: a vestment used in celebrating mass. The Latin original for Shrn. 112, 19 is; Hic constituit sacerdotes et levitas vestes sacratas in usu cotidiano non uti nisi in ecclesia. Cf. mæsse-reáf.
mæssian. This should be placed after mæsse-wín.
mæsse-niht. Add :-- Móna áþístrode on middes wintres mæsseniht, Chr. 827; P. 60, 23. On ealra hálgena mæsseniht, 971; P. 119, 23. On S&c-acute;&e-short; UNCERTAIN Ambrosius mæsseniht, 1095; P. 230, 27.
mæsse-preóst. Add :-- Leófgár wæs Haroldes eorles mæssepreóst, Chr. 1056; P. 186, 25. Se biscop sceal þrafian þá mæssepreóstas &thorn-bar; hié&dash-uncertain;healdan Godes &aelig-acute;we on riht, and þone híred þe hié ofer beóþ, and þá l&aelig-acute;wedan men þe hié aldormen ofer beón sceolan ; for þon se góda láreów sægde, þonne se mæssepreóst w&aelig-acute;re gel&aelig-acute;ded on éce forwyrd, þonne ne mihte hé þ&aelig-acute;re heorde þe hé Gode healdan sceolde n&aelig-acute;nige góde beón,
MÆSSEPREÓST-HÁD -- MAGAN 629
Bl. H. 45, 6-16. Mæssepreóstas sceolon symble æt heora húsum leorningmonna sceole habban, Ll. Th. ii. 414, 7.
mæssepreóst-hád. Add :-- Se ylca mæssepreóst Constantínus on mæssepreóstháde (on preóstháde, v.l.) his líf geendode idem (presbyter) Constantius in presbyteratus officio vitam finivit, Gr. D. 66, i. &AElig-acute;r his mæssepreóstháde, Shrn. 13, 23. Mæssepreóstháde onfónde sacerdotium accipientes (filii Leui), Scint. 108, 3.
mæsse-reáf. For 'Vestment' 1. 'Vestments', and add :-- Eall swá be mæssereáfe þe sume menn maciað of heora ealdum cláðum, Hml. A. 35, 279. Se hálga Swídun on scínendum mæssereáfe stód swylce hé wolde mæssian, Hml. S. 21, 354. Mæssepreóst sceal habban cl&aelig-acute;ne mæssereáf, Ll. Th. ii. 384, 3. ÞreÓ þéningbéc . . . and án mæssereáf, Cht. Crw. 23, 27. Habbað eów mid swylc mæssereáf and swylce hÚselfata swylce gé mid risnum þá þénunga þénian magon, Ll. Th. ii. 404, 26. Twá mæssereáf, C. D. B. iii. 660, 33.
mæsse-sang. Add: I. celebration of mass :-- Nán mæssesang beón ne mæg bútan þ&aelig-acute;m þrím þingum, &thorn-bar; is ofi&aelig-acute;tan and wín and wæter (cf. panis et vinuin et aqua sine quibus nequaquam missae celebrantur, III. 30, Ll. Th. ii. 406, 2. Hé him swíðlíce ondréd in þám mæssesange (in illa missarum celebritate), Gr. D. 309, 4. His gemynd sceal beón m&aelig-acute;rsad mid mæssesongum on eallum ciricum, Shrn. 84, 3. II. the service held on a saint's day, a (person's) mass. v. mæsse; I b :-- SciUNCERTAIN Agapites mæssesang mæg gemétan sé þe sécð on þám níwran sacra-mentorum, Shrn. 119, 4. [Messe-song, Gen. and Ex.
mæsse-steall, es; m. The place where the priest stood when saying mass (?), the altar (cf. gif preóst búton gehálgodon weófode mæssige, Ll. Th. ii. 292, 18. Se pápa hét hine mæssian at S. Petres weófode, Ch. 995; P. 130, 28. Hé stód æt ðám weófode swylce hé wolde mæssian, Hml. S. 21, 355 :-- Geearnian wé mid gódum d&aelig-acute;dum. 'þæt is mid cl&aelig-acute;ne ælmessan and mid leóhte tó úrum ciricean and tó úrum mæssesteallum, Nap, 43. [Prof. Max Förster suggests another meaning, and compares steall with stallum = a stall, seat in the choir of a church, Nap. 84.]
mæsse-þegnung, e; f. the service of mass :-- On óþran dagan on þ&aelig-acute;re fíftan tíde and sixtan and seofoþan nis ná niæsseþénung álýfed, ac man mót swíðe wel mæssan singan on &aelig-acute;rnemorgen, Angl. xi. 8, 15.
mæsse-úhta the hour of matins on a feast day, the matins themselves :-- Habbon þonne interuallum . . . bútan sunnanúhtan and mæsse-úhtan (festiutatibus sanctorum), þonne ne þearf nán interuallum beón, Chrd. 24, 7. Gé sculon singan sunnanúhtan and mæsseúhton, &aelig-acute;fre nigon ræpsas mid nigon r&aelig-acute;dingum, Ll. Th. ii. 384, 4. Cf. Crístesmæsse-úhta, Chr. 1021; P. 154, 31.
mæssian. Take here mæssian, placed wrongly in Dict. after mæsse-hrægel, and add :-- Sé pápa mid his ágenum handum him his pallium on sette . . . and hé syððan mid þám pallium þ&aelig-acute;r mæssode (mæssan sang, v.l.), swá se pápaUNCERTAIN him gewissode, Chr. 1022; P. 157, l. Messode, Hml. S. 3, 350. Se bisceop him eallum mæssode, 29, 261 : 22, 69. Hí (those under Moses' law) ne mæssoden n&aelig-acute;fre . . . húsel næs gehálgod &aelig-acute;r þám ðe se H&aelig-acute;lend cóm. 10, 222 : Hml. A. 17, 81. Hé hét mæssian for þæs forðfarenan sáwle, and ár&aelig-acute;rde þone deádan, Hml. S. 6, 209. Hé stód æt ðám weófode swylce hé wolde mæssian, 21, 355. Smeágung . . . hwilcan tíman on sunnandagan oþþe on óðran dagan man mæssian móte, Angl. xi. 7, 3, 6. Se H&aelig-acute;lend ne gecýst nú be nánum cynrene, ac of &aelig-acute;lcere m&aelig-acute;gðe tó his þénungum him tó mæssigenne, Hml. A. 17, 87. Sé þe geþrístl&aelig-acute;cð tó mæssianne oððon húsl tó ðicganne, and wát hine sylfne on synnum fúlne, Wlfst. 34, 14. [v. N. E. D. mass; vb.] v. ge-mæssian.
m&aelig-acute;st, adv. I. add: very much :-- Þæt orþancum ealde reccað, þá þe m&aelig-acute;gburge m&aelig-acute;st gefrúnon, Exod. 360. Alexandreas ealra rícost monna cynnes and hé m&aelig-acute;st geþah þara þe ic ofer foldan gefrægen hæbbe, Víd. 16. Þeáh leahtras bysigen monna módsefan m&aelig-acute;st and swíðost. Met. 22, 31: 62. M&aelig-acute;st and fyrmest, Ps. Th. 121, 7. II. add :-- Hé þár mycel gód gegaderode. . . þá hyt eall m&aelig-acute;st gegaderod wæs, Chr. 1065; P. 190, 28. M&aelig-acute;st ealle Africe gecirdon tó Geoweorþan universum pene Africam regno suo junxit. Ors. 5, 7 ; S. 228, 26.
mæstan. Add :-- Þú mæstest on ele heáfod mín inpinguasti in oleo caput meum, Ps. Rdr. 22, 5. v. ofer-mæstan.
mæsten; n. (not m.). In 1. 5 for L. M. read L. In. and add :-- Seó l&aelig-acute;s and ðæt mæsten is gem&aelig-acute;ne tó ðám án and twéntigum hídum, C. D. v. 319, 28. Æceren oððe bóc oððe óðer mæsten, Chrd. 15, 10.
m&aelig-acute;stlíce; adv. Very much :-- M&aelig-acute;stlícust magnopere, Angl. xiii. 447, 1169.
mæst-ling, es; m. A fatling :-- Mæstling altilia (Mt. 22, 4), An. Ox. 61. 29. v. mæst, mæstan, mæstel-bearh.
mæstling. Add :-- Mæstlinges electri (stannique metalla), An. Ox. 2, 27. [v. N. E. D. maslin.]
mæstling-smitþ. l. -smiþ: mæst-lón. v. 16.
m&aelig-acute;tan. Add: with acc. of person and of dream :-- Tó þ&aelig-acute;m sóðum ges&aelig-acute;lðum ic tiohige ðæt ic þé l&aelig-acute;de, þ&aelig-acute;r þín mód oft ymb r&aelig-acute;sweð and eác m&aelig-acute;t te ducere aggredimur ad veram felicitatem, quam tuus quoque somniat animus, Bt. 22, 2 ; S. 51, 13. Þá gemunde Iósep þá swefen þe hine æt sumon cyrre &aelig-acute;r m&aelig-acute;tte recordatus somniorum, quae aliquando viderat, Gen. 42, 9. Hé nán þincg þ&aelig-acute;re byrig ne cúþe gecnáwan . . . and hé wundrigende þóhte swilce hine on niht m&aelig-acute;tte . . . Hé cwæð: 'God gebletsige mé, hwæþer hit furþon sóð sý oððe hwæðer mé on swefne m&aelig-acute;te eall &thorn-bar; ic hér geseó f&aelig-acute;rlices wundres, Hml. S. 23, 512-523. Nó hé gemunde þæt him m&aelig-acute;ted (? metod, MS.; for construction cf. 157) wæs, Dan. 119.
m&aelig-acute;te. Add :-- Hé mót &aelig-acute;gðer witan ge l&aelig-acute;sse ge m&aelig-acute;re, ge betere ge m&aelig-acute;tre ðæs ðe tó túne belimpð, Angl. ix. 259, 23. Hý getrymedon him word m&aelig-acute;te firmauerunt sibi uerbum malum, Ps. Rdr. 63, 6. Micle ge méttan, C. D. B. iii. 491, 12. Ðá druncengeornan synt micele m&aelig-acute;ttran ðonne nýtenu, Hml. A. 145, 27. Swá bióð þá midmestan (m&aelig-acute;stan, v.l.) men onmiddan þám spácan, and þá betran neár þ&aelig-acute;re nafe, and þá m&aelig-acute;tran neár ð&aelig-acute;m felgum . . . þá felga longiað on þ&aelig-acute;m spácan. . . swá dóð þá m&aelig-acute;testan (m&aelig-acute;stan, v.l.) men on þ&aelig-acute;m midmestum, and þá midmestan on þ&aelig-acute;m betstan . . . þá m&aelig-acute;testan (m&aelig-acute;stan, v.l.) ealle hiora lufe wenden tó ðisse weorulde, Bt. 39, 7; S. 130, 1-9. [v. N. E. D. meet.UNCERTAIN] v. byrþen-, pund-, úþ-m&aelig-acute;te.
m&aelig-acute;te; adv. Poorly, badly :-- Him þúhte &thorn-bar; heora frið m&aelig-acute;ttor (mæctor, MS.) gel&aelig-acute;st w&aelig-acute;re þonne hit scolde, Ll. Th. i. 162, 3. v. or-, úþ-m&aelig-acute;te.
m&aelig-acute;þ. I. add :-- Swá þæs gyltes m&aelig-acute;ð beó secundum modum culp&e-hook;, Chrd. 62, l. II. add :-- Nis nánes mannes m&aelig-acute;ð &thorn-bar; cunne ásæcgan eal &thorn-bar; gód þe God hæfð gegearwod þám þe hine lufiað, Angl. xii. 514, 29. Se man hæfð gold, þæt is gód be his m&aelig-acute;de, Hml. Th. i. 254, 19. III. add :-- Intingan beseoh ná m&aelig-acute;þe causam respice non personam, Scint. 185, 12. Riht dóm ys þár ná m&aelig-acute;þa (person&e-hook;) ac weorcu beóþ besceá-wude, 3. IV. add: v. m&aelig-acute;þ-leás, -lic. V. add: v. m&aelig-acute;þ-full :-- On ð&aelig-acute;re sylfan grétinge &aelig-acute;lc sí gegearcod him m&aelig-acute;ð in ipsa salutatione omnis exibiatur humanitas, R. Ben. I. 88, 6. [v. N. E. D. methe.] v. hyge-, un-m&aelig-acute;þ.
m&aelig-acute;þ, mowing. Add :-- Se Godes þeówa cwæð: 'Árís and ber þis gréne híg þám horsum . . . nú is lytel tó láfe þysses m&aelig-acute;þes (cf. hé máweþ heig on þissere dene, 2), and swá þis gedón byþ, ic gá æfter þá' leva fenum viride, porta pabulum jumentis; ecce ego, quia parum superest, opere expleto te subsequor, Gr. D. 36, 31. v. m&aelig-acute;þ-méd ; máwan.
mæþel. Add: v. ge-maþel.
mæþel-friþ, es; n. Peace secured by law at a public assembly, the violation of which had to be compensated twofold :-- Ciricfriþ II. gylde; mæthlfriþ II. gylde, Ll. Lbmn, 3, 6.
m&aelig-acute;þ-full. Add: v. un-m&aelig-acute;þfull.
Mæð-hild. If this be a woman's name, it could not be that which later becomes Matilda, cf. Mathild, Chr. 1067; P. 202, 28: Mahtild, 1083; P. 215, 22. O.H.Ger. Maht-hilt.
mæþlan. Add: [v. N. E. D. mell.]
m&aelig-acute;þ-leás. Add :-- Bebeád Martínus þám m&aelig-acute;ðleásum scealfrum &thorn-bar; hí geswicon þæs fixnoðes, Hml. S. 31, 1322. v. m&aelig-acute;þ; IV.
m&aelig-acute;þ-lic. Add: v. m&aelig-acute;þ; IV: m&aelig-acute;þlíce. Add: v. un-m&aelig-acute;þlíce.
m&aelig-acute;þ-méd, e; f. Reward for mowing :-- Gytteorm for yrðe, m&aelig-acute;ðméd gutfirma ad arandum et firma pratorum fenandorum, Ll. Th. i. 440, 27.
m&aelig-acute;þung, e; f. Measuring, determination of amount, assessment :-- Seó m&aelig-acute;ðung (modus correptionis) is on þám bisceope and on þám ealdre þe under him bið, Chrd. 35, 18.
M&aelig-acute;þ-ware the Medes :-- Médware, Shrn. 155, 33.
m&aelig-acute;t-líc. v. or-, un-m&aelig-acute;tlíc: m&aelig-acute;tlíce. v. or-m&aelig-acute;tlíce: -m&aelig-acute;tu. v. ofer-m&aelig-acute;tu : m&aelig-acute;wect. v. m&aelig-acute;d-m&aelig-acute;wect.
maffian; p. ode To fall away from right conduct, be or become shameless :-- Wín and druncene wíf gedðd hwílon &thorn-bar; witon mafnað uinum et mulieres ebrios&e-hook; apostatare faciunt sapientes; wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away (Ecclus. 19, 2), Chrd. 74, 2. Mid maffi-gendre and prútlicre stæppincge petulanti tumidoque gestu incedere, 77, 2.
maga the stomach. Add :-- Hé cuæð ðæt gé móston drincan ge-wealden wínes for eówres magan mettrymnesse modico vino utere propter stomachum et frequentes tuas infirmitates, Past. 319, 7.
maga able. Add: having means :-- Gif man þone man betýhð þe bið l&aelig-acute;ssa maga (a person of less ability; qui minus possit) þone se cyninges þegn, Ll. Th. i. 154, 7. Sé þe l&aelig-acute;sse maga (mæge, mage, v. ll.) sý (qui minus potest, qui impotencior est [old Latin versions]), 414, 19. Þá preóstas þe áðer oððe ágen wylla oððe mage aelmeshand (a parent who had means but exhausted them by almsgiving; cf. Past. 325, 6-8) hæfenleáse gedyde clerici quos voluntas aut natiuitas pauperes fecit. Chrd. 12, 19. Cf. magian.
magan. For 'does not occur in W. S. , but' substitute: magan = posse occurs in Angl. xiii. 389, 337 : Scint. 46, 6 : 159, 6; in 1. 8 for mágon l. magon. I. add :-- Ne magon hý ús þonne &aelig-acute;nige góde, Wlfst. 122, 7. Ne ástyra ðú yrsunga unmihtigum men, ðeáh ðe ðú mæge bet, Hex. 46, 2. ¶ magan tó :-- Þás úus magon tó genógon nobis istn sufficiunt, Chrd. 90, 8. Hé wæs smeágende hwæt tó bóte mihte æt þ&aelig-acute;m f&aelig-acute;rcwealme. Ll. Th. i. 270, 9. ¶ magan wiþ. (I) dat. or uncertain :-- &AElig-acute;lc wiht mæg bet wyð cyle þonne wið h&aelig-acute;te omnia pene animantia patientius et tolerabilius ad summum frigoris quam ad summum caloris accedant, Ors. i. i; S. 24, 29. Þá getweóde hié hwæðer hié wið him mæhten cum desistendum certamine propter metum periculi arbitrarentur, i. 14; S. 56, 31. Mehte, 4, 6; S. 170, 21. (2) with acc. :--
630 MAGA-ÞÍHT -- MANIEND
Philippuse geþúhte þæt hé leng mid folcgefeohtum wið hié ne mehte, Ors. 3, 7; S. 118, 18. III i. expressing possibility where there are no prohibitive conditions:-- Hæbbe hé ungeligenra manna gewitnesse þe man gelýfan mæge, Ll. Th. i. 158, 13. Hý smeádon hú heora frið betere beón mæhte, 162, 2. Begytan hine magan forgyfenysse gelýfe consequi se posse ueniam credat, Scint. 46, 6. Hé s&aelig-acute;de náne gyltas magan beón álýsede. . . dixit nulla scelera posse redemi. . , 159, 6. (2) expressing the admissibility or certainty of a supposition :-- For ðám hé mæig wénan, gyf hé &thorn-bar; &aelig-acute;r forgýmð, &thorn-bar; . . . qua scire debel, si minus hoc servabit. . . , Ll. Th. i. 440, 13. Wite þú for sóð, gif &thorn-bar; þíne ágne welan w&aelig-acute;ron þe þú m&aelig-acute;ndest &thorn-bar; þú forlure, ne mihtest þú hí forleósan, Bt. 7, 3 ; F. 20, 18. Hé geséþ swá eáþelíce crístenne magan þolian ipse testatur Tam facile Xpianum posse carere, Angl. xiii. 389, 337. III c. i. add :-- Mid scipun þe mon dulmunus h&aelig-acute;tt, þe mon sægð þæt on án scip mæge án þúsend manna it is said that a thousand men can be put into one ship, Ors. 1. 10; S. 46, 33. IV. expressing permission or sanction. add: -- Ágyf þíne scíre, ne miht (mæht, L. ) þú lencg túnscíre bewitan, (iom non poteris uilicare], Lk. 16, 2. Gyf hé wel áginnan wile, ne mæig hé sleac beón, Angl. ix. 259, 21. Bútan hé þone geréfan hæbbe þe þæs wyrðe sý þe &thorn-bar; dón mæge, Ll. Th. i. 280, 15. IV a. in a legal statute may = shall or must :-- .x. wintre cniht mæg bión þiéfðe gewita a boy of ten shall be liable for complicity in a case of theft; puer decem annorum debet scire ne furtum faciat, Ll. Th. i. 106, 18. Gyf hit ðonne elles funden sý, ðonne mæg &thorn-bar; forfangfeoh leóhtre beón, 226, 5. Ic hæbbe gecoren and míne witan hwæt seó steór beón mæge, 276, 31. IV 3 c. ii. add :-- On &aelig-acute;ghwelc þára fata mihte twégen mittan oþþe þreó (cf. hyrdriae capientes singuli metretas binas vel ternas, Ju. 2, 6), Shrn. 48, 29. v. ofer-mæg.
mága-þiht; adj. Strong of stomach, v. þíht.
máge. Add :-- &THORN-bar; nán biscop ne nán mæssepreóst næbbe on his húse wunigende &aelig-acute;nigne wífman, búton hit sý his módor oððe his swustor, faðu oððe móddrige, oððe máge of þám þe ne mage nán unhlísa áspringan, Ll. Th. ii. 376, 23. Fón mágas tó and weddian heora mágan tó wife þám þe hire girnde, i. 254, 20. Gunnilde, Cnutes cynges mágan (sister's daughter), Chr. 1045; P. 165, 23. [v. N. E. D. mowe.] v. níd-máge.
Mage-s&aelig-acute;te.Add :-- In pago Mages&aelig-acute;tna, C. D. B. iii. 242, 23. See note, and Chr. P. ii. 197: 219.
magian; . p. ode To be strong, prevail :-- Ic magude ongeán hine preualui aduersus eum, Ps. Rdr. 12, 5. Ic magude &l-bar; swiþige, Ps. Spl. T. 12, 5. [O. H. Ger. magén valere, vigere.] Cf. maga.
magister. l. mágister, and add: I. a director, chief, ruler :-- Ðonne hé gemétte ðá scylde ðe hé stiéran scolde, hrædlíce hé gecýðde ðæt hé wæs mágister and ealdormonn ( magistrum se esse resoluit), Past. 117, 6: Gen. 40, 21 (in Dict.]. Hé sette him weorca mægestras (magistros operum), Ex. 1. 11. II. master as correlative of servant or man :-- Hit is niédðearf ðæt mon his hláford ondr&aelig-acute;de, and se cneoht his mágister, Past. 109, 14. III. the owner or tamer of an animal :-- Seó leó, deáh hió wel tam sé . . . and hire mágister (magistrum) swíðe lufige . . . heó ábít hire ládteów, Bt. 25; F. 88, 10. IV. a teacher :-- Se mágister (cf. láreow, 3), Past. 455, 20. Mid þám láreówdóme þæs heán mágistres Godes hé wæs on godcundlican þeódscipe getýd and gelæred summis providentibus magistris monasticis disciplinis erudiebatur, Guth. Gr. 112, 96. Nerón wolde hátan his ágenne mágister and his fósterfæder [familiarem praeceptoremque suum] ácwellan þæs nama wæs Seneca, Bt. 29, 2 ; S. 66, 24. Hí hæfdon mágistras gearwe, ðá ðe hig l&aelig-acute;rdon and týdon (magistros, qui docerent], Bd. 4, 2 ; Sch. 345, 14. V. (one's) master, he whose disciple one is :-- Be þ&aelig-acute;re hæfegan gémenne bearna cwæþ mín mægister Euripides in quo Euripidis mei sententiam probo, Bt. 31, 1 : F. 112, 20.
mágister-dóm, es; m. The office of a master or teacher :-- Hefe mægsterdómes pondus magisterii, Scint. 120, 9. On mægsterdóme in magisterio, 122, 13. [v. N. E. D. master-dom.]
magu. Dele last passage, and add: v. wuldor-magu : magu-tudor. l. -túdor.
mál. II. add :-- &THORN-bar; sciplið gewende to Legeceastre, and ð&aelig-acute;r ábiden heora máles (their pay) þe Ælfgár heom behét, Chr. 1055 ; P. 186, 19. v. friþ-, wiþer-mál.
máletung. Dele, and see maþelung.
malscrung. Add: -- Malscrung pressicium (for prestigium?), Hpt. 33, 246, 83. [N. E. D. masker.]
mál-sweord. Add :-- Ic geann mínon swurdhwítan þæs sceardes málswurdes, Cht. Th. 561, 23.
mamera, an; m. Deep sleep :-- Momra (printed momna) sopor, Wrt. Voc. ii. 120, 82. Mameran sopore, An. Ox. 3404. Mamran, 2, 203. v. mamor.
mamor. Dele second passage, and see preceding word.
man. Add: I. with correlative he :-- Ðonne mon má fæst ðonne hé ðyrfe, Past. 313, 1. On ð&aelig-acute;re gesundfulnesse mon forgiett his selfes, 35, 6. Hit is áwrieten ðæt mon ne scyle cweðan tó his fríend . . . , 325, 1. Seó hróf wæs &thorn-bar; man mid his handa ger&aelig-acute;cean mihte, Bl. H. 207, 22. Wudewanhád is &thorn-bar; man wunige on cl&aelig-acute;nnvsse æfter his gemacan, ægðer ge weras ge wíf, Hml. A. 20, 153. Þæt man drince swá swá him ne derede, Ælfc. T. Grn. 21, 36 : Past. 189, 9. Swá swá scyp brincð man ofer s&aelig-acute;; syððan hé tó lande cymð, þonne forl&aelig-acute;t hé &thorn-bar; scyp, Solil. H. 21, 20. II. with correlative they: -- Gif &aelig-acute;nig . . . fluge . . . , &thorn-bar; hine mon slóge swá raðe swá mon hiora fiónd wolde, Ors. 1, 12 ; S. 52, 35. Þæt hús þ&aelig-acute;r man ðweáð heora handa, Wrt. Voc. i. 57, 50. Nán mæssepreóst . . l&aelig-acute;re &thorn-bar; mon hys cyrcan geséce, and him heora teóðinge syllan, and þá geryhtu þe hig þám óþrum syllan sceoldan, Ll. Th. ii. 410, 32. III. with verb in plural:-- Mín ágen . . . man ofgán willað (wile, v.l. ) æt mé, Hml. S. 23, 599.
mán. Add :-- Mid deóflum drohtnoð habban in morðre and on máne, Wlfst. 187, 18. Uton forbúgan mán and morðor, 188, 14. Mán pro nefas, An. Ox. 53, 27. Synt mán ( nequitiae) on heora wunungum, Ps. L. 54, 16. Mánu flagitia, Scint. 88, 15. Hw&aelig-acute;r syndon úre godas þe swylcra mána gyrnen swilce hiora w&aelig-acute;ron, Ors. 1, 8; S. 40, 29.
mán; adj. Add :-- Þá oðswóran hié mid þ&aelig-acute;m bismerlicestan áðe þæt hié him n&aelig-acute;fre on fultume n&aelig-acute;re, þéh þá áðas w&aelig-acute;ren neár máne (or sbst.?] þonne sóðe turpissimam rupti foederis labem adcumulavere perjurio, Ors. 4, 3 ; S. 162, 12. Ic eom mánra áþa gewita, Angl. xii. 501, 19.
mán-áþ. Add :-- &AElig-acute;lcum geleáffullum men is tó warnigenne wið mánáðas (-áða, máne áðas, v. ll.). . . Manega men tellað tó lytlum gylte, &thorn-bar; hí óðre men mid mánáðum beswicen, Hml. A. 147, 89-93.
manáþ-swaru, e; f. Perjury :-- Be mánáðsware de perjurio, Ll. Th. ii. 130, 24.
-mancian. v. be-mancian.
mancus. Add :-- &AElig-acute;gehwilcre spr&aelig-acute;ce þe máre sý þonne . iiii. mancussas, Ll. Th. i. 154, 10. Án æstel on fíftegum mancessa (mon-, v. l.), Past. 9, 1. Hé hæfde þrý mancas (tres aureos) áhýdde . . . þá fundon hí þá ylcan þrý áhýdde mancas . . . secge him se bróþer &thorn-bar; hé sý onscunod fram eallum þám gebróðrum for þám mancessum (pro solidis) . . . tóweorpað þá . .III. mancossas (aureos) ofer hine, Gr. D. 344, 14-37. [The word is of Arabic origin, v. E. H. D. p. 78.]
mán-cynn (?) an evil race. v. mann-cynn; II. 2 (last passage).
mán-d&aelig-acute;d. Add :-- Mánd&aelig-acute;de piaculo, An. Ox. 2006. Mánd&aelig-acute;da facinorum, i. criminum, 921 : passionum, i. uitiorum, 1137.
mán-d&aelig-acute;da, an; m. An evil-doer, one that works iniquity :-- Morðslagan and mánd&aelig-acute;dan. . . and wiccan and unlybbwyrhtan, Nap. 65, 36.
mán-deorf. Add: bold in evil (?). v. dearf: -mane. v. ge-mane.
mán-full. Add :-- Mánful nefarius, Angl. xi. 117, 37. Mánfulne probrosum, An. Ox. 2783. Sittaþ mánfulle (perversi) on heáhsetlum, and hálige under heora fótum þryccaþ, Bt. 4 ; F. 8, 14. Þás mánfullan men þe wé ymbe specað w&aelig-acute;ron getealde for godas, Wlfst. 106, 15. Þára mánfulra forþforl&aelig-acute;tenesse on þás woruldspéda, Bt. 5, 1 ; F. 10, 22.
mánful-líc. Add :-- Iacób hæfde twá geswustru him tó wífe. . . Ac &thorn-bar; is nú mánfullic &aelig-acute;nigum menn tó dónne on þám crístendóme. Hml. A. 16, 73.
mánfullíce. Add :-- Is sé þe mánfullíce (nequiter) geeádmétt hine (se), Scint. 19, 14. Þám gelíc . . . þe mangodon mánfullíce in þám temple, Ll. Th. ii. 352, 22: Wlfst. 295, 25. Hí ðone heofenlican Æðeling mánfullíce ácwellan woldon, Hml. Th. i. 402, 9. Gezabel mánfullíce leofode on fúlum forligere and on &aelig-acute;lcere fracodnysse, Hml. S. 18, 270.
-mang mixing, v. &aelig-acute;g-, ge-mang : -mang mongering. v. ge-mang ; -mang -mong. v. á-, ge-, on-mang : -mangenness. v. ge-mangenness.
mangere. Add :-- Apollonius forlét his þone wurðfullan cynedóm and mangeres naman genam má þonne gifendes, Ap. Th. 10, 9. v. pening-mangere.
mangestre. v. smeoru-mangestre.
mangian (?) to mix :-- Suá is tó mon[g]ianne (mengenne, v. l.) ðá liéðnesse wið ðá réðnesse miscenda est lenitas cum severitate Past. 125, 13.
mangung. Add :-- Of mínra yldrena gestreóne mé becóm þis feoh on handa, and of þyssere ylcan byrig mangunge ic mé &thorn-bar; feoh ger&aelig-acute;hte, Hml. S. 23, 670. Áworpan hí woruldþénunga and mancgunga secularia officia negotique abjiciant, Chrd. 76, 35. v. cyric-mangung.
manian. I. add :-- Hé hié suá micle má lufað suá hé hié suíður manað and suingð ut eo se filios Dei sentiant, quo illos disciplinae flagella castigant, Past. 251, 22. Him fylgð God, ðonne hé hine monað . . . and hine spænð ðæt hé tó him gecierre Deus subsequens monet, qui ad se redire persuadet, 407, 9. Wé maniað &thorn-bar; man Sunnandæges freóls mid eallum mægene healde, Cht. E. 231, 18. II. add :-- Gif wé mid rícan mannan hwæt embe úre neóde manian willað si cum hominibus potentibus volumus aliqua suggerere, R. Ben. 45. 20. III. add :-- On óðre wísan sint tó monianne (cf. l&aelig-acute;ranne, 21) ðá iungan, Past. 179, 19. IV. add :-- Mínes sweóres fæder manode rihtes gafoles pater soceri mei exactionem canonis egerat, Gr. D. 305, 36. . Úre Drihten þreáð þá þe on fæstendagum hiora borga manian, Ll. Th. ii. 438, 34. v. of-manian.
maniend. Add: a creditor :-- Hé s&aelig-acute;de &thorn-bar; hé w&aelig-acute;re hefelíce geswenced fram his maniende (moniendan, v. l.) for twelf scillingum quia a creditore suo pro duodecim solidis graviter offligeretur, intimavit. Gr. D. 157, 32. Hé hét &thorn-bar; hé ágeáfe his maniende (-um, v. !. ), 158, 21.
MANIG -- MANNA 631
manig. I. add:-- Nóes and Abrahames and mæniges óðres word beóð ofergytene, Wlfst. 3, 38. Monegum men gescrincað his fét tó his homme, Lch. ii. 68, 2. Bútan hergiungum þe gewurdon an monigre þeóde, Ors. 3, 9; S. 128, 26. Hé heora monig ðúsend ofslóg, 3, 7; S. 110, 33. Þá Rómániscan m&aelig-acute;denu manega ðurhwunodon on m&aelig-acute;gðháde, Hml. S. 7, 293. Nis þæt gód &thorn-bar; þá monegan godas sién, Shrn. 101, 1. Mid monegum þúsendum, Ors. 5, 4; S. 224, 19. Manega ðúsenda engla, Hml. Th. ii. 334, 16. Monege óþre þeóda; and eác þá monegan cyningas, Ors. 5, 1; S. 214, 15: 4, 8; S. 186, 15. Þá monegan &aelig-acute;rran, 3, 11; S. 142, 6. II. add :-- Dáuid monigne forsende, Past. 36, 8, ¶ the forms in the following are peculiar :-- Swá monig (indeclinable -- quot. ?) beóð men ofer eorðan, swá beóð módgeþoncas quot homines, tot sententiae, Gn. Ex. 168. Dáuid monig (monigne, v. l.) forsende, Past. 37, 8. Þá heáfodmen . . . mænig man (mænig-man as a cpd. ?) mid þám swíðe gedrehtan, Chr. 1096 ; P. 233, 7. III. add :-- Monigum monna (monigum monnum, manegum menu, v. ll.) tó h&aelig-acute;le nonnullis saluti, Bd. 4, 19 ; Sch. 450, 20. v. for-, fore-manig.
manig-feald. I. add: -- Eów tíhþ swíþe manigfeald gedwola (multiplex error), Bt. 26, 1 ; F. 90, 8. Eárhringas of mænigfealdan gimcyinne geworhte, Nar. 26, 32. Þæne mænifealdan cræft multiformem machinam, An. Ox. 119. Mislicu wítu and manigfeald earfoþu carcer, lex, ceteraque legalium tormenta poenarum, Bt. 39, 2 ; F. 212, 27. &AElig-acute;lc deáþlic man swencþ hine selfne mid mistlicum and manigfealdum ymbhogum, and þeáh willniaþ ealle þurh mistlice paþas cuman tó ánum ende omnis mortalium cura, quam multiplicium studiorum labor exercet, . . . ad unum finem nititur pervenire, 24, 1 ; F. 80, 17. Mid mænifealdum (diuersis) híwum, An. Ox. 1043. Geswincfull geár þurh manigfealde ungyld and þurh mycele rénas, Chr. 1098 ; P. 234, 29. II. add :-- Eówer méd is menigfeald on heofonum (mercis uestra multa in caelo, Lk. 6, 23), Hml. Th. i. 556, 11. Mid mænifealdre opulenta (ubertate), An. Ox. 1028. Swá manigfeald yfel and swá micle unéþnesse tot pericula. Bt. 27, 2; F. 96, 12 : 38, 3 ; F. 200, 3. Unárímedum, mænifealdum numerosis, i. multis. An. Ox. 111. Þá mænifealdam collecta, 324. Mænifealde spissos, 563.
manigfealde; adv. In many ways, abundantly: -- His hálines and wundor w&aelig-acute;ron syððan manigfealde gecýdde geond ðis égland, Chr. 641; P. 27, 25. [v. N. E. D. manifold ; adv. O. H. Ger. managfalto.]
manigfealdian; p. ode To multiply, become numerous, abundant, & c. v. manig-feald; II. :-- Weahsað gé and monigfealdiað crescite et multiplicamini, Past. 109, 6. Þte gié monigfaldiga ut abundetis, Rtl. 13, 17. Mænifeal[dian] amplificare, An. Ox. 5215. [v. N. E. D. manifold. O. H. Ger. managfaltón.]
manigfeald-lic. Add: -- Unárimedlicu goldhord þ&aelig-acute;r w&aelig-acute;ron inne and úte, and monigfealdlicu hié w&aelig-acute;ron and missenlicra cynna, Nar. 5, 11. [Þurh mistlice and mænigfealdlice unriht and gyld, Chr. 1104 ; P. 239, 22.]
manigfealdlíce. Add: I. cf. manig-feald; I :-- Ðeáh ðe hié mon manigfealdlíce and mislíce styrede eos per tot varietatis latera mutabilitatis aura versaret. Past. 306, 5. Ætforan ódrum gyldum þe man myslíce geald, and men mid menigfealdlíce drehte, Chr. 1052 ; P. 173, 23. Þý l&aelig-acute;s þæt eów seó sægen monifealdlícor biþ onþúhte ne sim scribendi multiplex, Nar. 3, 29. Wé mihton ðás r&aelig-acute;dinge menigfealdlícor trahtnian the passage admits of more complex treatment, Hml. Th. i. 556, 13. II. cf. manig-feald; II. :-- Hé ne cwæþ ná menifealdlíce (in the plural), 'Tó órum anlícnissum,' ac ánfealdlíce (in the singular), 'Tó úre anlícnisse, ' Ælfc. Thw. Gen. 3, 16. Mænifealdlíce affatim, i. abunde, ubertim, An. Ox. 1689 : Chr. 1086; P. 219, 5. Ealle þá niht swíðe mænifealdlíce (in very large numbers) steorran of heofenan feóllan, náht be ánan oððe twám, ac swá þiclíce &thorn-bar; hit nán man áteallan ne mihte, 1095; P. 230, 28. Scæl ic monigfealdlecor sprecan wiþ þá I must speak more at large against them, Ors. 2, 1; S. 62, 9.
manigfeald-ness. Add: -- Hú micel monigfealdnes (multitudo) swétnesse þínre, Ps. L. 30, 20. Þeáh hé mid þ&aelig-acute;re mænigfealdnysse þ&aelig-acute;re synne bysgunge ábysgod sig licet multiplicitate negotii peccati suspensus sit, Ll. Th. ii. 176, 8. Wé nó þurh ðá mænigfealdnesse úra gebeda sind gehýrede non in multiloquio nos exaudiri scimus, R. Ben. 45, 20.
manig-híwe (?); adj. Multiform :-- Þæne mænifealdan &l-bar; [mæni]-híwan multiformem, Hpt. Gl. 409, 5.
manig-teáw. Add: -t&aelig-acute;we :-- Julius se mænigtywa cásere, Angl. viii. 306, 40. Hé wæs smið and mænigteáwa wyrhta, Hml. A. 134, 591.
manigteáw-ness. Add :-- Ðæt sunnan gér byð gesett on þrím hund dagum and fíf and syxtigum dagum and syx tídum þæs þe ásmeáde séo msenigtýwnes geþungenra wera, Angl. viii. 298, 5.
mán-lic; adj. Wicked, evil :-- Yrre and anda ús synd forbodene, manslyht and morðd&aelig-acute;da and ealle mánlice þing, Hml. A. 8, 190. Hé (Christ) ámeldode heora (the Jews') mánlice geþóhtas, and heora unrihtwísnysse hé him openlíce s&aelig-acute;de, 76, 75.
mánlíce ; adv. Wickedly, (of swearing) falsely, criminally :-- Sé ðe fæder oððe módor mánlíce wyrigð, hé sceal deáðe sweltan, Hml. Th. ii. 324, 29. Se gítsere wyle mánlíce swerian his sáwle tó forwyrde the covetous man will swear falsely to the destruction of his soul, Hex. 52, 29. Ðá forlæg se fæder (Jove) fúllíce, and manega his mágan mánlíce forwemde, Sal. K. 121, 38.
mann. I. add: (1) a human being irrespective of age or sex :-- Mín sunn, ic ðé tó men gebær, Hml. S. 25, 175. (a) used explicitly as a designation applicable to either sex :-- Nis nán wífhádes mann hire gelíca, Hml. Th. ii. 10, 12. Se man sé þe [ne] mæge bearn áfédan, nime þonne . . . meoluc on hyre handæ, Lch. iii. 68, 12. Gif mon ungewintrædne wífmon tó niédh&aelig-acute;mde geþreátige, sié &thorn-bar; swá þæs gewintredan monnes bót, Ll. Th. i. 78, 18. &THORN-bar; hé tó þám untruman men geeóde. Þá hé þá in eóde tó þ&aelig-acute;re f&aelig-acute;mnan, Bd. 5, 3; Sch. 564, 21. (b) in general or indefinite applications, body, person; in pl. people :-- For ð&aelig-acute;re orsorgnesse monn oft áðint on oferméttum. Past. 35, 2. Gif man ofslagen weorðe, ealle wé l&aelig-acute;tað efendýrne, Ll. Th. i. 152, 12. Gif hwá gewerde óðres monnes wíngeard, 50, 24. Gif man óðrum steóp ásette þ&aelig-acute;r mæn drincen, 32, 8, Leófan men, Wlfst. 6, 2, and often. Men ðá leófestan, 232, 12, and often. Ic cwæð þæt w&aelig-acute;ron ealle menn ungemete leáse (omnis homo mendax), Ps. Th. 115, 2. ( See also &aelig-acute;ghwilc, &aelig-acute;lc, &aelig-acute;nig, gehwilc, hwilc, n&aelig-acute;nig, nán, sum. ) (b α) where there is contrast of human and divine :-- Se munuc trýwsie hine sylfne wið God and wið men, Ll. Th. i. 306, 7. Uneáðelic &thorn-bar; ys mid mannum ; ac ealle þing synt mid Gode eáðelice, Mt. 19, 26. (b β) tó mannum cuman (cf. tó túne cuman) to happen, take place, of a season, begin :-- Gyf þú wylt witan &aelig-acute;niges mónðes gesceád, hwylce dæge hé cume tó mannum, Angl. viii. 304, 8. (c) of a child :-- Unc næs gem&aelig-acute;ne man (cf. habban bearn gem&aelig-acute;ne. v. gem&aelig-acute;ne; I. ¶ 1 a α), Hml, S. 2, 157. (d) used predicatively, (to be) man, to have human nature :-- Hé geswutelode þæt hé wæs sóð man, and for ðí metes behófode, Hml. Th. i. 178, 9. (2) in abstract or generic sense :-- Drihten, hwæt is se mann. , . oþþe hwæt is se mannes sunu ? quid est homo . . . aut filius hominis ?, Ps. Th. 8, 5. Restedæg wæs geworht for þám men, næs se man (homo) for ðám restedæge, Mk. 2, 27. Nis mé ege mannes, Ps. Th. 117, 6. Þeáh ic God ne ondr&aelig-acute;de, ne ic man ne onþracige, Lk. 18, 4. (3) man as in inner man :-- Se innra man, &thorn-bar; is séo sáwl, Ll. Th. ii. 224, 6: Verc. Först. 93, 4. (4) an adult male person :-- Lífes man uir ui&e-hook; (uenerabilis), An. Ox. 3699. Hé s&aelig-acute;de . . . heó man ne wæs, Hml. S. 2, 78. Gif bescoren man stéorleás gange. Ll. Th. i. 38, 12. Habban þá . xii. men heora metscype tógædere, 236, 6: 230, 22. II. add: (1) of free men :-- Gif mon wille . . . hláford sécan . . . sé þe hine tó men feormie . . . se þe hine tó men onfó, Ll. Th. i. 86, 2-9. Oft ágyltað ðá hláfordas and ðá menn wuniað on Godes hyldo plerumque offendunt qui regunt, et in patrisfamilias gratia permanent qui reguntur, Past. 321, 3. Gif hwá ymb cyninges feorh sierwie þurh hinc oþþe þurh wreccena feormunge oþþe his manna, Ll. Th. i. 62, 16. Se hláford ne derige his mannum, ne forðan his nýdþeówan, ii. 314, 2. Áh hláforda gehwylc formycle þearfe &thorn-bar; hé his men rihtlíce healde, i. 372, 13. (2) of unfree men (in a temporal or spiritual sense) :-- Nis ná má hláfordinga on worulde þonne twégen, God Ælmihtig and deófol. Sé þe Godes beboda hylt, hé is Godes man . . . ; and sé deófles wore beg&aelig-acute;ð, hé is deófles man, Wlfst. 298, 7-11. Beó hys mann, næs þín ágen, and beó geðafa &thorn-bar; þú æart hys þeówa noli esse velle quasi proprius et in tua potestate, sed . . . Domini te servum esse profitere, Solil. H. 53, 14. Gif man his mæn an wiófode freóls gefe, Ll. Th. i. 38, 15. Æt men fíftene peningas, æt horse healf swá, 224, 25. Be manna metsunge. Ánan esne gebyreð tó metsunge . . . , 436, 25. Wé cw&aelig-acute;don úrum þeówum mannum, 234, 3. Gé hláfordas, dóð gé eówrum monnum (servis) ðæt ilcce, Past. 201, 24. (2a) of a female slave :-- Se fruma wæs &thorn-bar; mon forstæl &aelig-acute;nne wimman Ælfsige . . . Ðá beféng Ælfsige þone mann æt Wulfstáne . . . Æfter þám bæd Ælfsige &aelig-acute;giftes his mannes, Cht. Th. 206, 19-30. (3) where both free and unfree are included :-- Manig strec man wyle werian his man swá hwæðer him þincð &thorn-bar; hé hine ýð áwerian mæge swá for frigne swá for þeówne, Ll. Th. i. 388, 2. (4) applied to members of a fighting force :-- Hé hié. . . on ð&aelig-acute;m ýtemestan ende his monna ásette in exercitu Antigoni dispersi sunt, Ors. 3, 11; S. 146, 35. III. used of a lord :-- Ic beóde &thorn-bar; hý nán man ne brocie . . . &thorn-bar; hý ne mótan ceósan swylcne mann swylce hý wyllan, Cht. Th. 492, 13. v. &aelig-acute;hte-, æsc-, &aelig-acute;wda-, ambiht-, brim-, burh-, carl-, ceáp-, celmert-, ciépe-, ealdor-, eórod-, esne-, fæsting-, fáh-, féster-, féþe-, flot-, freó-, fyrn-, geneát-, geó- (iú-), gesíþ-, gleó-, gum-, hægsteald-, h&aelig-acute;þen-, hagosteald-, heáfod-, healf-, here-, híre-, híred-, hundred-, hundredes, hynden-, inhird-, lah-, land-, leorning-, lid-, mægden-, mynster-, neáh-, norþ-, rípe-, rýne-, s&aelig-acute;-, scegþ-, scip-, scír-, scírig-, steór-, steóres, súþ-, teóþung-, tún-, túnes-, twi-, þeów-, un-, unfriþ-, w&aelig-acute;pen-, w&aelig-acute;pned-, weorc-. weorold-, wíg-, wræc-mann.
manna man. Add :-- Sió ungeðyld geniét ðone monnan ðæt hé geopenað all his ingeðonc, Past. 220, 9. 'Ne hera ðú n&aelig-acute;nne man on his lífe'. . . Sé ðe herian wille háligne mannan, herige hine. . . æfter his geendunge, Hml. Th. ii. 560, 18. 'Þú ácenst sunu.' Oncnáwað þurh þás word sóðne mannan ácennedne of m&aelig-acute;denlicum líchaman, i. 198, 10.
manna manna. Add: , an; m. :-- On ð&aelig-acute;re earce ðá st&aelig-acute;nenan bredu . . . and se swéta mete ðe hié héton moinnaa . . . sceal bión on ð&aelig-acute;m
632 MANN-CWILD -- MÁÞUM-FÆT
breóstum ðæs monnan swétnes, Past. 125, 23. Hét hé hider rignan mannum tó móse manna cynne, Ps. Th. 77, 25.
mann-cwild. Add :-- Ic ðæc biddo ðæt. . . him fiónd ne sceððe, ne hungor, ne monncwild, Shrn. 73, 5.
mann-cynn. II. add: (i) men, a number of people :-- Hwæt þ&aelig-acute;r moncynnes forwearð on &aelig-acute;gðere hand quantas nationes, quantosque populos idem turbo involverit, Ors. 1, 11; S. 50, 14. Hié gegæderedon eal moncynnes &thorn-bar; þ&aelig-acute;r l&aelig-acute;fed wæs, 2, 6; S. 88, 6. Mann slóh eall þet mancynn &thorn-bar; man ár&aelig-acute;can mihte, Chr. 1014; P. 145, 20. (2) a race of men, a people :-- Ðis mannkynn lifað fela geára hoc genus hominum multos vivit annos. Nar. 38, 22. Mannkynn . . . þá man háteð Silhearwan, 29. Seó burh (Alexandria) is m&aelig-acute;rost mid Egyptiscum mancynne, Hml. S. 15, 14. Manega of þám mancinne (the Jews), Ælfc. T. Grn. 20, 41. Ðreála ic on þæt mancyn ( the Israelites) sænde, Wlfst. 133, 19. Þæt is Gog and Magog, þæt beóð þá mancyn (máncyn?) þe Alexander beclýsde binnan muntclýsan (cf. Exsurgent ab Aquilone spurcissimae gentes, quas Alexander rex inclusit, Gog et Magog. See for this legend Bousset, 'The Antechrist Legend,' translated by Keane. v. mun-clýse). Ðá getácniæð alle deófles limæ, þæt beóð alle þá þe deófles weorc wyrcð, Wlfst. 84, 30. Manncynna ealdor Christ, Hml. Th. i. 588, 18.
mann-cyst, e; f. Manly virtue :-- Healdan wé þæt mid gódum d&aelig-acute;dum and mid æðelum mancystum, þæt wé beón gódum mannum gelíce in ðám mægenum þé wé dón magon, and in ðám d&aelig-acute;dum þe wé þurhteón magon, Verc. Först. 169. Cf. gum-cyst.
mann-fultum. Add :-- Ueriatus him geteáh tó micelne monfultum, ond monega túnas oferhergeade, Ors. 5, 2 ; S. 216, 8.
mann-myrþra, an; m. A homicide, murderer :-- Þá wíf þe dód áwegáworpnesse heora bearna . . . sýn hý geteald to manmyrðrum habeantur pro homicidis, Ll. Th. ii. 154, 36.
